title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
正德癸酉當天下鄉試之期
浙藩臬二司請於巡按監察
御史王堯封禮聘龍等以司
試事及期監察御史袁宗儒
奉
命代至寔維監臨惓茲重務謂臣
===
子以人事君之忠莫大於此
乃以龍與教諭林世明為考
試官教諭吳度蜀戴儉李昺
郝文瑞蔡元用何亦尹唐灰
訓導田獻張輅為同考試官
凡所以矢心誓眾明約厲禁
督察裁節之務經畫授成靡
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序

正德癸酉，當天下鄉試之期，浙藩臬二司請於巡按監察御史王堯封，禮聘龍等以司試事。及期，監察御史袁宗儒奉命代至，寔維監臨，惓茲重務，謂臣子以人事君之忠莫大於此。乃以龍與教諭林世明為考試官，教諭吳度蜀、戴儉、李昺、郝文瑞、蔡元用、何亦尹、唐灰，訓導田獻、張輅為同考試官。凡所以矢心誓眾、明約厲禁、督察裁節之務，經畫授成，靡
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the guiyou year of Zhengde [1513], when Provincial Examinations were due to be held throughout the empire, Zhejiang’s Provincial Administration Commission and Provincial Surveillance Commission petitioned the Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Wang Yaofeng, and ceremonially invited me, Long, and others to oversee the examination. When the appointed time arrived, Investigating Censor Yuan Zongru came under imperial orders to replace him and served as Supervising Official. Deeply concerned with this weighty responsibility, he declared that no act of a subject’s loyalty in serving his ruler surpassed that of providing him with worthy men.

He therefore appointed me, Long, and Instructor Lin Shiming as Examiners; and Instructors Wu Dushu [?], Dai Jian, Li Bing, Hao Wenrui, Cai Yuanyong, He Yiyin, and Tang Hui, together with Assistant Instructors Tian Xian and Zhang Lu, as Associate Examiners. All the measures for pledging our resolve and binding the assembled officials by oath, clarifying regulations and enforcing prohibitions, supervising and inspecting, and exercising judgment and control were planned and assigned for execution, with nothing…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有關遺維時雅好儒彥崇獎
作興則鎮守太監劉璟申飭
諸司開布公道則巡視右都
御史陶琰相成厥美則督造
太監楊輗晁進監舶太監王
堂督染太監杜甫鹽法監察
御史林季瓊清戎監察御史
===
喻文璧有事茲土者主事伍
全王念陸節胡璉罔不樂預
盛事而提調監試於內則右
布政使蔣昇左參政詹璽副
使鄭陽高貫協賛於外則右
參政陳仁官昶副使閻睿謝
琛左參議羅欽德右參議段
punctuated: 有關遺。維時雅好儒彥，崇獎作興，則鎮守太監劉璟；申飭諸司，開布公道，則巡視右都御史陶琰；相成厥美，則督造太監楊輗、晁進，監舶太監王堂，督染太監杜甫，鹽法監察御史林季瓊，清戎監察御史喻文璧。有事茲土者，主事伍全、王念、陸節、胡璉，罔不樂預盛事。而提調監試於內，則右布政使蔣昇、左參政詹璽、副使鄭陽、高貫；協賛於外，則右參政陳仁、官昶，副使閻睿、謝琛，左參議羅欽德、右參議段
translation_en: …nothing was overlooked [?]. At this time, the Regional Command Grand Eunuch Liu Jing esteemed outstanding Confucian scholars and encouraged and promoted their advancement. Tao Yan, Right Censor-in-chief on an inspection tour, admonished the various offices and ensured that impartial procedures prevailed. Supporting these worthy efforts were Yang Ni and Chao Jin, grand eunuchs supervising manufacture; Wang Tang, grand eunuch supervising maritime trade; Du Fu, grand eunuch supervising dyeing; Lin Jiqiong, Investigating Censor overseeing salt administration; and Yu Wenbi, Investigating Censor auditing military registers. The secretaries Wu Quan, Wang Nian, Lu Jie, and Hu Lian, who had official business in this region, all gladly participated in this important undertaking. Managing arrangements and supervising the examination within were Jiang Sheng, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Zhan Xi, Left Vice Administration Commissioner; and Zheng Yang and Gao Guan, Surveillance Vice Commissioners. Providing assistance outside were Chen Ren and Guan Chang, Right Vice Administration Commissioners; Yan Rui and Xie Chen, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Luo Qinde, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner; and Duan, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
敏僉事吳希由儲珊劉祥炳
汪大章王鼎而參將李隆都
指揮僉事陳璠張奎江洪傅
銘亦與焉其餘執事自收掌
試卷知府梁材劉斐以下咸
慎簡以充罔敢弗虔合提學
副使徐蕃所選士千八百人
===
如故事三試之拔其尤者九
十人錄其姓名與文以
獻而龍謹序其首曰
國朝取士之法參酌古制黜詞
賦以本經術併異路以歸科
目崇雅黜浮正習敦化可謂
簡要切實行之萬世而無弊
punctuated:
敏、僉事吳希由、儲珊、劉祥炳、汪大章、王鼎，而參將李隆、都指揮僉事陳璠、張奎、江洪、傅銘亦與焉。其餘執事，自收掌試卷知府梁材、劉斐以下，咸慎簡以充，罔敢弗虔。合提學副使徐蕃所選士千八百人，如故事三試之，拔其尤者九十人，錄其姓名與文以獻。
而龍謹序其首曰：「國朝取士之法，參酌古制，黜詞賦以本經術，併異路以歸科目，崇雅黜浮，正習敦化，可謂簡要切實，行之萬世而無弊
translation_en:
…Min [completing the name Duan Min on the preceding page], and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Wu Xiyou, Chu Shan, Liu Xiangbing, Wang Dazhang, and Wang Ding. Regional Commander Li Long and Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Chen Fan, Zhang Kui, Jiang Hong, and Fu Ming also participated. The other functionaries, beginning with Prefects Liang Cai and Liu Fei, who were responsible for receiving and keeping the examination papers, were all carefully selected for their duties; none dared be remiss. The 1,800 candidates selected by Education Intendant Xu Fan, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, were assembled and examined in three sessions according to established practice. Ninety of the most outstanding were chosen, and their names and compositions were recorded for presentation to the throne.
Long respectfully provides this preface at the beginning of the record, saying: “Our dynasty’s method of selecting men for office draws judiciously upon ancient institutions. It excludes ornate verse and rhapsodies, grounding selection in classical learning; it consolidates the various avenues of advancement into the examination system. It esteems refinement and rejects superficiality, rectifies scholarly habits, and strengthens moral transformation. It may be called simple, essential, practical, and sound—a system that could be practiced for ten thousand generations without ill effect …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣但文有規制進無雜途茲
欲據三試之作較一日之長
識拔特達之才以盡收一時
英傑斯亦難矣然道義積中
英華發外文也者道義之英
華也雖曰程試之文苟典雅
平正可以見其德之純雄健
===
通達可以見其才之充辯析
該洽可以見其學之博高朗
閎遠可以見其識之明即其
外以叩其中豪傑之士率於
此焉得之今兩浙多士鍾山
川之秀而涵濡
聖化之深學貫于經言根于理源
punctuated: 矣。但文有規制，進無雜途，茲欲據三試之作，較一日之長，識拔特達之才，以盡收一時英傑，斯亦難矣。然道義積中，英華發外，文也者，道義之英華也。雖曰程試之文，苟典雅平正，可以見其德之純；雄健通達，可以見其才之充；辯析該洽，可以見其學之博；高朗閎遠，可以見其識之明。即其外以叩其中，豪傑之士率於此焉得之。今兩浙多士鍾山川之秀，而涵濡聖化之深，學貫于經，言根于理，源
translation_en:
…indeed. Yet compositions have prescribed forms, and advancement admits no miscellaneous routes. To judge relative merit on a single day from the compositions of the three sessions, to recognize and select outstanding talent, and thereby gather all the eminent men of an age—this too is difficult. Nevertheless, moral principle accumulates within, and its finest expression emerges outwardly: writing is the finest expression of moral principle. Though these are compositions written for an examination, if they are classically elegant, balanced, and upright, one can discern the purity of their authors’ virtue; if vigorous and lucid, the fullness of their ability; if discriminating in analysis and comprehensive in scope, the breadth of their learning; if lofty, clear, expansive, and far-reaching, the clarity of their discernment. By examining outward expression to probe what lies within, one can generally discover men of exceptional worth.
Now the many scholars of Liangzhe embody the finest influences of its mountains and rivers and have been deeply imbued with the sage emperor’s transforming influence. Their learning thoroughly penetrates the Classics, and their words are rooted in principle; their sources…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
流有自而途轍不迷故發於
文者如醇雅如雄健如辯博
如高遠無所不備文質得中
初無所謂浮雜粗淺之弊則
夫德之所成才之所能學之
所至識之所達亦略得其一
二矣他日推之天下國家措
===
諸事業必有可觀者焉於戲
盛哉雖然士始固以文進而
其終之所立則又不止於文
士固可以文知而士之所以
為士有非文之所能盡也蓋
所貴於士者志欲正而守欲
專氣欲一而分欲定通則不
punctuated: 流有自而途轍不迷，故發於文者，如醇雅，如雄健，如辯博，如高遠，無所不備。文質得中，初無所謂浮雜粗淺之弊，則夫德之所成、才之所能、學之所至、識之所達，亦略得其一二矣。他日推之天下國家，措諸事業，必有可觀者焉。於戲，盛哉！雖然，士始固以文進，而其終之所立，則又不止於文。士固可以文知，而士之所以為士，有非文之所能盡也。蓋所貴於士者，志欲正而守欲專，氣欲一而分欲定，通則不
translation_en:
…their learning flows from an authentic source, and they do not stray from the proper path. Thus their writing possesses every quality: purity and elegance, vigor and strength, breadth of argument and learning, loftiness and far-reaching vision. Literary refinement and substance are properly balanced, entirely free of the faults of superficiality, incoherence, coarseness, and shallowness. From this one may also discern something of their moral attainments, their abilities, the extent of their learning, and the reach of their understanding. When, in days to come, they apply these to the realm and its governance and put them into practice, their achievements will surely merit attention. Ah, how splendid!
Nevertheless, although scholars initially advance through writing, what they ultimately establish goes beyond writing. Scholars may indeed be known through their writing, yet writing cannot fully reveal what makes a scholar worthy of that name. For what is valued in scholars is upright purpose, steadfast adherence to principle, undivided resolve, and a settled sense of their proper station. When their way is open, they must not…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以勢利易其志塞則不以事
變奪其氣益培才德以厚其
本益充學識以周其用使他
日立
朝居位論建如褚僕射陸宣公
之於唐清忠如趙清獻宗忠
簡之於宋德業文章如劉伯
===
温宋景濂之於
國朝庶幾不愧鄉之先哲無負
朝廷作養甄拔之意然後可尚
勗之哉
福建福州府儒學教授陳龍
謹序
punctuated:
以勢利易其志，塞則不以事變奪其氣，益培才德以厚其本，益充學識以周其用，使他日立朝居位，論建如褚僕射、陸宣公之於唐，清忠如趙清獻、宗忠簡之於宋，德業文章如劉伯温、宋景濂之於國朝，庶幾不愧鄉之先哲，無負朝廷作養甄拔之意，然後可尚。勗之哉！
福建福州府儒學教授陳龍謹序。
translation_en:
…not let power or profit alter their aspirations; when their advancement is blocked, they should not let changing circumstances rob them of their resolve. They should further cultivate their abilities and virtue to strengthen their foundations, and further expand their learning and knowledge to make their practical capabilities comprehensive. Thus, when they eventually take their places at court and occupy office, their deliberations and proposals may resemble those of Vice Director Chu and Lu Xuangong under the Tang; their integrity and loyalty, those of Zhao Qingxian and Zong Zhongjian under the Song; and their virtue, achievements, and literary accomplishments, those of Liu Bowen and Song Jinglian under our dynasty. They may then hope to stand without shame before the earlier worthies of their native region and not disappoint the court’s intention in nurturing, selecting, and promoting them. Only then will they merit esteem. Strive toward this!
Respectfully prefaced by Chen Long, Instructor of the Confucian School of Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian.

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
正德八年浙江鄉試
監臨官
巡按浙江監察御史袁宗儒〔醇夫直隸雄縣人戊辰進士〕
提調官
浙江等處承宣布政使司右布政使蔣昇〔誠之廣西全州人丁未進士〕
浙江等處承宣布政使司左參政詹璽〔廷信江西貴溪縣人甲辰進士〕
監試官
浙江等處提刑按察司副使鄭陽〔宗乾直隸安肅縣人丙辰進士〕
浙江等處提刑按察司副使高貫〔曾唯直隸江陰縣人己未進士〕
===
考試官
福建福州府儒學教授陳龍〔元輔江西新昌縣人壬子貢士〕
山東兗州府東平州汶上縣儒學教諭林世明〔自虚福建莆田縣人甲子貢士〕
同考試官
陝西西安府鄠縣儒學教諭吳度蜀〔大贍四川眉州人甲子貢士〕
直隸廣平府永年縣儒學教諭戴儉〔尚質河南祥符縣人丙午貢士〕
湖廣長沙府安化縣儒學教諭李昺〔德明廣西義寧縣人癸卯貢士〕
山西平陽府絳州稷山縣儒學教諭赦文瑞〔德麟陝西咸寧縣人丁卯貢士〕
福建福州府古田縣儒學教諭蔡元用〔勉行直隸無錫縣人庚午貢士〕
punctuated:
正德八年浙江鄉試

監臨官
巡按浙江監察御史袁宗儒〔醇夫，直隸雄縣人，戊辰進士〕。

提調官
浙江等處承宣布政使司右布政使蔣昇〔誠之，廣西全州人，丁未進士〕。
浙江等處承宣布政使司左參政詹璽〔廷信，江西貴溪縣人，甲辰進士〕。

監試官
浙江等處提刑按察司副使鄭陽〔宗乾，直隸安肅縣人，丙辰進士〕。
浙江等處提刑按察司副使高貫〔曾唯，直隸江陰縣人，己未進士〕。

考試官
福建福州府儒學教授陳龍〔元輔，江西新昌縣人，壬子貢士〕。
山東兗州府東平州汶上縣儒學教諭林世明〔自虚，福建莆田縣人，甲子貢士〕。

同考試官
陝西西安府鄠縣儒學教諭吳度蜀〔大贍，四川眉州人，甲子貢士〕。
直隸廣平府永年縣儒學教諭戴儉〔尚質，河南祥符縣人，丙午貢士〕。
湖廣長沙府安化縣儒學教諭李昺〔德明，廣西義寧縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
山西平陽府絳州稷山縣儒學教諭赦文瑞〔德麟，陝西咸寧縣人，丁卯貢士〕。
福建福州府古田縣儒學教諭蔡元用〔勉行，直隸無錫縣人，庚午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Zhejiang Provincial Examination, Eighth Year of Zhengde (1513)

Supervising Official
Yuan Zongru, Investigating Censor on巡inspection of Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Chunfu and was from Xiong County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the wuchen year.

Proctors
Jiang Sheng, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Chengzhi and was from Quanzhou, Guangxi. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.
Zhan Xi, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Tingxin and was from Guixi County, Jiangxi. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.

Examination Monitors
Zheng Yang, Vice Commissioner of the Zhejiang Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Zongqian and was from Ansu County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate of the bingchen year.
Gao Guan, Vice Commissioner of the Zhejiang Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Zengwei and was from Jiangyin County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year.

Examiners
Chen Long, Professor of the Confucian school of Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, had the courtesy name Yuanfu and was from Xinchang County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the renzi year.
Lin Shiming, Instructor of the Confucian school of Wenshang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, had the courtesy name Zixu and was from Putian County, Fujian. He was a tribute scholar of the jiazi year.

Associate Examiners
Wu Dushu, Instructor of the Confucian school of Hu County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, had the courtesy name Dashan and was from Meizhou, Sichuan. He was a tribute scholar of the jiazi year.
Dai Jian, Instructor of the Confucian school of Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Shangzhi and was from Xiangfu County, Henan. He was a tribute scholar of the bingwu year.
Li Bing, Instructor of the Confucian school of Anhua County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Deming and was from Yining County, Guangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the guimao year.
She Wenrui, Instructor of the Confucian school of Jishan County, Jiangzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, had the courtesy name Delin and was from Xianning County, Shaanxi. He was a tribute scholar of the dingmao year.
Cai Yuanyong, Instructor of the Confucian school of Gutian County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, had the courtesy name Mianxing and was from Wuxi County, Zhili. He was a tribute scholar of the gengwu year.

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
山東濟南府陵縣儒學教諭何亦尹〔公志廣東番禺縣人甲子貢士〕
直隸廣平府邯鄲縣儒學教諭唐奨〔天彞貴州普安州人丁卯貢士〕
河南河南府陝州靈寳縣儒學訓導田献〔宗道山東壽張縣人丁卯貢士〕
直隸池州府儒學訓導張輅〔從殷湖廣江夏縣人甲子貢士〕
印卷官
浙江等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事熊廣達〔九逵江西豐城縣人吏員〕
浙江等處提刑按察司經歷司知事吳鍔〔廷重廣西賀縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官
杭州府知府梁材〔大用南京金吾右衛籍順天府大城縣人己未進士〕
===
處州府知府劉斐〔文夫廣東海陽縣人己未進士〕
受卷官
兩浙都轉運鹽使司同知白翺〔鳳儀府軍前衛籍四川綿州人丁未進士〕
浙江市舶提舉司提舉黄相〔弼甫福建莆田縣人丙辰進士〕
杭州府錢塘縣知縣張文造〔汝升福建古田縣人乙卯貢士〕
彌封官
嘉興府推官俞璋〔朝相直隸太倉州人辛未進士〕
紹興府山陰縣知縣張煥〔主奎江西泰和縣人戊辰進士〕

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
出門如見大賓使民如承大祭己所不欲
勿施於人在邦無怨在家無怨
回之爲人也擇乎中庸得一善則拳拳服
膺而弗失之矣
仁人心也義人路也
易
初九素履往无咎
===
六二鴻漸于磐飲食衎衎吉
乾之策二百一十有六坤之策百四十有
四凡三百有六十當期之日二篇之
策萬有一千五百二十當萬物之數
也
變動不居周流六虛上下无常剛柔相易
書
刑期于無刑
五百里甸服百里賦納總二百里納銍三
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
出門如見大賓，使民如承大祭。己所不欲，勿施於人。在邦無怨，在家無怨。
回之爲人也，擇乎中庸，得一善，則拳拳服膺而弗失之矣。
仁，人心也；義，人路也。

易
初九：素履，往无咎。
六二：鴻漸于磐，飲食衎衎，吉。
乾之策二百一十有六，坤之策百四十有四，凡三百有六十，當期之日。二篇之策萬有一千五百二十，當萬物之數也。
變動不居，周流六虛，上下无常，剛柔相易。

書
刑期于無刑。
五百里甸服，百里賦納總，二百里納銍，三
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
When going out, behave as though meeting an honored guest; when employing the people, behave as though officiating at a great sacrifice. Do not impose on others what you yourself do not desire. In the state, incur no resentment; in the household, incur no resentment.
As a person, Hui chose the Mean as his course. Whenever he attained something good, he clasped it earnestly to his breast and never let it go.
Benevolence is the human heart; righteousness is the human path.

Book of Changes
Initial Nine: Treading simply, one may proceed without blame.
Six in the Second Place: The wild goose gradually advances to the rock. Eating and drinking in contentment. Auspicious.
The yarrow stalks for Qian number 216, and those for Kun 144, making 360 in all, corresponding to the days of a year. The stalks for the two parts of the text number 11,520, corresponding to the number of the myriad things.
Changing and moving without rest, they circulate through the six empty positions. Their ascent and descent follow no fixed rule; the firm and yielding exchange places.

Book of Documents
The aim of punishments is to bring about the absence of punishments.
Within five hundred li lies the royal domain. Within the first hundred li, the grain levy is delivered with the whole stalk; within the second hundred li, the ears of grain are delivered; within the third…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
百里納秸服四百里粟五百里米
茲亦惟天若元德永不忘在王家
文王惟克厥宅心乃克立茲常事司牧人
以克俊有德
詩
南有樛木葛藟纍之樂只君子福履綏之
南有樛木葛藟荒之樂只君子福履
將之南有樛木葛藟縈之樂只君子
福履成之
===
爰居爰處爰笑爰語
考卜維王宅是鎬京維龜正之武王成之
念茲皇祖陟降庭止維予小子夙夜敬止
春秋
公追戎于濟西莊公十八年
諸侯盟于扈文公十五年
宋人圍滕宣公九年宋師伐滕宣公十年
季孫斯叔孫州仇仲孫何忌帥師伐邾取
漷東田及沂西田癸巳叔孫州仇仲
punctuated:
百里納秸服，四百里粟，五百里米。
茲亦惟天若，元德永不忘在王家。
文王惟克厥宅心，乃克立茲常事、司牧人，以克俊有德。
詩
南有樛木，葛藟纍之。樂只君子，福履綏之。南有樛木，葛藟荒之。樂只君子，福履將之。南有樛木，葛藟縈之。樂只君子，福履成之。
爰居爰處，爰笑爰語。
考卜維王，宅是鎬京。維龜正之，武王成之。
念茲皇祖，陟降庭止。維予小子，夙夜敬止。
春秋
公追戎于濟西，莊公十八年。
諸侯盟于扈，文公十五年。
宋人圍滕，宣公九年。宋師伐滕，宣公十年。
季孫斯、叔孫州仇、仲孫何忌帥師伐邾，取漷東田及沂西田。癸巳，叔孫州仇、仲
translation_en:
…at [three] hundred li, deliver grain in the stalk as the required service; at four hundred li, unhusked grain; at five hundred li, husked grain.
This, too, accords with Heaven: great virtue shall never be forgotten in the royal house.
King Wen could settle his mind, and thus could establish these regular officers and shepherds of the people, employing those who possessed outstanding virtue.

Book of Odes
In the south are trees with downward-curving branches; kudzu and other vines entwine them. Joyful is the noble lord; blessings bring him peace. In the south are trees with downward-curving branches; kudzu and other vines cover them. Joyful is the noble lord; blessings sustain him. In the south are trees with downward-curving branches; kudzu and other vines wind around them. Joyful is the noble lord; blessings bring him fulfillment.
Here they dwell, here they settle; here they laugh, here they talk.
The king examined the divination and made his home in Haojing. The tortoise shell determined it; King Wu accomplished it.
Mindful of the august ancestors, who ascend and descend in the court, I, the young one, remain reverent morning and night.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The duke pursued the Rong west of the Ji River. Eighteenth year of Duke Zhuang.
The regional lords made a covenant at Hu. Fifteenth year of Duke Wen.
Men of Song besieged Teng. Ninth year of Duke Xuan. The army of Song attacked Teng. Tenth year of Duke Xuan.
Jisun Si, Shusun Zhouqiu, and Zhongsun Heji led an army against Zhu and took the lands east of the Huo River and west of the Yi River. On the guisi day, Shusun Zhouqiu and Zhong…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
孫何忌及邾子盟于句繹哀公二年
禮記
凡侍坐於大司成者遠近間三席可以問
終則負墻列事未盡不問
獨樂其志不厭其道備舉其道不私其欲
是故情見而義立樂終而德尊
盡其道端其義而教生焉
獻君君舉旅行酬而后獻卿卿舉旅行酬
而后獻大夫大夫舉旅行酬而后獻
===
士士舉旅行酬而后獻庶子
第貳場
論
脩身則道立
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢親耕籍田詔文帝二年
擬唐以長孫無忌為右僕射誥貞觀元年
擬宋起太師文彥博平章軍國重事班宰
相上謝表元祐元年
punctuated:
孫何忌及邾子盟于句繹。哀公二年。
禮記
凡侍坐於大司成者，遠近間三席，可以問；終則負墻，列事未盡不問。
獨樂其志，不厭其道；備舉其道，不私其欲。是故情見而義立，樂終而德尊。
盡其道，端其義，而教生焉。
獻君，君舉旅行酬，而后獻卿；卿舉旅行酬，而后獻大夫；大夫舉旅行酬，而后獻士；士舉旅行酬，而后獻庶子。
第貳場
論
脩身則道立。
詔誥表內科一道。
擬漢親耕籍田詔。文帝二年。
擬唐以長孫無忌為右僕射誥。貞觀元年。
擬宋起太師文彥博平章軍國重事班宰相上謝表。元祐元年。
translation_en:
…Zhongsun Heji and the Viscount of Zhu made a covenant at Juyi. Second year of Duke Ai.

Record of Rites

Whenever attending the Grand Director of Music, seated in his presence, one should leave a distance of three mats. One may then ask questions. When finished, one withdraws to sit against the wall. Until he has finished setting forth the matters under discussion, one does not ask questions.

He takes delight solely in his purpose and never tires of his Way; he fully puts that Way into practice without selfishly indulging his desires. Thus feelings become manifest and righteousness is established; when the music ends, virtue is held in honor.

Fully realize its Way and set its principles aright, and instruction will arise from it.

Offer wine to the ruler. After the ruler raises his cup and the reciprocal drinking proceeds around the company, offer wine to the ministers. After the ministers raise their cups and the reciprocal drinking proceeds around the company, offer wine to the grandees. After the grandees raise their cups and the reciprocal drinking proceeds around the company, offer wine to the servicemen. After the servicemen raise their cups and the reciprocal drinking proceeds around the company, offer wine to the younger sons.

Second Session

Discourse

Cultivate oneself, and the Way becomes established.

One topic is assigned [?] from among imperial edicts, proclamations of appointment, and memorials.

Compose an edict in the voice of the Han emperor concerning his personally plowing the imperial field. Second year of Emperor Wen.

Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Zhangsun Wuji Vice Director of the Right of the Department of State Affairs. First year of Zhenguan.

Compose a memorial of thanks in the voice of Wen Yanbo upon his recall under the Song as Grand Preceptor to deliberate on important military and state affairs, with precedence above the chief councilors. First year of Yuanyou.

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
判語〔五條〕
舉用有過官吏
錢粮互相覺察
見任官輒自立碑
私越冒度関津
詐教誘人犯法
第叁場
策五道
問古昔帝王之有天下必制度以飭治功
===
脩典章以詔後世我
國家
祖宗列聖
御製諸書布之天下固已家傳人誦雖文身左
衽之國罔不祗若而尊信之頃者
孝宗敬皇帝仰承
英廟之志復有會典之作我
皇上繼述益勤命儒臣讐校而頒布焉凡百五
十年之間沿革損益之政無乎不具
punctuated:
判語〔五條〕
舉用有過官吏。
錢粮互相覺察。
見任官輒自立碑。
私越冒度関津。
詐教誘人犯法。

第叁場
策五道
問：古昔帝王之有天下，必制度以飭治功，脩典章以詔後世。我國家祖宗列聖御製諸書，布之天下，固已家傳人誦，雖文身左衽之國，罔不祗若而尊信之。頃者，孝宗敬皇帝仰承英廟之志，復有會典之作。我皇上繼述益勤，命儒臣讐校而頒布焉。凡百五十年之間沿革損益之政，無乎不具，
translation_en:
Legal judgments 〔five items〕
Recommending and employing officials and clerks with past offenses.
Mutual monitoring and detection of irregularities concerning money and grain.
Serving officials erecting commemorative steles for themselves without authorization.
Clandestinely crossing or fraudulently passing through barriers and ferries.
Deceitfully instructing or enticing others to violate the law.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: When the emperors and kings of antiquity possessed All Under Heaven, they invariably established institutions and regulations to put the work of government in order, and revised statutes and ordinances to instruct later generations. The books imperially composed by the successive sage rulers, the ancestors of our dynasty, have been disseminated throughout the realm. They have indeed been handed down in every household and recited by everyone. Even countries whose people tattoo their bodies and fasten their garments on the left all reverently comply with them, honor them, and trust them. Recently, Emperor Xiaozong Jing, reverently carrying forward the intentions of Yingzong, undertook the compilation of the Collected Statutes (Huidian). Our reigning emperor, ever more diligent in continuing and fulfilling his predecessors’ work, commanded his scholarly ministers to collate and revise it and then promulgate it. It comprehensively includes all governmental measures retained or changed, reduced or augmented, over the course of one hundred and fifty years…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
今士大夫得覩
宸編若獲拱璧私家之藏永爲世寳不知是典
近何所稽遠何所取而
制作之本意可仰窺而測識之邪夫有典有則
貽厥子孫
先帝爲後世慮至深遠也今日臣工敢不誦之
體而行之不知其要何在諸生幸以
其所知者告我
問人君之治天下非賞無以慶善非罰
===
無以威惡固也然酬酢運用之間少戾
其常則不免於過中失正之弊均賞矣
而不足以爲勸均罰矣而不足以爲懲
是果何說哉古之人有懼殃民而不許
求郎之請者有念至公而不私秦府舊
人者又有因太原未平而不與使相者
賞善如是無乃吝之過而近於刻印刓
忍弗予者乎有因上書而除肉刑者有
念不能全民之生而再定箠令者又有
punctuated:
今士大夫得覩宸編，若獲拱璧，私家之藏，永爲世寳。不知是典近何所稽，遠何所取，而制作之本意可仰窺而測識之邪？夫有典有則，貽厥子孫，先帝爲後世慮至深遠也。今日臣工敢不誦之，體而行之？不知其要何在？諸生幸以其所知者告我。

問：人君之治天下，非賞無以慶善，非罰無以威惡，固也。然酬酢運用之間，少戾其常，則不免於過中失正之弊。均賞矣，而不足以爲勸；均罰矣，而不足以爲懲，是果何說哉？古之人有懼殃民而不許求郎之請者，有念至公而不私秦府舊人者，又有因太原未平而不與使相者。賞善如是，無乃吝之過，而近於刻印刓忍弗予者乎？有因上書而除肉刑者，有念不能全民之生而再定箠令者，又有
translation_en:
…Now that scholar-officials can behold this imperial compilation, they treasure it as though they had obtained a great jade disc, keeping it in their private collections as an heirloom for generations. We ask: what recent precedents does this compendium consult, and what does it draw from the distant past? Can we reverently discern and comprehend the original intent behind its compilation? To possess statutes and rules and bequeath them to one’s descendants—the late emperor’s concern for later generations was indeed profound and far-reaching. How could the officials serving today fail to recite them, embody them, and put them into practice? But where does the essential point lie? Let you candidates kindly tell us what you know.

Question: In governing the realm, a ruler cannot commend goodness without rewards or deter evil without punishments: this is certainly so. Yet in responding to affairs and applying these measures, even a slight departure from the proper norm inevitably risks exceeding the mean and losing what is right. Rewards may alike be bestowed, yet fail to encourage; punishments may alike be imposed, yet fail to deter. How, indeed, is this to be explained? Among the rulers of antiquity, one feared bringing harm upon the people and therefore refused a request for appointment as a Gentleman (lang); another, mindful of the utmost impartiality, declined to favor former members of the Prince of Qin’s establishment; and another withheld appointment as Commissioner with Rank of Grand Councilor (shixiang) because Taiyuan had not yet been pacified. In rewarding goodness this way, were they not excessively grudging, approaching the conduct of the ruler who had a seal engraved but wore down its edges while unable to bring himself to award it? There was one who abolished mutilating punishments in response to a written petition; another, concerned that he could not preserve the lives of the people, twice revised the regulations governing flogging; and there was also one who…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
讀明堂鍼炙書而禁鞭背者恤刑如是
無乃畏之過而近於斷死刑垂涕泣者
乎茲欲一賞而人無不勸一怒而人無不
威其要安在考之論刑賞者說亦不一
或曰善爲國者賞不僭而刑不濫又曰
寧僭無濫矣何仕者復有世祿之制刑
國復有重典之施歟或曰爲政者不賞
私勞不罰私怨是矣何孔門問答復有
以直報怨以德報德之說將舊有德怨
===
之人待之不能不異歟或者又曰有功
不賞有罪不刑雖唐虞不能以化天下
而與不賞而民勸不怒而民威於鈇鉞
者何背馳也或者又曰有功則賞有罪
則刑雖敢不竭心盡力以脩職業而宋
臣又謂有功而後爵天下必有遺善故
有無功而爵者有罪而後罰天下必有
遺惡故有無罪而罰者斯二說者又何
如其抵捂也諸生明經待問久矣於是
punctuated: 讀《明堂鍼炙書》而禁鞭背者。恤刑如是，無乃畏之過，而近於斷死刑垂涕泣者乎？茲欲一賞而人無不勸，一怒而人無不威，其要安在？考之論刑賞者，說亦不一。或曰：「善爲國者，賞不僭而刑不濫。」又曰：「寧僭無濫矣。」何仕者復有世祿之制，刑國復有重典之施歟？或曰：「爲政者，不賞私勞，不罰私怨。」是矣，何孔門問答復有「以直報怨，以德報德」之說？將舊有德怨之人，待之不能不異歟？或者又曰：「有功不賞，有罪不刑，雖唐虞不能以化天下。」而與「不賞而民勸，不怒而民威於鈇鉞」者，何背馳也？或者又曰：「有功則賞，有罪則刑，雖敢不竭心盡力以脩職業？」而宋臣又謂：「有功而後爵，天下必有遺善，故有無功而爵者；有罪而後罰，天下必有遺惡，故有無罪而罰者。」斯二說者，又何如其抵捂也？諸生明經待問久矣，於是
translation_en: …there was also one who, after reading the Book of Acupuncture and Moxibustion of the Hall of Light (Mingtang zhenjiu shu), prohibited flogging the back. With such solicitude in administering punishment, was this not excessive apprehension, approaching the conduct of one who shed tears when deciding capital sentences? Now, if we wish a single reward to encourage everyone, and a single display of anger to awe everyone, wherein lies the essential principle? Examining discussions of punishments and rewards, we find that their explanations are not uniform. Some say: “Those who govern a state well do not confer undeserved rewards or impose excessive punishments.” They also say: “Better to confer undeserved rewards than to impose excessive punishments.” Why, then, is there also a system of hereditary stipends for officeholders, and an application of severe laws in punishing states [?]? Some say: “Those who govern do not reward services rendered to them personally or punish private grudges.” This is correct; yet why do the questions and answers in Confucius’s school also contain the statement, “Repay resentment with uprightness, and kindness with kindness”? Must one, then, necessarily treat differently those toward whom one has previously felt gratitude or resentment? Others say: “If merit goes unrewarded and guilt unpunished, even the rulers of Tang and Yu could not transform the world.” Why does this run counter to the statement, “Without rewards the people are encouraged; without anger the people are more awed than by execution axes”? Others again say: “When there is merit, reward it; when there is guilt, punish it. Who would then dare [?] not devote all his heart and strength to fulfilling his official duties?” Yet a minister of the Song also said: “If ranks are granted only after meritorious service, some good in the world will inevitably be overlooked; hence there are those granted rank without meritorious service. If punishment is imposed only after an offense, some evil in the world will inevitably escape notice; hence there are those punished without an offense.” How is it that these two explanations likewise contradict each other? You students have long studied the Classics and awaited questioning. Concerning these…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
二事與前數說相與質而訂之何如
問風俗教化儒先論之詳矣教化本於朝
廷而責任於守令風俗移于好尚而振
作于士人固史以來所傳循吏非一然
觀其所稱者不曰力行教化則曰教以
禮讓可舉其人而言之歟今之為守令
者以因循苟免為賢嚴急集事為能至
於古之教化槩乎其未聞也其故何哉
又嘗觀乎古人之有意於風俗者其嘉
===
言善行誠可師法故有誤認車牛而不
與較者有苦居畎畝而不入城府者有
歸亡父之金而不肯受者有遜其園為
黌舍者有退居于洛而不言時事者之
數者非甚高遠而難能也今有之不亦
可以興廉而崇讓乎有為無不是父母
之說者有為難得兄弟之說者有為絕
交令可交出妻令可嫁之說者有為居
是邦不非其大夫之說者又有為律設
punctuated:
二事與前數說，相與質而訂之，何如？
問：風俗教化，儒先論之詳矣。教化本於朝廷，而責任於守令；風俗移于好尚，而振作于士人。固史以來所傳循吏非一，然觀其所稱者，不曰力行教化，則曰教以禮讓，可舉其人而言之歟？今之為守令者，以因循苟免為賢，嚴急集事為能；至於古之教化，槩乎其未聞也，其故何哉？又嘗觀乎古人之有意於風俗者，其嘉言善行，誠可師法。故有誤認車牛而不與較者，有苦居畎畝而不入城府者，有歸亡父之金而不肯受者，有遜其園為黌舍者，有退居于洛而不言時事者。之數者，非甚高遠而難能也，今有之，不亦可以興廉而崇讓乎？有為「無不是父母」之說者，有為「難得兄弟」之說者，有為「絕交令可交，出妻令可嫁」之說者，有為「居是邦，不非其大夫」之說者，又有為「律設
translation_en:
…these two matters together with the several preceding arguments: how would you examine and adjudicate them in relation to one another?
Question: Earlier Confucian scholars discussed customs and moral education in detail. Moral education originates at court, while responsibility for it rests with prefects and magistrates; customs change with prevailing preferences, while their renewal depends upon scholars. The histories have transmitted accounts of many exemplary local officials [?]. Yet when we examine what they are praised for, it is either vigorously carrying out moral education or teaching ritual propriety and deference. Can you name these men and discuss them? Those serving as prefects and magistrates today regard following established routines and merely avoiding blame as virtue, and regard stern urgency in getting things done as competence. As for the moral education practiced in antiquity, they seem never to have heard of it. Why is this?
I have also considered the ancients who took an interest in customs: their admirable words and good deeds truly deserve to be emulated. There were those who did not dispute with someone who mistakenly claimed their cart and ox; those who lived in hardship among the fields and would not enter cities or government offices; those who refused to accept gold returned as belonging to their deceased father; those who yielded their gardens for use as school buildings; and those who retired to Luo and did not discuss current affairs. These deeds are not so lofty and remote as to be difficult to accomplish. If people practiced them today, could they not encourage integrity and exalt deference?
Some advocated the saying, “There are no parents who are in the wrong”; others, “Brothers are hard to come by”; others, “When ending a friendship, leave room for friendship to resume; when divorcing a wife, leave her able to remarry”; and others, “When residing in a state, do not disparage its grand masters.” Still others advocated the saying, “The statutes establish…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大法禮順人情之說者是數者亦非空
言而無施也今信而行之不猶可以寬
鄙而敦薄乎夫禮義廉耻謂之四維四
維之張弛其所係大矣吾爲此懼而相
與折衷冀有聞焉幸毋迂以視我
問西漢尚寬大東漢尚節義史氏之論尚
矣今以西漢之人物考之有不受卒徒
𧈪背者有不聽兩吏挾持者有見大將
軍而不拜者有至虜庭而不屈者上欲
===
起禮樂也徵之而不肯行上方興文學
也答以不在多言由是觀之西漢之節
義何歉於東漢哉夫兩漢之節義信皆
有之矣而先儒又有爲東漢節義不如
西漢之說者是果然歟否歟迨至于唐
有死守江淮者有伏閤極諫者有布衣
對策極言時政者有太學儒生倡義止
亂者宋之時又有使虜庭而抗論者有
年彊仕而勇退者有被謫雖困而無書
punctuated:
大法，禮順人情之說者。是數者亦非空言而無施也，今信而行之，不猶可以寬鄙而敦薄乎？夫禮義廉耻，謂之四維，四維之張弛，其所係大矣。吾爲此懼，而相與折衷，冀有聞焉，幸毋迂以視我。

問：西漢尚寬大，東漢尚節義，史氏之論尚矣。今以西漢之人物考之，有不受卒徒𧈪背者，有不聽兩吏挾持者，有見大將軍而不拜者，有至虜庭而不屈者。上欲起禮樂也，徵之而不肯行；上方興文學也，答以不在多言。由是觀之，西漢之節義何歉於東漢哉？夫兩漢之節義，信皆有之矣，而先儒又有爲東漢節義不如西漢之說者，是果然歟，否歟？迨至于唐，有死守江淮者，有伏閤極諫者，有布衣對策極言時政者，有太學儒生倡義止亂者。宋之時，又有使虜庭而抗論者，有年彊仕而勇退者，有被謫雖困而無書
translation_en:
…the overarching standards, and that ritual accords with human feelings. These several views, too, are not empty words without practical application. If people today believed and practiced them, could they not likewise broaden narrow minds and deepen shallow character? Ritual propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame are called the Four Bonds. Whether these bonds are taut or slack has momentous consequences. My concern over this prompts me to seek a balanced judgment together with you, hoping to learn something. Please do not regard me as impractical.

Question: The Western Han prized magnanimity; the Eastern Han prized integrity and righteousness. This judgment of the historians is longstanding. Yet if we examine the people of the Western Han, there were those who would not submit to having their backs mistreated by soldiers [?]; those who would not allow two functionaries to hold them on either side; those who would not bow upon meeting the General-in-Chief; and those who reached the court of the northern enemy and would not yield. When the emperor wished to revive rites and music, one whom he summoned refused to go. When the emperor was promoting literary learning, another replied that it did not depend on many words. Viewed in this light, how was the integrity and righteousness of the Western Han inferior to that of the Eastern Han? Both Han dynasties certainly possessed these virtues. Yet some earlier Confucian scholars also maintained that the Eastern Han fell short of the Western Han in integrity and righteousness. Was this really so, or not?

Coming down to the Tang, there were those who defended the Jiang–Huai region to the death; those who prostrated themselves at the palace gate and remonstrated to the utmost; those who, while holding no office, answered policy questions by speaking with complete frankness about current government; and students of the Imperial University who championed righteousness and halted disorder. In the Song, too, there were those who went as envoys to the enemy’s court and argued unyieldingly; those who resolutely retired at forty, the prime age for official service; and those who, though in straitened circumstances after banishment, sent no letters …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
至京師者有交游雖舊而無書抵政府
者唐宋之節義如是又何歉於兩漢哉
然後世之論獨以節義歸之於東漢者
其故安在而史氏之言去漢未遠果不
足信否歟是必有攸當之說請明言之
且以觀平居之所養
問今日之務所重而可議者莫切於食與
兵蓋非兵無以禦侮非食無以供費古
者藏兵於民而兵足用田不加賦而食
===
足供固無庸議矣厥後創業如漢高提
兵恒數十萬以一蕭何餽餉而有餘守
成如文帝遣四將軍以禦匈奴其兵亦
已衆矣然屢蠲田租或詔減半而國用
不聞告竭不知當時何以能然也今兵
掌於司馬督於憲臣簡閱之法清理之
規未嘗廢也但四方諸路之兵不足以
制諸路之寇卒遇有警至勤
王師或募土兵或調邊將噫我兵之弱何至
punctuated:
至京師者，有交游雖舊而無書抵政府者。唐宋之節義如是，又何歉於兩漢哉？然後世之論，獨以節義歸之於東漢者，其故安在？而史氏之言，去漢未遠，果不足信否歟？是必有攸當之說，請明言之，且以觀平居之所養。
問：今日之務，所重而可議者，莫切於食與兵。蓋非兵無以禦侮，非食無以供費。古者藏兵於民而兵足用，田不加賦而食足供，固無庸議矣。厥後創業如漢高，提兵恒數十萬，以一蕭何餽餉而有餘；守成如文帝，遣四將軍以禦匈奴，其兵亦已衆矣。然屢蠲田租，或詔減半，而國用不聞告竭，不知當時何以能然也。今兵掌於司馬，督於憲臣，簡閱之法、清理之規，未嘗廢也。但四方諸路之兵，不足以制諸路之寇，卒遇有警，至勤王師，或募土兵，或調邊將。噫！我兵之弱何至
translation_en:
…to the capital; there were also those who, despite longstanding friendships, sent no letters to the chief ministers. Such was the moral integrity and righteousness of the Tang and Song: how were they in any way inferior to those of the two Han dynasties? Yet later commentators attribute moral integrity and righteousness exclusively to the Eastern Han. Why is this? And is the historian’s statement, made not long after the Han [?], really unworthy of belief? There must be a sound explanation. Please state it clearly, so that we may also discern what you have cultivated in your everyday life.
Question: Among the important affairs of the present day that merit discussion, none is more pressing than provisions and troops. Without troops there is no means of resisting aggression; without provisions there is no means of meeting expenses. In antiquity, soldiers were maintained among the common people, and troops were sufficient for service; no additional taxes were imposed on farmland, and provisions were sufficient for use. That, of course, needs no discussion. Later, a founder such as Gaozu of Han regularly led armies numbering several hundred thousand, yet with Xiao He alone supplying their provisions, there was a surplus. A ruler preserving an established dynasty, such as Emperor Wen, dispatched four generals to resist the Xiongnu, and his troops, too, were already numerous. Nevertheless, he repeatedly remitted the land tax, sometimes ordering it reduced by half, and we never hear that state resources were exhausted. How was this possible at the time?
Today, troops are administered by the Minister of War and supervised by censorial officials. The procedures for mustering and inspecting them, and the regulations for scrutinizing and rectifying their rolls, have never been abandoned. Yet the troops of the various regions throughout the realm cannot subdue the bandits in those regions. When an alarm suddenly arises, it becomes necessary to call upon the imperial army, either recruiting local troops or transferring frontier commanders. Alas! How has the weakness of our troops reached…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
是哉兵食之供掌於司徒綱於藩司其
征輸之法儲峙之規未少變也但各省
一歲之積不足以供一歲之費一有所
需則束手無策非請
內帑則截綱運矣噫我財之匱何至是哉豈
典兵理財者未得其人將兵之訓練者
未精而逃亡者未盡復伍歟冗食之員
尚多而無益之費未盡裁省歟抑別有
其故也或者曰邇年盜賊動以千萬非
===
區區尋常兵力之可勝而天下府庫之
空虛民力之重困又非一朝一夕可以
完復而捄藥者宜大有所處不知其計
將安出願明言之
punctuated: 是哉？兵食之供掌於司徒，綱於藩司，其征輸之法、儲峙之規未少變也。但各省一歲之積，不足以供一歲之費；一有所需，則束手無策，非請內帑，則截綱運矣。噫！我財之匱何至是哉？豈典兵理財者未得其人，將兵之訓練者未精，而逃亡者未盡復伍歟？冗食之員尚多，而無益之費未盡裁省歟？抑別有其故也？或者曰：「邇年盜賊動以千萬，非區區尋常兵力之可勝；而天下府庫之空虛、民力之重困，又非一朝一夕可以完復，而捄藥者宜大有所處。」不知其計將安出？願明言之。
translation_en:
…come to such a state? The provision of military supplies is administered by the Minister of Revenue and coordinated by the Provincial Administration Commissions. The methods of taxation and transport and the regulations for stockpiling have not changed in the slightest. Yet each province’s accumulation for one year is insufficient to meet that year’s expenditure. Whenever a need arises, officials find themselves helpless, with no plan: they either request funds from the imperial privy treasury or divert tax shipments. Alas! How has the scarcity of our resources reached such a state? Is it that suitable men have not been found to manage military affairs and finances? Or is the training of the troops inadequate, and have the deserters not all been restored to the ranks? Are there still too many superfluous personnel drawing support, and have useless expenditures not yet been fully curtailed? Or is there some other cause?

Some say: “In recent years, bandits have frequently numbered in the thousands and tens of thousands; ordinary military forces of modest size cannot overcome them. Moreover, the empty treasuries throughout the realm and the severe exhaustion of the people’s resources cannot be fully restored overnight. Those seeking a remedy should therefore undertake substantial measures.” What plan, then, can be devised? Please explain it clearly.

translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“When going out, comport yourself as though meeting an honored guest; when employing the people, act as though assisting at a great sacrifice. Do not impose on others what you yourself do not desire. In the state, incur no resentment; in the household, incur no resentment.”

Zhao Tingfu

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: Those writing on this passage generally manage to say something about it, but their compositions are either stale or verbose, making them exceedingly tiresome to read. Suddenly I came upon this script: its phrasing is fresh and clear, yet accords with classical standards. How could one fail to feel respect for it?

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: The Master tells Zhonggong about the practice of humaneness and its results. His words are simple and concise, yet inexhaustible in meaning. This composition is restrained and unadorned, lofty and antique in manner, and fully brings out their subtle import. I imagine that beyond literary accomplishment, its author must possess learning of another kind.

Comment by Associate Examiner Hao, Instructor: The topic itself is dignified and imposing. Most compositions vie with one another in ostentatious language. In this composition, principle exceeds what the words express. I select it.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: He expounds the sage’s words in solemn and dignified language. Surely he understands composition!

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: The writing flows and the reasoning is sound. This is beyond the reach of shallow learning.

To fulfill both reverence and reciprocity, so that mutual trust prevails both within and without: this is the sage’s instruction to a worthy man on practicing humaneness. For if one takes reverence as one’s guiding principle and practices reciprocity, selfish intentions find no room, and the virtue of the heart is complete. Those within and without…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之人焉有不孚者哉夫子因仲弓問仁而告之
以此謂夫學莫先於爲仁而仁莫切於敬恕是
故敬者德之聚持己不敬則私意有所容於內
非所以爲仁也要必戒慎常存一出門也雖無
大賓是見肅恭收斂儼若接大賓於揖讓之間
罔敢以慢心乗之一使民也雖非大祭是承嚴
恭寅畏恍若承大祭於對越之頃罔敢以易心
處之若然則敬以持己而仁之體立矣恕者仁
之方待物不恕則私意有所容於外亦非所以
===
爲仁也要必近取諸身以人之心不異於我也
凡我所不欲者則勿以之而施於人待人猶待
己也我之心不殊於人也凡我所不願者則勿
以之而加於彼處己猶處人也若然則恕以及
物而仁之用行矣敬恕兼盡則心德以全由是
外而在邦也自上及下皆相安於敬恕之間欽
仰愛慕而怨惡之不形蓋感應之機自有不約
而同者焉內而在家也由親及疎咸相承於敬
恕之餘歡欣怡愉而怨讟之不作蓋動物之誠
punctuated: 之人焉有不孚者哉？夫子因仲弓問仁而告之以此，謂夫學莫先於爲仁，而仁莫切於敬恕。是故敬者，德之聚。持己不敬，則私意有所容於內，非所以爲仁也。要必戒慎常存：一出門也，雖無大賓是見，肅恭收斂，儼若接大賓於揖讓之間，罔敢以慢心乗之；一使民也，雖非大祭是承，嚴恭寅畏，恍若承大祭於對越之頃，罔敢以易心處之。若然，則敬以持己，而仁之體立矣。恕者，仁之方。待物不恕，則私意有所容於外，亦非所以爲仁也。要必近取諸身：以人之心不異於我也，凡我所不欲者，則勿以之而施於人，待人猶待己也；我之心不殊於人也，凡我所不願者，則勿以之而加於彼，處己猶處人也。若然，則恕以及物，而仁之用行矣。敬恕兼盡，則心德以全。由是外而在邦也，自上及下，皆相安於敬恕之間，欽仰愛慕，而怨惡之不形，蓋感應之機，自有不約而同者焉；內而在家也，由親及疎，咸相承於敬恕之餘，歡欣怡愉，而怨讟之不作，蓋動物之誠
translation_en:
…among these people, how could any fail to respond with trust? When Zhonggong asked about benevolence, the Master instructed him in these terms, meaning that in learning nothing takes precedence over practicing benevolence, and that nothing is more essential to benevolence than reverent attentiveness and sympathetic consideration. Thus reverent attentiveness is where virtue gathers. If one conducts oneself without reverence, selfish intentions find room within; this is no way to practice benevolence. One must always maintain vigilance and care. Whenever one goes out, even if no distinguished guest is there to be received, one must be solemn, respectful, and collected, just as though receiving a distinguished guest with bows and courtesies, never daring to let an attitude of negligence intrude. Whenever one employs the people, even if one is not officiating at a great sacrifice, one must be solemn, respectful, and awestruck, as though conducting a great sacrifice in the presence of the spirits, never daring to approach it lightly. In this way, reverence governs one's conduct, and the substance of benevolence is established.

Sympathetic consideration is the method of benevolence. If one deals with others without it, selfish intentions find room in one's outward dealings; this too is no way to practice benevolence. One must draw an analogy from what is nearest—oneself. Since others' hearts do not differ from one's own, whatever one does not desire, one must not inflict on others: one treats others as one treats oneself. Since one's own heart does not differ from those of others, whatever one does not wish for, one must not impose upon them: one deals with oneself as one deals with others. In this way, sympathetic consideration reaches others, and the functioning of benevolence is put into practice.

When reverent attentiveness and sympathetic consideration are both fully realized, the virtue of the heart becomes complete. Thus, in one's outward life in the state, people from the highest to the lowest all live at ease with one another amid reverence and consideration. They feel respect, admiration, affection, and attachment, while resentment and hatred do not emerge. For the workings of influence and response naturally bring agreement without prior arrangement. Within the household, from close kin to distant relations, all support one another through the beneficent effects of reverence and consideration. They are joyful and content, and resentment and reproach do not arise. For the sincerity that moves others…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
自有不戒而孚者焉夫敬恕之功盡而無怨之
效臻仁不外是矣脫效之未臻是功之未至也
雍也盍亦知所自考以爲加勉也哉抑仁一也
敬恕之旨視克復之訓若有弗類何也蓋天之
生物因材而篤聖人教人亦因人而施期於有
成而已雖然一敬可徹於上下而恕亦未可易
而視之也誠能從事於此而有得焉亦將無巳
之可克矣
回之爲人也擇乎中庸得一善則拳拳服
===
膺而弗失之矣
陳器
同考試官教諭何批理學文字最難措詞
多則冗短則晦此作發明透徹而人若不竟其說者
豈可多得
同考試官教諭戴批能擇能守處講者率多
膚淺非所以語顏子也此作能槩括其梗槩而探索
其淵微理到而文自工過時輩遠矣
同考試官教諭吳批意正大而詞簡明視綴搭
punctuated:
自有不戒而孚者焉。夫敬恕之功盡，而無怨之效臻，仁不外是矣。脫效之未臻，是功之未至也。雍也，盍亦知所自考，以爲加勉也哉？抑仁一也，敬恕之旨視克復之訓，若有弗類，何也？蓋天之生物，因材而篤；聖人教人，亦因人而施，期於有成而已。雖然，一敬可徹於上下，而恕亦未可易而視之也。誠能從事於此而有得焉，亦將無巳之可克矣。
「回之爲人也，擇乎中庸，得一善，則拳拳服膺而弗失之矣。」
陳器
同考試官教諭何批：「理學文字，最難措詞。多則冗，短則晦。此作發明透徹，而人若不竟其說者，豈可多得？」
同考試官教諭戴批：「能擇能守處，講者率多膚淺，非所以語顏子也。此作能槩括其梗槩，而探索其淵微，理到而文自工，過時輩遠矣。」
同考試官教諭吳批：「意正大而詞簡明，視綴搭
translation_en:
…there is naturally a sincerity that inspires trust without admonition. When the work of reverence and sympathetic understanding is fully accomplished, and its result—freedom from resentment—is attained, benevolence lies in nothing beyond this. If that result has not yet been attained, the work has not yet reached completion. Yong, should you not also recognize what to examine in yourself, so as to redouble your efforts? Yet benevolence is one: why does the purport of reverence and sympathetic understanding seem unlike the teaching of overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety? Heaven, in bringing things into being, nurtures them according to their capacities; the sage, in teaching people, likewise adapts his instruction to each person, seeking only their accomplishment. Nevertheless, reverence alone can extend through every level, and sympathetic understanding must not be regarded lightly either. If one truly applies oneself to these and gains understanding, one will eventually have no self left to overcome [?].
“As a person, Hui chose the Mean; whenever he attained something good, he clasped it earnestly to his breast and never let it go.”
Chen Qi.
Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “In writing on the Learning of Principle, choosing one's words is especially difficult. Too many make the writing prolix; too few make it obscure. This composition elucidates its subject thoroughly, yet seems not to exhaust what it has to say [?]. How often can such a work be found?”
Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor, comments: “In explaining the capacity to choose and to hold fast, commentators are generally superficial; this is no way to discuss Master Yan. This composition encompasses the essentials while probing their profound subtleties. With the principles fully realized, literary skill follows naturally. It far surpasses the work of its contemporaries.”
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “Its ideas are upright and elevated, and its language concise and clear. Compared with those who stitch together…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
陳言而晦塞題意者相去何如蓋玩理而有心得者
考試官教諭林批詞藻沛然了無纖麗習氣
可爲鳴盛之作矣讀之一倡三歎
考試官教授陳批根理之言自是典雅且氣充
才贍而筆端有力非名士不及此
聖人稱大賢之於道擇之精而守之固也蓋擇
善固難而守善尤難大賢能擇能守此所以見
稱於聖人也歟昔子思因道之所以不明故引
夫子稱美顏子之言有曰天下有一定之理而
===
昧焉者不能擇人心有一定之操而惰焉者不
能守吾見回之爲人也以明健之資加好學之
篤知道之散於事者不能無過與不及也則必
隨事觀理辨之別之以求其所謂中庸者何在
理之寓於物者不能無過中失正也則必即物
窮理審之擇之以求其所謂中庸者何居精權
度於衆論之間務求至當不易之理有以要其
歸持藻鑑於兩端之際務求大中至正之道有
以見其的若然則其擇之也精矣及於辨別之
punctuated:
陳言而晦塞題意者，相去何如？蓋玩理而有心得者。
考試官教諭林批：詞藻沛然，了無纖麗習氣，可爲鳴盛之作矣。讀之一倡三歎。
考試官教授陳批：根理之言，自是典雅，且氣充才贍，而筆端有力，非名士不及此。
聖人稱大賢之於道，擇之精而守之固也。蓋擇善固難，而守善尤難。大賢能擇能守，此所以見稱於聖人也歟！昔子思因道之所以不明，故引夫子稱美顏子之言，有曰：「天下有一定之理，而昧焉者不能擇；人心有一定之操，而惰焉者不能守。吾見回之爲人也，以明健之資，加好學之篤，知道之散於事者，不能無過與不及也，則必隨事觀理，辨之別之，以求其所謂中庸者何在；理之寓於物者，不能無過中失正也，則必即物窮理，審之擇之，以求其所謂中庸者何居。精權度於衆論之間，務求至當不易之理，有以要其歸；持藻鑑於兩端之際，務求大中至正之道，有以見其的。若然，則其擇之也精矣。及於辨別之
translation_en:
…How does this compare with those who string together stale phrases and obscure the meaning of the topic? Surely this is the work of someone who has pondered principle and attained an understanding of his own.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: His literary expression flows abundantly, entirely free of the habitual taste for delicate ornament. This may be called a work that celebrates a flourishing age. Reading it, one responds to a single leading voice with three sighs of admiration.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: Words rooted in principle are naturally dignified and elegant. Moreover, his vital force is full, his talent ample, and his brush powerful. Only a distinguished scholar could attain this.

The Sage praised the Great Worthy for discerning the Way precisely and holding to it firmly. For choosing the good is certainly difficult, but holding to the good is harder still. The Great Worthy could both choose and hold fast: was this not why the Sage praised him? Formerly, Zisi, addressing the reasons why the Way was not clearly understood, cited the Master's words praising Master Yan, saying:

“Under Heaven there is a fixed principle, but those whose understanding is obscured cannot discern it; the human heart has a fixed moral commitment, but the indolent cannot maintain it. I observe that Hui, endowed with clarity and strength and deeply devoted to learning, knows that in the Way's manifestation in affairs there will inevitably be excess and deficiency. He therefore observes principle in each affair, distinguishing and discriminating, to discover where what is called the Mean lies. Since principle as embodied in things cannot be free from deviations beyond the mean and departures from correctness, he necessarily approaches things and investigates their principle exhaustively, examining and selecting, to discover where what is called the Mean resides. He refines his weighing and measuring amid the many competing opinions, striving to find the supremely fitting and unchanging principle by which to grasp their ultimate purport. He holds up the mirror of discernment between the two extremes, striving to find the Way of perfect centrality and utmost correctness by which to perceive the true standard. In this manner, his discernment is indeed precise. And when, after distinguishing and discriminating…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
餘得一中庸之道必拳拳而着之於心胷之間
務使理與心融而人欲不得以雜之審擇之際
得一中正之理必拳拳而着之於靈府之內務
使心與理契而私欲不得以間之會萬理於一
原曷甞暫合遽離而復陷於過與不及之差乎
貫始終於一致何甞暫得遽失而復淪於過中
失正之謬乎若然則其守之也固矣吁回之能
擇能守如此則非知者過之而不肖者之不及
也子思引之以見道之所由明也歟抑道在天
===
下欲明而行之惟存乎人故必智如大舜而道
所以行仁如顏子而道所以明不然欲道之明
之行難矣子思作中庸深為此懼故引大舜顏
淵之事以示人蓋欲人以智仁為入道之門不
致斯道終於不明不行也子思之功不亦大
乎
仁人心也義人路也
施信
同考試官訓導張批〔題本難體貼作者多不能〕
punctuated:
餘，得一中庸之道，必拳拳而着之於心胷之間，務使理與心融，而人欲不得以雜之；審擇之際，得一中正之理，必拳拳而着之於靈府之內，務使心與理契，而私欲不得以間之。會萬理於一原，曷甞暫合遽離，而復陷於過與不及之差乎？貫始終於一致，何甞暫得遽失，而復淪於過中失正之謬乎？若然，則其守之也固矣。吁！回之能擇能守如此，則非知者過之而不肖者之不及也。子思引之，以見道之所由明也歟？抑道在天下，欲明而行之，惟存乎人。故必智如大舜，而道所以行；仁如顏子，而道所以明。不然，欲道之明之行，難矣。子思作《中庸》，深為此懼，故引大舜、顏淵之事以示人，蓋欲人以智仁為入道之門，不致斯道終於不明不行也。子思之功，不亦大乎？

仁，人心也；義，人路也。

施信

同考試官訓導張批〔題本難體貼，作者多不能〕
translation_en:
…after distinguishing and discriminating, whenever he apprehended a way of the Mean, he would earnestly hold it within his heart, striving to make principle and mind blend together so that human desires could not adulterate it. In examining and choosing, whenever he apprehended a principle of centrality and correctness, he would earnestly hold it within the inner chamber of his mind, striving to bring mind into accord with principle so that selfish desires could not come between them. Uniting the myriad principles in a single source, when did he ever briefly accord with it and then abruptly depart, falling once again into the error of excess or deficiency? Maintaining a single consistency from beginning to end, when did he ever briefly attain it and then abruptly lose it, sinking once again into the error of exceeding the mean and losing what is correct? Thus his hold upon it was indeed firm. Ah! Hui’s ability to choose and to hold fast was such that he was unlike the knowledgeable who overshoot it or the unworthy who fall short. Did Zisi cite him to show how the Way comes to be understood? Yet the Way exists throughout the world, and its elucidation and practice depend entirely upon people. Thus only with wisdom like that of the great Shun can the Way be practiced, and with benevolence like that of Master Yan can the Way be understood. Otherwise, it is difficult to bring about the understanding and practice of the Way. In composing the Doctrine of the Mean, Zisi was deeply concerned about this. He therefore cited the deeds of the great Shun and Yan Yuan to instruct people, intending that they take wisdom and benevolence as the gateway into the Way, so that it would not ultimately remain neither understood nor practiced. Was not Zisi’s contribution great?

“Benevolence is the human heart; righteousness is the human path.”

Shi Xin

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
據理摹寫每下筆不覺便有羞句此篇詞理俱粋到言
心處更融會親切殆非草草於心學者
考試官教諭林批〔朱傳解仁義與他處自別此作辨認既真故語自不苟當不以富麗求之也〕
考試官教授陳批〔破渾厚講尤不疎說理文字正可作式於此故錄之〕
大賢揭所性之大而著其切於人焉蓋性莫大
於仁義而仁義實切於人身也自非大賢各舉
而名之何以知其然哉昔孟子之意語夫語理
===
於浡昧則人難知孰若名之於切近而人易曉
哉是故立人之道有所謂仁也人皆知其曰仁
而已孰知仁之所以為仁其切於己乎蓋仁也
者即人之心也四端之善兼統於方寸之間萬
善之元囊括於一腔之內寂然不動一生意之
充周所謂虛靈不昧者此也感而遂通一善念
之蘊藉所謂神妙不測者此也夫有是心即有
是仁外心以言仁則心為血肉之軀耳豈人心
之外別有所謂仁哉立人之道有所謂義也人
punctuated:
據理摹寫，每下筆，不覺便有羞句。此篇詞理俱粋，到言心處，更融會親切，殆非草草於心學者。
考試官教諭林批〔朱傳解仁義，與他處自別。此作辨認既真，故語自不苟，當不以富麗求之也。〕
考試官教授陳批〔破渾厚，講尤不疎。說理文字，正可作式於此，故錄之。〕
大賢揭所性之大，而著其切於人焉。蓋性莫大於仁義，而仁義實切於人身也。自非大賢各舉而名之，何以知其然哉？昔孟子之意，語夫語理於浡昧，則人難知，孰若名之於切近，而人易曉哉？是故立人之道，有所謂仁也。人皆知其曰仁而已，孰知仁之所以為仁，其切於己乎？蓋仁也者，即人之心也。四端之善，兼統於方寸之間；萬善之元，囊括於一腔之內。寂然不動，一生意之充周，所謂虛靈不昧者此也；感而遂通，一善念之蘊藉，所謂神妙不測者此也。夫有是心，即有是仁。外心以言仁，則心為血肉之軀耳，豈人心之外，別有所謂仁哉？立人之道，有所謂義也。人
translation_en:
…to depict it in accordance with principle; whenever writers put brush to paper, they unwittingly produce embarrassing phrases [?]. In this essay, both diction and reasoning are refined. Where it discusses the mind, its understanding is especially integrated and intimate. Its author can hardly be someone who treats the learning of the mind casually.

Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔Zhu Xi’s commentary explains benevolence and righteousness here differently from elsewhere. This essay discerns that distinction correctly, so its language is naturally careful. One should not look to it for ornate splendor.〕

Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: 〔The opening is substantial and rounded, and the exposition is particularly attentive. As a piece of writing that elucidates principle, this can indeed serve as a model; hence its inclusion.〕

The great worthy brought to light what is greatest in our inherent nature and made manifest its intimate relevance to human beings. For nothing in our nature is greater than benevolence and righteousness, and benevolence and righteousness are indeed intimately relevant to our own persons. Had the great worthy not singled out and named each, how could we know this to be so? Mencius’s intention in former times was this: to speak of principle in obscure terms [?] makes it difficult for people to understand. How could that compare with naming it through what is close at hand, so that people can readily comprehend it?

Thus, in the Way that establishes humanity, there is what is called benevolence. People all know only that it is called benevolence. Who understands what makes benevolence benevolence, and how intimately it concerns oneself? Benevolence is precisely the human mind. The goodness of the four beginnings is comprehensively united within the mind’s square inch; the source of all goodness is encompassed within the breast. Still and unmoving, it is filled throughout with the impulse of life: this is what is meant by being empty and numinously aware, never obscured. When stimulated, it responds with understanding, holding within itself a good thought: this is what is meant by being wondrous and unfathomable. Wherever there is this mind, there is this benevolence. If one speaks of benevolence apart from the mind, then the mind becomes merely a body of flesh and blood. Could there be something separately called benevolence outside the human mind?

In the Way that establishes humanity, there is what is called righteousness. People…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皆知其曰義而已孰知義之所以爲義其切於
身乎蓋義也者即人之路也天理當行實爲踐
履之地人事質幹允爲蹈廸之途無偏無黨一
蕩蕩之康莊所謂周道如砥者是也無反無側
一平平之大道所謂其直如矢者是也夫有是
義即有是路外路以言義則路為邪曲之徑耳
豈人路之外别有所謂義哉仁而謂之人心則
可以見其爲此身酬酢萬變之主而不可須臾
失矣義而謂之人路則可以見其爲出入往来
===
必由之道而不可須臾舍矣仁義之切於人如
此人可不知所以求之哉雖然仁義根於人心
之固有何假聖賢之立名邪天下不知易故孔
子以生生名易天下不知中故子思以喜怒哀
樂名中天下溺於功利而不知有仁義故孟子
以人心人路名仁義蓋非聖賢意也覺天下之
不知者也聖賢立言垂訓每如此而人猶有放
其心而不求舍其路而不由者亦獨何心哉
易其
punctuated:
皆知其曰義而已，孰知義之所以爲義，其切於身乎？蓋義也者，即人之路也。天理當行，實爲踐履之地；人事質幹，允爲蹈廸之途。無偏無黨，一蕩蕩之康莊，所謂「周道如砥」者是也；無反無側，一平平之大道，所謂「其直如矢」者是也。夫有是義，即有是路；外路以言義，則路為邪曲之徑耳。豈人路之外，别有所謂義哉？仁而謂之人心，則可以見其爲此身酬酢萬變之主，而不可須臾失矣；義而謂之人路，則可以見其爲出入往来必由之道，而不可須臾舍矣。仁義之切於人如此，人可不知所以求之哉？雖然，仁義根於人心之固有，何假聖賢之立名邪？天下不知易，故孔子以生生名易；天下不知中，故子思以喜怒哀樂名中；天下溺於功利而不知有仁義，故孟子以人心人路名仁義。蓋非聖賢意也，覺天下之不知者也。聖賢立言垂訓每如此，而人猶有放其心而不求、舍其路而不由者，亦獨何心哉？

易其
translation_en:
…all know only that it is called righteousness. Who understands what makes righteousness righteousness, and how intimately it concerns oneself? Righteousness is the human path. Where heavenly principle ought to be put into practice is truly the ground on which to tread; the essential substance of human affairs [?] is indeed the way along which to proceed. Without partiality or faction, it is a broad and open thoroughfare: this is what is meant by “The road of Zhou is smooth as a whetstone.” Without deviation or inclination, it is a level highway: this is what is meant by “As straight as an arrow.” Where there is this righteousness, there is this path. To speak of righteousness apart from the path would leave the path a mere crooked byway. Could there be some separate thing called righteousness outside the human path?

Calling benevolence the human heart shows that it is the master by which one responds to the myriad changes, and that it must not be lost for even a moment. Calling righteousness the human path shows that it is the way one must follow in going out and coming in, in departing and returning, and that it must not be abandoned for even a moment. Since benevolence and righteousness concern people so intimately, can people fail to understand how to seek them?

Yet benevolence and righteousness are rooted in what the human heart inherently possesses. Why should they require the sages and worthies to give them names? Because the world did not understand change, Kongzi defined change through ceaseless generation. Because the world did not understand equilibrium, Zisi defined equilibrium through joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure. Because the world was sunk in achievement and profit and did not know benevolence and righteousness, Mengzi defined benevolence and righteousness as the human heart and the human path. These were not inventions of the sages and worthies; they served to awaken those in the world who did not understand. This is invariably how the sages and worthies establish their teachings and leave instruction to posterity. Yet there are still people who let their hearts stray without seeking them, and abandon their path without following it. What sort of hearts can they have?

Book of Changes. [The following character, 其, is unclear here.] …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
六二鴻漸于磐飲食衎衎吉
陸鈳

之義他日不苟於禄位可以占矣
同考試官教諭蔡批豐贍中典雅自存非
才富而理到者不能得士如此可以冠本房矣
同考試官教諭郁批本爻生意出處之義
畢見佳作也
考試官教諭林批命意造詞皆在經傳
===
中出沒惟深於易者能之
考試官教授陳批理明詞贍
漸之六二有進得其所之象有進獲乎善之占
蓋進以有德有應為貴也六二兼之則其進之
安而善之獲也有以哉周公繫爻之意以為君
子之仕也不以爵禄之榮為念而以出處之正
為難漸之六二柔順中正而得漸進之道上應
九五而有可進之機則是為人臣者外比於賢
宅俊於我乎是職有高而不危之休也上麗大
punctuated:
六二：鴻漸于磐，飲食衎衎，吉。
陸鈳
同考試官教諭唐批：文詞中發出人臣事君之義，他日不苟於禄位，可以占矣。
同考試官教諭蔡批：豐贍中典雅自存，非才富而理到者不能。得士如此，可以冠本房矣。
同考試官教諭郁批：本爻生意、出處之義畢見，佳作也。

translation_en:
Six in the second place: The wild goose gradually advances to the rock. It eats and drinks in contentment. Auspicious.
Lu Ke 陸鈳
Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: The language brings out the principles by which a minister serves his ruler. From this one may predict that in future he will not be careless about accepting emolument and rank.
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: Within its richness and abundance, classical elegance remains evident. Only someone with abundant talent and a thorough grasp of principle could achieve this. Having obtained a candidate like this, we may rank him first in this examining section.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor: Both the vitality of this line and the principles governing entering office or remaining in retirement are fully revealed. An excellent composition.
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The conception and phrasing move throughout the classic and its commentaries. Only someone deeply versed in the Book of Changes could accomplish this.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: Clear in principle and rich in expression.
The second, yin line of Gradual Progress presents an image of advancing and finding one's proper place, and a prognostication of advancing and attaining what is good. For in advancement, what matters is possessing virtue and having a corresponding line. Six in the second place combines both; thus there is good reason why its advancement is secure and it attains what is good! The Duke of Zhou's intention in appending words to this line was that, when a gentleman takes office, he does not concern himself with the glory of rank and emolument, but regards acting correctly in entering office or remaining in retirement as the difficult matter. Six in the second place of Gradual Progress is yielding and compliant, central and correct, and thus accords with the way of gradual advancement. Above, it corresponds to Nine in the fifth place, and therefore has an opportunity to advance. Thus, as a minister, he associates outwardly with the worthy: the duty of placing outstanding men in office rests with him [?], and he enjoys the good fortune of being exalted without peril; above, he attaches himself to the great …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
明公孤於我乎是任無處非其據之嫌也於是
享鼎之大烹而優游於見食於人之時俯仰何
愧怍乎受夬之施祿而委蛇於退食自公之際
情意何順乎適殆猶鴻焉將翺將翔漸于磐石
而棲止之自安也以飲以啄逺於水涯而和樂
之自若也其象如此其占維何蓋德薄而位尊
者必來負乗之誚功卑而祿崇者難免素餐之
譏今既有德而有應吾知其譽達於顯比之君
而朱紱方來有以荷天休之滋至道行於孚嘉
===
之日而大車以載足以勝重任而不疑平居之
抱負發而爲俊偉之事功天位與共三公不爲
過也言孰加焉疇昔之涵養措而爲光大之勳
業天祿與食萬鍾不爲泰也吉孰尚焉夫以君
子之不苟於進而進得所安如此其君臣相遇
之際殆非偶然者周公以是而著六二爻義其
示占者之意深矣抑考此爻之義古之人有行
之者伊呂是也觀其保衡商家弼成周室厥功
偉矣然使成湯無三聘之勤而文王無後車之
punctuated: 明，公孤於我乎是任，無處非其據之嫌也。於是享鼎之大烹，而優游於見食於人之時，俯仰何愧怍乎？受夬之施祿，而委蛇於退食自公之際，情意何順乎適！殆猶鴻焉，將翺將翔，漸于磐石，而棲止之自安也；以飲以啄，逺於水涯，而和樂之自若也。其象如此，其占維何？蓋德薄而位尊者，必來負乗之誚；功卑而祿崇者，難免素餐之譏。今既有德而有應，吾知其譽達於顯比之君，而朱紱方來，有以荷天休之滋至；道行於孚嘉之日，而大車以載，足以勝重任而不疑。平居之抱負，發而爲俊偉之事功，天位與共，三公不爲過也，言孰加焉？疇昔之涵養，措而爲光大之勳業，天祿與食，萬鍾不爲泰也，吉孰尚焉？夫以君子之不苟於進，而進得所安如此，其君臣相遇之際，殆非偶然者。周公以是而著六二爻義，其示占者之意深矣。抑考此爻之義，古之人有行之者，伊呂是也。觀其保衡商家，弼成周室，厥功偉矣。然使成湯無三聘之勤，而文王無後車之
translation_en:
…brilliance. Entrusted with the responsibilities of a duke or junior guardian, he incurs no suspicion of occupying a position that is not rightfully his. Thus he enjoys the sumptuous cooking of the Cauldron hexagram and rests at ease while receiving sustenance from others: whether looking down or up, what cause has he for shame? He receives the distribution of emoluments described in the Breakthrough hexagram and moves at ease when withdrawing from public service to eat: how harmonious and content are his feelings! He is much like a wild goose, about to soar and take flight, gradually advancing to a boulder and settling there in natural security; drinking and pecking, far from the water’s edge, it remains harmonious and happy.

Such is the image; what, then, is the prognostication? Those whose virtue is slight but whose position is exalted inevitably invite the reproach of carrying a burden while riding in a carriage; those whose achievements are meager but whose emoluments are generous can hardly escape criticism for eating without earning their keep. Now, possessing both virtue and a corresponding response above, he will, I know, gain a reputation that reaches a ruler who openly seeks union with the worthy. Vermilion knee-covers will soon come to him, enabling him to receive Heaven’s blessings in ever greater abundance. His Way will be put into practice when sincerity wins approval; like a great wagon bearing its load, he will be fully capable of shouldering weighty responsibilities, without doubt.

The aspirations he has nurtured in ordinary life emerge as outstanding accomplishments. Sharing in Heaven-conferred office, he would not be excessively exalted even among the Three Dukes: what words could add to this? The self-cultivation of former days is put to work in splendid achievements. Sharing in Heaven-conferred emoluments, he would not be excessively rewarded even with ten thousand measures of grain: what good fortune could surpass this?

Since the gentleman does not advance heedlessly, yet upon advancing finds such a secure place, his encounter with his ruler can hardly be accidental. It was on this basis that the Duke of Zhou set forth the meaning of the six in the second place. Profound indeed was his intention in instructing those who consult the oracle!

Moreover, if we examine the meaning of this line, there were men of antiquity who put it into practice: Yi Yin and Lü Shang. Consider how one protected and guided the house of Shang, and the other assisted in establishing the house of Zhou: their achievements were great indeed. Yet had Cheng Tang not diligently issued three invitations, and had King Wen not provided, in a carriage following his own, …

text:
載則二公之志亦終於莘野渭濱而已是知行
道者君子之本心而所以得行其道者則顧所
遇何如耳後世之士汲汲以仕進爲心而昧於

同考試官教諭郝批此題重在當期之日與當
萬物之數士子類無的見挑剔明白僅見此篇噫若子
者可以語數學矣
考試官教諭林批數學最難而子能言之
可嘉
考試官教授陳批蓍數之妙此作盡之
punctuated:
載，則二公之志亦終於莘野、渭濱而已。是知行道者，君子之本心，而所以得行其道者，則顧所遇何如耳。後世之士汲汲以仕進爲心，而昧於出處之宜，蓋亦不占而已矣。
乾之策二百一十有六，坤之策百四十有四，凡三百有六十，當期之日。二篇之策萬有一千五百二十，當萬物之數也。
趙廷富
同考試官教諭唐批：蓍策一題，多病於詞說之贅。此篇明白簡當，非衆作可及。其精於理學者與！
同考試官教諭蔡批：蓍數最爲微妙，子能探而發之，錄之以式来學。
同考試官教諭郝批：此題重在當期之日與當萬物之數。士子類無的見，挑剔明白，僅見此篇。噫！若子者，可以語數學矣。
考試官教諭林批：數學最難，而子能言之，可嘉。
考試官教授陳批：蓍數之妙，此作盡之。
translation_en:
…to carry him in his carriage, then the aspirations of those two men would likewise have ended in the fields of Shen and on the banks of the Wei. Thus we know that putting the Way into practice is the gentleman’s fundamental desire; whether he can do so depends upon the circumstances he encounters. Scholars of later ages anxiously set their hearts on entering office and advancing, yet fail to understand when it is proper to serve or withdraw. Surely they simply fail to consult the Changes.
The stalk count for Qian is two hundred and sixteen; that for Kun is one hundred and forty-four. Together they total three hundred and sixty, corresponding to the days of a year. The stalk count for the two parts is eleven thousand five hundred and twenty, corresponding to the number of the myriad things.
Zhao Tingfu
Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: Answers on the topic of yarrow stalks often suffer from excessive verbiage. This essay is clear, concise, and apt, beyond the reach of ordinary compositions. Surely its author is proficient in the Learning of Principle!
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: The numbers of the yarrow stalks are exceedingly subtle. You have been able to investigate and elucidate them. This essay is recorded as a model for future students.
Comment by Associate Examiner Hao, Instructor: The emphasis of this topic lies in “corresponding to the days of a year” and “corresponding to the number of the myriad things.” Candidates generally lack precise insight; only in this essay have I seen these points clearly teased out. Ah! With someone like you one can discuss the study of numbers.
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The study of numbers is exceedingly difficult, yet you can explain it. This merits praise.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: This composition fully sets forth the subtleties of the yarrow-stalk numbers.

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大傳論過揲之策有純卦之所準者有全經之
所準者蓋蓍数與造化相為流通者也不自其
所準觀之何以見其妙哉大傳論数法至此則
以過揲之策生於河圖之四面者言之意謂数
雖具於蓍策妙實符乎造化何也蓋揲蓍三變
之末九六迭出之餘三奇而九四之則為三十
有六也積而至於六畫之乾則為三十有六者
凡六而得二百一十有六之策焉三偶而六四
之則為二十有四也積而至於六畫之坤則為
===
二十有四者凡六而得百四十有四之策焉以
乾策之二百一十有六合坤策之百四十有四
共為数也凡三百有六十寧不有以當期之日
乎蓋一歲之日有氣盈有朔虛雖不能無多寡
之殊而三百六十乃其成数也二卦之策適與
之而相當初若有擬議焉者其妙也何如至若
乾為陽物凡百九十二之陽爻散見於二篇者
皆乾也而其策莫非三十有六即是數而乗之
以諸陽則得夫六千九百一十二策焉坤為陰
punctuated: 大傳論過揲之策，有純卦之所準者，有全經之所準者，蓋蓍数與造化相為流通者也。不自其所準觀之，何以見其妙哉？大傳論数法至此，則以過揲之策生於河圖之四面者言之，意謂数雖具於蓍策，妙實符乎造化。何也？蓋揲蓍三變之末，九六迭出之餘，三奇而九，四之則為三十有六也。積而至於六畫之乾，則為三十有六者凡六，而得二百一十有六之策焉。三偶而六，四之則為二十有四也。積而至於六畫之坤，則為二十有四者凡六，而得百四十有四之策焉。以乾策之二百一十有六合坤策之百四十有四，共為数也，凡三百有六十，寧不有以當期之日乎？蓋一歲之日有氣盈，有朔虛，雖不能無多寡之殊，而三百六十乃其成数也。二卦之策適與之而相當，初若有擬議焉者，其妙也何如！至若乾為陽物，凡百九十二之陽爻散見於二篇者，皆乾也，而其策莫非三十有六。即是數而乗之以諸陽，則得夫六千九百一十二策焉。坤為陰
translation_en: The Great Commentary discusses the stalks counted off in sorting: some totals correspond to the pure hexagrams, while others correspond to the entire Classic. For the numbers of the milfoil stalks and the processes of creation and transformation are interconnected. Unless we examine what these numbers correspond to, how can we perceive their subtlety? At this point in its discussion of numerical methods, the Great Commentary speaks of the counted-off stalks as deriving from the four sides of the River Chart (Hetu). Its meaning is that although the numbers are embodied in the milfoil stalks, their subtle workings truly accord with creation and transformation. Why is this so? At the completion of the three changes in sorting the milfoil, after nine and six have emerged in turn, three odd results yield nine; multiplying this by four gives thirty-six. Accumulating these for the six lines of Qian gives six sets of thirty-six, yielding 216 stalks. Three even results yield six; multiplying this by four gives twenty-four. Accumulating these for the six lines of Kun gives six sets of twenty-four, yielding 144 stalks. Combining Qian’s 216 stalks with Kun’s 144 gives a total of 360. Does this not correspond to the days of a year? In reckoning the days of a year, there is a surplus in the solar-term cycle and a shortfall in the lunar-month cycle. Although differences of greater and lesser amounts are unavoidable, 360 is the round total. The stalk totals of the two hexagrams correspond exactly to it, almost as though this correspondence had been deliberately planned. How subtle this is! As for Qian, it represents yang entities: all 192 yang lines appearing throughout the two parts of the Classic belong to Qian, and each has thirty-six stalks. Multiplying this number by all the yang lines yields 6,912 stalks. Kun represents yin …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
物凡百九十二之陰爻分布於二篇者皆坤也
而其策莫非二十有四即是數而乗之以諸陰
則得夫四千六百八策焉以陽爻之六千九百
一十二策合陰爻之四千六百八策其爲數也
凡萬有一千五百二十寧不有以當萬物之數
乎蓋天下之物有氣化有形化其數雖不止於
萬而萬者其多乃其常數也二篇之策適與之
而相當初若有比度焉者其妙也又何如是則
乾策坤策蓍數之一定也而於造化有所準曰
===
數物數造化之有常也而於蓍策不能外筮法
之妙有如此夫抑斯論也蓋謂陽主乎進少陽
進而未極乎盈則不足以爲化陰主於退少陰
退而未極乎虛則不足以爲變故卦之乾坤爻
之奇偶獨以二老計之至於以二少計之則其
數莫不有脗合焉者此亦夫子之意而諸儒之
說也
書
刑期于無刑
punctuated:
物，凡百九十二之陰爻分布於二篇者，皆坤也，而其策莫非二十有四。即是數而乗之以諸陰，則得夫四千六百八策焉。以陽爻之六千九百一十二策，合陰爻之四千六百八策，其爲數也，凡萬有一千五百二十，寧不有以當萬物之數乎？蓋天下之物，有氣化，有形化，其數雖不止於萬，而萬者其多，乃其常數也。二篇之策，適與之而相當，初若有比度焉者，其妙也又何如？是則乾策坤策，蓍數之一定也，而於造化有所準；曰數物數，造化之有常也，而於蓍策不能外。筮法之妙，有如此夫！抑斯論也，蓋謂陽主乎進，少陽進而未極乎盈，則不足以爲化；陰主於退，少陰退而未極乎虛，則不足以爲變。故卦之乾坤、爻之奇偶，獨以二老計之。至於以二少計之，則其數莫不有脗合焉者。此亦夫子之意，而諸儒之說也。

書

刑期于無刑。
translation_en:
…entity. All 192 yin lines distributed through the two parts of the Book of Changes belong to Kun, and the stalk count for each is invariably twenty-four. Multiplying this number by the total number of yin lines gives 4,608 stalks. Adding the 6,912 stalks of the yang lines to the 4,608 stalks of the yin lines yields a total of 11,520. Does this not suffice to correspond to the number of the myriad things? Among the things under Heaven, some arise through the transformation of vital energy and others through the transformation of physical forms. Although their number exceeds ten thousand, “ten thousand” expresses their multitude and is their conventional number. The stalk count of the two parts corresponds precisely to this, seemingly as though deliberately measured against it. How marvelous this too is! Thus, the stalk counts of Qian and Kun are fixed numbers in milfoil divination, yet they have their counterparts in the workings of creation. The number of days [?] and the number of things are constants in creation, yet neither lies outside the reckoning of the milfoil stalks. Such is the subtlety of the method of divination!

Furthermore, this discussion means that yang governs advance: when young yang advances but has not reached the utmost fullness, it cannot bring about transformation. Yin governs retreat: when young yin retreats but has not reached the utmost emptiness, it cannot bring about change. Thus, calculations for the hexagrams Qian and Kun and for odd and even lines use only the two old forms, old yang and old yin. As for calculations using the two young forms, their numbers likewise all accord. This, too, is the Master's meaning and the explanation of the Confucian scholars.

Book of Documents

“The aim of punishments is to bring about the absence of punishments.”

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
俞振強
同考試官訓導張批題不難於遣詞而難於
上下文不相粘礙此作得之是宜錄出
考試官教諭林批莊整可觀
考試官教授陳批此篇詞不繁而意自足
得作二典體
聖君稱士師始不免於刑之施心實期於刑之
措夫刑以不用為美也大臣於用刑之時而心
期於不用焉聖君稱之也宜哉昔帝舜不聽禹
===
之讓而稱皐陶之美以勸勉之若曰人但知汝
皐陶以刑為之職耳抑孰知其心存之美邪是
故臣工之多未必無違教者焉設或有之而刑
其可已乎汝為士師之官蓋嘗明以弼教而五
刑之是用矣民庶之衆未必無梗化者焉容或
有之而刑其可廢乎汝居掌刑之職蓋嘗明以
輔治而五刑之惟允矣墨也劓也推之而得其
情則舉以加之使知不善者有所懲剕宫也大
辟也審之而當其罪則因以施之使知為惡者
punctuated:
俞振強

同考試官訓導張批：題不難於遣詞，而難於上下文不相粘礙。此作得之，是宜錄出。

考試官教諭林批：莊整可觀。

考試官教授陳批：此篇詞不繁而意自足，得作二典體。

聖君稱士師，始不免於刑之施，心實期於刑之措。夫刑以不用為美也，大臣於用刑之時，而心期於不用焉，聖君稱之也宜哉！昔帝舜不聽禹之讓，而稱皐陶之美以勸勉之，若曰：「人但知汝皐陶以刑為之職耳，抑孰知其心存之美邪？是故臣工之多，未必無違教者焉。設或有之，而刑其可已乎？汝為士師之官，蓋嘗明以弼教，而五刑之是用矣。民庶之衆，未必無梗化者焉。容或有之，而刑其可廢乎？汝居掌刑之職，蓋嘗明以輔治，而五刑之惟允矣。墨也，劓也，推之而得其情，則舉以加之，使知不善者有所懲；剕、宫也，大辟也，審之而當其罪，則因以施之，使知為惡者
translation_en:
Yu Zhenqiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: The difficulty of this topic lies not in choosing words, but in keeping the preceding and following passages from becoming entangled and obstructing one another. This composition achieves that and therefore merits inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Dignified and orderly; worthy of attention.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: This essay fully conveys its meaning without excessive verbiage. It successfully adopts the style of the Two Canons.

The sage ruler praised the judge: although at first he could not avoid imposing punishments, his heart truly looked forward to their being set aside. For the excellence of punishments lies in their remaining unused. When a great minister, even while applying punishments, hopes in his heart that they will cease to be needed, how fitting it is that the sage ruler should praise him!

Formerly, Emperor Shun did not accept Yu’s yielding of precedence, but praised Gao Yao’s virtues to encourage him, as though saying: “People know only that you, Gao Yao, have punishment as your duty. Yet who understands the admirable purpose you cherish in your heart? Among the many officials, there may well be some who disobey instruction. Should there be such men, could punishment cease? Serving as judge, you have indeed applied the five punishments with discernment to support moral instruction. Among the multitude of common people, there may well be some who resist transforming influence. Should there be such people, could punishment be abolished? Holding the office responsible for punishments, you have indeed assisted government with discernment, ensuring that the five punishments are justly applied. As for tattooing and cutting off the nose, once investigation establishes the facts, you impose them, so that people know that misconduct brings chastisement. As for amputation of the feet, castration, and death, once careful examination establishes the punishment appropriate to the crime, you administer it accordingly, so that those who do evil know …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有所懼汝之不免於用刑者如是原汝之心豈
欲恃以為治邪將以致夫治隆之功使在朝廷
也禮義流行純乎道德之懿而刑法殆為虛器
矣將以收夫俗美之效使在閭閻也德化洋溢
藹乎淳朴之風而理官若為虛設矣一心之所
願直欲舉國皆遵其教而過焉有所不為則墨
劓之刑雖小不用焉一念之所存直欲舉世皆
從其化而罪焉决於不犯則剕宮大辟之典雖
重不施焉吁臯陶有無刑之期而今卒能副之
===
如此此伯禹之所以讓而帝舜所以稱之也歟
大抵聖人之治德為化民之本刑為輔治之法
然謂之輔則見其用於時者皆聖人之不得已
也有虞之刑司之以明慎之臯陶主之以欽恤
之帝舜尚不足以為恃必求至于不犯有司四
方風動而後已彼後世之鍛鍊以為能根連株
繫而不忌者獨何心哉
茲亦惟天若元德永不忘在王家
王鏞
punctuated:
有所懼。汝之不免於用刑者如是，原汝之心，豈欲恃以為治邪？將以致夫治隆之功，使在朝廷也，禮義流行，純乎道德之懿，而刑法殆為虛器矣；將以收夫俗美之效，使在閭閻也，德化洋溢，藹乎淳朴之風，而理官若為虛設矣。一心之所願，直欲舉國皆遵其教，而過焉有所不為，則墨劓之刑雖小，不用焉；一念之所存，直欲舉世皆從其化，而罪焉决於不犯，則剕宮大辟之典雖重，不施焉。吁！臯陶有無刑之期，而今卒能副之如此，此伯禹之所以讓，而帝舜所以稱之也歟？大抵聖人之治，德為化民之本，刑為輔治之法。然謂之輔，則見其用於時者，皆聖人之不得已也。有虞之刑，司之以明慎之臯陶，主之以欽恤之帝舜，尚不足以為恃，必求至于不犯有司、四方風動而後已。彼後世之鍛鍊以為能，根連株繫而不忌者，獨何心哉？

茲亦惟天若，元德永不忘在王家。
王鏞
translation_en:
…have something to fear. Such are the circumstances in which you cannot avoid employing punishments. Yet, tracing this back to your intentions, could you possibly wish to rely on them to govern? Your purpose is to achieve flourishing government, so that ritual propriety and righteousness prevail at court, in the unalloyed excellence of the Way and virtue, and penal laws become virtually empty instruments. Your purpose is to bring about admirable customs, so that virtue’s transforming influence spreads throughout the neighborhoods, a spirit of simplicity and sincerity abounds, and judicial officials seem to hold offices with nothing to do. Your wholehearted wish is simply that the entire realm should heed its teachings and refrain from wrongdoing; then even the lesser punishments of tattooing and cutting off the nose would go unused. Your constant intention is simply that all under Heaven should follow its transforming influence and resolutely avoid committing crimes; then even the weightier penalties of amputation of the feet, castration, and death would not be imposed. Ah! Gao Yao hoped for an end to punishment, and ultimately fulfilled that hope in this way. Was this not why Bo Yu deferred to him and Emperor Shun praised him?

In general, under the sages’ government, virtue is the foundation for transforming the people, and punishment is a means of assisting government. Yet calling it an assistance shows that whenever the sages employed it, they did so only because they had no alternative. The punishments of Youyu were administered by the discerning and cautious Gao Yao and overseen by the reverent and compassionate Emperor Shun. Even so, punishment was not sufficient to rely upon. They would not rest until people ceased to fall afoul of the judicial authorities and all four quarters responded as grass bends before the wind. What sort of intentions, then, did those men of later ages harbor, who considered themselves capable for fabricating criminal cases and felt no compunction about implicating and arresting everyone connected with them?

“Here too Heaven is favorable; great virtue shall never be forgotten in the royal house.”
Wang Yong 王鏞

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導張批茲字只指稽德饋祀而
言元德亦不過此士子乃併前羞考說來於元德上卒
無歸着惟此篇體貼經傳作出且文氣老成規度嚴肅
宜錄之以式
考試官教諭林批簡實可觀
考試官教授陳批理明詞順可取可取
聖君教妹臣能有謹酒之實則膺天眷於無窮
矣夫天之休命得之固難而有永尤難也非妹
臣有謹酒之實天之所眷豈若是哉昔者武王
===
告康叔欲其教妹土之臣也其意謂夫汝庶士
有正庶伯君子毋以脩德爲無益謹酒爲小德
也誠能反觀內省悉稽乎中正之德而有盛大
之實克羞饋祀自用夫宴樂之飲而無沉湎之
累如此有不足以得天者乎吾知禍福不常天
至難諶也鑒此元德自有以順之於冲漠之中
予奪靡定天未易得也眷此大德自有以若之
於亭毒之表天非有私於汝也而富貴以厚其
生者方興而未艾汝非有求於天也而福澤以
punctuated:
同考試官訓導張批：茲字只指稽德饋祀而言，元德亦不過此。士子乃併前羞考說來，於元德上卒無歸着。惟此篇體貼經傳作出，且文氣老成，規度嚴肅，宜錄之以式。
考試官教諭林批：簡實可觀。
考試官教授陳批：理明詞順，可取可取。
聖君教妹臣能有謹酒之實，則膺天眷於無窮矣。夫天之休命，得之固難，而有永尤難也。非妹臣有謹酒之實，天之所眷豈若是哉？昔者武王告康叔，欲其教妹土之臣也。其意謂夫汝庶士、有正、庶伯、君子，毋以脩德爲無益，謹酒爲小德也。誠能反觀內省，悉稽乎中正之德，而有盛大之實，克羞饋祀，自用夫宴樂之飲，而無沉湎之累，如此，有不足以得天者乎？吾知禍福不常，天至難諶也；鑒此元德，自有以順之於冲漠之中。予奪靡定，天未易得也；眷此大德，自有以若之於亭毒之表。天非有私於汝也，而富貴以厚其生者，方興而未艾；汝非有求於天也，而福澤以
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: The word “this” refers only to examining one’s virtue and presenting sacrificial offerings; “great virtue,” too, means no more than this. Candidates have brought in the preceding passage about presenting offerings to deceased fathers, ultimately failing to give “great virtue” a definite meaning. This essay alone was composed with close attention to the classic and its commentary. Moreover, its writing is mature and its structure disciplined and dignified. It should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Concise and substantial; worthy of attention.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: Clear in reasoning and fluent in expression. Worth accepting, worth accepting.

When a sage ruler instructs the ministers of Mei to exercise genuine restraint in drinking, they will receive Heaven’s favor without end. Heaven’s gracious mandate is certainly difficult to obtain, but keeping it forever is more difficult still. Unless the ministers of Mei genuinely exercised restraint in drinking, how could Heaven favor them thus? Formerly, King Wu admonished Kang Shu, wishing him to instruct the ministers of the territory of Mei. His meaning was this: You officers, heads of offices, chiefs, and gentlemen must not consider cultivating virtue useless, or restraint in drinking a minor virtue. If you can truly turn your gaze inward and examine yourselves, thoroughly investigate the virtue of centrality and correctness, and possess its abundant substance, you will be able to present sacrificial offerings and partake of drink at feasts without the burden of drunken indulgence. With conduct such as this, could anything be lacking in your winning Heaven’s favor? I know that calamity and blessing are inconstant, and Heaven is exceedingly difficult to trust. Yet, discerning this great virtue, Heaven will have cause to accord with it amid its silent, formless workings. Giving and taking away are unsettled, and Heaven’s favor is not easily obtained. Yet, regarding this great virtue, Heaven will have cause to favor it beyond the manifest workings of its nurturing power.
