title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
庇其身者滋至而無已曰名曰位昔固見錄於
王家矣今則居之安而綿綿不絕不但居之一
時也將歷悠久而常保矣豈復有瑕殄者乎曰
職曰禄昔嘗見錫於王家矣今則守之固而源
源不竭非但守之一時也將至悠遠而常享矣
寧復有棄絕者乎吁武王欲其臣之謹酒而舉
天若元德為勸如此其亦誘掖之至者歟嗟夫
妹土臣民蕞爾之微耳况以康叔往為之君宜
其無難化者武王乃致告之如此者何哉蓋商
===
受酗酒天下化之而妹土為其故都染惡尤深
武王誅君弔民一新其政孰有急於是邪禹於
子孫嘗有甘酒之訓成湯風愆之戒亦以酣歌
寓乎其間古昔聖人未嘗不拳拳于是也噫彼
昏不知隄糟池酒者何哉
詩
考卜維王宅是鎬京維龜正之武王成之
王容
同考試官教諭何批稽疑决疑處作者多挑剔
punctuated:
庇其身者滋至而無已。曰名曰位，昔固見錄於王家矣，今則居之安而綿綿不絕，不但居之一時也，將歷悠久而常保矣，豈復有瑕殄者乎？曰職曰禄，昔嘗見錫於王家矣，今則守之固而源源不竭，非但守之一時也，將至悠遠而常享矣，寧復有棄絕者乎？吁！武王欲其臣之謹酒，而舉天若元德為勸如此，其亦誘掖之至者歟！嗟夫！妹土臣民，蕞爾之微耳，况以康叔往為之君，宜其無難化者。武王乃致告之如此者，何哉？蓋商受酗酒，天下化之，而妹土為其故都，染惡尤深。武王誅君弔民，一新其政，孰有急於是邪？禹於子孫嘗有甘酒之訓，成湯風愆之戒亦以酣歌寓乎其間。古昔聖人未嘗不拳拳于是也。噫！彼昏不知隄，糟池酒者何哉？

詩

考卜維王，宅是鎬京。維龜正之，武王成之。

王容

translation_en:
…the blessings that shelter you will come ever more abundantly, without end. As for reputation and rank, you were already enrolled in the royal service; now you will occupy your position securely, in an unbroken succession. You will hold it not merely for a time, but preserve it enduringly through long ages. What blemish or destruction could then befall you? As for office and emoluments, these were previously bestowed upon you by the royal house; now you will hold them firmly, with their flow never exhausted. You will retain them not merely for a time, but enjoy them enduringly into the distant future. How could they again be withdrawn or cut off?

Ah! King Wu wished his ministers to exercise restraint in drinking, and encouraged them in this way by invoking Heaven’s favor toward great virtue. Was this not the utmost in guidance and support? Alas! The ministers and people of Mei constituted only a tiny territory. Moreover, with Kang Shu going there to become their ruler, surely none should have been difficult to transform. Why, then, did King Wu address them with such earnest admonitions? It was because Shou of Shang drank to excess and all under Heaven followed his example. Mei, being his former capital, was especially deeply infected by this evil. King Wu punished its ruler, comforted its people, and wholly renewed its government. What could have been more urgent than this? Yu once admonished his descendants against delighting in wine; Cheng Tang’s warning against the fault of wanton indulgence likewise included drunken singing. The sages of antiquity never ceased to attend earnestly to this matter. Alas! What of those who, benighted and knowing no restraint, indulge in lees and pools of wine [?]?

The Book of Odes

“It was the king who examined the divination and settled here in Haojing. The tortoise determined it; King Wu brought it to completion.”

Wang Rong

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不明此作認題精確而詞又足以發之令人拭目
同考試官教諭戴批剖析詳明而詞意警拔駸
駸然追逼古作蓋不梏於專經者
同考試官教諭吳批作此篇者形容都遷氣象
綺語動盈卷帙顧於遷都不苟處不相發此作因題命
意根理遣詞使武王當年心事宛然在目竒士也
考試官教諭林批氣昌理到掃去陳言時
作中不多得
考試官教授陳批詞豊贍而意圓活宜錄
===
以式承學
稽諸神以定都決諸神以建都詩人美聖君然
也夫遷都國之大事也聖君必稽於神而後決
焉其慎重之意何如哉此詩美武王遷鎬而作
也蓋謂我武王當四方攸同之日遂有遷都于
鎬之舉以爲開國承家非細故也烏可苟哉與
其謀於人也不若謀之於神乃考之於卜于以
決吉凶於猶豫之間與其斷於己也不若斷之
於神乃稽之於占于以質休咎於疑似之頃遷此
punctuated:
不明。此作認題精確，而詞又足以發之，令人拭目。
同考試官教諭戴批：剖析詳明，而詞意警拔，駸駸然追逼古作，蓋不梏於專經者。
同考試官教諭吳批：作此篇者，形容都遷氣象，綺語動盈卷帙，顧於遷都不苟處不相發。此作因題命意，根理遣詞，使武王當年心事宛然在目，竒士也。
考試官教諭林批：氣昌理到，掃去陳言，時作中不多得。
考試官教授陳批：詞豊贍而意圓活，宜錄以式承學。
稽諸神以定都，決諸神以建都，詩人美聖君然也。夫遷都，國之大事也，聖君必稽於神而後決焉，其慎重之意何如哉！此詩美武王遷鎬而作也。蓋謂我武王當四方攸同之日，遂有遷都于鎬之舉，以爲開國承家，非細故也，烏可苟哉！與其謀於人也，不若謀之於神，乃考之於卜，于以決吉凶於猶豫之間；與其斷於己也，不若斷之於神，乃稽之於占，于以質休咎於疑似之頃。遷此
translation_en:
…are not made clear. This composition grasps the topic precisely, and its language adequately brings out its meaning, making the reader look afresh.
Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor, comments: The analysis is detailed and clear, while the language and ideas are striking and distinguished, advancing swiftly toward the standard of ancient compositions. The author is evidently someone not confined by specialization in a single Classic.
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: Those who compose on this passage describe the grandeur of the capital’s relocation, readily filling entire volumes with ornate language, yet fail to illuminate the care with which the relocation was undertaken. This composition takes its central idea from the topic and grounds its wording in principle, bringing King Wu’s concerns in those days vividly before our eyes. An exceptional talent indeed!
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: Its vigor is abundant and its reasoning fully developed; it sweeps away hackneyed expressions. Such work is rarely found among contemporary compositions.
Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: Its language is rich and ample, and its ideas rounded and supple. It deserves to be recorded as a model for those pursuing learning.
To consult the spirits in determining the capital’s site, and to seek their decision in establishing the capital: this is what the poet praises in the sage ruler. Relocating the capital is a great affair of state. The sage ruler must consult the spirits before making his decision. How profound is his care and caution! This poem was composed to praise King Wu’s relocation to Hao. It means that when the four quarters had become united under our King Wu, he undertook to move the capital to Hao. He considered that founding a state and securing its ruling house were no trifling matters: how could one act carelessly? Rather than seek counsel from men, it was better to seek it from the spirits. Thus he consulted the turtle-shell oracle, to determine good or ill fortune amid uncertainty. Rather than decide by himself, it was better to seek a decision from the spirits. Thus he examined the divinatory signs, to ascertain blessing or calamity at a moment of doubt. In moving to this…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
鎬京必欲得形勝而據之建宗社營宮室居重
馭輕而爲萬國都會之區也居此鎬京必欲得
險阻而依之築城邑立朝市宅中圖大而垂萬
世無疆之休也于斯時也灼彼元龜適有以協
人謀考成象於墨食之初有吉而無凶也先矣
王者之都向之猶豫以决燃彼楚焞適有以符
已見驗成卦於鑽刺之後有休而無咎也信矣
邦畿之地昔之疑似以定於是斷自宸衷據此
天下之形勝宗社以建宮室以營制度煥乎其
===
聿新也所謂萬邦之方者在是出自睿筭依此
天下之險阻城邑以築朝市以立規模秩乎其
鼎建也所謂下民之王者在是吁武王遷鎬必
决之神謀而不敢焉苟如此君道之盡不於此
而可見乎詩人所以美之也宜矣大抵遷都所
以爲民而出於爲民之外者皆私也亦所以爲
後世謀而爲後亦爲民也武王之遷鎬以豐邑
難容而遷是故爲民而遷耳遷之而謀無不悉
亦爲民而謀焉耳視彼後世若長安之都惟圖
punctuated: 鎬京，必欲得形勝而據之，建宗社，營宮室，居重馭輕，而爲萬國都會之區也。居此鎬京，必欲得險阻而依之，築城邑，立朝市，宅中圖大，而垂萬世無疆之休也。于斯時也，灼彼元龜，適有以協人謀，考成象於墨食之初，有吉而無凶也。先矣，王者之都！向之猶豫以决。燃彼楚焞，適有以符已見，驗成卦於鑽刺之後，有休而無咎也。信矣，邦畿之地！昔之疑似以定。於是斷自宸衷，據此天下之形勝，宗社以建，宮室以營，制度煥乎其聿新也，所謂萬邦之方者在是。出自睿筭，依此天下之險阻，城邑以築，朝市以立，規模秩乎其鼎建也，所謂下民之王者在是。吁！武王遷鎬，必决之神謀，而不敢焉苟如此，君道之盡，不於此而可見乎？詩人所以美之也，宜矣！大抵遷都所以爲民，而出於爲民之外者皆私也。亦所以爲後世謀，而爲後亦爲民也。武王之遷鎬，以豐邑難容而遷，是故爲民而遷耳。遷之而謀無不悉，亦爲民而謀焉耳。視彼後世，若長安之都，惟圖
translation_en:
…to Haojing, he was determined to secure a strategically advantageous site and occupy it, establish the ancestral temple and altars of state, and construct palaces, using the commanding center to govern the subordinate regions and making it the capital where the myriad states would converge. In settling at Haojing, he was determined to secure natural defenses and rely upon them, build city walls, establish the court and marketplaces, and plan great undertakings from this central position, bequeathing boundless blessings for ten thousand generations.

At this time, the great tortoise shell was scorched, and its indications accorded with human deliberations. When the resulting configurations were examined as the cracks first met the ink markings, there was good fortune and no ill fortune. The royal capital was thus indicated beforehand [?], and earlier hesitation was resolved. The thornwood brand was kindled, and its indications confirmed his own judgment [?]. When the resulting divinatory figures were examined after the shell had been drilled and pierced, there were blessings and no misfortune. The site of the royal domain was confirmed, and former doubts were settled.

Then, deciding within his sovereign heart, he occupied this strategically advantageous site in the realm. The ancestral temple and altars of state were established, and the palaces constructed: the institutions shone in their renewal. Here was what the ode calls “the model for the myriad states.” Through his sagacious calculations, he relied upon these natural defenses of the realm. City walls were built, and the court and marketplaces established: the grand design took shape in orderly fashion. Here was what the ode calls “the king of the people below.”

Ah! When King Wu moved to Haojing, he insisted upon settling the matter through consultation with the spirits, and was so unwilling to act carelessly. Can we not see here how fully he fulfilled the Way of the ruler? It was fitting indeed that the poet should praise him!

Generally speaking, moving the capital is undertaken for the people; any motive beyond serving the people is selfish. It also constitutes planning for later generations, and serving later generations likewise means serving the people. King Wu moved to Haojing because the settlement at Feng could scarcely accommodate them; thus he moved solely for the people. That his deliberations concerning the move left nothing unexamined likewise meant only that he deliberated for the people. Consider those of later ages: in establishing the capital at Chang’an, the sole intention was…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以一面控制諸侯洛陽之遷惟欲以舊迹比隆
周室良非所以爲斯民圖者果可與周武同日
而語哉
念茲皇祖陟降庭止維予小子夙夜敬止
陳器
同考試官教諭何批武王之孝止是箇敬字故
成王欲勉敬以承之詞浮於理者殊爲可厭求其渾厚
爾雅而善寫成王意緒者有如此篇
同考試官教諭戴批官樣題目作者不泛則略
===
此篇說理精到造語警策殆邃於經學者
同考試官教諭吳批孝敬書生之常談固不
難於操筆詞峻整而思舂容此作得之
考試官教諭林批形容成王追慕之意妙在
紆餘宛轉之中醞藉之學固如是
考試官教授陳批平淡典雅如太羹玄酒
自有深味可錄
表前王克孝之實勉在己持敬之常賢王然也
夫敬之所在即孝之所在也成王表前王之孝
punctuated:
以一面控制諸侯，洛陽之遷，惟欲以舊迹比隆周室，良非所以爲斯民圖者，果可與周武同日而語哉？

念茲皇祖，陟降庭止。維予小子，夙夜敬止。
陳器

同考試官教諭何批：武王之孝，止是箇敬字，故成王欲勉敬以承之。詞浮於理者，殊爲可厭。求其渾厚爾雅而善寫成王意緒者，有如此篇。

同考試官教諭戴批：官樣題目，作者不泛則略。此篇說理精到，造語警策，殆邃於經學者。

同考試官教諭吳批：孝敬，書生之常談，固不難於操筆。詞峻整而思舂容，此作得之。

考試官教諭林批：形容成王追慕之意，妙在紆餘宛轉之中，醞藉之學固如是。

考試官教授陳批：平淡典雅，如太羹玄酒，自有深味，可錄。

表前王克孝之實，勉在己持敬之常，賢王然也。
夫敬之所在，即孝之所在也。成王表前王之孝
translation_en:
…to control the feudal lords from a single vantage point, while the transfer to Luoyang sought only, through its ancient associations, to rival the glory of the Zhou royal house. These were certainly not plans made for the people's sake. Can they really be spoken of in the same breath as King Wu of Zhou?

“Mindful of this august ancestor, ascending and descending in the court, I, the young son, remain reverent morning and night.”
Chen Qi 陳器

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: King Wu's filial devotion comes down to the single word “reverence”; hence King Cheng wished to exert himself in reverence so as to carry it forward. Writing whose rhetoric exceeds its reasoning is particularly tiresome. For an essay that is substantial and classically elegant, and skillfully conveys King Cheng's thoughts and feelings, we have this piece.

Comment by Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor: With a conventional examination topic, writers tend to be either vague or cursory. This essay's exposition of principle is precise and thorough, and its phrasing incisive and admonitory. Its author is surely deeply versed in classical learning.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: Filial devotion and reverence are common topics among scholars, so taking up the brush to write about them is certainly no difficulty. This piece achieves dignified, well-ordered language and ample, unhurried thought.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Its portrayal of King Cheng's longing admiration achieves its subtle effect through leisurely, winding expression. Learning rich in reserve is indeed like this.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: Plain and classically elegant, like the unseasoned sacrificial broth and the ritual water called “dark wine,” it possesses a deep savor of its own. Worth recording.

To display the former king's actual achievement of filial devotion, and to urge himself to maintain constant reverence: this is how a worthy king acts.
Where reverence resides, filial devotion resides also. King Cheng displayed the former king's filial devotion…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而自勉以敬其得繼述之道者歟此成王免喪
朝廟而作歎前王永世克孝而勉之以敬蓋謂
昔我皇考之念皇祖痛儀容之永隔而追慕之
心不忘於頃刻惟欲繼其志也念覆育之深恩
而哀慕之情不替於斯須惟欲述其事也心之
所至目常之在皇祖雖遠常若見其陟之于庭
而覩無像於有像恍乎謦欬之有聞念之所切
視之如存皇祖雖往恒若見其降之于庭而視
無形於有形宛乎儀容之相接皇考之克孝如
===
此是皆一敬之所存也顧予小子年甫幼冲負
此守成之託一或不敬則先業隳矣敢自怠乎
眇躬凉薄撫此盈成之運一有不敬則先緒墜
矣敢自畫乎故必夙焉而興虔恭寅畏不以夙
而或懈一以皇考之念皇祖者而念我皇考務
有以踐其遺規也夜焉而寐戰兢惕勵不以夜
而少替一以皇考之思皇祖者而思我皇考務
有以步其後塵也噫成王述前王之孝而勉在
巳之敬如此其所以就文武之業而崇大化之
punctuated: 而自勉以敬，其得繼述之道者歟？此成王免喪朝廟而作，歎前王永世克孝，而勉之以敬。蓋謂：「昔我皇考之念皇祖，痛儀容之永隔，而追慕之心不忘於頃刻，惟欲繼其志也；念覆育之深恩，而哀慕之情不替於斯須，惟欲述其事也。心之所至，目常之在，皇祖雖遠，常若見其陟之于庭，而覩無像於有像，恍乎謦欬之有聞；念之所切，視之如存，皇祖雖往，恒若見其降之于庭，而視無形於有形，宛乎儀容之相接。皇考之克孝如此，是皆一敬之所存也。顧予小子，年甫幼冲，負此守成之託，一或不敬，則先業隳矣，敢自怠乎？眇躬凉薄，撫此盈成之運，一有不敬，則先緒墜矣，敢自畫乎？故必夙焉而興，虔恭寅畏，不以夙而或懈，一以皇考之念皇祖者而念我皇考，務有以踐其遺規也；夜焉而寐，戰兢惕勵，不以夜而少替，一以皇考之思皇祖者而思我皇考，務有以步其後塵也。」噫！成王述前王之孝，而勉在巳之敬如此，其所以就文武之業而崇大化之
translation_en:
…and exhorted himself to reverence: had he not grasped the way to carry on his predecessors’ intentions and deeds? King Cheng composed this upon completing his mourning and attending the ancestral temple. He praised the former king’s lifelong filial devotion and urged himself to reverence. His meaning was this:

“When my august late father remembered my august grandfather, he grieved that he was forever parted from his countenance and bearing. Never for a moment forgetting his longing for him, he wished only to carry on his intentions. Remembering the profound kindness with which he had been sheltered and nurtured, he never for an instant diminished his sorrowful affection, wishing only to continue his deeds. Wherever his heart turned, his eyes constantly rested [?]. Though my august grandfather was far removed, he always seemed to see him ascending in the courtyard. He beheld the unseen as though visibly present, almost hearing the sound of his cough. So keen was his remembrance that he regarded him as still alive. Though my august grandfather had departed, he constantly seemed to see him descending in the courtyard. He saw the formless as though possessing form, as if his countenance and bearing were directly before him. Such was my august late father’s filial devotion, and all of it rested upon reverence alone.

“Yet I, the young one, am still of tender years and bear this charge to preserve what has been accomplished. Should I once fail in reverence, the achievements of my forebears would fall into ruin. Dare I be negligent? Insignificant and deficient in virtue, I preside over this age of full prosperity. Should I ever lack reverence, the legacy of my forebears would collapse. Dare I set limits upon my efforts? Thus I must rise early, devout, respectful, reverent, and apprehensive, never allowing the early hour to occasion any slackness. Just as my august late father remembered my august grandfather, so must I remember my august late father, striving to put his bequeathed rules into practice. I must retire late at night, trembling with caution, vigilant and diligent, never allowing the late hour to diminish my efforts. Just as my august late father thought of my august grandfather, so must I think of my august late father, striving to follow in his footsteps.”

“Ah! Such was King Cheng’s account of the former king’s filial devotion and his exhortation to himself to maintain reverence. The means by which he brought the achievements of Kings Wen and Wu to completion and exalted the foundation of great moral transformation…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
本端在此矣抑考敬者千聖傳心之要致治保
邦之本也故欽明若堯允恭若舜祗德若禹聖
敬若湯乃知自古帝王創業垂統未有不本於
敬也成王有見於此思前王創業之難知在巳
守成不易故於嗣大歷服之初拳拳以敬自勉
可謂得聖賢傳心之法嗣王繼述之要也其所
以基命宥密緝熈大業而爲有周守成令主夫
豈無自而然哉
春秋
===
宋人圍滕〔宣公九年〕宋師伐滕〔宣公十年〕
吳榮賀
同考試官教諭李批〔聖經稱人稱師之意𩔖能發之明白痛快如此作殊勘當是老於經學者錄之〕
考試官教諭林批〔以仁義二字發明稱人稱師之旨良是〕
考試官教授陳批〔辭嚴義正春秋字當如此作〕
大國始乘難以虐小春秋貶其不仁繼縱惡而
punctuated:
本端在此矣。抑考敬者，千聖傳心之要，致治保邦之本也。故欽明若堯，允恭若舜，祗德若禹，聖敬若湯，乃知自古帝王創業垂統，未有不本於敬也。成王有見於此，思前王創業之難，知在巳守成不易，故於嗣大歷服之初，拳拳以敬自勉，可謂得聖賢傳心之法、嗣王繼述之要也。其所以基命宥密，緝熈大業，而爲有周守成令主，夫豈無自而然哉？

春秋

宋人圍滕〔宣公九年〕，宋師伐滕〔宣公十年〕。
吳榮賀
同考試官教諭李批〔聖經稱人稱師之意，𩔖能發之明白痛快，如此作殊勘當是老於經學者，錄之。〕
考試官教諭林批〔以仁義二字發明稱人稱師之旨，良是。〕
考試官教授陳批〔辭嚴義正，春秋字當如此作。〕

大國始乘難以虐小，春秋貶其不仁；繼縱惡而
translation_en:
…the foundation lies precisely here. Moreover, reverence [?] is the essential teaching transmitted from mind to mind by the sages, and the foundation for achieving good government and preserving the state. Thus Yao was reverent and discerning, Shun truly respectful, Yu reverent in virtue, and Tang sagely and reverent. We thereby know that, from antiquity, no emperor or king established a dynasty and handed down its succession without grounding it in reverence. King Cheng understood this. Reflecting on the difficulty with which the former kings had founded their enterprise, he knew that preserving their accomplishments would be no easy task for him. Thus, at the outset of succeeding to the great mandate and royal office, he earnestly exhorted himself to reverence. He may indeed be said to have grasped the method by which sages and worthies transmitted their inner teaching, and the essentials by which a succeeding king carries on his predecessors’ work. How could his establishing the mandate through profound and quiet exertion, continuing and illuminating the great enterprise, and becoming an excellent ruler who preserved the Zhou inheritance have come about without a source?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“The men of Song besieged Teng.” 〔Ninth year of Duke Xuan.〕 “The army of Song attacked Teng.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Xuan.〕
Wu Ronghe

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔The sacred classic’s intention in using “men” and “army” can be elucidated with such clarity and force. An essay like this is particularly worthy [?]; its author must be a seasoned student of the classics. Select it.〕

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔Using the two terms “benevolence” and “righteousness” to elucidate the purport of “men” and “army” is indeed correct.〕

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: 〔The language is stern and the principles correct. Writing on the Spring and Autumn Annals [?] should be done in this manner.〕

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
虐小春秋譏其不義此宋兩加兵於滕皆非其
道也春秋一稱人一稱師豈無意哉且滕介於
宋敖慢不恭宋也圍之似不為過者經以人稱
說者曰刺伐喪也則凡不恭之國將置而不問
乎蓋當是時滕昭不祿變故方殷人所共憫者
也凡有仁心者必將哀矜惻怛弔恤之不暇矣
況於鄰壤之邦玉帛往来之舊乎宋不念此顧以
私忿小怨命將出師汲汲於滕之是圍焉假曰
滕不事己不為無罪盍亦思己德無乃有闕歟
===
乃乗其喪以圍之欺人之孤而不忌弱人之寡
而罔卹其與見落穽不能求反擠之而下石者
何異邪非至不仁者莫之忍為經於圍滕特以
人稱意蓋如此夫滕雖見圍負固自若宋復伐
之似無足怪者經以師稱說者曰譏用衆也則
凡負固之邦將諉而不討乎蓋當是時徵舒不
軌惡逆滔天人得而誅者也苟有仗義者必將
怒目切齒致辟之恐後矣況於上公之尊先代
伯業之餘乎宋不慮此顧以細故微瑕揚兵耀
punctuated:
虐小，《春秋》譏其不義。此宋兩加兵於滕，皆非其道也。《春秋》一稱人，一稱師，豈無意哉？且滕介於宋，敖慢不恭宋也，圍之似不為過者。經以人稱，說者曰：「刺伐喪也。」則凡不恭之國，將置而不問乎？蓋當是時，滕昭不祿，變故方殷，人所共憫者也。凡有仁心者，必將哀矜惻怛，弔恤之不暇矣，況於鄰壤之邦，玉帛往来之舊乎？宋不念此，顧以私忿小怨，命將出師，汲汲於滕之是圍焉。假曰滕不事己，不為無罪，盍亦思己德無乃有闕歟？乃乗其喪以圍之，欺人之孤而不忌，弱人之寡而罔卹，其與見落穽不能求，反擠之而下石者何異邪？非至不仁者，莫之忍為。經於圍滕，特以人稱，意蓋如此。
夫滕雖見圍，負固自若，宋復伐之，似無足怪者。經以師稱，說者曰：「譏用衆也。」則凡負固之邦，將諉而不討乎？蓋當是時，徵舒不軌，惡逆滔天，人得而誅者也。苟有仗義者，必將怒目切齒，致辟之恐後矣，況於上公之尊，先代伯業之餘乎？宋不慮此，顧以細故微瑕，揚兵耀
translation_en:
…oppressing a small state, the Spring and Autumn Annals censures its unrighteousness. These two occasions on which Song took up arms against Teng both departed from the proper way. The Spring and Autumn Annals calls them “men” on one occasion and an “army” on the other: could this be without significance? Now Teng lay beside Song and treated Song arrogantly and disrespectfully, so besieging it might seem no transgression. Yet the Classic calls the attackers “men.” Commentators say: “This condemns attacking a state in mourning.” Does this mean that every disrespectful state should be left alone and not called to account? At that time, however, Duke Zhao of Teng had died; calamity was at its height, and everyone shared in pitying the state. Anyone with a benevolent heart would surely have been fully occupied with grief and compassion, offering condolences and relief. How much more should this have been true of a neighboring state with a longstanding exchange of jade and silk gifts! Song gave no thought to this. Instead, over private anger and petty grievances, it appointed a commander and dispatched troops, hastening to besiege Teng. Even granting that Teng was not without fault for failing to serve Song, should Song not also have considered whether its own virtue was deficient? Instead, it exploited Teng’s mourning to besiege it, bullying its orphaned heir without restraint and weakening its bereaved people without compassion. How was this different from seeing someone fall into a pit and, instead of rescuing him [?], pushing him farther in and dropping stones upon him? Only someone utterly lacking benevolence could bear to do this. This, presumably, is why the Classic specifically uses “men” in recording the siege of Teng.
Although Teng had been besieged, it continued as before to rely on its fortifications, so Song’s attacking it again might seem unsurprising. Yet the Classic calls the attackers an “army.” Commentators say: “This censures the deployment of a large force.” Does this mean that every state relying on its fortifications should be left aside without punitive action? At that time, however, Zhengshu had committed an act of treason; his wickedness and rebellion reached to Heaven, and anyone was entitled to put him to death. Anyone upholding righteousness would surely have glared in anger and gnashed his teeth, fearing that he might be too late to bring the culprit to punishment. How much more should this have been true of one holding the exalted rank of senior duke and inheriting the legacy of a predecessor’s hegemony! Song gave no thought to this. Instead, over trifling matters and minor faults, it paraded its troops and flaunted…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
武區區於滕之是伐焉借曰滕不降心在所必
討盍亦思事豈無大於此者歟乃動大衆以伐
之舍所重而務所輕棄所急而治所緩其與不
能三年之喪而緦小功之察者何殊邪非至不
義者莫之暇爲經於伐滕特以師稱意蓋如此
吁始而圍滕非仁也而春秋貶之繼而伐滕非
義也而春秋譏之然則後之用師者其可不本
於仁義哉抑考宋之伐喪非仁矣後日士匄侵
齊聞喪乃還其庶幾仁人之心乎宋之不能討
===
徵舒非義矣未幾楚莊入陳執而戮之其庶幾
仗義之舉乎又以見人心理義之天雖春秋之
世未盡泯而夷狄之國未嘗無也噫
季孫斯叔孫州仇仲孫何忌帥師伐邾取
漷東田及沂西田癸巳叔孫州仇仲孫何
忌及邾子盟于句繹〔哀公二年〕
葉應驄
同考試官教諭李批〔此題胡氏發明列書三卿書伐書取書盟責哀公之意殆盡作者體認失真率以〕
punctuated:
武，區區於滕之是伐焉。借曰滕不降心，在所必討，盍亦思事豈無大於此者歟？乃動大衆以伐之，舍所重而務所輕，棄所急而治所緩，其與不能三年之喪而緦小功之察者何殊邪？非至不義者莫之暇爲。經於伐滕特以師稱，意蓋如此。吁！始而圍滕，非仁也，而春秋貶之；繼而伐滕，非義也，而春秋譏之。然則後之用師者，其可不本於仁義哉？抑考宋之伐喪，非仁矣；後日士匄侵齊，聞喪乃還，其庶幾仁人之心乎？宋之不能討徵舒，非義矣；未幾楚莊入陳，執而戮之，其庶幾仗義之舉乎？又以見人心理義之天，雖春秋之世未盡泯，而夷狄之國未嘗無也。噫！

季孫斯、叔孫州仇、仲孫何忌帥師伐邾，取漷東田及沂西田。癸巳，叔孫州仇、仲孫何忌及邾子盟于句繹。〔哀公二年〕
葉應驄
同考試官教諭李批〔此題胡氏發明列書三卿、書伐、書取、書盟，責哀公之意殆盡。作者體認失真，率以〕
translation_en:
…military might, devoting its efforts merely to attacking Teng. Even supposing that Teng refused to submit and therefore had to be punished, should Song not also have considered whether there were greater matters than this? Yet it mobilized a great army to attack Teng, neglecting what was weighty to pursue what was slight, abandoning what was urgent to attend to what could wait. How did this differ from those who cannot observe the three-year mourning but scrutinize the details of the three-month and five-month mourning rites? Only the utterly unrighteous would have leisure for such conduct. This, presumably, is why the Classic specifically uses the term “army” in recording the attack on Teng.

Alas! First, besieging Teng was inhumane, and the Spring and Autumn Annals censured it; then, attacking Teng was unrighteous, and the Spring and Autumn Annals reproached it. Could those who employ armies in later ages, then, fail to ground their actions in humaneness and righteousness? Consider further: Song’s attack upon a state in mourning was inhumane. Later, when Shi Gai invaded Qi, he heard that it was in mourning and withdrew. Did this not approach the disposition of a humane man? Song’s failure to punish Zhengshu was unrighteous. Not long afterward, King Zhuang of Chu entered Chen, seized Zhengshu, and executed him. Did this not approach an act undertaken in the cause of righteousness? This also shows that the Heaven-endowed principles and righteousness in the human heart had not wholly disappeared even in the age of the Spring and Autumn Annals, nor were they ever entirely absent from the states of the Yi and Di peoples. Ah!

Jisun Si, Shusun Zhouchou, and Zhongsun Heji led an army to attack Zhu and took the lands east of the Huo River and west of the Yi River. On the guisi day, Shusun Zhouchou and Zhongsun Heji made a covenant with the Viscount of Zhu at Gouyi. 〔Second year of Duke Ai.〕

Ye Yingcong

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔On this topic, Master Hu’s elucidation of the separate listing of the three ministers and the recording of the attack, the seizure of land, and the covenant has almost fully brought out the intention to hold Duke Ai responsible. Essay writers misunderstand the true meaning and generally take…〕

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
〔責邾責三卿混之而於盟鄫子處又爲傳所窘專以季氏立說非矣此作得之是用錄出以破群惑〕
考試官教諭林批〔春秋五經斷案此作議擬切當正謂老吏不如也〕
考試官教授陳批〔書法明白較之舍經任傳者自別〕
兵興而失有所左春秋詳致其責信講而利有
所歸春秋特紀其實此我魯伐邾之役哀公獨
任其責而句繹之盟季孫不與其列也書法詳
===
略寧無意哉在昔季孫當國有事於邾一逞於
兵則叔孫仲孫之衆悉行一放於利則漷東沂
西之田是取既又以二卿要邾君即句繹以講
盟焉則是役也倡之者季孫和之者叔仲若何
而歸罪於哀公誠以有國者必攬權馭下而以
禮義自處也哀公得國公室不張假鈇鉞於三
卿掃元戎於四境伐國取地若罔聞知以臣抗
君略不能禁政柄於是乎隳哉贅旒干馬而成
矣況邾之於魯弔問方通何負於我轍未及息
punctuated:
〔責邾、責三卿混之，而於盟鄫子處，又爲傳所窘，專以季氏立說，非矣。此作得之，是用錄出，以破群惑。〕
考試官教諭林批〔《春秋》，五經斷案。此作議擬切當，正謂老吏不如也。〕
考試官教授陳批〔書法明白，較之舍經任傳者自別。〕
兵興而失有所左，《春秋》詳致其責；信講而利有所歸，《春秋》特紀其實。此我魯伐邾之役，哀公獨任其責，而句繹之盟，季孫不與其列也。書法詳略，寧無意哉？在昔季孫當國，有事於邾，一逞於兵，則叔孫、仲孫之衆悉行；一放於利，則漷東、沂西之田是取。既又以二卿要邾君，即句繹以講盟焉。則是役也，倡之者季孫，和之者叔仲，若何而歸罪於哀公？誠以有國者必攬權馭下，而以禮義自處也。哀公得國，公室不張，假鈇鉞於三卿，掃元戎於四境，伐國取地，若罔聞知；以臣抗君，略不能禁。政柄於是乎隳哉！贅旒干馬而成矣。況邾之於魯，弔問方通，何負於我？轍未及息
translation_en:
[ …confusing blame directed at Zhu with blame directed at the three ministers. At the passage concerning the covenant with the Viscount of Zeng [?], they are further constrained by the commentary and base their explanation exclusively on the Ji lineage. This is wrong. The present composition grasps the point; it has therefore been selected for inclusion to dispel these widespread misconceptions.]
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: [The Spring and Autumn Annals delivers judgment upon the Five Classics. This composition’s deliberations and proposed judgments are precisely appropriate: truly, even a seasoned judicial official could not equal it.]
Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: [Its explanation of the principles governing the Annals’ wording is clear. It plainly distinguishes itself from those who abandon the classic and rely upon its commentaries.]
When arms are raised and fault falls on a particular party, the Spring and Autumn Annals assigns responsibility in detail; when good faith is pledged and advantage accrues to a particular party, the Annals expressly records the facts. In this campaign by our state of Lu against Zhu, Duke Ai alone bears responsibility, while Jisun is not included among those listed at the covenant of Gouyi. Can the fullness and brevity of the wording be without purpose?
Formerly, when Jisun controlled the state and undertook action against Zhu, once he indulged his desire for war, the forces of both Shusun and Zhongsun all marched out; once he gave free rein to his desire for gain, the lands east of the Huo and west of the Yi were seized. He then used the two ministers to compel the ruler of Zhu to go to Gouyi and conclude a covenant. Thus, in this campaign, Jisun took the lead and Shusun and Zhongsun followed. Why, then, is the blame assigned to Duke Ai? It is because the ruler of a state must hold authority in his own hands, control his subordinates, and conduct himself according to ritual propriety and righteousness.
When Duke Ai acquired the state, the ducal house failed to assert itself. He lent the axes of punitive authority to the three ministers, who swept their war chariots across the borders, attacked another state, and seized its lands, while he acted as though he had neither heard nor known of it. Ministers defied a ruler, and he could do nothing to stop them. Thus was sovereign authority brought to ruin! He had become a mere dangling pennant, ‘gan ma’ [?]. Moreover, Zhu and Lu had only just exchanged visits of condolence: how had Zhu wronged us? The carriage wheels had not yet come to rest …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而諸卿繼伐其邦以禮爲國者若是乎我之於
邾壤域相接何釁可尋伐猶未足又取地而盟
其君以義睦鄰者若是乎噫權柄移則辱有不
免禮義失則物無以親將何以爲國哉故春秋
列書三卿書伐書取書盟所以詳其責也而三
卿之罪則不待於貶矣然伐既三卿同伐盟必
三卿同盟若何而獨書叔仲誠以盟者各盟其
所得而無得不與也伐邾之旅雖三卿並興而
取田之利實二卿獨得內貪邾地以自廣而據
===
非其有外結邾君以自安而犯非其分在得之
戒罔知抗尊之嫌奚顧若季孫則取同取也然
念公室四分輸我已半委之以補其不足矣何
嘗列名姓於載書伐同伐也然謂家難再遭賴
彼以脫歸之以償其私勞矣曷曽厠足跡於壇
坫噫同於取而不同於得與於伐而不與於盟
豈可以無别哉故春秋不書季孫而獨書叔孫
仲孫及邾子盟所以紀其實也而季孫之情亦
不容於掩矣雖然吾於叔仲二卿姑置勿論獨
punctuated:
而諸卿繼伐其邦，以禮爲國者若是乎？我之於邾，壤域相接，何釁可尋？伐猶未足，又取地而盟其君，以義睦鄰者若是乎？噫！權柄移則辱有不免，禮義失則物無以親，將何以爲國哉？故《春秋》列書三卿，書伐，書取，書盟，所以詳其責也，而三卿之罪則不待於貶矣。
然伐既三卿同伐，盟必三卿同盟，若何而獨書叔仲？誠以盟者各盟其所得，而無得不與也。伐邾之旅，雖三卿並興，而取田之利，實二卿獨得。內貪邾地以自廣，而據非其有；外結邾君以自安，而犯非其分。在得之戒罔知，抗尊之嫌奚顧？若季孫，則取同取也，然念公室四分，輸我已半，委之以補其不足矣，何嘗列名姓於載書？伐同伐也，然謂家難再遭，賴彼以脫，歸之以償其私勞矣，曷曽厠足跡於壇坫？噫！同於取而不同於得，與於伐而不與於盟，豈可以無别哉？故《春秋》不書季孫，而獨書叔孫、仲孫及邾子盟，所以紀其實也，而季孫之情亦不容於掩矣。雖然，吾於叔仲二卿姑置勿論，獨
translation_en:
…yet the ministers followed this by attacking that state. Is this how one governs a state through ritual propriety? Our territory adjoins that of Zhu: what grounds for a quarrel could there be? Not content with attacking it, they also seized territory and bound its ruler by a covenant. Is this how one maintains good relations with neighbors through righteousness? Alas! Once authority passes into other hands, humiliation becomes unavoidable; once ritual propriety and righteousness are lost, others cannot be drawn into amity. How, then, can one govern a state? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals names the three ministers in turn and records the attack, the seizure, and the covenant, setting out their responsibility in detail. Their guilt needs no further expression of censure.
Yet if all three ministers joined in the attack, surely all three would have joined in the covenant. Why, then, does the text name only Shusun and Zhongsun? In truth, those who made the covenant each did so concerning what they had acquired; whoever gained nothing did not participate. Although all three ministers raised forces for the expedition against Zhu, only two actually gained the benefit of the seized fields. At home, they coveted Zhu’s land to enlarge their own holdings, occupying what was not theirs; abroad, they allied with Zhu’s ruler to secure themselves, overstepping the bounds of their station. They knew nothing of the admonition against acquisitiveness; how could they heed the impropriety of setting themselves against a superior?
As for Jisun, he too participated in the seizure. But he reflected: “The ducal house’s resources have been divided into four portions, and half already comes to me.” He therefore relinquished the proceeds to make up the others’ shortfall. When did he ever enter his name in the covenant document? He likewise participated in the attack. But he reasoned: “My house has twice suffered calamity, and I relied on them to escape.” He therefore assigned the proceeds to them as recompense for their services to his own house. When did he ever set foot at the covenant altar? Alas! To share in the seizure but not in its gains, and to participate in the attack but not in the covenant—how could these distinctions be ignored? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals does not name Jisun, but records only that Shusun and Zhongsun made a covenant with the Viscount of Zhu, thereby recording the facts. Nor can Jisun’s motives be concealed. Nevertheless, I shall for now leave the two ministers, Shusun and Zhongsun, aside without further discussion, and only…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
惜乎意如逐君遺臭萬年昭公孫齊其鑒不遠
季斯既不能蓋前人之愆哀公亦不知鑒覆車
之轍見囚之禍適越之辱豈非自貽伊戚哉然
則後之為君臣者宜柰何亦曰我其立政立事
無有作福作威
禮記
獨樂其志不厭其道備舉其道不私其欲
是故情見而義立樂終而德尊
陳煥
===
同考試官訓導田批樂記題似易而難且作者
多在後二句欠安頓着實輒以成己成物善始善終立
破可厭此作取樂觀其深一語括之不覺意見自別且
通篇詞氣舂容殊不見有斧鑿痕是不可以
不錄也
考試官教諭林批觀子之文可以見子之
所養殆有得於樂之和者矣
考試官教授陳批樂義無出此者可隹可隹
原樂之為用也大著樂之所觀者深蓋為己為
punctuated:
惜乎！意如逐君，遺臭萬年；昭公孫齊，其鑒不遠。季斯既不能蓋前人之愆，哀公亦不知鑒覆車之轍，見囚之禍、適越之辱，豈非自貽伊戚哉？然則後之為君臣者宜柰何？亦曰：「我其立政立事，無有作福作威。」
禮記
獨樂其志，不厭其道；備舉其道，不私其欲。是故情見而義立，樂終而德尊。
陳煥
同考試官訓導田批：樂記題似易而難，且作者多在後二句欠安頓着實，輒以成己成物、善始善終立破，可厭。此作取「樂觀其深」一語括之，不覺意見自別，且通篇詞氣舂容，殊不見有斧鑿痕，是不可以不錄也。
考試官教諭林批：觀子之文，可以見子之所養，殆有得於樂之和者矣。
考試官教授陳批：樂義無出此者，可隹可隹。
原樂之為用也大，著樂之所觀者深。蓋為己為
translation_en:
…What a pity! Yiru drove out his ruler and left a name infamous for ten thousand years; Duke Zhao fled to Qi, a warning not far removed. Ji Si could not make amends for his predecessor’s wrongdoing, and Duke Ai likewise failed to heed the tracks of the overturned carriage. Were the calamity of imprisonment and the humiliation of going to Yue not sorrows he brought upon himself? What, then, should rulers and ministers of later ages do? Simply this: “Let us establish government and conduct affairs, without arrogating the power to bestow blessings or wield terror.”
Record of Rites
“He takes joy alone in his aspirations, without tiring of his Way; he fully puts his Way into practice, without keeping his desires to himself. Thus his feelings become manifest and righteousness is established; when the music ends, virtue is honored.”
Chen Huan
Comment by Associate Examiner Tian, Assistant Instructor: A topic from the Record of Music seems easy but is difficult. Moreover, writers generally fail to give the final two clauses a firm and substantive place in their treatment. They invariably frame their opening with ‘perfecting oneself and perfecting others’ or ‘beginning well and ending well’—a tiresome practice. This composition takes the single phrase ‘through music one observes what is profound’ to encompass the topic, and its interpretation emerges as distinctive without apparent effort. Furthermore, the language and cadence throughout are measured and ample, with no trace of forced workmanship. It cannot be left unrecorded.
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Reading your composition, one can discern what you have cultivated within yourself. You seem indeed to have gained something of the harmony of music.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: No exposition of the meaning of music surpasses this. Admirable, admirable! [?]
To investigate the operation of music is to see its greatness; to set forth what can be discerned through music is to reveal its profundity. For, whether acting for oneself or for…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
人非樂無以成其用之大也而德與義存焉者
又豈不於樂而可見哉古者樂舞之理蓋如此
且樂之道有所謂極幽不隱者矣舞之容有所
謂奮疾不拔者矣而脩己及人之道於是乎存
焉是故君子以之而為己則必歌咏以陶其情
性之正舞蹈以消其邪慢之非而悅懌之心優
游乎進脩之地者要所以養其和平之德也何
有於厭斁邪君子以之而為人必因其情性之
失正教之歌咏以融液之因其邪慢之未消教
===
之舞蹈以動盪之而覺悟之方周悉乎誘掖之
間者要所以溥其至公之愛也肯終於獨樂邪
夫樂之為用如此則其本之所存從可知矣故
自樂之初言之先鼓警戒三步見方雖未及乎
文采節奏之飾而欣喜歡愛之情已見情之見
者一志和行成之發越也向使百體之義有未
正則情隨事遷樂以情爭而何以見其義之立
乎以樂之終言之君子好善小人聽過要不出
乎和平公愛之間而風移俗易之化以成化之
punctuated: 人，非樂無以成，其用之大也。而德與義存焉者，又豈不於樂而可見哉？古者樂舞之理，蓋如此。且樂之道，有所謂極幽不隱者矣；舞之容，有所謂奮疾不拔者矣。而脩己及人之道，於是乎存焉。是故君子以之而為己，則必歌咏以陶其情性之正，舞蹈以消其邪慢之非，而悅懌之心優游乎進脩之地者，要所以養其和平之德也。何有於厭斁邪？君子以之而為人，必因其情性之失正，教之歌咏以融液之；因其邪慢之未消，教之舞蹈以動盪之。而覺悟之方周悉乎誘掖之間者，要所以溥其至公之愛也。肯終於獨樂邪？夫樂之為用如此，則其本之所存從可知矣。故自樂之初言之，先鼓警戒，三步見方，雖未及乎文采節奏之飾，而欣喜歡愛之情已見。情之見者，一志和行成之發越也。向使百體之義有未正，則情隨事遷，樂以情爭，而何以見其義之立乎？以樂之終言之，君子好善，小人聽過，要不出乎和平公愛之間，而風移俗易之化以成。化之
translation_en:
…others: without music, neither undertaking can be brought to completion. Such is the greatness of its operation. And since virtue and righteousness reside within it, how could they not also be discerned through music? Such, indeed, was the principle of music and dance in antiquity. Moreover, the Way of music is such that, as the saying goes, “even what is most deeply hidden does not remain concealed”; the bearing of dance is such that “vigorous and swift movement does not wrench one out of place.” Within these resides the Way of cultivating oneself and extending that cultivation to others.

Thus, when the gentleman uses music for himself, he invariably sings to nurture the rectitude of his feelings and nature, and dances to dispel the faults of perversity and arrogance. His delighted heart moves freely and at ease in the realm of advancing self-cultivation: the essential purpose is to nourish his harmonious and balanced virtue. How could there be any weariness or aversion? When the gentleman uses music for others, he teaches them to sing because their feelings and nature have lost their rectitude, thereby softening and transforming them; because their perversity and arrogance have not yet been dispelled, he teaches them to dance, thereby stirring and shaking them free. His methods of awakening their understanding are comprehensive and thorough in guiding and assisting them: the essential purpose is to extend his utterly impartial love to all. Would he be content, in the end, to enjoy music alone?

Since music operates in this way, we can accordingly understand where its foundation lies. Thus, speaking of the beginning of music, the drums first sound an admonition to attentiveness, and three steps disclose the direction of the dance. Although the embellishments of patterned display and rhythm have not yet appeared, feelings of joy, delight, affection, and love are already manifest. The manifestation of these feelings is the outward expression of unified intention, harmony, and accomplished conduct [?]. If the right ordering of the body's hundred parts had not been established, feelings would shift with circumstances, and music would contend under their influence. How, then, could the establishment of righteousness be seen?

Speaking of the conclusion of music, the gentleman comes to delight in goodness, and the common person heeds his own faults. In essence, this does not go beyond harmony, balance, impartiality, and love; through these, the transformation that changes prevailing habits and customs is accomplished. The transformation's…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
成者一反情和志之充周也向使一身之德有
未脩則以欲忘道教與民違而何以見其德之
尊乎是則成已成物之功每溢乎聲容之表而
善始善終之妙恒存乎德義之間信乎樂觀其
深矣吁是其可以偽為之哉抑求之樂舞之為
道先王所以動天地感鬼神推之政治無施不
可故足以成化善俗如古之雍熈太和所謂感
人心而天下和平要皆一德之流行無間也後
世不知出此適足以為導慾增悲之具觀之害
===
德之音祭祀弗用八佾之舞忍於僭竊者可鑒
已又何義立德尊之足云也邪
盡其道端其義而教生焉
同考試官訓導田批祭統一題塲中作者
惑於下文類多泛說殊不知此篇專為祭言下
文之意蓋謂必如此絜矩方能盡道端義固非即
指絜矩為道義也晚得此篇深合經傳且法度嚴
整宜錄以為學經者式
張瀾
punctuated:
成者，一反情和志之充周也。向使一身之德有未脩，則以欲忘道，教與民違，而何以見其德之尊乎？是則成已成物之功，每溢乎聲容之表，而善始善終之妙，恒存乎德義之間。信乎，樂觀其深矣！吁！是其可以偽為之哉？抑求之樂舞之為道，先王所以動天地、感鬼神，推之政治，無施不可，故足以成化善俗。如古之雍熈太和，所謂感人心而天下和平，要皆一德之流行無間也。後世不知出此，適足以為導慾增悲之具。觀之害德之音，祭祀弗用；八佾之舞，忍於僭竊者，可鑒已。又何義立德尊之足云也邪？

盡其道，端其義，而教生焉。

同考試官訓導田批：祭統一題，塲中作者惑於下文，類多泛說。殊不知此篇專為祭言，下文之意，蓋謂必如此絜矩，方能盡道端義，固非即指絜矩為道義也。晚得此篇，深合經傳，且法度嚴整，宜錄以為學經者式。

張瀾
translation_en:
…The completion of this transformation is entirely the full realization of returning to one’s true feelings and harmonizing one’s intent. If the virtue of one’s own person remained uncultivated, desires would cause one to forget the Way, and instruction would be at odds with the people. How, then, could the exaltation of virtue be manifest? Thus the achievement of perfecting oneself and other beings always extends beyond sounds and ceremonial movements, while the subtle capacity to begin well and end well constantly resides in virtue and righteousness. Truly, music reveals what lies deep within! Ah! Could this possibly be counterfeited? Furthermore, if we examine the Way of music and dance, these were the means by which the former kings moved Heaven and Earth and touched the spirits. Extended to government, they could be applied everywhere. Thus they sufficed to accomplish moral transformation and improve customs. The concord and supreme harmony of antiquity—what is meant by moving people’s hearts so that all under Heaven becomes peaceful and harmonious—were, in essence, the uninterrupted operation of a single virtue. Later generations did not understand how to proceed from this foundation, and music became merely an instrument for inciting desire and increasing sorrow. Consider that sounds harmful to virtue were excluded from sacrifices, and that some could bring themselves to usurp the dance in eight ranks: these offer a warning. How, then, could one even speak of establishing righteousness and exalting virtue?

“Fulfill its Way and set right its righteousness, and instruction arises from it.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Tian, Instructor: On this topic from “The System of Sacrifices” (Jitong), candidates in the examination hall were misled by the text that follows and mostly offered vague generalities. They failed to recognize that this chapter speaks specifically of sacrifice. The subsequent text means that only by thus applying the measuring square—that is, treating others by the standard one would apply to oneself—can one fulfill the Way and set right righteousness. It certainly does not identify the measuring square itself as the Way and righteousness. I came upon this essay late in the process. It accords closely with the classic and its commentary, and its composition is rigorous and orderly. It should be recorded as a model for students of the classics.

Zhang Lan.

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭林批〔以祭講盡道端義最是〕
考試官教授陳批〔合經傳旨〕
祭有以順其當然斯教之所由興也蓋祭者教
之本也然有不以順於禮而致其備焉教亦何
自而興哉祭統君子之意謂夫祭之所以成教
者豈徒本於備物之謂哉亦曰求諸道義而致
其備焉耳誠以祭必有道所以達是禮之當然
循而行之者也君子則竭誠共物務盡其道而
無所遺三牲八簋之具水草陸產之陳凡所以
===
致其備者一以是為之定制焉曽何執己見而
有所乖亂邪祭必有義所以協是禮之當然行
而宜之者也君子則因物稱情務端其義而有
所立宜少者不可多應隆者不可殺凡所以備
於物者一以是為之裁制焉曽何徇己私而有
所加損邪夫君子盡道端義如此則其祭以嚴
上自足以感人心一念之忠祭以追養自足以
觸人心一念之孝由是己以度物教之以尊其
君長則凡臣工之效職於下莫不知尊所當尊
punctuated:
考試官教諭林批〔以祭講盡道端義，最是。〕
考試官教授陳批〔合經傳旨。〕
祭有以順其當然，斯教之所由興也。蓋祭者，教之本也。然有不以順於禮而致其備焉，教亦何自而興哉？《祭統》君子之意，謂夫祭之所以成教者，豈徒本於備物之謂哉？亦曰求諸道義而致其備焉耳。誠以祭必有道，所以達是禮之當然，循而行之者也。君子則竭誠共物，務盡其道而無所遺。三牲八簋之具，水草陸產之陳，凡所以致其備者，一以是為之定制焉。曽何執己見而有所乖亂邪？祭必有義，所以協是禮之當然，行而宜之者也。君子則因物稱情，務端其義而有所立。宜少者不可多，應隆者不可殺。凡所以備於物者，一以是為之裁制焉。曽何徇己私而有所加損邪？夫君子盡道端義如此，則其祭以嚴上，自足以感人心一念之忠；祭以追養，自足以觸人心一念之孝。由是己以度物，教之以尊其君長，則凡臣工之效職於下，莫不知尊所當尊
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔Explaining “fully realizing the Way and setting righteousness aright” through sacrifice is entirely correct.〕
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: 〔Accords with the purport of the classic and its commentary.〕
Sacrifice provides a means of following what is proper, and this is how moral teaching arises. Sacrifice is indeed the root of moral teaching. Yet if its preparations are made complete without conforming to ritual propriety, how could moral teaching arise from it? The intention of the gentleman in “Principles of Sacrifice” is to say: can sacrifice’s power to accomplish moral teaching rest merely on the provision of offerings? It means only seeking completeness through the Way and righteousness. For sacrifice necessarily has its Way: that by which one apprehends what is proper to this rite and follows it in practice. The gentleman therefore exhausts his sincerity and supplies the offerings, striving to realize its Way fully, leaving nothing out. The provision of the three sacrificial animals and the eight gui vessels, the presentation of aquatic plants and the produce of the land—all the means of making the preparations complete take this alone as their fixed standard. How could he cling to his own opinions and introduce deviation or disorder?
Sacrifice necessarily has its righteousness: that by which one accords with what is proper to this rite and performs it fittingly. The gentleman therefore makes the offerings correspond to his feelings, striving to set its righteousness aright and establish a firm basis. What ought to be modest must not be made abundant; what calls for lavish treatment must not be diminished. All the material preparations are regulated solely by this standard. How could he indulge his private desires by adding or taking away?
When the gentleman thus fully realizes the Way and sets righteousness aright, his sacrifice, through reverence for superiors, is sufficient in itself to awaken an impulse of loyalty in people’s hearts; through continuing to nourish the departed, it is sufficient in itself to stir an impulse of filial devotion. From this, taking himself as a measure for others [?], he teaches them to honor their rulers and superiors. Then, among all officials performing their duties below, none fails to know that he should honor those entitled to honor…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
事君能致其身焉所謂明君在上而諸臣服從
是已天下之教不本於祭之嚴上而生乎由是
推已及人教之以孝於其親則凡子孫之克念
於家莫不知親所當親事父母能竭其力焉所
謂崇事宗廟社稷而子孫順孝是已天下之教
不本於祭之追養而生乎夫教生於祭祭主乎
順而所以順於禮者即所以順於道義也立教
君子可不知所務哉抑又驗之天下之教固必
以祭為本而行之實存乎人故下文必舉而歸
===
之絜矩之君子誠得其人則一德格天百神受
職至禮不讓而天下自治三代之隆尚矣竊惑
乎是禮不明於後世乃至有神君太乙瀆亂不
經太祫太嘗尊卑無序而圓丘方澤亦或分合
而無常是蓋不知禮為何物尚何望教之成也
噫
第貳塲
論
脩身則道立
punctuated:
事君能致其身焉。所謂「明君在上而諸臣服從」，是已。天下之教不本於祭之嚴上而生乎？由是推已及人，教之以孝於其親，則凡子孫之克念於家，莫不知親所當親，事父母能竭其力焉。所謂「崇事宗廟社稷而子孫順孝」，是已。天下之教不本於祭之追養而生乎？夫教生於祭，祭主乎順，而所以順於禮者，即所以順於道義也。立教君子可不知所務哉？抑又驗之，天下之教固必以祭為本，而行之實存乎人，故下文必舉而歸之絜矩之君子。誠得其人，則一德格天，百神受職，至禮不讓而天下自治。三代之隆尚矣！竊惑乎是禮不明於後世，乃至有神君太乙，瀆亂不經；太祫太嘗，尊卑無序；而圓丘方澤亦或分合而無常。是蓋不知禮為何物，尚何望教之成也？噫！

第貳塲

論

脩身則道立
translation_en:
…and can devote their very lives to serving their ruler. This is what is meant by: “When an enlightened ruler is above, all his ministers obey.” Does not the moral instruction of all under Heaven arise from the reverence for superiors expressed in sacrifice? From this, one extends consideration of oneself to others and teaches them filial devotion to their parents. Then all descendants who remain mindful of their duties at home know to love those whom they ought to love, and can exert their utmost strength in serving their parents. This is what is meant by: “When the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain are served with reverence, descendants are obedient and filial.” Does not the moral instruction of all under Heaven arise from the continued nurture of the departed expressed in sacrifice? Moral instruction arises from sacrifice; sacrifice centers on accord; and what accords with ritual also accords with the Way and righteousness. Can the gentleman who establishes moral instruction fail to know where to direct his efforts?

Consider this further: the moral instruction of all under Heaven must indeed take sacrifice as its foundation, but its actual practice depends on the person. Thus the following passage necessarily attributes it to the gentleman who applies the measuring square of reciprocity. If the right person is truly found, his undivided virtue reaches Heaven, the hundred spirits perform their offices, and, when the highest rites are performed without yielding them to another, all under Heaven becomes orderly of itself. How exalted was the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties! I am privately perplexed that these rites were not understood in later ages, to the point that worship of Shenjun and Taiyi became profane, disorderly, and contrary to the canonical norms; the great combined ancestral sacrifice and the great autumn sacrifice [?] lacked proper ordering of the exalted and the lowly; and sacrifices at the Round Mound and the Square Pool were sometimes separated and sometimes combined, with no constancy. This surely shows ignorance of what ritual is. How could one still hope for moral instruction to succeed? Alas!

Second Session

Discourse

“Cultivate oneself, and the Way is established.”

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
陳器
同考試官教諭何批
連日閱卷論場文字殊無
可人意者晚得此篇議論馴雅亹亹千餘言若不出於
風簷寸晷之下者可敬也
同考試官教諭戴批
論題本自平正但作者不
能體認類皆凌虛駕空率意滿紙殊為可厭晚得此卷
本㫖不失而文思清新可以式後學矣
同考試官教諭吳批
論場文字作者類千餘
言而馴雅者甚少惟此卷不離九經達道而命辭立意
===
自然出群是可録也
考試官教諭林批
初得前場固已知為佳
士及讀此論尤可以占胷中所養秋闈首選舍子其
誰歟
考試官教授陳批
論題雖平易而作者實
難措手惟此卷不為章㫖所繞而讀之灑然佳作也
治天下國家有機也有本也君子端其本
斯可以運其機而神其化矣夫天下國家
之大兆民之衆君子欲以一人之身號令
punctuated:
陳器。

同考試官教諭何批：連日閱卷，論場文字殊無可人意者。晚得此篇，議論馴雅，亹亹千餘言，若不出於風簷寸晷之下者，可敬也。

同考試官教諭戴批：論題本自平正，但作者不能體認，類皆凌虛駕空，率意滿紙，殊為可厭。晚得此卷，本㫖不失，而文思清新，可以式後學矣。

同考試官教諭吳批：論場文字，作者類千餘言，而馴雅者甚少。惟此卷不離九經達道，而命辭立意自然出群，是可録也。

考試官教諭林批：初得前場，固已知為佳士；及讀此論，尤可以占胷中所養。秋闈首選，舍子其誰歟？

考試官教授陳批：論題雖平易，而作者實難措手。惟此卷不為章㫖所繞，而讀之灑然，佳作也。

治天下國家，有機也，有本也。君子端其本，斯可以運其機而神其化矣。夫天下國家之大，兆民之衆，君子欲以一人之身號令
translation_en:
Chen Qi 陳器.

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: For several days I have been reading examination scripts, and among the discourses there have been scarcely any that pleased me. Late in the day I obtained this essay. Its argument is measured and elegant, unfolding fluently over more than a thousand words, as though it had not been composed beneath wind-swept eaves in the brief time allotted. It merits respect.

Comment by Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor: The discourse topic is itself straightforward and balanced, but the writers have failed to grasp it. Almost all soar into empty speculation, filling their pages with whatever comes to mind—most tiresome indeed. Late in the day I obtained this script. It preserves the essential purport, while its literary conception is lucid and fresh. It can serve as a model for later students.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: The discourses generally run to more than a thousand words, but very few are measured and elegant. This script alone remains grounded in the nine guiding principles of government and the universally applicable Way, while its phrasing and conception naturally surpass the rest. It deserves inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: When I first received his script from the preceding session, I already knew him to be an excellent scholar. Reading this discourse gives still greater insight into his inner cultivation. For first place in the autumn Provincial Examination, whom could we choose but you?

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: Although the discourse topic is straightforward, writers in fact find it difficult to tackle. This script alone avoids becoming entangled in the purport of the textual passage, and reading it leaves one refreshed. It is an excellent composition.

Governing the world, the state, and the family involves both a pivotal mechanism and a foundation. When the gentleman sets his foundation right, he can set that mechanism in motion and make his transforming influence wondrously effective. Given the vastness of the world, the state, and the family, and the multitude of the people, the gentleman wishes, in his own single person, to issue commands…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
指揮於其間而使之風動景從未可以強
而致也有機焉有本焉君子修其身以端
其本神其機立其表則一鼓舞振作間殆
猶風行草上無不偃仆而化行矣人徒見
其神也然不知本端於此機在於我其觀
法感化之功固已妙於不言之表而亦何
待於容力也邪孔子告哀公問政而曰脩
身道立其亦示之以本與機也請論其旨
凡天下之事循其本執其機則所務者寡
===
而可以御煩所守者近而可以及逺若逐
末遺本事事而爲之制物物而爲之防則
吾心愈勞事物愈衆日不暇給亦徒見其
勞擾而已何以明之今夫一人之身至静
也以一人而化一人至少也諄諄而告諭
之切切而戒飭之明遣而導之拜受而退
已違矣况天下國家之大民物之衆欲恃
吾聰明謹吾條章嚴吾政刑驅引之使偕
歸大道不已逺乎故夫天之生物也必敦
punctuated:
指揮於其間，而使之風動景從，未可以強而致也。有機焉，有本焉。君子修其身以端其本，神其機，立其表，則一鼓舞振作間，殆猶風行草上，無不偃仆而化行矣。人徒見其神也，然不知本端於此，機在於我，其觀法感化之功，固已妙於不言之表，而亦何待於容力也邪？孔子告哀公問政而曰：「脩身道立。」其亦示之以本與機也。請論其旨。
凡天下之事，循其本，執其機，則所務者寡而可以御煩，所守者近而可以及逺。若逐末遺本，事事而爲之制，物物而爲之防，則吾心愈勞，事物愈衆，日不暇給，亦徒見其勞擾而已。何以明之？今夫一人之身，至静也；以一人而化一人，至少也。諄諄而告諭之，切切而戒飭之，明遣而導之，拜受而退，已違矣。况天下國家之大，民物之衆，欲恃吾聰明，謹吾條章，嚴吾政刑，驅引之使偕歸大道，不已逺乎？故夫天之生物也，必敦
translation_en:
…direct affairs among them and make them respond as to the wind and follow like shadows: this cannot be achieved through coercion. There is a pivotal mechanism, and there is a root. The gentleman cultivates himself to set his root aright, gives wondrous efficacy to his pivotal mechanism, and establishes himself as an example. Then, with a single act of encouragement and inspiration, it is almost as though wind were passing over grass: none fail to bend, and his transforming influence spreads. People see only its wondrous efficacy. They do not understand that the root is set aright here, and that the pivotal mechanism lies within oneself. The effects of looking to his example and being moved and transformed by it already work wondrously beyond words. What need, then, is there to exert force? When Duke Ai asked about government, Confucius told him: “Cultivate yourself, and the Way is established.” This too showed him the root and the pivotal mechanism. Let me discuss its meaning.
In all affairs under Heaven, if one follows their root and grasps their pivotal mechanism, one can manage complexity while attending to few things, and reach far while holding fast to what is near. But if one pursues the branches and neglects the root, devising a regulation for every affair and a precaution for every thing, then the mind grows ever more weary and affairs ever more numerous. The day affords insufficient time to deal with them; all one achieves is toil and vexation. How can this be demonstrated? Consider a single individual: in himself, he is perfectly still. For one person to transform one other person is to work on the smallest possible scale. One instructs him earnestly, admonishes him insistently, and guides him with clear instructions [?]; yet, though he bows in acceptance and withdraws, he has already gone against them. How much more so with the vastness of the realm and its states and families, and the multitude of people and things! If I wish to rely on my own intelligence, make my regulations meticulous, and make my administration and punishments strict, driving and leading everyone to return together to the great Way, would this not fall far short? Thus, when Heaven brings forth living things, it must deepen…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
厚其化而後形者形色者色若物物而雕
刻之則不能矣户之啓閉也必圓轉其樞
而後左則左右則右若時時而上下之則
不能矣君子之於天下國家不端其本執
其機而亦何能神其化也邪且吾以一人
之身立乎萬民之上有所言論震若雷霆
有所作爲明並日月過言過動下之人得
於觀法視效之餘固已深入於心而不可
解矣乃爲之條章立之法制驅之而從於
===
善所令反於所好其誰聽從之邪故君子
知機在於我本在於身而身不可以不脩
也身之所主者心而内不可以不一也内既
一而衣服容儀不可以不飭也敬以自守
動由於規矩之中禮以自防務立於無過
之地凡有一言必擬之而後言惟恐過言
而招尤凡舉一事必議之而後動惟恐過
動而招悔姦聲亂色不敢留於聰明淫樂
慝禮不敢接於心術惰慢邪僻之氣不敢
punctuated: 厚其化，而後形者形，色者色；若物物而雕刻之，則不能矣。户之啓閉也，必圓轉其樞，而後左則左，右則右；若時時而上下之，則不能矣。君子之於天下國家，不端其本、執其機，而亦何能神其化也邪？且吾以一人之身立乎萬民之上，有所言論，震若雷霆；有所作爲，明並日月。過言過動，下之人得於觀法視效之餘，固已深入於心而不可解矣。乃爲之條章，立之法制，驅之而從於善，所令反於所好，其誰聽從之邪？故君子知機在於我，本在於身，而身不可以不脩也。身之所主者心，而内不可以不一也。内既一，而衣服容儀不可以不飭也。敬以自守，動由於規矩之中；禮以自防，務立於無過之地。凡有一言，必擬之而後言，惟恐過言而招尤；凡舉一事，必議之而後動，惟恐過動而招悔。姦聲亂色，不敢留於聰明；淫樂慝禮，不敢接於心術；惰慢邪僻之氣，不敢
translation_en:
…enrich its transforming power, and only then do things acquire their forms and colors. If it tried to carve and fashion each thing individually, it could not succeed. For a door to open and close, its pivot must turn smoothly; only then will it move left or right as required. If one constantly tried to move it up and down, it could not work. In dealing with all under Heaven and the state, if the gentleman does not set the root right and grasp the pivot, how can he make his transforming influence wondrously effective?

Moreover, standing alone above the myriad people, whenever I speak, my words resound like thunder; whenever I act, my deeds shine alongside the sun and moon. When I err in speech or action, those below observe and imitate me, and what they take from my example has already sunk deep into their hearts and cannot be dislodged. If I then draw up regulations for them, establish laws and institutions, and drive them toward goodness, my commands contradict my preferences: who will heed and obey them?

Thus the gentleman knows that the pivot lies in himself and the root in his own person, so he must cultivate himself. What governs his person is the heart, so his inner life must be unified. Once it is unified, his clothing, bearing, and deportment must also be put in order. He maintains himself through reverence, keeping his movements within the bounds of proper standards; he guards himself through ritual propriety, striving to occupy a position free from fault. Whenever he has something to say, he considers it before speaking, fearing that an error in speech might invite blame. Whenever he undertakes something, he deliberates before acting, fearing that an error in action might bring regret. He dares not let corrupt sounds and seductive sights linger in his hearing and vision; he dares not let licentious music and depraved rites touch his thoughts and intentions; he dares not let impulses of indolence, arrogance, perversity, and depravity…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
施於四體深宮得肆之地所以謹飭而防
閑者無異於大廷清廟之上一念萌動之
天所以省察而克治者無異於十手十目
之間好學以為知力行以為仁知恥以為
勇語父子則極其仁語君臣則極其義語
夫婦長幼朋友無不各止其極而五倫備
矣由是身修行立道成德尊以之而親師
友則賢否明以之而處家人則九族睦以
之而待小大之臣各得其情以之而治庶
===
民百工各安其分以之而御諸侯遠人各
歸其德而懷其仁出乎身而加乎民動不
離於規矩發乎邇而見乎遠舉不踰於法
度人誰不有父子舍吾何以為親人誰不
有君臣舍吾何以為義人誰不有夫婦長
幼朋友舍吾何以求其序別信焉譬之表
立於此本身而家自家而朝廷而國而天
下咸於我乎取正所謂動而世為天下道
行而世為天下法言而世為天下則者是
punctuated:
施於四體。深宮得肆之地，所以謹飭而防閑者，無異於大廷清廟之上；一念萌動之天，所以省察而克治者，無異於十手十目之間。好學以為知，力行以為仁，知恥以為勇。語父子，則極其仁；語君臣，則極其義；語夫婦、長幼、朋友，無不各止其極，而五倫備矣。
由是身修行立，道成德尊。以之而親師友，則賢否明；以之而處家人，則九族睦；以之而待小大之臣，各得其情；以之而治庶民百工，各安其分；以之而御諸侯遠人，各歸其德而懷其仁。出乎身而加乎民，動不離於規矩；發乎邇而見乎遠，舉不踰於法度。人誰不有父子？舍吾何以為親？人誰不有君臣？舍吾何以為義？人誰不有夫婦、長幼、朋友？舍吾何以求其序、別、信焉？
譬之表立於此，本身而家，自家而朝廷，而國，而天下，咸於我乎取正。所謂「動而世為天下道，行而世為天下法，言而世為天下則」者，是
translation_en:
…manifest themselves in the four limbs. In the depths of the palace, where one might act without restraint, one exercises the same vigilance and restraint as in the great court or the pure ancestral temple. At the moment a single thought first stirs, one examines and masters it just as if ten hands were pointing and ten eyes watching. Through love of learning one attains wisdom; through vigorous practice, benevolence; through knowing shame, courage. In the relationship between father and son, one brings benevolence to its utmost; in that between ruler and minister, righteousness. In the relationships between husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends, each attains its highest standard, and the five human relationships are thus fulfilled.
In this way, the person is cultivated and conduct established, the Way perfected and virtue exalted. Applying this to association with teachers and friends, one distinguishes the worthy from the unworthy; to dealings with family members, one brings harmony to the nine degrees of kinship; to the treatment of officials great and small, one responds appropriately to each one's circumstances; to governing the common people and the many artisans, one enables each to rest content in their allotted station; and to directing the feudal lords and people from afar, one causes all to turn toward one's virtue and cherish one's benevolence. What proceeds from one's person extends to the people, with no movement departing from the rules; what begins close at hand becomes manifest far away, with no action exceeding the established standards. Who does not have the relationship of father and son? Apart from my example, how would they achieve familial affection? Who does not have the relationship of ruler and minister? Apart from my example, how would they achieve righteousness? Who does not have the relationships of husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends? Apart from my example, how would they seek the proper order, distinctions, and trustworthiness in these relationships?
It is like a measuring standard erected here: beginning with one's own person and extending to the family, then from the family to the court, the state, and all under Heaven, all take their standard of rectitude from me. As the saying goes, “In his movements he becomes for generations a guide to all under Heaven; in his conduct he becomes for generations a model for all under Heaven; in his words he becomes for generations a standard for all under Heaven.” This is …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也視效之餘不言而喻感化之妙不疾而
速吾但垂衣裳於九五之尊動容貌於穆
清之上一鼓舞一轉移之間天下固已從
風而靡矣尚何假於區區刑賞法制之具
諄諄言語告誡之末乎雖以魯國微弱勉
強而力行之端其本執其機神其化固可
以柔遠人而懷諸侯孔子之論不徒託之
空言惜乎哀公知問而不知用也抑孔子
告哀公以九經而天下國家之本在身是
===
脩身一言實為九者之本而其身之所以
脩者有要焉亦曰誠而已能主於誠則知
身之當脩而求其所以脩雖曰齊明盛服
非禮不動而日用事物之微動靜食息之
末何者為禮何者非禮必辨析而講明之
則所向不差而可以無過舉矣親親也尊
賢也敬大臣也體群臣也子庶民也來百
工也柔遠人也懷諸侯也尚何舉而不當
哉是脩身為九經之本而明善又為脩身
punctuated: 也。視效之餘，不言而喻；感化之妙，不疾而速。吾但垂衣裳於九五之尊，動容貌於穆清之上，一鼓舞、一轉移之間，天下固已從風而靡矣。尚何假於區區刑賞法制之具、諄諄言語告誡之末乎？雖以魯國微弱，勉強而力行之，端其本，執其機，神其化，固可以柔遠人而懷諸侯。孔子之論，不徒託之空言，惜乎哀公知問而不知用也！抑孔子告哀公以九經，而天下國家之本在身，是脩身一言，實為九者之本。而其身之所以脩者，有要焉，亦曰誠而已。能主於誠，則知身之當脩，而求其所以脩。雖曰齊明盛服，非禮不動，而日用事物之微、動靜食息之末，何者為禮，何者非禮，必辨析而講明之，則所向不差，而可以無過舉矣。親親也，尊賢也，敬大臣也，體群臣也，子庶民也，來百工也，柔遠人也，懷諸侯也，尚何舉而不當哉？是脩身為九經之本，而明善又為脩身
translation_en:
…is what this means. Through observing and emulating, people understand without being told; through the wondrous power of moral transformation, results come swiftly without haste. I need only let my robes hang down in the exalted position of the sovereign and compose my bearing in the august purity of the court: with each act of inspiration and redirection, all under Heaven will already bend like grass before the wind. What need would there then be for such paltry instruments as punishments, rewards, laws, and regulations, or such secondary measures as repeated verbal admonitions? Even with Lu’s weakness and limited strength, if its ruler exerted himself to put this into practice, rectifying the foundation, grasping the pivotal means, and making his transforming influence wondrously effective, he could assuredly conciliate people from afar and win the allegiance of the feudal lords. Confucius’s argument was no mere empty talk. Alas, Duke Ai knew to ask but did not know to put it into practice!

Furthermore, Confucius instructed Duke Ai in the nine guiding principles, yet the foundation of governing all under Heaven, the state, and the family lies in one’s own person. Thus the single expression “cultivating oneself” is truly the foundation of all nine. There is also an essential means by which one cultivates oneself: it is simply sincerity. If one can make sincerity one’s guiding commitment, one will recognize the need to cultivate oneself and seek the means of doing so. Although it is said, “Be purified and reverent, dress properly, and make no movement contrary to ritual propriety,” one must distinguish and clearly elucidate what accords with ritual propriety and what does not, even in the minutiae of everyday affairs and the smallest details of activity and rest, eating and breathing. Then one’s course will not go astray, and one can act without error. In treating relatives with affection, honoring the worthy, respecting the great ministers, showing consideration for the body of officials, treating the common people as one’s children, attracting the various artisans, conciliating people from afar, and winning the allegiance of the feudal lords, what action could then be inappropriate? Thus cultivating oneself is the foundation of the nine guiding principles, while understanding goodness is, in turn, the foundation of cultivating oneself…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之本其要則主於一誠故曰凡爲天下國
家有九經所以行之者一也
表
擬宋起太師文彦博平章軍國重事班宰
相上謝表元祐元年
陸鈳
同考試官教諭唐批起用宿德元老是元祐
初盛事讀是表令人躍然
同考試官教諭蔡批人主重宗社之計而倚
===
毗老臣老臣念祖宗之恩而忠愛君上是作具見
此意錄之不專以其辭也
同考試官教諭郝批詞意並佳
考試官教諭林批得四六體而意勝之
可敬可敬
考試官教授陳批典麗宜錄
元祐元年四月某日臣彦博伏蒙
聖慈起臣以太師平章軍國重事班宰相上者
臣誠惶誠恐稽首頓首
punctuated:
之本，其要則主於一誠。故曰：「凡爲天下國家有九經，所以行之者一也。」

表
擬宋起太師文彦博平章軍國重事班宰相上謝表，元祐元年。
陸鈳

同考試官教諭唐批：「起用宿德元老，是元祐初盛事。讀是表，令人躍然。」
同考試官教諭蔡批：「人主重宗社之計而倚毗老臣，老臣念祖宗之恩而忠愛君上，是作具見此意。錄之不專以其辭也。」
同考試官教諭郝批：「詞意並佳。」
考試官教諭林批：「得四六體，而意勝之。可敬，可敬！」
考試官教授陳批：「典麗，宜錄。」

元祐元年四月某日，臣彦博伏蒙聖慈起臣以太師平章軍國重事、班宰相上者，臣誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。
translation_en:
…the foundation. The essential point is to be guided solely by sincerity. Thus it is said: “For governing the world, states, and families, there are nine guiding principles; that by which they are put into practice is one.”

Memorial
A model memorial of thanks in the voice of Wen Yanbo of the Song, upon being recalled as Grand Preceptor to deliberate on important military and state affairs, with precedence above the chief councilors. First year of Yuanyou [1086].
By Lu Ke.

Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor, comments: “The recall of this venerable elder of long-established virtue was a splendid event at the beginning of the Yuanyou era. Reading this memorial makes one’s spirits leap.”
Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “The sovereign, taking seriously the interests of the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain, relies upon an elderly minister; the elderly minister, mindful of the grace of the imperial ancestors, is loyal and devoted to his sovereign. This composition fully expresses these sentiments. It is selected for inclusion for more than its language alone.”
Associate Examiner Hao, Instructor, comments: “Both the language and the ideas are excellent.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “It achieves the four-and-six parallel-prose form, while its ideas surpass even its form. Admirable, admirable!”
Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “Classically elegant; it merits inclusion.”

On a certain day of the fourth month of the first year of Yuanyou, your servant Yanbo has humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious command recalling me as Grand Preceptor to deliberate on important military and state affairs, with precedence above the chief councilors. Your servant, in utmost trepidation and fear, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly knocks his forehead upon it…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
上言伏以朔輝紫極台階垂象于三師鵷
羽
玉墀風采具瞻乎百辟顧舊銜之尚在而新
寵之洊加居公孤輔弼之先任彌綸叅賛之
大幸非承乏懼益增慚蓋必有不世之賢
斯可稱非常之任故商相有待於巖築而
三公不備於周官伏念〔臣彦博〕性本迂愚才
非經濟甫登仕版旋領州麾随事以就功
名矢心而圖報稱一資一級漸叨兩府之
===
榮屢仆屢興不替
三朝之眷覩四時之有序敢戀
恩私慕二疏之見幾乞全骸骨濯纓伊洛喜
心志與俱清結社耆英訝鬚眉之盡白惟
宴閒之為幸付黜陟於不聞詎意衰殘復
蒙
甄拔茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
春秋鼎盛
punctuated: 上言：伏以朔輝紫極，台階垂象于三師；鵷羽玉墀，風采具瞻乎百辟。顧舊銜之尚在，而新寵之洊加，居公孤輔弼之先，任彌綸叅賛之大。幸非承乏，懼益增慚。蓋必有不世之賢，斯可稱非常之任。故商相有待於巖築，而三公不備於周官。伏念〔臣彦博〕性本迂愚，才非經濟。甫登仕版，旋領州麾，随事以就功名，矢心而圖報稱。一資一級，漸叨兩府之榮；屢仆屢興，不替三朝之眷。覩四時之有序，敢戀恩私？慕二疏之見幾，乞全骸骨。濯纓伊洛，喜心志與俱清；結社耆英，訝鬚眉之盡白。惟宴閒之為幸，付黜陟於不聞。詎意衰殘，復蒙甄拔。茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，春秋鼎盛，
translation_en:
… submits this memorial: I humbly observe that the radiance of the new moon illuminates the Purple Pole [?], while the stars of the Three Steps display the celestial counterparts of the Three Preceptors; phoenix feathers grace the jade steps [?], and all the officials look up to their distinguished bearing. My former title still remains, yet new favor has repeatedly been bestowed upon me. I am placed foremost among the dukes and lesser guardians who assist the sovereign, entrusted with the great responsibility of coordinating affairs and aiding Your Majesty. Though fortunate that my appointment is not merely to fill a vacancy, I feel apprehension and increasing shame. Only a worthy man rarely seen in any age can adequately discharge an extraordinary office. Thus the chief minister of Shang had to be sought among those building at the cliffs, and the Offices of Zhou did not require all three ducal posts to be filled.

I humbly reflect that 〔your servant Yanbo〕 is by nature impractical and foolish, without the talent to order the realm. Soon after entering the official registers, I was entrusted with the command of a prefecture. As circumstances arose, I sought to achieve merit and reputation, pledging my heart to render service commensurate with the favor received. Through successive grades and ranks, I gradually came to enjoy the honor of serving in the Two Administrations. Repeatedly cast down and raised up again, I never lost the favor shown me through three reigns. Seeing that the four seasons follow their proper sequence, how could I cling to personal favor? Admiring the two Shu for recognizing the moment to withdraw, I begged leave to retire with my body intact. Washing my cap strings in the Yi and Luo rivers, I rejoiced that my heart and aspirations grew clear along with their waters. Forming a fellowship of venerable worthies, I marveled that our beards and eyebrows were all white. I counted peaceful leisure alone as my good fortune and paid no heed to dismissals or promotions. How could I have imagined that, decrepit and failing, I would once again be selected for advancement?

This is surely because I have humbly had the good fortune to encounter 〇〇〇〇, in the prime of life …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
睿知夙成紹述
列聖之洪謨有因有革密邇
太皇之至訓克長克君刬新法而海宇騰歡去
儉人而仕途清軌首納元寮之薦深惟輔
德之言謂老臣寔繫天命而屬人心雖靖
恭可服四夷而尊中國濟事則日知不足
成功則歲計有餘曾無敝冕之嫌遂辱安
車之
召且
憫龍鍾之已甚更
加禮遇之過隆軍國平章細事不煩念慮
殿庭趨拜崇階特邁班行兩月始預
經筵六日一朝
斧扆禮不責全於筋骨人惟求舊於遺忘是
固
天地之洪恩而實
帝王之盛節臣敢不黾策頺齡對揚
休命譬息肩之已久而重任曷辭慨髀肉之
punctuated: 睿知夙成，紹述列聖之洪謨，有因有革；密邇太皇之至訓，克長克君。刬新法而海宇騰歡，去儉人而仕途清軌。首納元寮之薦，深惟輔德之言，謂老臣寔繫天命而屬人心，雖靖恭可服四夷而尊中國。濟事則日知不足，成功則歲計有餘。曾無敝冕之嫌，遂辱安車之召。且憫龍鍾之已甚，更加禮遇之過隆。軍國平章，細事不煩念慮；殿庭趨拜，崇階特邁班行。兩月始預經筵，六日一朝斧扆。禮不責全於筋骨，人惟求舊於遺忘。是固天地之洪恩，而實帝王之盛節。臣敢不黾策頺齡，對揚休命！譬息肩之已久，而重任曷辭；慨髀肉之
translation_en:
…Your sagely wisdom matured early. You carry forward the grand designs of the successive sage emperors, retaining some practices and reforming others; closely heeding the supreme instructions of the Grand Emperor, you are able both to lead and to rule. You abolished the New Policies, bringing rejoicing throughout the realm, and removed petty men [?], restoring integrity to official careers. You first accepted the recommendation of your chief minister and gave deep consideration to his words concerning assistance to your virtue: that this old servant truly bore upon Heaven’s Mandate and commanded the allegiance of the people; that reverent devotion could bring the peoples of the four quarters into submission and enhance the standing of the Central Kingdom. In conducting affairs, I daily recognized my shortcomings; in reckoning achievements, there was a surplus from year to year. You did not disdain me as a worn-out ceremonial cap, but graciously summoned me with a carriage in which I could ride seated.

Moreover, pitying my extreme decrepitude, you accorded me exceptionally generous ceremonial treatment. In deliberating upon military and state affairs, I was not troubled with minor matters; when proceeding to bow in the palace court, my exalted rank placed me well above the assembled officials. Only once in two months did I attend the Classics Colloquium, and once in six days I paid court before the imperial throne. In matters of ceremony, you did not demand full performance from my aging limbs; in choosing a servant, you sought an old hand despite his failing memory. This is indeed a vast kindness like that of Heaven and Earth, and truly the magnificent conduct of an emperor.

How could your servant fail to spur himself on in his declining years and gratefully uphold your gracious command! Though my shoulders have long rested from their burden, how could I decline a weighty charge? Lamenting the flesh upon my thighs…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
復生而據鞍思奮將見逼桑榆之晩皆為
効犬馬之年矙以求明快覩
太平之治前而復却尚追彙進之踪庶一言
以興邦有懷未泯假衆工而集事舊墨猶
存雖勵已之志未衰懼報
君之日已短伏願
緝煕聖學唯先正心
總攬乾綱永懷論相冀真才之必得期
大業以日隆
===
天休至而克堪周召釋二人之懼
君道成而勇退阿衡作一德之書
宗社靈長引歷年於勿替
明良終始歌
帝德以無疆臣彦博無任感
天荷
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以[]
punctuated: 復生而據鞍思奮，將見逼桑榆之晩，皆為効犬馬之年。矙以求明，快覩太平之治；前而復却，尚追彙進之踪。庶一言以興邦，有懷未泯；假衆工而集事，舊墨猶存。雖勵已之志未衰，懼報君之日已短。伏願緝煕聖學，唯先正心；總攬乾綱，永懷論相。冀真才之必得，期大業以日隆。天休至而克堪，周召釋二人之懼；君道成而勇退，阿衡作一德之書。宗社靈長，引歷年於勿替；明良終始，歌帝德以無疆。臣彦博無任感天荷聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以[]
translation_en:
…has grown back, yet, taking my place in the saddle, I long to exert myself. Thus even these declining years, approaching their sunset, shall all be years of service like that of a dog or horse. Peering in search of clarity [?], I shall joyfully behold the reign of Great Peace; advancing and then drawing back, I shall still follow the course of those who advance together. Hoping that a single utterance might bring prosperity to the realm, I have not relinquished my aspirations; relying on the many officials to accomplish affairs, I still retain the old guiding precedents. Though my resolve to exert myself has not weakened, I fear that my remaining days for repaying my sovereign are already few.
I humbly wish that, in making Your sagely learning ever more luminous, You give first priority to rectifying the mind; and that, in holding supreme authority firmly in Your grasp, You always attend to the selection of chief ministers. I hope that truly able men will assuredly be found, and that Your great enterprise will flourish day by day. When Heaven’s blessings arrive and can be worthily borne, the Dukes of Zhou and Shao will be relieved of their apprehensions; when the sovereign’s Way is perfected and his minister courageously retires, Aheng will compose the chapter “Common Possession of Pure Virtue.” May the ancestral temples and altars of state enjoy enduring divine protection, extending their years without decline; and may enlightened ruler and worthy ministers remain united from beginning to end, singing of imperial virtue without limit.
Your servant Yanbo, overwhelmed with gratitude for Heaven’s favor and the Sage’s bounty, is stirred to the utmost and filled with trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks and [?]…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
鄭蒙吉
同考試官教諭唐批初場文勢滂沛論又有
波瀾至五策洶洶湧出而
聖製一策各遡源委非有本者不能如是噫子其衆水之滄海歟
同考試官教諭蔡批我
===
朝
聖製輝煌照耀今古真與二帝三王之德業同符合轍此策能鋪陳其盛
而揚厲于數言之間其亦漸染
聖化之深者與
同考試官教諭郝批此策能鋪叙我
孝宗皇帝制作之盛而末又以正心結之蓋有志於經世非沉酣口耳
者能到
考試官教諭林批鋪張
聖訓超越前代有識之士也
punctuated:
聞。

第叁場，策，第一問。
鄭蒙吉。

同考試官教諭唐批：初場文勢滂沛，論又有波瀾，至五策，洶洶湧出，而聖製一策，各遡源委。非有本者不能如是。噫！子其衆水之滄海歟？

同考試官教諭蔡批：我朝聖製，輝煌照耀今古，真與二帝三王之德業同符合轍。此策能鋪陳其盛，而揚厲于數言之間，其亦漸染聖化之深者與？

同考試官教諭郝批：此策能鋪叙我孝宗皇帝制作之盛，而末又以正心結之。蓋有志於經世，非沉酣口耳者能到。

考試官教諭林批：鋪張聖訓，超越前代，有識之士也。
translation_en:
…for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session: Policy Essays, Question One.
Zheng Mengji.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: In the first session, his prose flowed abundantly; his discourse, too, had surging waves. When it came to the five policy essays, they poured forth in a mighty torrent. In the essay on imperial compositions, he traced each matter to its source and through its development. No one without a firm foundation could achieve this. Ah! Are you perhaps the vast ocean into which all waters flow?

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: The imperial compositions of our dynasty shine brilliantly across past and present. They truly accord with the virtue and accomplishments of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, like matching tallies and coinciding wheel tracks. This policy essay sets forth their grandeur and extols it in a few words. Surely its author, too, has been deeply imbued with the sage ruler’s transforming influence!

Comment by Associate Examiner Hao, Instructor: This policy essay sets forth the flourishing achievements of our Emperor Xiaozong in establishing institutions and regulations, and concludes with the rectification of the mind. Its author clearly aspires to ordering the world; this is beyond the reach of those absorbed in merely repeating what they have heard.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: He amply expounds the sacred teachings, which surpass those of previous dynasties. He is a scholar of discernment.

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授陳批
孝宗制作之盛前代罕比此篇能條對詳盡非素服膺者不能
聖人繼治而守文不惟有全盛之治功而尤有
大備之制作治功之全盛者見之於當時
而天下有以蒙其仁制作之大備者垂之
於後世而後世有以被其澤於乎傳稱功
業之隆悠遠以致高厚高厚又悠久者於
此足徵矣請因明問而敬陳之昔者
高皇帝之興也殪滅群兇肅清中夏
===
駿德神功與天地同其大典章文物與日月
同其明制作之盛有
祖訓
大誥
諸司職掌諸書自古創業之君所未遑也
太宗文皇帝克纘武功益隆文治又有
聖學心法
孝順事實之作
宣宗章皇帝纘承大業脩明百度又有五倫書
punctuated:
考試官敎授陳批：孝宗制作之盛，前代罕比。此篇能條對詳盡，非素服膺者不能。

聖人繼治而守文，不惟有全盛之治功，而尤有大備之制作。治功之全盛者，見之於當時，而天下有以蒙其仁；制作之大備者，垂之於後世，而後世有以被其澤。於乎！傳稱「功業之隆，悠遠以致高厚，高厚又悠久」者，於此足徵矣。請因明問而敬陳之。昔者高皇帝之興也，殪滅群兇，肅清中夏。駿德神功，與天地同其大；典章文物，與日月同其明。制作之盛，有《祖訓》、《大誥》、《諸司職掌》諸書，自古創業之君所未遑也。太宗文皇帝克纘武功，益隆文治，又有《聖學心法》、《孝順事實》之作。宣宗章皇帝纘承大業，脩明百度，又有《五倫書》
translation_en:
Examiner Chen, an Instructor, comments: “The magnificence of Xiaozong’s institutional and literary achievements has seldom been equaled in earlier dynasties. This essay answers the points in detail and exhaustively; only someone who has long taken these matters to heart could accomplish this.”

When a sage succeeds to the government and preserves its established institutions, he achieves not only consummate success in governing but also supremely comprehensive institutional and literary works. His consummate achievements in governing are manifest in his own time, enabling all under Heaven to enjoy his benevolence; his comprehensive institutional and literary works are transmitted to later generations, enabling them to receive his beneficence. Ah! The transmitted text speaks of “the grandeur of achievements, extending far and wide to attain loftiness and depth, and, with that loftiness and depth, enduring long.” Here this is amply demonstrated. Allow me respectfully to set this forth in response to your discerning question.

When Emperor Gao arose, he destroyed the hosts of villains and pacified the central realm. His great virtue and divine achievements equaled Heaven and Earth in magnitude; his statutes, institutions, and cultural accomplishments equaled the sun and moon in brilliance. Among his magnificent institutional and literary works were the Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun), the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao), and the Duties of the Various Offices (Zhusi zhizhang)—works for which founding rulers since antiquity had never found the leisure. Emperor Taizong Wen carried forward these martial achievements and further enhanced civil governance. He also produced the Essential Methods of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa) and Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi). Emperor Xuanzong Zhang inherited the great enterprise and restored and clarified all institutions; there was also the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之作凡此皆自古守成之君所難能也猗
歟休哉迨于
英宗甞有條格之作未及成書而中止之豈亦
若有待者邪我
孝宗敬皇帝以天縱之資撫盈成之運緝熈
聖學達于古今躬親萬機明燭幽隱一十八
年之間深仁厚澤洽民肌膚大化旁流無
遠弗届守成之業於是乎至而無以復加
矣所謂全盛之治功者不于是哉然自
===
國初以來百司庶務之繁凡閣文書之富日
就散漫遂
命儒臣纂集成編名曰會典逺有所取自洪
武戊申之歲近有所稽迄弘治壬戌之秋
主之以
諸司職掌類之以
頒降群書附之以歷年事例大綱槩舉而官
職制度寓焉衆目畢張而名数儀文繫焉
始於宗人府終于兩京諸衞其凡一百有
punctuated:
之作。凡此皆自古守成之君所難能也。猗歟休哉！迨于英宗，甞有條格之作，未及成書而中止之，豈亦若有待者邪？我孝宗敬皇帝以天縱之資，撫盈成之運，緝熈聖學，達于古今，躬親萬機，明燭幽隱。一十八年之間，深仁厚澤洽民肌膚，大化旁流，無遠弗届。守成之業於是乎至，而無以復加矣。所謂全盛之治功者，不于是哉？
然自國初以來，百司庶務之繁，凡閣文書之富，日就散漫，遂命儒臣纂集成編，名曰《會典》。逺有所取，自洪武戊申之歲；近有所稽，迄弘治壬戌之秋。主之以《諸司職掌》，類之以頒降群書，附之以歷年事例。大綱槩舉，而官職制度寓焉；衆目畢張，而名数儀文繫焉。始於宗人府，終于兩京諸衞，其凡一百有
translation_en:
…was composed. All these were achievements difficult even for rulers since antiquity who preserved an inherited realm. Ah, how splendid! In Yingzong’s reign, work was undertaken on a compilation of regulations, but it was halted before a book could be completed. Was this perhaps also awaiting a later ruler? Our Emperor Xiaozong Jing, endowed by Heaven, presided over an age of established prosperity. He continually cultivated and illuminated his sagely learning, comprehending past and present; he personally attended to the myriad affairs of government, his insight illuminating even what was obscure and hidden. Over eighteen years, his profound benevolence and abundant beneficence penetrated the people’s very flesh and skin. His great transforming influence spread everywhere, reaching even the most distant places. The work of preserving the inherited realm thus reached its pinnacle, beyond which nothing could be added. Was this not what is called the achievement of government at its fullest flourishing?
Yet since the dynasty’s founding, the numerous affairs of the various offices and the abundant documents of the repositories [?] had become increasingly scattered. He therefore commanded his scholarly ministers to gather and compile them into a work entitled the Collected Statutes (Huidian). Its earlier sources extended back to the wushen year of Hongwu [1368], and its more recent evidence reached down to the autumn of the renxu year of Hongzhi [1502]. It took the Duties of the Various Offices (Zhusi zhizhang) as its foundation, arranged material by category from the various officially promulgated books, and appended administrative precedents from successive years. Its principal divisions set out the broad framework, encompassing official posts and institutions; its subsidiary headings were fully laid out, incorporating prescribed designations and numbers, ceremonial forms, and formal observances. Beginning with the Court of the Imperial Clan and ending with the various Guards of the two capitals, these numbered in all one hundred and …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
七均事實以分其卷多或析之少或合之
其凡百有八十如
大明律服制有圖則仍附禮部如詹事府職
掌未載則系以春坊六部之建置沿革總
書於吏部五府之建置沿革總書于中府
朝廷之
詔勅臣下之
奏議有增革沿罷者則直書之其事繫於年
或年繫於事則指事分款而連書之自有
===
載籍以来未有是典之明且備也開局之
年為弘治丁巳至正德辛未
今上皇帝孝隆繼述乃
命儒臣校正而刋布焉天下臣工爭先快覩
信乎獲之者如拱璧藏之者為世寶也明
問又欲聞夫今日臣工誦而習之體而行
之之要生也不敏敢出位而妄言邪竊嘗
窺之矣總建六部分設諸司則六卿不可
不知率屬之義政以類分事各責成則庶
punctuated:
七。均事實以分其卷，多或析之，少或合之，其凡百有八十。如《大明律》服制有圖，則仍附禮部；如詹事府職掌未載，則系以春坊。六部之建置沿革，總書於吏部；五府之建置沿革，總書于中府。朝廷之詔勅、臣下之奏議，有增革沿罷者，則直書之。其事繫於年，或年繫於事，則指事分款而連書之。自有載籍以来，未有是典之明且備也。開局之年為弘治丁巳，至正德辛未，今上皇帝孝隆繼述，乃命儒臣校正而刋布焉。天下臣工爭先快覩，信乎獲之者如拱璧，藏之者為世寶也。
明問又欲聞夫今日臣工誦而習之、體而行之之要。生也不敏，敢出位而妄言邪？竊嘗窺之矣。總建六部，分設諸司，則六卿不可不知率屬之義；政以類分，事各責成，則庶
translation_en:
…107 in all. The material was apportioned into volumes according to its extent: larger bodies of material were sometimes divided, and smaller ones combined, making 180 volumes in all. For example, the diagrams of mourning dress in the Great Ming Code were retained under the Ministry of Rites; where the duties of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent had not been recorded, they were linked to the Spring Offices. The establishment and subsequent organizational changes of the Six Ministries were recorded together under the Ministry of Personnel; those of the Five Chief Military Commissions were recorded together under the Central Chief Military Commission. Imperial edicts and commands, and memorials and deliberations submitted by officials, were recorded directly whenever they concerned additions, reforms, continuations, or abolitions. Whether events were arranged by year or years attached to events, the material was divided into entries by subject and recorded in sequence. Since written records first existed, there has never been a compendium so clear and comprehensive as this. The compilation office was opened in the dingsi year of Hongzhi [1497]. In the xinwei year of Zhengde [1511], His Majesty the present Emperor, in his profound filial devotion to carrying forward his predecessor’s work, ordered Confucian officials to revise, correct, and publish it. Officials throughout the realm competed to be the first to enjoy reading it. Truly, those who obtain it regard it as a precious jade disk held in both hands, and those who preserve it make it a treasure for generations.
