Your discerning question also asks to hear the essential means by which officials today should recite and study it, embody its principles, and put them into practice. I, a student of limited ability, dare I step beyond my station and speak recklessly? Yet I have privately attempted to examine this matter. Since the Six Ministries are established at the central level, with their various subordinate offices separately constituted, the six ministers must understand their duty to lead their subordinates. Since government business is divided by category, and responsibility is assigned for the completion of each task, the various…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
官不可不知董正之義自粟米之征以至
竹木之税皆有其数當體之以戒侵漁自
太學之教以至庠序之育皆有其方當體
之以崇道化體禮制以一民志則十一其
綱體律意以防民奸則四百六十其條論
功以勦殺北虜為首遼東女直次之内地
反賊又次之將臣之所當體也行止語黙
必須循理務循公義以協衆情毋求細事
羅織人過憲臣之所當體也典所是吾不
===
得而違也典所因吾不得而革也典所無
吾不得而有也則吾之所執者無非
先帝之舊章矣雖然
帝王之治本之於心焉耳是典主於記事而不
及心然非心存理得又何以盡事物之變
哉故
先帝御製序文又舉純乎天理以為之訓是即
先正其心之意草茅所負之暄也願以獻
于
punctuated:
官不可不知董正之義。自粟米之征以至竹木之税，皆有其数，當體之以戒侵漁；自太學之教以至庠序之育，皆有其方，當體之以崇道化。體禮制以一民志，則十一其綱；體律意以防民奸，則四百六十其條。論功以勦殺北虜為首，遼東女直次之，内地反賊又次之，將臣之所當體也。行止語黙，必須循理，務循公義，以協衆情；毋求細事，羅織人過，憲臣之所當體也。典所是，吾不得而違也；典所因，吾不得而革也；典所無，吾不得而有也。則吾之所執者，無非先帝之舊章矣。
雖然，帝王之治，本之於心焉耳。是典主於記事而不及心，然非心存理得，又何以盡事物之變哉？故先帝御製序文，又舉純乎天理以為之訓，是即先正其心之意。草茅所負之暄也，願以獻于
translation_en:
…officials must understand their duty to supervise and rectify. From levies on grain to taxes on bamboo and timber, all have prescribed amounts; officials should put these into practice to guard against extortion. From instruction at the Imperial University to education in local schools, all have prescribed methods; officials should put these into practice to advance moral transformation through the Way. To embody the ritual institutions and thereby unite the people’s aspirations, there are eleven principal divisions; to embody the intent of the laws and thereby prevent wrongdoing among the people, there are four hundred and sixty articles. In assessing military merit, suppressing and killing the northern barbarians ranks first, the Nüzhi of Liaodong second, and rebels within the realm third. These are the provisions that military commanders should put into practice. In action and repose, speech and silence, one must follow principle, striving to uphold public justice so as to accord with the sentiments of all; one must not seize upon trifles to fabricate charges against others. These are the provisions that censorial officials should put into practice. What the Compendium affirms, I may not contravene; what it retains from precedent, I may not abolish; what it does not provide for, I may not introduce. Thus, everything I uphold is among the established regulations of the late emperor.
Nevertheless, the government of emperors and kings is founded upon the heart alone. This Compendium chiefly records affairs and does not address the heart. Yet unless the heart is preserved and principle apprehended, how can one fully comprehend the changes of affairs and things? Thus, in his personally composed preface, the late emperor also set forth purity in accordance with Heaven’s principle as an admonition. This expresses precisely the intention of first rectifying one’s heart. Such is the warmth of the sun enjoyed by this humble rustic, which I wish to offer to …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
明天子謹對
第二問
陳器
同考試官教諭何批此策作者多欠斷案是
篇文整意到如老將用兵奇正迭出而終有節制士
林巨擘也
同考試官教諭戴批有考覈有斷制如燭照
數計略無所遺傑作也宜置優選
同考試官教諭吳批五策皆佳刑賞一策尤
詳明豐贍而必以公心為主其為知本之論與高薦
何忝
考試官教諭林批斟酌刑賞合於古而宜
於今場中不多見
考試官教授陳批不惑問目卓有斷制可
知他日之猷為矣
行賞罰者當協至公之道議賞罰者當求
至一之歸夫賞罰者人主之大柄治天下
之大法也有公心以為之本則處賞罰之
punctuated:
明天子，謹對。
第二問
陳器
同考試官教諭何批：此策作者多欠斷案，是篇文整意到，如老將用兵，奇正迭出，而終有節制，士林巨擘也。
同考試官教諭戴批：有考覈，有斷制，如燭照數計，略無所遺，傑作也，宜置優選。
同考試官教諭吳批：五策皆佳，刑賞一策尤詳明豐贍，而必以公心為主，其為知本之論與！高薦何忝？
考試官教諭林批：斟酌刑賞，合於古而宜於今，場中不多見。
考試官教授陳批：不惑問目，卓有斷制，可知他日之猷為矣。
行賞罰者當協至公之道，議賞罰者當求至一之歸。夫賞罰者，人主之大柄、治天下之大法也。有公心以為之本，則處賞罰之
translation_en:
…to the enlightened Son of Heaven. I respectfully submit this reply.
Second Policy Question
Chen Qi 陳器
Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: Most who wrote on this policy question lacked a definite judgment. This essay is well ordered and fully develops its ideas. Like a veteran general deploying troops, it alternates unconventional and regular tactics, yet maintains discipline throughout. Its author is a leading figure among scholars.
Comment by Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor: It offers investigation and decisive judgments, illuminating matters as clearly as a candle and accounting for them as precisely as a tally, leaving virtually nothing out. A masterly work, deserving placement among the superior selections.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: All five policy essays are excellent. The essay on punishments and rewards is especially detailed, clear, and ample, and consistently makes impartiality its guiding principle. Surely this is an argument that understands the fundamentals! How could a high recommendation be undeserved?
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Its weighing of punishments and rewards accords with antiquity and suits the present. Such work is seldom seen in the examination hall.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: Unconfused by the question’s wording, the author displays outstanding powers of judgment. From this one can discern his future plans and accomplishments.
Those who administer rewards and punishments should accord with the way of utmost impartiality; those who discuss rewards and punishments should seek a fully unified conclusion. Rewards and punishments are the ruler’s great instruments of authority and the great means of governing all under Heaven. With an impartial mind as their foundation, then, in handling matters of rewards and punishments…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
事而無不當論賞罰之說而無不定矣然
則法固為治之所當有而本尤爲治之不
可缺也歟請略陳之惟辟作福五服五彰
爵賞所以待有功也不及則吝吝固不可
然太過而僭則名器輕輕則人心賤如昔
之所謂車載斗量者得之非榮矣復何所
勸乎惟辟作威五刑五用刑罰所以待有
罪也不及則縱縱固不可然太過而濫則
刑政紊紊則人心駭如昔之所謂重足側
===
目者無所趨避矣亦何所懲乎故夫求郎
之請爲公主若可以曲從也而懼其殃民
則漢明帝不之許秦邸宮僚念舊人若可
以超遷也而害於至公則唐太宗不之許
至宋藝祖於曹彬與之以緡錢靳之以使
相以太原之未平耳之三君者謂之公可
也謂之吝不可也視刓印弗與者大有逕
庭肉刑之用舊矣而文帝始除之蓋感緹
縈之請也笞箠之令足矣而景帝復定之
punctuated: 事而無不當，論賞罰之說而無不定矣。然則法固為治之所當有，而本尤爲治之不可缺也歟？請略陳之。惟辟作福，五服五彰，爵賞所以待有功也。不及則吝，吝固不可；然太過而僭，則名器輕，輕則人心賤。如昔之所謂車載斗量者，得之非榮矣，復何所勸乎？惟辟作威，五刑五用，刑罰所以待有罪也。不及則縱，縱固不可；然太過而濫，則刑政紊，紊則人心駭。如昔之所謂重足側目者，無所趨避矣，亦何所懲乎？故夫求郎之請，爲公主，若可以曲從也，而懼其殃民，則漢明帝不之許。秦邸宮僚，念舊人，若可以超遷也，而害於至公，則唐太宗不之許。至宋藝祖於曹彬，與之以緡錢，靳之以使相，以太原之未平耳。之三君者，謂之公可也，謂之吝不可也。視刓印弗與者，大有逕庭。肉刑之用舊矣，而文帝始除之，蓋感緹縈之請也。笞箠之令足矣，而景帝復定之。
translation_en:
…the administration of rewards and punishments will invariably be appropriate, and discussion of their principles will invariably reach a settled conclusion. Thus, although laws are certainly necessary for government, is not its foundation still more indispensable? Allow me to explain briefly. “Only the sovereign confers blessings”; “the five kinds of ceremonial dress distinguish the five ranks.” Ranks and rewards are the means of treating those who have rendered meritorious service. To give too little is to be grudging, and that is certainly unacceptable. Yet excessive grants that overstep proper distinctions cheapen titles and insignia; once cheapened, they are held in contempt. When, as people once said, their recipients can be “carted by the wagonload and measured by the peck,” receiving them brings no honor. What incentive can they then provide? “Only the sovereign exercises punitive authority”; “the five punishments each have their application.” Punishments are the means of treating the guilty. To impose too little is to indulge them, and that is certainly unacceptable. Yet excessive and indiscriminate punishment throws penal administration into disorder, and disorder terrifies people. When, as people once said, they “stand with feet pressed together and look sideways,” they have no way to turn or escape. How can punishment then deter wrongdoing?

Thus, a princess’s request for an appointment as a Gentleman might seem to warrant special accommodation, but Emperor Ming of Han refused it, fearing that it would bring harm to the people. The officials of the Prince of Qin’s establishment might seem to merit exceptional promotion out of regard for their former service, but Emperor Taizong of Tang refused, since this would compromise complete impartiality. As for the founding emperor of Song, he gave Cao Bin strings of cash but withheld the title of Military Commissioner with Chancellor designation, solely because Taiyuan had not yet been pacified. These three rulers may be called impartial; they cannot be called grudging. They differed greatly from one who wore down the edges of a seal through handling yet would not bestow it.

Mutilating punishments had long been employed when Emperor Wen first abolished them, moved by Tiying’s petition. The regulations governing flogging were already sufficient, yet Emperor Jing revised them further…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
蓋懼殘民之生也至於太宗之禁鞭背則
因鍼灸之書知五臟之附不得而不禁之
耳之數事者謂之公可也謂之縱不可也
與涕泣死刑者大相遼邈酌古之道定今
之宜賞不必予之太驟也奪之太速也賞
一人而當其功則人皆以為慶孰不敏於
為善刑不必加之太重也赦之太数也罰
一人而當其罪則人皆以為威孰不勇於
去惡且刑賞之說古人論之詳矣蔡聲子
===
===
曰善為國者賞不僭而刑不濫固矣而文
王之世禄所以重世功周官之重典所以
懲亂國其為不僭不濫均焉周人有言曰
為政者不賞私勞不罰私怨固矣而孔門
報怨以直者非矯情報德以德者非朋比
其與無私之意同焉有功不賞有罪不誅
雖唐虞不能以化天下宣帝有是言也示
人以治道之常耳不賞而民勸不怒而民
威中庸有是言也所以著誠敬之效不待
punctuated: 蓋懼殘民之生也。至於太宗之禁鞭背，則因鍼灸之書，知五臟之附，不得而不禁之耳。之數事者，謂之公可也，謂之縱不可也，與涕泣死刑者大相遼邈。酌古之道，定今之宜，賞不必予之太驟也，奪之太速也。賞一人而當其功，則人皆以為慶，孰不敏於為善？刑不必加之太重也，赦之太数也。罰一人而當其罪，則人皆以為威，孰不勇於去惡？且刑賞之說，古人論之詳矣。蔡聲子曰：「善為國者，賞不僭而刑不濫。」固矣。而文王之世禄，所以重世功；周官之重典，所以懲亂國，其為不僭不濫均焉。周人有言曰：「為政者，不賞私勞，不罰私怨。」固矣。而孔門報怨以直者非矯情，報德以德者非朋比，其與無私之意同焉。「有功不賞，有罪不誅，雖唐虞不能以化天下。」宣帝有是言也，示人以治道之常耳。「不賞而民勸，不怒而民威。」中庸有是言也，所以著誠敬之效，不待
translation_en:
…because he feared destroying his people's lives. As for Taizong's prohibition of flogging the back, a book on acupuncture and moxibustion taught him how the five internal organs were connected to it, leaving him no choice but to prohibit the practice. These several acts may be called impartial, but cannot be called lax. They differ vastly from shedding tears over capital punishment.

Weigh the methods of antiquity to determine what is appropriate today. Rewards need not be conferred too hastily or withdrawn too quickly. If one person is rewarded in accordance with his merit, everyone regards it as cause for rejoicing: who would not be eager to do good? Punishments need not be imposed too severely, nor pardons granted too frequently. If one person is punished in accordance with his crime, everyone regards it with awe: who would not be resolute in abandoning evil?

Moreover, the ancients discussed punishments and rewards in detail. Cai Shengzi said, “Those skilled at governing a state do not confer undeserved rewards or impose excessive punishments.” This is certainly so. Yet King Wen's hereditary emoluments served to honor merit sustained across generations, while the severe statutes in the Offices of Zhou served to chastise disordered states. These equally exemplify rewards that are not undeserved and punishments that are not excessive. The people of Zhou had a saying: “Those who govern do not reward services rendered to them privately or punish private grievances.” This is certainly so. Yet in the school of Confucius, repaying resentment with uprightness was no distortion of one's feelings, and repaying kindness with kindness was no partisan collusion. These accord with the same principle of impartiality.

“If merit goes unrewarded and crime unpunished, even the rulers of Tang and Yu could not transform the world.” Emperor Xuandi said this merely to show people the constant principles of government. “Without rewards, the people are encouraged; without anger, the people stand in awe.” The Doctrine of the Mean says this to reveal the efficacy of sincerity and reverence, without waiting for…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有言而人自化不待有為而人自服一則
以明其用一則以循其本體用相資何背
馳乎有功則賞有罪則刑誰敢不竭心盡
力以脩職業此太宗通論馭臣之道耳宋
臣蘇軾復有所謂無功之爵無罪之罰者
則言六德六行之賢偽言偽行之士先王
不待其功之顯而後爵之不待其罪之顯
而後罰之一則語其顯一則闡其微顯微
一道何抵捂乎由是觀之人君惟患其賞
===
之不公不患於人之不勸惟患其罰之不
公不患於人之不懲至于所以求其公者
又必黽勉於學問之間戒慎於理欲之際
在己之喜怒不妄在人之邪正莫逃然後
大道之公在我執此以應天下之變以盡
萬物之情將無所施而不當而况於刑賞
間邪鄙見如是不識執事以為何如
第三問 葉應驄
punctuated:
有言而人自化，不待有為而人自服。一則以明其用，一則以循其本，體用相資，何背馳乎？有功則賞，有罪則刑，誰敢不竭心盡力以脩職業？此太宗通論馭臣之道耳。宋臣蘇軾復有所謂無功之爵、無罪之罰者，則言六德六行之賢、偽言偽行之士。先王不待其功之顯而後爵之，不待其罪之顯而後罰之。一則語其顯，一則闡其微，顯微一道，何抵捂乎？由是觀之，人君惟患其賞之不公，不患於人之不勸；惟患其罰之不公，不患於人之不懲。至于所以求其公者，又必黽勉於學問之間，戒慎於理欲之際。在己之喜怒不妄，在人之邪正莫逃，然後大道之公在我。執此以應天下之變，以盡萬物之情，將無所施而不當，而况於刑賞間邪？鄙見如是，不識執事以為何如？

第三問，葉應驄。
translation_en:
…for words to be spoken before people transform themselves, nor for action to be taken before people submit of their own accord. One statement clarifies the practical operation; the other traces the underlying foundation. Substance and function sustain each other: how could they run counter to one another? “Reward those who have merit and punish those who have committed offenses: who would dare not devote all his heart and strength to fulfilling his official duties?” This is simply Taizong’s general account of the way to govern ministers. The Song minister Su Shi also spoke of “conferring rank without merit and imposing punishment without an offense.” He was referring to worthy men possessing the six virtues and six forms of exemplary conduct, and to men whose words and deeds were false. The former kings did not wait until the worthy men’s achievements became manifest before conferring rank upon them, nor until the others’ offenses became manifest before punishing them. One statement addresses what is manifest; the other elucidates what is subtle. The manifest and the subtle belong to a single Way: how could they conflict?

Viewed in this light, a ruler need only worry that his rewards are unfair, not that people will fail to be encouraged; he need only worry that his punishments are unfair, not that people will fail to be deterred. As for how to attain such fairness, he must also exert himself diligently in learning and remain vigilant at the boundary between moral principle and selfish desire. His own pleasure and anger must not be arbitrary, and the wickedness or uprightness of others must not escape his discernment. Only then will the impartiality of the great Way reside in him. Holding to this in responding to the changes of the world and fully comprehending the true circumstances of all things, he will act appropriately in every application—how much more so in matters of punishment and reward! Such is my humble view. I do not know what you, honored examiners, will think of it.

Third policy question. Ye Yingcong.

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭李批教化風俗作者類能言
之然不過就題掇補故實成文獨此乃能吐出胸中許多
竒氣議論有餘所謂士人美節子殆素養者矣
考試官教諭林批詞氣精彩波瀾浩瀚
自是不凡錄之以示式也
考試官教授陳批子平居抱負充足有
意於教化風俗於此可覘
善言天下之治者無貴乎遠有所慕亦無
貴乎近有所遺夫古今天下之心一也民
===
以是善亦以是偷治以是隆亦以是替是
必有教化風俗為之機焉以轉移于其間
者矣然則所以張主而維持之者亦何容
心於遠者之足慕而近者之可遺也哉羅
氏曰教化者朝廷之先務廉耻者士人之
美節風俗者天下之大事至哉言矣愚請
得而大其說焉以為今日明問復人之言
曰觀化在朝觀俗在野又曰慕古者焉不
便於今好今者必無意於古愚則曰天下
punctuated:
同考試官教諭李批：教化風俗，作者類能言之，然不過就題掇補故實成文。獨此乃能吐出胸中許多竒氣，議論有餘。所謂士人美節，子殆素養者矣。
考試官教諭林批：詞氣精彩，波瀾浩瀚，自是不凡，錄之以示式也。
考試官教授陳批：子平居抱負充足，有意於教化風俗，於此可覘。
善言天下之治者，無貴乎遠有所慕，亦無貴乎近有所遺。夫古今天下之心一也，民以是善，亦以是偷；治以是隆，亦以是替。是必有教化風俗為之機焉，以轉移于其間者矣。然則所以張主而維持之者，亦何容心於遠者之足慕，而近者之可遺也哉？羅氏曰：「教化者，朝廷之先務；廉耻者，士人之美節；風俗者，天下之大事。」至哉言矣！愚請得而大其說焉，以為今日明問復。人之言曰：「觀化在朝，觀俗在野。」又曰：「慕古者焉不便於今，好今者必無意於古。」愚則曰：「天下
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Writers can generally discuss moral instruction and customs, but they do no more than gather and piece together historical precedents to compose an essay on the topic. This writer alone pours forth the extraordinary spirit within his breast, with arguments in abundance. As for what is called the fine integrity of scholars, you have surely cultivated it long before now.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The language and spirit are brilliant, its waves vast and surging. It is unquestionably exceptional; we have included it to serve as a model.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: Your habitual aspirations are substantial, and you are concerned with moral instruction and customs: this essay allows us to glimpse these qualities.

Those who speak well about governing All-under-Heaven do not prize admiration for the distant past, nor do they prize neglect of what is close at hand. For the hearts of people throughout the world are the same in antiquity and today. Through this, the people become good, but also become lax; government flourishes, but also declines. Moral instruction and customs must constitute the pivotal force that brings about these shifts. How, then, could those charged with promoting and sustaining them entertain the thought that the distant past deserves admiration while the present may be neglected? Master Luo said: “Moral instruction is the foremost task of the court; integrity and a sense of shame are the fine virtues of scholars; customs are a great concern of All-under-Heaven.” How consummate these words are! I venture to expand upon his statement in reply to your discerning question today. It has been said: “To observe moral transformation, look to the court; to observe customs, look among the people.” It has also been said: “How could those who admire antiquity fail to suit the present [?]? Those who favor the present must have no interest in antiquity.” I, however, say: “All-under-Heaven …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之心一也舉放勳之憂勤泯於知識之地
則可以合朝野之歡以漢武之多慾假諸
仁義之途祗見其有古今之異耳蓋嘗徵
之於古求其可宜於今者而粗有得焉教
化本於朝廷而責任於守令執事之論公
矣然今之為守令者果能脫去因循苟免
之陋習嚴急集事之苛聲可續班范二史
所傳循良者乎信有之愚不可得而盡知
也風俗移于好尚而振作于士人執事之
===
憂切矣然今之為士人者果能涵養平居
廉靜之節君子長者之心可無愧於古之
嘉言善行者乎信有之愚亦不可得而盡
知也不可得而盡知則凡所以扶植教化
于上陶成風俗于下其責將安歸邪抑求
之遠而易忽近而易玩者邪夫亦曰驗之
古今人心而已矣古者力行教化若文翁
之守蜀郡若黃霸之守潁川一時光後相
望具載班史者六人至于今猶能使人動
punctuated: 之心一也。舉放勳之憂勤，泯於知識之地，則可以合朝野之歡；以漢武之多慾，假諸仁義之途，祗見其有古今之異耳。蓋嘗徵之於古，求其可宜於今者，而粗有得焉。教化本於朝廷，而責任於守令，執事之論公矣。然今之為守令者，果能脫去因循苟免之陋習、嚴急集事之苛聲，可續班范二史所傳循良者乎？信有之，愚不可得而盡知也。風俗移于好尚，而振作于士人，執事之憂切矣。然今之為士人者，果能涵養平居廉靜之節、君子長者之心，可無愧於古之嘉言善行者乎？信有之，愚亦不可得而盡知也。不可得而盡知，則凡所以扶植教化于上、陶成風俗于下，其責將安歸邪？抑求之遠而易忽、近而易玩者邪？夫亦曰驗之古今人心而已矣。古者力行教化，若文翁之守蜀郡，若黃霸之守潁川，一時光後相望，具載班史者六人，至于今猶能使人動
translation_en:
…the hearts of all under Heaven are one. If the anxious diligence of Fangxun [the sage ruler Yao] is brought to bear and effaced from conscious awareness [?], it can unite court and countryside in joy; if Emperor Wu of Han’s many desires are cloaked in benevolence and righteousness, one sees only a disparity between antiquity and the present. I have examined antiquity, seeking what might suit the present, and have gained a rough understanding.

Moral instruction has its foundation at court, while responsibility for it rests with prefects and county magistrates: your judgment on this is impartial. Yet can those serving as prefects and county magistrates today truly cast off the bad habits of merely following precedent and seeking to escape blame, and the reputation for harshness incurred by pressing urgently to get things done? Can they carry on the tradition of the exemplary, benevolent officials whose biographies appear in the two histories by Ban Gu and Fan Ye? Surely there are such men, but I cannot know them all.

Customs shift with prevailing preferences, and their renewal depends upon scholars: your concern is deeply felt. Yet can today’s scholars truly cultivate, in their everyday lives, integrity and quiet restraint, and the disposition of gentlemen and venerable elders, so as to stand without shame beside the fine words and good deeds of the ancients? Surely there are such men, but again I cannot know them all. If they cannot all be known, where, then, should responsibility lie for sustaining moral instruction above and molding customs below? Or should we seek it in what is distant and easily overlooked, or near at hand and easily treated lightly? We need only test it against human hearts, past and present.

In antiquity, those who vigorously practiced moral instruction included Wen Weng as governor of Shu Commandery and Huang Ba as governor of Yingchuan. Six such men, succeeding one another and bringing lustre to later ages [?], are fully recorded in Ban Gu’s History of the Han. Even today they can still cause people, whenever they act …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
必稽之以為美談興行禮讓若衞颯任延
若秦彭劉矩當時同為范史所傳者十有
二人要皆勞來躬行使民異地而同化故
說者謂三代而下惟兩漢風化近厚今也
守令之選簡自天曹而授之以政凡所以
承宣教化豈不以古之人望之也然而每
病於奉行之未至者無乃文程束約之過
嚴使豪傑不得得其志乎否則陋習苛聲
之咎將何以自釋也古者善行著稱如劉
===
文饒之宏度龐德公之高致范希文之不
私其家司馬君實之恬退自娛而京兆小
民猶能却歸亡父之金是皆高風靖節百
世而下凛乎猶可想見者嘉言可述如羅
仲素論舜之孝蘇瓊息普明兄弟之爭古
語所謂善終乎夫婦朋友之道禮曰不非
其大夫以全上下之交而卓茂又有律設
大法禮順人情以為通變之說是皆微言
正論藹然有益於世教可舉而行之者故
punctuated:
必稽之，以為美談。興行禮讓，若衞颯、任延，若秦彭、劉矩，當時同為范史所傳者十有二人，要皆勞來躬行，使民異地而同化。故說者謂三代而下，惟兩漢風化近厚。今也守令之選，簡自天曹而授之以政，凡所以承宣教化，豈不以古之人望之也？然而每病於奉行之未至者，無乃文程束約之過嚴，使豪傑不得得其志乎？否則陋習苛聲之咎，將何以自釋也？
古者善行著稱，如劉文饒之宏度、龐德公之高致、范希文之不私其家、司馬君實之恬退自娛，而京兆小民猶能却歸亡父之金，是皆高風靖節，百世而下，凛乎猶可想見者。嘉言可述，如羅仲素論舜之孝、蘇瓊息普明兄弟之爭，古語所謂善終乎夫婦朋友之道，《禮》曰「不非其大夫」，以全上下之交，而卓茂又有「律設大法，禮順人情」以為通變之說，是皆微言正論，藹然有益於世教，可舉而行之者。故
translation_en:
… invariably consult these accounts and recount them as admirable tales. As for promoting ritual propriety and deference, there were Wei Sa and Ren Yan, Qin Peng and Liu Ju: twelve men of that period whose biographies were all recorded in Fan Ye’s History of the Later Han. In essence, they all comforted and encouraged the people and personally practiced what they taught, bringing people in different places under the same transforming influence. Thus commentators say that, after the Three Dynasties, only under the Former and Later Han did moral influence and customs approach true generosity. Today, prefects and magistrates are selected by the celestial ministry and entrusted with government. In all that concerns receiving and disseminating moral instruction, are they not expected to measure up to the men of antiquity? Yet we repeatedly find their implementation wanting. Might the constraints imposed by documentary requirements be so strict that outstanding men cannot fulfill their ambitions [?]? Otherwise, how will they absolve themselves of blame for debased practices and a reputation for harshness?
Among the ancients renowned for good conduct were Liu Wenrao, with his magnanimity; Pang Degong, with his lofty aspirations; Fan Xiwen, who did not favor his own household; and Sima Junshi, who found contentment in tranquil retirement. Even an ordinary person of Jingzhao could refuse and return gold left by a deceased father [?]. These were all examples of lofty character and steadfast integrity: a hundred generations later, we can still picture them with awe. Among admirable sayings worth recounting are Luo Zhongsu’s discussion of Shun’s filial piety and Su Qiong’s words that ended the dispute between Puming and his brothers. There is also the ancient saying about bringing to a good conclusion the proper relations between husband and wife and between friends. The Book of Rites says, “Do not speak ill of one’s great officer,” thereby preserving the relationship between superior and subordinate. Zhuo Mao also offered the statement, “Statutes establish broad rules; ritual accords with human feelings,” as an explanation of adapting to changing circumstances. These are all subtle sayings and sound judgments, richly beneficial to the moral instruction of the age, which can be adopted and put into practice. Thus …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
說者謂古今風俗惟有道君子可以維持
之今也士人之節出自天性而養之以善
凡所以激勵風化孰不以古之人期之也
然而每患於積習之相移者無乃群排聚
笑之弗容使頓失其初心乎否則飭躬勵行
之戒亦可以自治也若之何而可逃其責
哉矧夫天下之大以一人而領萬化不見
其不足以兆民而懷一人不見其有餘方
今天下之教化天下之風俗亦匪必人人
===
而面命之事事而拘持之也責之守令使
各以古人之心爲心則循良傳不可以不
讀也他日紹前脩而輝史筆者將非今之
賢守令而誰歸飭之士人使各以古人之
言行爲法則座右銘不可一日無也他日
追往哲而風後世者將非今之賢士大夫
而誰歸若是而曰教化之不可行風俗之
不可厚吾不之信也雖然成天下之化者
守令士人也所以運天下之化者吾
punctuated: 說者謂古今風俗，惟有道君子可以維持之。今也，士人之節出自天性，而養之以善，凡所以激勵風化，孰不以古之人期之也？然而每患於積習之相移者，無乃群排聚笑之弗容，使頓失其初心乎？否則，飭躬勵行之戒，亦可以自治也。若之何而可逃其責哉？矧夫天下之大，以一人而領萬化，不見其不足；以兆民而懷一人，不見其有餘。方今天下之教化、天下之風俗，亦匪必人人而面命之，事事而拘持之也。責之守令，使各以古人之心爲心，則《循良傳》不可以不讀也。他日紹前脩而輝史筆者，將非今之賢守令而誰歸？飭之士人，使各以古人之言行爲法，則座右銘不可一日無也。他日追往哲而風後世者，將非今之賢士大夫而誰歸？若是而曰教化之不可行，風俗之不可厚，吾不之信也。雖然，成天下之化者，守令士人也；所以運天下之化者，吾
translation_en:
…commentators say that, in antiquity and today, only gentlemen who possess the Way can sustain proper customs. Now, the integrity of scholars springs from their innate nature and is nurtured through goodness. In all efforts to encourage moral transformation, who does not expect them to measure up to the ancients? Yet there is constant concern that ingrained habits will lead them astray. Might this be because collective rejection and ridicule leave them no place, causing them suddenly to lose their original resolve? Otherwise, the admonition to discipline oneself and strive for upright conduct should also enable them to govern themselves. How, then, can they evade their responsibility?
Moreover, vast though the realm is, one man directs its myriad transformations without proving inadequate; the multitudes cherish that one man without their numbers proving excessive. In bringing moral instruction to the realm and shaping its customs today, it is surely unnecessary to instruct every person face to face or to regulate every affair. Entrust this responsibility to prefects and county magistrates, requiring each to take the minds of the ancients as his own: then the Biographies of Benevolent Officials must be read. In days to come, who will carry on the achievements of earlier worthies and lend lustre to the historical record, if not today’s worthy prefects and county magistrates? Admonish scholars, requiring each to take the words and deeds of the ancients as his model: then they must not go a single day without an admonitory inscription beside their seats. In days to come, who will emulate past sages and influence later generations, if not today’s worthy scholar-officials? If, with this accomplished, anyone says that moral instruction cannot be put into practice or customs made upright, I do not believe it.
Nevertheless, those who bring the realm’s moral transformation to fruition are prefects, county magistrates, and scholars; those who set that transformation in motion are our…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
君與吾相也運之以仁民亦從而仁之運之
以非仁則亦唯恐其從矣其成與否何足
計哉噫此所以禮義之風廉恥之俗每必
於人心去惡從善之機而轉移之誠使士
人賢矣守令賢矣天下之人心得以大其
善而小其惡矣夫然後反而求之敎化本
原之地爲之勸懲黜陟之典行焉此則機
之謂也亦所以守天下之化者也愚不敏
他又何足以知之
===
第四問
陳煥
同考試官訓導田批秋闈策士以節義正欲觀
其所養何如此卷於前人行事之槩條答無遺可以占平居
之志向矣他日效用其所建立必有可觀者
考試官敎諭林批節義雖非士君子全節
然亦兩間正氣扶植世敎所不可少者此卷條對詳明
且能知所宗尚可佳也
考試官敎授陳批此卷隨問而對宛然不
punctuated:
君與吾相也。運之以仁，民亦從而仁之；運之以非仁，則亦唯恐其從矣。其成與否，何足計哉！噫！此所以禮義之風、廉恥之俗，每必於人心去惡從善之機而轉移之。誠使士人賢矣，守令賢矣，天下之人心得以大其善而小其惡矣。夫然後反而求之敎化本原之地，爲之勸懲黜陟之典行焉。此則機之謂也，亦所以守天下之化者也。愚不敏，他又何足以知之？

第四問
陳煥

同考試官訓導田批：秋闈策士以節義，正欲觀其所養何如。此卷於前人行事之槩，條答無遺，可以占平居之志向矣。他日效用，其所建立必有可觀者。

考試官敎諭林批：節義雖非士君子全節，然亦兩間正氣，扶植世敎所不可少者。此卷條對詳明，且能知所宗尚，可佳也。

考試官敎授陳批：此卷隨問而對，宛然不
translation_en:
…our sovereign and our chief councilor. If they direct moral transformation through benevolence, the people too will follow them in being benevolent; if they direct it through what is not benevolent, one can only fear that the people will follow them. What point would there then be in reckoning whether that transformation succeeds? Alas! This is why the prevalence of ritual propriety and righteousness, and customs of integrity and shame, must always be redirected at the crucial point when people’s hearts turn away from evil toward goodness. If the scholars truly become worthy, and the prefects and magistrates become worthy, the hearts of all under Heaven will be able to enlarge their goodness and diminish their evil. Only then should one turn back to seek the source of moral instruction and put into practice the established measures for encouragement and punishment, dismissal and promotion. This is what is meant by the crucial point; it is also the means of preserving moral transformation throughout the realm. I am slow of understanding: what more could I presume to know of this?

Fourth Policy Question
Chen Huan

Comment by Associate Examiner Tian, Assistant Instructor: In the autumn Provincial Examination, we question candidates on integrity and righteousness precisely to see what they have cultivated within themselves. This paper answers point by point, omitting none of the broad outlines of the deeds of earlier men. From it we can discern the aspirations the candidate maintains in his daily life. When he enters service in the future, his achievements will surely merit attention.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Although integrity and righteousness do not constitute the whole of a gentleman’s moral character, they are nevertheless manifestations of the upright vital force between Heaven and Earth, indispensable to sustaining moral instruction in society. This paper’s answers are detailed and clear, and the candidate also understands what he should honor and emulate. It is commendable.

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
窘參之前二場皆稱本房之冠固無以易子矣
對崇節義者君子之美名稽名實者後儒
之公論蓋有節義之名不若循其實若併
與其實而亡之不若猶宗其名之為愈也
此後儒之責實者有取於西京史氏之憫
時者獎進乎東漢而不及唐宋吾士君子
立身行己之間又安得不擇取於是哉請
因明問而陳之三代而上聖學大明公論
素著士君子生於其時幼而學壯而仕行
===
其所無事而已降自秦漢人心放失聖學
湮微輿論不主於廟堂而縉紳草茅或執
其柄於是乎始有節義之名者矣且以兩
漢言之高祖除秦之暴約法三章史氏稱
其尚寬大是也若光武當士夫頽鈍之後
而大興振作之功召嚴光褒卓茂論文講
道崇尚儒學而東都一代之士風已倡起
於斯時矣於是陳蕃竇武之徒繼世而起
高名大節與日月而爭光危言峻行雖死
punctuated:
窘，參之前二場，皆稱本房之冠，固無以易子矣。

對：崇節義者，君子之美名；稽名實者，後儒之公論。蓋有節義之名，不若循其實；若併與其實而亡之，不若猶宗其名之為愈也。此後儒之責實者有取於西京，史氏之憫時者獎進乎東漢而不及唐宋。吾士君子立身行己之間，又安得不擇取於是哉？請因明問而陳之。三代而上，聖學大明，公論素著。士君子生於其時，幼而學，壯而仕，行其所無事而已。降自秦漢，人心放失，聖學湮微，輿論不主於廟堂，而縉紳草茅或執其柄，於是乎始有節義之名者矣。且以兩漢言之，高祖除秦之暴，約法三章，史氏稱其尚寬大，是也。若光武當士夫頽鈍之後，而大興振作之功，召嚴光，褒卓茂，論文講道，崇尚儒學，而東都一代之士風已倡起於斯時矣。於是陳蕃、竇武之徒繼世而起，高名大節，與日月而爭光；危言峻行，雖死
translation_en:
…without being at a loss. Comparing this with the answers from the preceding two sessions, all rank first among the scripts in this examining room. Truly, there is no one who could displace you.

Response: Esteeming integrity and righteousness brings the gentleman an honorable reputation; examining reputation against reality is the impartial judgment of later Confucian scholars. To possess a reputation for integrity and righteousness is not as good as practicing them in substance. Yet if even their substance is to be lost, it is better still to honor their name. Thus later Confucian scholars, who demand substance, find merit in the Western Han, while historians, lamenting the circumstances of their times, commend the Eastern Han without extending such praise to the Tang and Song. How, then, can we gentlemen fail to choose discriminatingly among these examples in establishing ourselves and conducting our lives? Allow me to set this out in response to your illuminating question.

In the Three Dynasties and earlier, the learning of the sages shone brightly, and impartial judgments had long been manifest. Gentlemen born in that age studied in youth and entered office in maturity, simply acting without contrivance. From the Qin and Han onward, people let their moral minds go astray, and the learning of the sages became obscured and faint. Public judgment was no longer presided over at court; instead, officials and scholars out of office sometimes wielded its authority. Only then did a distinct reputation for integrity and righteousness arise.

Consider the two Han dynasties. Gaozu removed the Qin’s oppressive rule and reduced the laws to three articles. Historians describe him as valuing magnanimity, and rightly so. Guangwu, coming after a period when the educated elite had grown dispirited and ineffectual, undertook a great effort to reinvigorate them. He summoned Yan Guang, honored Zhuo Mao, discussed writings and expounded the Way, and esteemed Confucian learning. The ethos of the educated elite throughout the Eastern Han dynasty was already being fostered at that time. Thereupon men such as Chen Fan and Dou Wu arose in succeeding generations. Their lofty reputations and great integrity rivaled the sun and moon in brilliance; upright in speech and uncompromising in conduct, even though they died…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
亡而不悔桓靈以後國家失柄姦雄拱手
環視神器莫敢先動猶延數十年而後亡
史氏謂東漢之尚節義者不以此歟以西
漢人物而言坐事下獄不肯受卒徒之唾
背有若田延年者矣因誣被逮不肯受兩
吏之挾持有若蕭望之者矣以大將軍之
尊重而長揖不拜有汲長孺焉以匈奴之
暴驁而漢節不屈有蘇子卿焉高帝欲興
禮樂召魯兩生守乎儒禮而不至武帝大
===
崇文教迎魯申公告以力行之一言西京
高尚之士如此初不聞有節義之名蓋能
循其實耳故東萊吕氏謂東漢之節義不
如西漢豈不以東都之張其名而西京之
得其實乎若史氏謂東漢尚節義而西漢
不之尚者豈不以西漢之嫚罵折辱東漢
之能振作乎自是而後有唐焉其節義之
臣若巡遠力守睢陽捍安史之亂而江淮
賴之以保障陽城欲壞相麻劾裴延齡之
punctuated:
亡而不悔。桓靈以後，國家失柄，姦雄拱手環視神器，莫敢先動，猶延數十年而後亡。史氏謂東漢之尚節義者，不以此歟？以西漢人物而言，坐事下獄，不肯受卒徒之唾背，有若田延年者矣；因誣被逮，不肯受兩吏之挾持，有若蕭望之者矣。以大將軍之尊重，而長揖不拜，有汲長孺焉；以匈奴之暴驁，而漢節不屈，有蘇子卿焉。高帝欲興禮樂，召魯兩生，守乎儒禮而不至；武帝大崇文教，迎魯申公，告以力行之一言。西京高尚之士如此，初不聞有節義之名，蓋能循其實耳。故東萊吕氏謂東漢之節義不如西漢，豈不以東都之張其名，而西京之得其實乎？若史氏謂東漢尚節義，而西漢不之尚者，豈不以西漢之嫚罵折辱，東漢之能振作乎？
自是而後，有唐焉。其節義之臣，若巡遠力守睢陽，捍安史之亂，而江淮賴之以保障；陽城欲壞相麻，劾裴延齡之
translation_en:
…and did not regret it even in death. After the reigns of Huan and Ling, the state lost its hold on power. Treacherous men of ambition stood with folded hands, casting their eyes upon the sacred vessel of sovereignty, yet none dared move first. The dynasty thus endured for several more decades before falling. Was this not why historians spoke of the Eastern Han as esteeming integrity and righteousness? Among the figures of the Western Han, there was Tian Yannian, who, facing imprisonment for an offense, refused to suffer guards and convicts spitting upon his back; and Xiao Wangzhi, who, arrested on false accusations, refused to be held between two officers. There was Ji Changru, who merely bowed with clasped hands rather than prostrating himself before the General-in-Chief, despite that officer’s exalted rank; and Su Ziqing, who would not lower the Han envoy’s tally before the violent arrogance of the Xiongnu. Emperor Gao wished to promote rites and music and summoned two scholars from Lu, but they held fast to Confucian ritual principles and did not come. Emperor Wu greatly promoted literary learning and moral instruction and invited Master Shen of Lu, who offered him the single admonition to put principles earnestly into practice. Such were the lofty scholars of the Western Capital. At the time, one did not hear their conduct celebrated under the name of integrity and righteousness: they simply lived up to its substance. Thus Master Lü of Donglai said that the Eastern Han’s integrity and righteousness did not equal those of the Western Han. Was this not because the Eastern Capital proclaimed the name, whereas the Western Capital possessed the substance? As for historians saying that the Eastern Han esteemed integrity and righteousness whereas the Western Han did not, was this not because the Western Han subjected scholars to abuse and humiliation, while the Eastern Han was able to rouse and encourage them?
Thereafter came the Tang. Among its ministers of integrity and righteousness were Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan, who stoutly defended Suiyang against the An–Shi Rebellion, providing the protection upon which the Jiang–Huai region depended; and Yang Cheng, who wished to destroy the hemp-paper edict appointing a chief councilor and impeach Pei Yanling for his …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
奸朝廷賴之而振肅劉蕡對制策極言時
政雖權奸無所避忌何蕃在太學倡以大
義而六館不敢從亂其氣節有可尚也自
唐而後有宋焉其節義之臣若富弼奉使
虜庭議論慷慨而折服其君臣錢若水年
當強仕急流勇退而輕視乎富貴唐介謫
於英州困亦極矣而終無一書以至京師
劉器之交於温公情亦厚矣而卒無一言
抵於政府其節槩有可嘉也夫唐宋之節
===
義無愧於西京而西京之節義不讓於東
漢史氏獨以是名歸之東京者蓋以漢唐
宋三代士之蹈節而仗義者代不乏人元
氣賴之以不絕國家賴之以久存天地賴
之以有立者也至於上人之振作者獨光
武明章之為烈耳噫國家而不尚節義則
其後也苟且廢墮而無以振作乎人心士
大夫而不尚節義則其流也委靡頑鈍而
無以興起乎事業是節義雖非三代以上
punctuated:
奸，朝廷賴之而振肅。劉蕡對制策，極言時政，雖權奸，無所避忌。何蕃在太學，倡以大義，而六館不敢從亂。其氣節有可尚也。自唐而後有宋焉，其節義之臣，若富弼奉使虜庭，議論慷慨，而折服其君臣；錢若水年當強仕，急流勇退，而輕視乎富貴；唐介謫於英州，困亦極矣，而終無一書以至京師；劉器之交於温公，情亦厚矣，而卒無一言抵於政府。其節槩有可嘉也。
夫唐宋之節義，無愧於西京，而西京之節義，不讓於東漢。史氏獨以是名歸之東京者，蓋以漢唐宋三代，士之蹈節而仗義者，代不乏人，元氣賴之以不絕，國家賴之以久存，天地賴之以有立者也。至於上人之振作者，獨光武、明、章之為烈耳。噫！國家而不尚節義，則其後也苟且廢墮，而無以振作乎人心；士大夫而不尚節義，則其流也委靡頑鈍，而無以興起乎事業。是節義雖非三代以上
translation_en:
…treachery, and through him the court recovered its vigor and discipline. Liu Fen, answering an imperial policy question, spoke with utmost candor about current government, shrinking from nothing even where powerful, treacherous officials were concerned. He Fan, while at the Imperial University, championed the great principles of righteousness, so that the Six Colleges dared not join the rebellion. Their moral courage and integrity deserve esteem. After the Tang came the Song. Among its ministers of integrity and righteousness was Fu Bi, who went as envoy to the barbarian court, argued with impassioned conviction, and won over its ruler and ministers. Qian Ruoshui, at forty—the age for vigorous official service—courageously withdrew amid the swift current of public life, holding wealth and rank of little account. Tang Jie, banished to Yingzhou, suffered the utmost hardship, yet never sent a single letter to the capital. Liu Qizhi enjoyed a deeply affectionate friendship with the Duke of Wen, yet never conveyed a single word to the chief councillors. Their principled conduct deserves praise.
The integrity and righteousness of the Tang and Song were worthy of the Western Han, and those of the Western Han were no less than those of the Eastern Han. As for historians assigning this reputation exclusively to the Eastern Han: throughout the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, no age lacked scholars who upheld integrity and stood for righteousness. Through them the vital force remained unbroken, the state long endured, and Heaven and Earth maintained their foundations. But as for rulers actively fostering these qualities, the achievement belonged uniquely to Emperors Guangwu, Ming, and Zhang. Alas! If a state does not esteem integrity and righteousness, the eventual result is expediency and neglect, leaving no means of invigorating people’s hearts. If scholar-officials do not esteem integrity and righteousness, the resulting tendency is toward listlessness and moral obtuseness, leaving no means of rousing them to accomplishment. Thus, although integrity and righteousness were not, in the Three Dynasties and earlier, …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之美名而實士君子立身行已之大端也
若徒託東都黨錮之名而專為全身固位
之計以小人之無忌憚而曰由大中以出
則是相率為孔光張禹而後已世道將焉
攸賴哉昔人有言求士於三代之上惟恐
其好名三代之下惟恐其不好名愚於節
義亦云不識執事以為何如
第五問
俞振強
===
同考試官訓導張批論兵食而末歸之守令
尤為確論天下事有一不由於良吏乎他日效用稱良
吏者必若人矣
考試官教諭林批時務策只看處置處
置有方儘是策手
考試官教授陳批鋪叙詳明斷制允當其
策場中之傑出者乎
法有垂於久者守之不可以不固事有變
於今者處之不可以不宜蓋體國經久百
punctuated:
之美名，而實士君子立身行已之大端也。若徒託東都黨錮之名，而專為全身固位之計，以小人之無忌憚而曰由大中以出，則是相率為孔光、張禹而後已，世道將焉攸賴哉？昔人有言：「求士於三代之上，惟恐其好名；三代之下，惟恐其不好名。」愚於節義亦云，不識執事以為何如？

第五問
俞振強

同考試官訓導張批：論兵食而末歸之守令，尤為確論。天下事有一不由於良吏乎？他日效用稱良吏者，必若人矣。

考試官教諭林批：時務策只看處置，處置有方，儘是策手。

考試官教授陳批：鋪叙詳明，斷制允當，其策場中之傑出者乎？

法有垂於久者，守之不可以不固；事有變於今者，處之不可以不宜。蓋體國經久百
translation_en:
…a fine designation from the Three Dynasties or earlier, yet integrity and righteousness are indeed fundamental to how a gentleman establishes himself and conducts his life. If one merely invokes the partisan proscriptions of the Eastern Han as a pretext, while scheming solely to preserve oneself and secure one’s position, acting with the unscrupulousness of a petty man while claiming to proceed from the great mean, then men will simply lead one another into becoming Kong Guang and Zhang Yu. On what, then, could the moral order of the world depend? Someone of old said: “When seeking worthy men in the Three Dynasties and earlier, one fears only that they seek fame; after the Three Dynasties, one fears only that they do not seek fame.” I would say the same concerning integrity and righteousness. I wonder what you think of this.

Fifth Question
Yu Zhenqiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: His discussion of troops and provisions ultimately turns to prefects and county magistrates—an especially sound argument. Is there any affair in the realm that does not depend on good officials? When he enters service in the future, this man will surely be counted among the good officials.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: In a policy essay on current affairs, look only at the proposed measures. His measures are well conceived: he is thoroughly accomplished at policy essays.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: His exposition is detailed and clear, and his judgments are sound and appropriate. Surely this is one of the outstanding candidates in the policy examination!

Laws handed down over a long period must be upheld firmly; affairs that have changed in the present must be handled appropriately. For in organizing the state to endure over time, the hundred [?]…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於民斂之則什一之征散之則三年之積
故無不足之食厥後創業如漢高誅秦蹙
項提兵數十萬以一蕭何饋餉而有餘意
者得人專運之故歟守成如漢文遣將四
出以大禦匈奴累蠲田租而軍儲不匱意
者恭儉休息之效歟我
國家之兵制掌於司馬督於憲臣有五府都
司以總其綱有衞所官旗以分其目其制
可謂密矣况簡閱有法清理有規乎邇者
punctuated: 於民，斂之則什一之征，散之則三年之積，故無不足之食。厥後，創業如漢高，誅秦蹙項，提兵數十萬，以一蕭何饋餉而有餘，意者得人專運之故歟？守成如漢文，遣將四出，以大禦匈奴，累蠲田租而軍儲不匱，意者恭儉休息之效歟？我國家之兵制，掌於司馬，督於憲臣，有五府都司以總其綱，有衞所官旗以分其目，其制可謂密矣，况簡閱有法，清理有規乎？邇者，
translation_en:
…from the people: collection was through a levy of one tenth, and disbursement drew upon reserves sufficient for three years; thus there was never a shortage of food. Subsequently, among founders of dynasties, Gaozu of Han destroyed Qin and pressed Xiang Yu hard, leading several hundred thousand troops. With Xiao He alone supplying provisions, there was more than enough. Might this have been because he found the right man to take sole charge of transport? Among rulers who preserved an established dynasty, Emperor Wen of Han dispatched generals in all directions to repel the Xiongnu in force. Though he repeatedly remitted the land tax, military stores were never depleted. Might this have been the result of his reverence and frugality and his policy of allowing the people rest and recuperation?
Our dynasty’s military establishment is administered by the Minister of War and supervised by censorial officials. The Five Chief Military Commissions and the Regional Military Commissions oversee its general organization, while the officers and banner personnel of the guards and battalions divide responsibility for its particulars. Its organization may indeed be called meticulous. Moreover, are there not methods for mustering and inspecting troops, and regulations for scrutinizing and rectifying the rolls? Recently, …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有事于蜀于江于
畿內而所在兵力為之不足至厪
宵旰之憂而募土兵調邊將者其故有三焉埋
沒紊於坐冊逃亡隱於偽籍一也寄名於
籍而役占於私家二也承平日乆人不知
兵為將者皆膏粱之廕子為兵者皆尺五
之市人三也安得我兵之不寡哉
國家之國計掌於戶部有京兆藩司以總其
政有郡守縣令以分其職其制可謂善矣
===
况征輸有法儲峙有規乎邇因饋餉于蜀
于江于
畿內而兵食為之告匱至煩
九重之聽以發
內帑截綱運者其故亦有二焉旱潦相仍歲
無全賦一也豪黠侵漁而不畏禁網二也
五方之財止有此數高庾大廩鮮有蓋藏
冗食奢華一切糜費三也安得我財之不
匱焉今之計於軍政也必以
punctuated:
有事于蜀、于江、于畿內，而所在兵力為之不足，至厪宵旰之憂，而募土兵、調邊將者，其故有三焉：埋沒紊於坐冊，逃亡隱於偽籍，一也；寄名於籍，而役占於私家，二也；承平日乆，人不知兵，為將者皆膏粱之廕子，為兵者皆尺五之市人，三也。安得我兵之不寡哉？
國家之國計掌於戶部，有京兆、藩司以總其政，有郡守、縣令以分其職，其制可謂善矣。况征輸有法，儲峙有規乎？邇因饋餉于蜀、于江、于畿內，而兵食為之告匱，至煩九重之聽，以發內帑、截綱運者，其故亦有二焉：旱潦相仍，歲無全賦，一也；豪黠侵漁，而不畏禁網，二也；五方之財止有此數，高庾大廩鮮有蓋藏，冗食奢華，一切糜費，三也。安得我財之不匱焉？今之計於軍政也，必以
translation_en:
…military troubles arose in Shu, in Jiang [?], and in the capital region, and the military strength available in each locality proved inadequate. This caused His Majesty such anxiety that he attended to affairs before dawn and after dark, while local troops were recruited and frontier commanders transferred. There are three reasons for this. First, men are lost from view amid confused service registers [?], and desertions are concealed through falsified rolls. Second, men have their names entered on the rolls but are appropriated for service in private households. Third, prolonged peace has left people ignorant of military affairs: commanders are all sons of wealthy families enjoying hereditary privilege, while soldiers are all undersized townsmen [?]. How could our troops fail to be insufficient?
The state's finances are administered by the Ministry of Revenue. The metropolitan prefecture and Provincial Administration Commissions oversee their administration, while prefects and district magistrates divide the responsibilities. This system may indeed be called sound. Moreover, there are established methods for collecting and transporting revenues and regulations for stockpiling supplies. Recently, however, provisioning forces in Shu, in Jiang [?], and in the capital region has exhausted military food supplies. The matter has even had to be brought to the imperial attention, prompting disbursements from the Privy Treasury and the diversion of grain-transport convoys. There are also two reasons for this [the text enumerates three]. First, droughts and floods follow one another, so that no year yields the full tax revenue. Second, powerful and cunning men embezzle and exploit, without fear of legal prohibitions. Third, the wealth of all regions is limited to a fixed amount; lofty granaries and great storehouses contain few reserves, while supernumerary dependants, extravagance, and luxury consume resources in every way. How could our finances fail to be exhausted? In planning military administration today, we must employ…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
祖宗之法而整頓之搜其埋沒禁其偽籍嚴其
訓練剔其隱占而又有不從者重罰以懲
之其既從也生息以蕃之如此則諸路之
兵亦足以禦諸路之寇矣於
國計也必以
祖宗之法而調度之備其旱潦稽其侵漁汰其
冗食禁其奢靡有羨餘也則倉庾以儲之
有措置也則歲月以積之如此則天下之
食亦足以供天下之兵矣然此特就事論
===
事耳若要其極與其急於兵食孰若急於
弭盜與其急於弭盜孰若急於安民安民
之道無他焉在乎慎選守令重其權久其
任使民尊之信之而已今之守令固未必
皆賢也而民恒有輕忽之心何者利不能
為民興也害不能為民除也以近事言之
賊至而不能禦賊去而不能追也其無益
於民者如此而欲民相信而服從也不亦
難乎必也得其賢也言聽而計用信賞而
punctuated:
祖宗之法而整頓之，搜其埋沒，禁其偽籍，嚴其訓練，剔其隱占，而又有不從者，重罰以懲之；其既從也，生息以蕃之。如此，則諸路之兵亦足以禦諸路之寇矣。於國計也，必以祖宗之法而調度之，備其旱潦，稽其侵漁，汰其冗食，禁其奢靡。有羨餘也，則倉庾以儲之；有措置也，則歲月以積之。如此，則天下之食亦足以供天下之兵矣。然此特就事論事耳。
若要其極，與其急於兵食，孰若急於弭盜？與其急於弭盜，孰若急於安民？安民之道無他焉，在乎慎選守令，重其權，久其任，使民尊之信之而已。今之守令固未必皆賢也，而民恒有輕忽之心。何者？利不能為民興也，害不能為民除也。以近事言之，賊至而不能禦，賊去而不能追也。其無益於民者如此，而欲民相信而服從也，不亦難乎？必也得其賢也，言聽而計用，信賞而
translation_en:
…the laws of the imperial ancestors to put military affairs in order: seek out soldiers concealed from the rolls, prohibit fraudulent registration, enforce rigorous training, and root out the covert appropriation of soldiers for private service. Those who still refuse to comply should be deterred by severe punishment; once they comply, allow them to recuperate and increase their numbers. In this way, the troops of the various regions will suffice to repel the bandits of those regions. As for state finances, resources must likewise be managed according to the laws of the imperial ancestors: make provision against droughts and floods, investigate embezzlement and extortion, eliminate those who consume provisions without rendering service, and prohibit extravagance. When there is a surplus, store it in granaries; where measures have been put in place, let reserves accumulate over months and years. In this way, the provisions of the realm will suffice to supply its troops. Yet this merely addresses each matter on its own terms.
If we seek the ultimate solution, rather than making troops and provisions our urgent concern, would it not be better to make suppressing banditry our urgent concern? Rather than making suppressing banditry our urgent concern, would it not be better to make securing the people's well-being our urgent concern? The way to secure their well-being is simply to choose prefects and magistrates carefully, strengthen their authority, and lengthen their tenure, so that the people respect and trust them. Certainly, the prefects and magistrates of today are not necessarily all worthy, but the people habitually regard them with contempt. Why? They cannot promote what benefits the people or remove what harms them. To speak of recent events, when bandits arrive, they cannot repel them; when bandits leave, they cannot pursue them. Being so useless to the people, is it not difficult for them to expect the people's trust and obedience? Worthy men must indeed be obtained, their words heeded and their plans employed, rewards reliably bestowed, and…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
必罰藩司觀其風俗之大而不較其簿領
之煩瑣監司察其賢否之大而不較其一
刑一政之得失使其志得以上達而其澤
得以下敷如是而民不相敬信不相悅服
乃復去而為盜萬萬無是理也明問所謂
大處分者亦唯不過責之有司之職如前
之云耳舍是固不能以有為也自古有治
人無治法此雖老生之常談而至理實不
外是惟執事進而教之幸甚
===
点燃
punctuated:
必罰。藩司觀其風俗之大，而不較其簿領之煩瑣；監司察其賢否之大，而不較其一刑一政之得失。使其志得以上達，而其澤得以下敷。如是而民不相敬信，不相悅服，乃復去而為盜，萬萬無是理也。明問所謂大處分者，亦唯不過責之有司之職，如前之云耳。舍是，固不能以有為也。自古有治人，無治法。此雖老生之常談，而至理實不外是。惟執事進而教之，幸甚。

点燃。
translation_en:
…and punishments unfailingly imposed. The Provincial Administration Commission should attend to the broader condition of local customs, rather than quibble over the minutiae of paperwork; the surveillance authorities should assess the larger question of whether these officials are worthy, rather than quibble over the merits or faults of each punishment or administrative measure. Let their intentions be conveyed upward and their beneficence spread downward. If this is done, there is absolutely no reason why the people should fail to respect and trust them, fail to submit willingly, and instead go off and become bandits. The major measures mentioned in your illuminating question amount simply to holding the responsible officials accountable for their duties, as stated above. Apart from this, nothing can really be accomplished. Since antiquity, there have been men who bring about good government, but no methods that do so by themselves. Though this is an old scholar’s commonplace, the ultimate principle lies nowhere else. I would be most grateful if you would offer further instruction.

“Light” or “ignite” [?].

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
三歲取士額浙江九十人度
地定才著為令甲遵行既久
奉率彌周是為正德八年之
秋巡按浙江監察御史袁宗
儒循近
制限列郡之士一千八百人以世
===
明等典試事鎖院校閱中式
者二十而一擇其文之醇與
士之邑里名氏內外百執事
職名為鄉試錄錄成謂世明
當序其後竊惟浙古揚州地
也其見於圖經記序辭賦倡
和諸集者曰帶江海抱湖山
banxin: 鄉試錄後序 六十一
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

三歲取士，額浙江九十人。度地定才，著為令甲，遵行既久，奉率彌周。是為正德八年之秋，巡按浙江監察御史袁宗儒循近制，限列郡之士一千八百人，以世明等典試事。鎖院校閱，中式者二十而一。擇其文之醇，與士之邑里名氏、內外百執事職名，為鄉試錄。錄成，謂世明當序其後。竊惟浙，古揚州地也。其見於圖經、記序、辭賦、倡和諸集者，曰：「帶江海，抱湖山。」
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

Scholars are selected every three years, with Zhejiang allotted a quota of ninety. The number of talented men to be selected was determined according to the territory and established in statute. These provisions have long been observed, and compliance has become ever more thorough. In the autumn of the eighth year of Zhengde [1513], Yuan Zongru, Investigating Censor巡按 assigned to inspect Zhejiang, followed the recent regulations, limiting the candidates from the prefectures to eighteen hundred and appointing me, Shiming, and others to conduct the examination. Sequestered within the examination compound, we assessed their papers; one candidate in twenty passed. We selected the finest of their compositions and compiled them, together with the successful candidates’ home localities and names and the titles and names of all officials serving inside and outside the compound, into the Record of the Provincial Examination. When the record was complete, I was told that I should write its postface.

I humbly reflect that Zhejiang was part of ancient Yangzhou. In illustrated geographical accounts, records and prefaces, literary compositions and rhapsodies, and collections of poems exchanged in response to one another, it is described as “girdled by rivers and sea, embracing lakes and mountains”…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
曰江東一都會東南一大都
會而會稽天目赤城鴈蕩之
為山錢塘震澤浙江鏡湖姚
江之為水峻岐秀麗嵽嵲蜿
蜒流注停蓄環抱委蛇清淑
所鍾陶和孕粹物受其偏尚
有嘉木異卉以資民用魚龍
===
隱見變怪滄溟萬頃間時出
雲雨以蘇枯槁而況人受其
正者乎故求其美俗曰士知
所學曰家習儒業同受學漢
祖者懷仁輔義詞約而達是
雖投札口授萬世立言者所
不能喻遭遇唐宗者十八登
punctuated: 曰江東一都會，東南一大都會。而會稽、天目、赤城、鴈蕩之為山，錢塘、震澤、浙江、鏡湖、姚江之為水，峻岐秀麗，嵽嵲蜿蜒，流注停蓄，環抱委蛇，清淑所鍾，陶和孕粹。物受其偏，尚有嘉木異卉以資民用，魚龍隱見變怪滄溟萬頃間，時出雲雨以蘇枯槁，而況人受其正者乎？故求其美俗，曰士知所學，曰家習儒業。同受學漢祖者，懷仁輔義，詞約而達，是雖投札口授，萬世立言者所不能喻。遭遇唐宗者，十八登
translation_en:
…it is called “a metropolis east of the Yangzi” and “a great metropolis of the southeast.” Its mountains—Kuaiji, Tianmu, Chicheng, and Yandang—and its waters—Qiantang, Zhenze, the Zhejiang, Jinghu, and the Yao River—rise steeply in beautiful branching heights, tower and wind, flow and gather, encircle and meander. Here pure and beneficent influences concentrate, fostering harmony and nurturing the finest essences. Even other living things, which receive only a partial share of these influences, include fine trees and rare plants that supply the people's needs. Fish and dragons appear and disappear, undergoing wondrous transformations amid the vast blue sea, at times sending forth clouds and rain to revive what has withered. How much more, then, must this be true of human beings, who receive these influences in their proper fullness!

Thus, when we seek evidence of the region's admirable customs, we hear that “its scholars know what they should study” and that “its households cultivate Confucian learning.” Those who studied together under the founding emperor of the Han [?] cherished benevolence and upheld righteousness; their language was concise yet expressive. Though these words were committed to writing or imparted orally, those who establish enduring teachings for all ages cannot comprehend them [?]. The man who found favor with an emperor of the Tang, at eighteen attained…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
進士瀉胸中之蘊論諫數百
皆本仁義文起八代之衰則
其考試時所取士也王忠文
紹興中廷對下筆數千言百
忠憤所激可與天人三策相
表裏高宗親擢為第一朱文
公嘗稱之曰磊磊落落君子
===
人也有梅溪集朗誦之氣象
自别呂成公召試館職文特
典美嘗讀陸九淵之文喜之
及試禮部得一卷曰此江西
小陸之文也揭示果九淵人
服其精陳文節公著書明道
簡冊充棟片言落筆傳誦震
punctuated: 進士，瀉胸中之蘊，論諫數百，皆本仁義，文起八代之衰，則其考試時所取士也。王忠文紹興中廷對，下筆數千言，百忠憤所激，可與天人三策相表裏。高宗親擢為第一。朱文公嘗稱之曰：「磊磊落落，君子人也。」有《梅溪集》，朗誦之，氣象自别。呂成公召試館職，文特典美，嘗讀陸九淵之文，喜之。及試禮部，得一卷，曰：「此江西小陸之文也。」揭示，果九淵，人服其精。陳文節公著書明道，簡冊充棟，片言落筆，傳誦震
translation_en:
…attained jinshi status and poured forth what lay within his breast in hundreds of discourses and remonstrances, all grounded in benevolence and righteousness. His writing revived literature after eight dynasties of decline: he was thus one of the men selected through examination.

Wang Zhongwen, responding at the Palace Examination during the Shaoxing reign, wrote several thousand words, inspired by loyal indignation [?]. His answer could stand alongside the Three Policy Responses on Heaven and Humanity as mutually illuminating works. Emperor Gaozong personally placed him first. Zhu Wengong once praised him, saying, “Open and upright—a gentleman indeed.” His collected writings, the Meixi Collection, possess a distinctive presence when read aloud.

Lü Chenggong was summoned to an examination for a post in the imperial library; his writing was exceptionally elegant and refined. He once read an essay by Lu Jiuyuan and admired it. Later, while examining candidates at the Ministry of Rites, he came upon a script and said, “This is the writing of young Lu from Jiangxi.” When the identity was disclosed, it proved indeed to be Jiuyuan. People admired his discernment.

Chen Wenjie wrote books elucidating the Way, with volumes enough to fill a building. Even a few words from his brush were passed about and recited, resounding…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
響塲屋相師文體丕變其作
為論學論者謂之决科之文
呂公以為其長不獨在文字
間金仁山所著大學疏義尚
書表註論孟考證中庸標註
諸書許白雲聞而從之求聖
賢之心而著為四書叢說二
===
人之書雖非專為科舉而作
要亦科舉之士之所不能遺
也我
朝國初宋景濂劉伯温王忠文
諸大儒作為文字微詞奥義
渾厚典則是正國人之所矜
式今所取士冀得諸若人而
punctuated:
響，塲屋相師，文體丕變。其作為《論學論》者，謂之决科之文。呂公以為其長不獨在文字間。金仁山所著《大學疏義》《尚書表註》《論孟考證》《中庸標註》諸書，許白雲聞而從之，求聖賢之心，而著為《四書叢說》。二人之書，雖非專為科舉而作，要亦科舉之士之所不能遺也。
我朝國初，宋景濂、劉伯温、王忠文諸大儒作為文字，微詞奥義，渾厚典則，是正國人之所矜式。今所取士，冀得諸若人而
translation_en:
…resounded; candidates in the examination halls took his writings as models, and literary style underwent a great transformation. His Discourse on Learning (Lun xue lun) was called a composition that secured success in the examinations. Master Lü considered that his strengths lay not only in literary composition. Jin Renshan wrote such books as Exposition of the Meaning of the Great Learning, Tabulated Annotations on the Book of Documents, Textual Investigations of the Analects and Mencius, and Highlighted Annotations on the Doctrine of the Mean. Hearing of him, Xu Baiyun became his follower, sought to understand the minds of the sages and worthies, and wrote Collected Explanations of the Four Books. Although these two men's books were not written specifically for the civil-service examinations, they were nevertheless indispensable to examination candidates.
At the beginning of our dynasty, such great Confucian scholars as Song Jinglian, Liu Bowen, and Wang Zhongwen produced writings of subtle expression and profound meaning, substantial and rich, classical and well ordered. These were precisely the models that the people of the realm esteemed and emulated. In selecting men through the examinations today, we hope to obtain men like these and …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
用之其仰止思齊效規摸矩
力追古作於千百載之上渾
厚正大典則純明與理俱勝
者固深嘉樂進求其進也則
融通變化師其意不泥其迹
豈但獵涉記誦祖襲陳言而
務為同次則理勝乎文雖無
===
前輩渾厚正大典則純明氣
象要亦近似無相齟齬繼是
而勉焉以充以馴致其極拭
目改觀莫可涯涘故在不遺
下此則非所敢知焉今日取
士他日用之其光明俊偉立
遠大事業以步鄉先哲後塵
punctuated: 用之。其仰止思齊，效規摸矩，力追古作於千百載之上，渾厚正大，典則純明，與理俱勝者，固深嘉樂進。求其進也，則融通變化，師其意，不泥其迹，豈但獵涉記誦，祖襲陳言，而務為同？次則理勝乎文，雖無前輩渾厚正大、典則純明氣象，要亦近似，無相齟齬。繼是而勉焉，以充以馴致其極，拭目改觀，莫可涯涘，故在不遺。下此則非所敢知焉。今日取士，他日用之，其光明俊偉，立遠大事業，以步鄉先哲後塵
translation_en:
…and employ them. Those who look up to these predecessors and aspire to equal them, follow their standards and models, and strive to match ancient writings from hundreds or thousands of years ago—whose writing is rich and substantial, upright and grand, exemplary and pure in its clarity, and excels together with the principles it conveys—certainly merit our deep appreciation and willing advancement. In seeking their further progress, we expect them to assimilate what they have learned and transform it, taking the predecessors’ intent as their teacher without clinging to their outward traces. Surely they should not merely browse, memorize, and repeat inherited phrases, striving only for sameness?

Next come those whose grasp of principle surpasses their literary accomplishment. Although they lack the rich substance, upright grandeur, exemplary form, and pure clarity of their predecessors, they nevertheless approach them and are not at odds with them. If they continue to exert themselves, developing their abilities and gradually reaching their fullest achievement, we may look afresh upon them with new eyes: their prospects admit of no bounds. Thus we take care not to overlook them. Those below this level, however, are not such as we would venture to recognize.

We select men today to employ them in the future, hoping that, radiant in integrity and outstanding in ability, they will establish great and enduring achievements, following in the footsteps of the earlier worthies of their home province…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
又由是而求其上焉是固以
人事君者至願若但假文詞
以為進身之階而他日所行
與今所學經傳所傳授聖賢
所議觀鄉邦先哲無一相當
者遂使論者謂以文欺人襲
取之敝至謂文不可以得士
===
嗚呼是豈文之罪哉故以文
取士固主司者之所當盡心
而勉焉以塞責者也至於主
司之所願望而不能悉用其
力者則爾多士之責也其勉
之哉
山東兗州府東平州汶上縣
punctuated:
又由是而求其上焉，是固以人事君者至願。若但假文詞以為進身之階，而他日所行，與今所學、經傳所傳授、聖賢所議觀、鄉邦先哲，無一相當者，遂使論者謂以文欺人、襲取之敝，至謂文不可以得士。嗚呼！是豈文之罪哉？故以文取士，固主司者之所當盡心而勉焉以塞責者也。至於主司之所願望而不能悉用其力者，則爾多士之責也。其勉之哉！

山東兗州府東平州汶上縣
translation_en:
…and from this foundation seek still greater heights: this is indeed the deepest wish of those who serve their sovereign by selecting men. But if you merely use literary composition as a ladder to advancement, and your subsequent conduct accords in no respect with what you now study, what the classics and their commentaries transmit, what the sages and worthies discuss and observe [?], or the example of your locality’s earlier worthies, you will lead critics to speak of the abuses of deceiving others through literary composition and gaining advancement by imitation [?], and even to claim that literary composition cannot identify worthy men. Alas! How could this be the fault of literary composition? Thus, selecting men through literary composition is certainly a responsibility to which those presiding over the examination must devote their utmost care and effort. But fulfilling the hopes of those presiding over the examination, where their own efforts cannot fully reach, is the responsibility of you assembled scholars. Apply yourselves diligently!

Wenshang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text: 儒學教諭林世明謹序
punctuated: 儒學教諭林世明謹序。
translation_en: …Lin Shiming, Instructor of the Confucian School, respectfully composed this preface.

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
正德癸酉當天下鄉試之期
浙藩臬二司請於巡按監察
御史王堯封禮聘龍等以司
試事及期監察御史袁宗儒
奉
命代至寔維監臨睠兹重務謂臣
===
子以人事君之忠莫大於此
乃以龍與教諭林世明為考
試官教諭吳度蜀戴儉李昺
郝文瑞蔡元用何亦尹唐夔
訓導田獻張輅為同考試官
凡所以矢心誓衆明約厲禁
督察裁節之務經畫授成靡
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序

正德癸酉，當天下鄉試之期，浙藩臬二司請於巡按監察御史王堯封，禮聘龍等以司試事。及期，監察御史袁宗儒奉命代至，寔維監臨。睠兹重務，謂臣子以人事君之忠，莫大於此。乃以龍與教諭林世明為考試官，教諭吳度蜀、戴儉、李昺、郝文瑞、蔡元用、何亦尹、唐夔，訓導田獻、張輅為同考試官。凡所以矢心誓衆、明約厲禁、督察裁節之務，經畫授成，靡
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the guiyou year of the Zhengde reign [1513], when Provincial Examinations were due to be held throughout the empire, Zhejiang’s Provincial Administration Commission and Provincial Surveillance Commission petitioned Wang Yaofeng, the Regional Inspecting Censor, to formally engage me, Long, and others to administer the examination. When the appointed time arrived, Investigating Censor Yuan Zongru came under imperial orders to take his place and served as Supervising Official. Regarding this weighty responsibility, he held that no act of loyalty by a subject serving his ruler surpassed that of providing him with worthy men. He therefore appointed me, Long, and Instructor Lin Shiming as Examiners; Instructors Wu Dushu, Dai Jian, Li Bing, Hao Wenrui, Cai Yuanyong, He Yiyin, and Tang Kui, together with Assistant Instructors Tian Xian and Zhang Lu, were appointed Associate Examiners. All arrangements for pledging our resolve and administering oaths to those assembled, clarifying rules and enforcing prohibitions, and overseeing and regulating proceedings were planned and assigned for execution, without …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有關遺維時雅好儒彥崇奬
作興則鎮守太監劉璟申飭
諸司開布公道則巡視右都
御史陶琰相成厥美則督造
太監楊軋晁進監舶太監王
堂督染太監杜甫鹽法監察
御史林季瓊清戎監察御史
===
喻文璧有事茲土者主事伍
全王念陸節胡璉罔不樂預
盛事而提調監試於內則右
布政使蔣昇左參政詹璽副
使鄭陽高貫協賛於外則右
參政陳仁官昶副使閻睿謝
琛左參議羅欽德右參議段
punctuated: 有關遺。維時雅好儒彥，崇奬作興，則鎮守太監劉璟；申飭諸司，開布公道，則巡視右都御史陶琰；相成厥美，則督造太監楊軋、晁進，監舶太監王堂，督染太監杜甫，鹽法監察御史林季瓊，清戎監察御史喻文璧。有事茲土者，主事伍全、王念、陸節、胡璉，罔不樂預盛事。而提調監試於內，則右布政使蔣昇、左參政詹璽、副使鄭陽、高貫；協賛於外，則右參政陳仁、官昶，副使閻睿、謝琛，左參議羅欽德、右參議段
translation_en:
…anything overlooked [?]. At that time, the Regional Commander, Grand Eunuch Liu Jing, esteemed outstanding Confucian scholars and encouraged and promoted their advancement. Tao Yan, the touring Right Censor-in-Chief, admonished the various offices and fostered impartial conduct. Those who assisted in bringing this worthy undertaking to fruition were Yang Zha and Chao Jin, Grand Eunuchs supervising manufacture; Wang Tang, Grand Eunuch supervising maritime trade; Du Fu, Grand Eunuch supervising dyeing; Lin Jiqiong, Investigating Censor responsible for the salt administration; and Yu Wenbi, Investigating Censor responsible for inspecting military registers. Bureau Secretaries Wu Quan, Wang Nian, Lu Jie, and Hu Lian, who had official business in this territory, all gladly participated in the great undertaking.

Those administering and supervising the examination within the compound were Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Jiang Sheng, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Zhan Xi, and Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zheng Yang and Gao Guan. Those providing assistance outside were Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners Chen Ren and Guan Chang, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Yan Rui and Xie Chen, Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner Luo Qinde, and Right Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner Duan…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
敏僉事吳希由儲珊劉祥炳
汪大章王𤩽而叅將李隆都
指揮僉事陳璠張奎江洪傅
銘亦與焉其餘執事自收掌
試卷知府梁材劉斐以下咸
慎簡以充罔敢弗虔合提學
副使徐蕃所選士千八百人
===
如故事三試之拔其尤者九
十人錄其姓名與文以
獻而龍謹序其首曰
國朝取士之法叅酌古制黜詞
賦以本經術併異路以歸科
目崇雅黜浮正習敦化可謂
簡要切實行之萬世而無弊
punctuated:
敏，僉事吳希由、儲珊、劉祥炳、汪大章、王𤩽，而叅將李隆、都指揮僉事陳璠、張奎、江洪、傅銘亦與焉。其餘執事，自收掌試卷知府梁材、劉斐以下，咸慎簡以充，罔敢弗虔。合提學副使徐蕃所選士千八百人，如故事三試之，拔其尤者九十人，錄其姓名與文以獻。而龍謹序其首曰：
國朝取士之法，叅酌古制，黜詞賦以本經術，併異路以歸科目，崇雅黜浮，正習敦化，可謂簡要切實，行之萬世而無弊。
translation_en:
…Min; and the surveillance assistant commissioners Wu Xiyou, Chu Shan, Liu Xiangbing, Wang Dazhang, and Wang [?] 王𤩽. Assistant Regional Commander Li Long and Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Chen Fan, Zhang Kui, Jiang Hong, and Fu Ming also participated. The remaining functionaries, beginning with Prefects Liang Cai and Liu Fei, who received and kept the examination papers, were all carefully selected to fill their duties; none dared be remiss. The 1,800 candidates selected by Education Intendant Xu Fan, a surveillance vice commissioner, were assembled and examined in three sessions according to established precedent. The ninety most outstanding were selected, and their names and writings were recorded for presentation to the throne. Long respectfully placed a preface at the beginning, saying:
Our dynasty’s method of selecting men for office draws judiciously upon ancient institutions. It rejects ornate verse and rhapsodies in order to ground selection in classical learning, and consolidates the different avenues of advancement into the examination system. It esteems refinement and rejects superficiality, rectifies habits, and strengthens moral cultivation. It may be called concise, essential, practical, and sound—a system that could be practiced for ten thousand generations without ill effects…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣但文有規制進無雜途兹
欲據三試之作較一日之長
識拔特達之才以盡收一時
英傑斯亦難矣然道義積中
英華發外文也者道義之英
華也雖曰程試之文苟典雅
平正可以見其德之純雄健
===
通達可以見其才之充辯析
該洽可以見其學之博高朗
閎遠可以見其識之明即其
外以叩其中豪傑之士率於
此焉得之今兩浙多士鍾山
川之秀而涵濡
聖化之深學貫于經言根于理源
punctuated: 矣。但文有規制，進無雜途，兹欲據三試之作，較一日之長，識拔特達之才，以盡收一時英傑，斯亦難矣。然道義積中，英華發外，文也者，道義之英華也。雖曰程試之文，苟典雅平正，可以見其德之純；雄健通達，可以見其才之充；辯析該洽，可以見其學之博；高朗閎遠，可以見其識之明。即其外以叩其中，豪傑之士率於此焉得之。今兩浙多士，鍾山川之秀，而涵濡聖化之深，學貫于經，言根于理，源
translation_en:
…indeed. Yet compositions must follow prescribed forms, and advancement admits no miscellaneous routes. To judge the relative merits displayed on a single occasion from the compositions of the three examination sessions, discerning and selecting exceptionally gifted men so as to gather all the outstanding talents of the age—this too is difficult. Nevertheless, the Way and righteousness accumulate within, and their finest flowering appears without: writing is the finest flowering of the Way and righteousness. Even in compositions written for examination, elegance, refinement, balance, and correctness reveal the purity of a man's virtue; vigor and fluency reveal the fullness of his talent; analytical precision and comprehensive knowledge reveal the breadth of his learning; loftiness, clarity, breadth, and depth reveal the lucidity of his discernment. By examining outward expression to probe what lies within, one can generally discover men of outstanding ability.

Now the many scholars of Liangzhe embody the finest influences of its mountains and rivers and are deeply steeped in the transforming influence of the sage emperor. Their learning encompasses the Classics, their words are rooted in principle, and their sources…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
流有自而途轍不迷故發於
文者如醇雅如雄健如辯博
如高逺無所不備文質得中
初無所謂浮雜粗淺之弊則
夫德之所成才之所能學之
所至識之所達亦略得其一
二矣他日推之天下國家措
===
諸事業必有可觀者焉於戲
盛哉雖然士始固以文進而
其終之所立則又不止於文
士固可以文知而士之所以
爲士有非文之所能盡也蓋
所貴於士者志欲正而守欲
專氣欲一而分欲定通則不
punctuated: 流有自而途轍不迷，故發於文者，如醇雅，如雄健，如辯博，如高逺，無所不備，文質得中，初無所謂浮雜粗淺之弊。則夫德之所成、才之所能、學之所至、識之所達，亦略得其一二矣。他日推之天下國家，措諸事業，必有可觀者焉。於戲，盛哉！雖然，士始固以文進，而其終之所立，則又不止於文。士固可以文知，而士之所以爲士，有非文之所能盡也。蓋所貴於士者，志欲正而守欲專，氣欲一而分欲定，通則不
translation_en:
…their learning flows from an established source, and they do not stray from the proper path. Thus, what finds expression in their writing encompasses everything: purity and elegance, vigor and strength, analytical breadth, and loftiness of vision. Literary refinement and substance are properly balanced, entirely free from the faults of superficiality, incoherence, coarseness, and shallowness. From this, one can gain some sense of what their virtue has achieved, what their talents can accomplish, how far their learning extends, and what their discernment comprehends. When, in days to come, they apply these qualities to the affairs of the realm and the state and put them into practice, there will surely be achievements worthy of admiration. Ah, how splendid!
Nevertheless, although scholars initially advance through their writing, what they ultimately establish goes beyond writing alone. Scholars can indeed be known through their writing, yet writing cannot fully reveal what makes a scholar a scholar. What is prized in scholars is that their aspirations be upright, their adherence steadfast, their resolve undivided, and their sense of their proper station settled. When successful, they must not…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以勢利易其志塞則不以事
變奪其氣益培才德以厚其
本益充學識以周其用使他
日立
朝居位論建如褚僕射陸宣公
之於唐清忠如趙清獻宗忠
簡之於宋德業文章如劉伯
===
溫宋景濂之於
國朝庶幾不愧鄉之先哲無負
朝廷作養甄拔之意然後可尚
勗之哉
福建福州府儒學教授陳龍
謹序
punctuated:
以勢利易其志，塞則不以事變奪其氣，益培才德以厚其本，益充學識以周其用，使他日立朝居位，論建如褚僕射、陸宣公之於唐，清忠如趙清獻、宗忠簡之於宋，德業文章如劉伯溫、宋景濂之於國朝，庶幾不愧鄉之先哲，無負朝廷作養甄拔之意，然後可尚。勗之哉！
福建福州府儒學教授陳龍謹序。
translation_en:
…change their aspirations for the sake of power or profit; when thwarted, they must not let changing circumstances rob them of their spirit. They should further cultivate their abilities and virtue to strengthen their foundations, and further enlarge their learning and understanding to make their capacities fully adequate for service. Thus, when they one day take their places at court and hold office, their deliberations and proposals may resemble those of Vice Director Chu and Lu Xuangong under the Tang; their integrity and loyalty, those of Zhao Qingxian and Zong Zhongjian under the Song; and their moral accomplishments and literary writings, those of Liu Bowen and Song Jinglian under our dynasty. They may then hope to stand without shame before the earlier worthies of their native province and not disappoint the court’s intention in nurturing, selecting, and promoting them. Only then will they merit esteem. Strive toward this!
Preface respectfully written by Chen Long, Prefectural School Instructor of Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian.

translation_en:
Zhejiang Provincial Examination, eighth year of Zhengde (1513).

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
山東濟南府陵縣儒學教諭何亦尹〔公志廣東番禺縣人甲子貢士〕
直隸廣平府邯鄲縣儒學教諭唐彛〔天彛貴州普安州人丁卯貢士〕
河南河南府陝州靈寶縣儒學訓導田猷〔宗道山東壽張縣人丁卯貢士〕
直隸池州府儒學訓導張輅〔從殷湖廣江夏縣人甲子貢士〕
印卷官
浙江等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事熊廣達〔九達江西豐城縣人吏員〕
浙江等處提刑按察司經歷司知事呉鍔〔廷重廣西賀縣人監生〕

===

punctuated:
山東濟南府陵縣儒學教諭何亦尹〔公志，廣東番禺縣人，甲子貢士〕。直隸廣平府邯鄲縣儒學教諭唐彛〔天彛，貴州普安州人，丁卯貢士〕。河南河南府陝州靈寶縣儒學訓導田猷〔宗道，山東壽張縣人，丁卯貢士〕。直隸池州府儒學訓導張輅〔從殷，湖廣江夏縣人，甲子貢士〕。

translation_en:
He Yiyin, Instructor at the Confucian School of Ling County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, had the courtesy name Gongzhi and was from Panyu County, Guangdong. He was a tribute student of the jiazi year.

Tang Yi, Instructor at the Confucian School of Handan County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Tianyi and was from Pu’an Subprefecture, Guizhou. He was a tribute student of the dingmao year.

Tian You, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Lingbao County, Shan Subprefecture, Henan Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Zongdao and was from Shouzhang County, Shandong. He was a tribute student of the dingmao year.

Zhang Lu, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Chizhou Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Congyin and was from Jiangxia County, Huguang. He was a tribute student of the jiazi year.

回之爲人也擇乎中庸得一善則拳拳服

仁人心也義人路也
易
初九素履往无咎

第壹場

仁，人心也；義，人路也。

First Session

Four Books
When going out, act as though meeting an honored guest; when employing the people, act as though assisting at a great sacrifice. Do not impose on others what you yourself do not desire. In the state, incur no resentment; in the household, incur no resentment.
As a person, Hui chooses the Mean. Whenever he attains something good, he holds it close to his heart and never loses it.
Benevolence is the human heart; righteousness is the human path.

Book of Changes
Initial nine: Tread with simplicity. Going forward brings no blame.
Six in the second place: The wild goose gradually advances to the rock. Eating and drinking in contentment: auspicious.
The yarrow stalks of Qian number 216; those of Kun number 144. Together they total 360, corresponding to the days of a year. The stalks of the two parts total 11,520, corresponding to the number of the myriad things.
Changing and moving without rest, circulating through the six positions, rising and descending without constancy, the firm and yielding exchange places.

The aim of punishments is to achieve an absence of punishment.

text:

禮記
凡侍坐於大司成者遠近間三席可以問
終則負墻列事未盡不問
獨樂其志不厭其道備舉其道不私其欲
是故情見而義立樂終而德尊
盡其道端其義而教生焉
獻君君舉旅行酬而后獻卿卿舉旅行酬
一而后獻大夫大夫舉旅行酬而后獻
===

第貳場
論
脩身則道立

擬唐以長孫無忌為右僕射誥貞觀元年

punctuated:
