title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
虐小春秋譏其不義此宋兩加兵於滕皆非其
道也春秋一稱人一稱師豈無意哉且滕介於
宋敖慢不恭宋也圍之似不為過者經以人稱
說者曰刺伐喪也則凡不恭之國將置而不問
乎蓋當是時滕昭不祿變故方殷人所共憫者
也凡有仁心者必將哀矜惻怛弔恤之不暇矣
況於鄰〔壤〕之邦玉帛往来之舊乎宋不念此顧以
私忿小怨命將出師汲汲於滕之是圍焉假曰
滕不事己不為無罪盍亦思己德無乃有闕歟
===
乃乗其喪以圍之欺人之孤而不忌弱人之寡
而罔卹其與見落穽不能救反擠之而下石者
何異邪非至不仁者莫之忍為經於圍滕特以
人稱意蓋如此夫滕雖見圍負固自若宋復伐
之似無足怪者經以師稱說者曰譏用衆也則
凡負固之邦將諉而不討乎蓋當是時徵舒不
軌惡逆滔天人得而誅者也苟有仗義者必將
怒目切齒致辟之恐後矣況於上公之尊先代
伯業之餘乎宋不慮此顧以細故微瑕揚兵耀
punctuated:
虐小，《春秋》譏其不義。此宋兩加兵於滕，皆非其道也。《春秋》一稱人，一稱師，豈無意哉？且滕介於宋，敖慢不恭，宋也圍之，似不為過者。經以人稱，說者曰：「刺伐喪也。」則凡不恭之國，將置而不問乎？蓋當是時，滕昭不祿，變故方殷，人所共憫者也。凡有仁心者，必將哀矜惻怛，弔恤之不暇矣，況於鄰〔壤〕之邦，玉帛往来之舊乎？宋不念此，顧以私忿小怨，命將出師，汲汲於滕之是圍焉。假曰滕不事己，不為無罪，盍亦思己德無乃有闕歟？乃乗其喪以圍之，欺人之孤而不忌，弱人之寡而罔卹，其與見落穽不能救，反擠之而下石者，何異邪？非至不仁者，莫之忍為。經於圍滕，特以人稱，意蓋如此。
夫滕雖見圍，負固自若，宋復伐之，似無足怪者。經以師稱，說者曰：「譏用衆也。」則凡負固之邦，將諉而不討乎？蓋當是時，徵舒不軌，惡逆滔天，人得而誅者也。苟有仗義者，必將怒目切齒，致辟之恐後矣，況於上公之尊，先代伯業之餘乎？宋不慮此，顧以細故微瑕，揚兵耀
translation_en:
…oppressed the small state, and the Spring and Autumn Annals censures its unrighteousness. These two occasions on which Song took up arms against Teng were both contrary to the proper way. The Spring and Autumn Annals calls the aggressors “men” on one occasion and an “army” on the other: could this be without significance? Now Teng lay beside Song and was arrogant and disrespectful, so Song’s besieging it might seem no transgression. Yet the Classic calls the aggressors “men.” The commentators say: “This condemns attacking a state in mourning.” Then should every disrespectful state be left alone and not called to account? At that time, however, Duke Zhao of Teng had died; calamity was at its height, and all sympathized with Teng. Anyone with a benevolent heart would have been wholly occupied with grief and compassion, offering condolences and relief. How much more should this have been so for a neighboring state, long accustomed to exchanging jade and silk in diplomatic visits? Song gave no thought to this. Instead, out of private anger and petty resentment, it ordered its generals to send forth troops and hastened to besiege Teng. Granted that Teng’s failure to serve Song was not blameless, should Song not also have considered whether its own virtue was deficient? Instead, it took advantage of Teng’s mourning to besiege it, bullying its orphaned heir without restraint and further weakening its bereaved people without pity. How was this different from seeing someone fall into a pit and, instead of rescuing him, pushing him farther down and casting stones upon him? Only the utterly inhumane could bear to do such a thing. This, presumably, is why the Classic specifically uses “men” in recording the siege of Teng.
Although Teng had suffered a siege, it continued as before to rely on its fortifications, so Song’s attacking it again might seem unsurprising. Yet the Classic calls the aggressors an “army.” The commentators say: “This censures the deployment of a large force.” Then should every state that relies on its fortifications be left alone without punitive action? At that time, however, Zhengshu had acted treasonously; his wicked rebellion reached to Heaven, and anyone was entitled to put him to death. Anyone who upheld righteousness would have glared in anger and gnashed his teeth, fearing only that he might be too late to bring Zhengshu to justice. How much more should this have been so for Song, with the dignity of a senior duke and the surviving legacy of its earlier ruler’s hegemony? Song gave no thought to this. Instead, over trifling matters and minor faults, it paraded its troops and flaunted…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
武區區於滕之是伐焉借曰滕不降心在所必
討盍亦思事豈無大於此者歟乃動大衆以伐
之舍所重而務所輕棄所急而治所緩其與不
能三年之喪而緦小功之察者何殊邪非至不
義者莫之暇焉經於伐滕特以師稱意蓋如此
吁始而圍滕非仁也而春秋貶之繼而伐滕非
義也而春秋譏之然則後之用師者其可不本
於仁義哉抑考宋之伐喪非仁矣後日士匄侵
齊聞喪乃還其庶幾仁人之心乎宋之不能討
===
徵舒非義矣未幾楚莊入陳執而戮之其庶幾
仗義之舉乎又以見人心理義之天雖春秋之
世未盡泯而夷狄之國未嘗無也噫
季孫斯叔孫州仇仲孫何忌帥師伐邾取
漷東田及沂西田癸巳叔孫州仇仲孫何
忌及邾子盟于句繹哀公二年
葉應驄
同考試官教諭李 批
此題胡氏發明列書三卿書伐書取書盟責哀公之意殆盡作者體認失真率以
punctuated:
武，區區於滕之是伐焉。借曰滕不降心，在所必討，盍亦思事豈無大於此者歟？乃動大衆以伐之，舍所重而務所輕，棄所急而治所緩，其與不能三年之喪而緦小功之察者何殊邪？非至不義者莫之暇焉。經於伐滕特以師稱，意蓋如此。吁！始而圍滕，非仁也，而《春秋》貶之；繼而伐滕，非義也，而《春秋》譏之。然則後之用師者，其可不本於仁義哉？抑考宋之伐喪，非仁矣；後日士匄侵齊，聞喪乃還，其庶幾仁人之心乎？宋之不能討徵舒，非義矣；未幾楚莊入陳，執而戮之，其庶幾仗義之舉乎？又以見人心理義之天，雖春秋之世未盡泯，而夷狄之國未嘗無也。噫！

季孫斯、叔孫州仇、仲孫何忌帥師伐邾，取漷東田及沂西田。癸巳，叔孫州仇、仲孫何忌及邾子盟于句繹。哀公二年。

葉應驄。

同考試官教諭李批：此題胡氏發明列書三卿，書伐、書取、書盟，責哀公之意殆盡。作者體認失真，率以
translation_en:
…military might, preoccupied with attacking Teng alone. Even granting that Teng would not submit and had to be punished, should they not have considered whether there were matters greater than this? Yet they mobilized a great army to attack it, setting aside what mattered greatly to pursue what mattered little, neglecting urgent affairs to attend to those that could wait. How did this differ from failing to observe the three-year mourning while scrutinizing the details of the three-month and five-month mourning rites? Only the utterly unrighteous would find leisure for this. This, presumably, is why the Classic specifically uses the term “army” in recording the attack on Teng. Alas! The initial siege of Teng was inhumane, and the Spring and Autumn Annals censures it; the subsequent attack on Teng was unrighteous, and the Spring and Autumn Annals criticizes it. How, then, could those who employ armies in later ages fail to ground their actions in benevolence and righteousness? Moreover, consider that Song’s attack upon a state in mourning was inhumane. Later, Shi Gai invaded Qi, but withdrew upon hearing of its mourning: did this not approach the heart of a benevolent man? Song’s failure to punish Zheng Shu was unrighteous. Before long, King Zhuang of Chu entered Chen, seized him, and put him to death: did this not approach an act undertaken in the cause of righteousness? This further shows that the Heaven-given moral principles and righteousness within the human heart had not wholly disappeared even in the age of the Spring and Autumn Annals, nor were they ever entirely absent from the states of the Yi and Di peoples. Alas!

“Jisun Si, Shusun Zhouchou, and Zhongsun Heji led an army to attack Zhu, taking the lands east of the Huo River and west of the Yi River. On the guisi day, Shusun Zhouchou and Zhongsun Heji made a covenant with the Viscount of Zhu at Gouyi.” Second year of Duke Ai.

Ye Yingcong.

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
責邾責三卿混之而於盟邾子處又為傳所窘專以季
氏立說非矣此作得之是用錄出以破群惑
考試官教諭林批春秋五經斷案此作議
擬切當正謂老吏不如也
考試官教授陳批書法明白較之舍經任
傳者自别
兵興而失有所在春秋詳致其責信講而利有
所歸春秋特紀其實此我魯伐邾之役哀公獨
任其責而句繹之盟季孫不與其列也書法詳
===
略寧無意哉在昔季孫當國有事於邾一逞於
兵則叔孫仲孫之眾悉行一放於利則漷東沂
西之田是取既又以二卿要邾君即句繹以講
盟焉則是役也倡之者季孫和之者叔仲若何
而歸罪於哀公誠以有國者必攬權馭下而以
禮義自處也哀公得國公室不張假鈇鉞於三
卿掃元戎於四境伐國取地若罔聞知以臣抗
君略不能禁政柄於是乎隳哉贅旒千焉而成
矣况邾之於魯弔問方通何負於我轍未及息
punctuated:
責邾、責三卿混之，而於盟邾子處，又為傳所窘，專以季氏立說，非矣。此作得之，是用錄出，以破群惑。
考試官教諭林批：春秋，五經斷案。此作議擬切當，正謂老吏不如也。
考試官教授陳批：書法明白，較之舍經任傳者自别。
兵興而失有所在，春秋詳致其責；信講而利有所歸，春秋特紀其實。此我魯伐邾之役，哀公獨任其責，而句繹之盟，季孫不與其列也。書法詳略，寧無意哉？在昔季孫當國，有事於邾，一逞於兵，則叔孫、仲孫之眾悉行；一放於利，則漷東、沂西之田是取。既又以二卿要邾君，即句繹以講盟焉。則是役也，倡之者季孫，和之者叔仲，若何而歸罪於哀公？誠以有國者必攬權馭下，而以禮義自處也。哀公得國，公室不張，假鈇鉞於三卿，掃元戎於四境，伐國取地，若罔聞知；以臣抗君，略不能禁。政柄於是乎隳哉！贅旒千焉而成矣。况邾之於魯，弔問方通，何負於我？轍未及息，
translation_en:
…confusing blame directed at Zhu with blame directed at the three ministers. And where the text records the covenant with the ruler of Zhu, they are again constrained by the commentary and base their explanation exclusively on the Ji lineage. This is mistaken. The present essay gets it right; it has therefore been selected for inclusion to dispel widespread confusion.
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: The Spring and Autumn Annals is the final adjudication of the Five Classics. This essay’s deliberation and judgment are precisely fitting: one may truly say that even a seasoned judicial official could not match it.
Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: The principles governing the wording of the Annals are clearly explained. This plainly distinguishes the essay from those that abandon the classic and rely on its commentary.
When troops are raised and fault lies somewhere, the Spring and Autumn Annals sets out the responsibility in detail; when pledges of good faith are negotiated and advantage accrues somewhere, the Annals specifically records the facts. In this campaign by our state of Lu against Zhu, Duke Ai alone bears responsibility; yet at the covenant at Gouyi, Jisun was not among those present. Could the fullness and brevity of the record’s wording be without significance? Formerly, when Jisun controlled the state and undertook action against Zhu, as soon as he indulged his appetite for warfare, the forces of Shusun and Zhongsun all marched; as soon as he gave free rein to his pursuit of gain, the lands east of the Huo and west of the Yi were seized. He then used the two ministers to compel the ruler of Zhu to come to Gouyi and negotiate a covenant. Thus, in this campaign, Jisun took the lead and Shusun and Zhongsun followed. Why, then, attribute the blame to Duke Ai? It is precisely because the ruler of a state must hold authority, control his subordinates, and conduct himself according to ritual propriety and righteousness. When Duke Ai gained the state, the ducal house failed to assert itself. He lent the axes of punitive authority to the three ministers, who swept their war chariots across the borderlands. They attacked a state and seized territory, while he acted as though he had neither heard nor known of it. Ministers set themselves against a ruler, and he could do nothing to restrain them. Thus was the authority of government ruined! He became a mere pendant on the banner of state [?]. Moreover, Zhu had only just exchanged visits of condolence and inquiry with Lu. In what way had it wronged us? Before the carriage wheels had even come to rest…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而諸卿繼伐其邦以禮爲國者若是乎我之於
邾壤域相接何釁可尋伐猶未足又取地而盟
其君以義睦鄰者若是乎意權柄移則辱有不
免禮義失則物無以親將何以爲國哉故春秋
列書三卿書伐書取書盟所以詳其責也而三
卿之罪則不待於貶矣然伐既三卿同伐盟必
三卿同盟若何而獨書叔仲誠以盟者各盟其
所得而無得不與也伐邾之旅雖三卿並興而
取田之利實二卿獨得內貪邾地以自廣而據
===
非其有外結邾君以自安而犯非其分在得之
戒罔知抗尊之嫌矣顧若季孫則取同取也然
念公室四分輸我已半委之以補其不足矣何
嘗列名姓於載書伐同伐也然謂家難再遭賴
彼以脫歸之以償其私勞矣曷曾厠足跡於壇
坫意同於取而不同於得與於伐而不與於盟
豈可以無別哉故春秋不書季孫而獨書叔孫
仲孫及邾子盟所以紀其實也而季孫之情亦
不容於掩矣雖然吾於叔仲二卿姑置勿論獨
punctuated:
而諸卿繼伐其邦，以禮爲國者若是乎？我之於邾，壤域相接，何釁可尋？伐猶未足，又取地而盟其君，以義睦鄰者若是乎？意權柄移，則辱有不免；禮義失，則物無以親，將何以爲國哉？故《春秋》列書三卿，書伐、書取、書盟，所以詳其責也，而三卿之罪則不待於貶矣。
然伐既三卿同伐，盟必三卿同盟，若何而獨書叔仲？誠以盟者各盟其所得，而無得不與也。伐邾之旅，雖三卿並興，而取田之利，實二卿獨得。內貪邾地以自廣，而據非其有；外結邾君以自安，而犯非其分。在得之戒罔知，抗尊之嫌矣。顧若季孫，則取同取也，然念公室四分，輸我已半，委之以補其不足矣，何嘗列名姓於載書？伐同伐也，然謂家難再遭，賴彼以脫，歸之以償其私勞矣，曷曾厠足跡於壇坫？意同於取而不同於得，與於伐而不與於盟，豈可以無別哉？故《春秋》不書季孫，而獨書叔孫、仲孫及邾子盟，所以紀其實也，而季孫之情亦不容於掩矣。
雖然，吾於叔仲二卿姑置勿論，獨
translation_en:
…yet the ministers followed this by attacking that state. Is this how one governs a state through ritual propriety? Our territory adjoins that of Zhu: what grounds for conflict could be sought? Not content with attacking, they also seized land and made a covenant with its ruler. Is this how one maintains good relations with neighbors through righteousness? Surely, when authority passes into other hands, humiliation becomes unavoidable; when ritual propriety and righteousness are lost, there is no means of securing others’ attachment. How, then, can one govern a state? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals names the three ministers individually and records the attack, the seizure, and the covenant, setting out their responsibility in detail. Their guilt requires no further expression of condemnation.
Yet since all three ministers joined in the attack, surely all three would have joined in the covenant. Why, then, does the text name only Shusun and Zhongsun? It is because each participant covenanted over what he had acquired; one who acquired nothing did not participate. Although all three ministers mobilized together for the campaign against Zhu, only two actually enjoyed the benefit of the seized fields. At home, they coveted Zhu’s land to enlarge their own holdings, occupying what was not theirs; abroad, they bound Zhu’s ruler by covenant to secure themselves, overstepping their proper station. They disregarded the warning against acquisitiveness and incurred suspicion of defying their superior [?]. As for Jisun, he indeed joined in the seizure. Yet he reflected that, of the ducal house’s revenues divided into four shares, half already went to him, and yielded the land to make up the others’ shortfall. When was his name ever entered in the covenant document? He likewise joined in the attack. Yet he reasoned that his house had twice encountered trouble and had relied on the others to escape it; he therefore assigned the land to them as recompense for their services to his family. When did he ever set foot at the covenant altar? Surely, to share in seizing but not in acquiring, and to participate in attacking but not in covenanting, are distinctions that cannot be ignored. Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals does not name Jisun, but records only that Shusun and Zhongsun covenanted with the Viscount of Zhu. This records the actual circumstances, while also leaving Jisun’s motives impossible to conceal.
Nevertheless, I shall for the moment leave the two ministers, Shusun and Zhongsun, undiscussed, and only…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
惜乎意如逐君遺臭萬年昭公孫齊其鑒不遠
季斯既不能蓋前人之愆哀公亦不知鑒覆車
之轍見囚之禍適越之辱豈非自貽伊戚哉然
則後之為君臣者宜柰何亦曰我其立政立事
無有作福作威
禮記
獨樂其志不厭其道備舉其道不私其欲
是故情見而義立樂終而德尊
陳煥
===
===
同考試官訓導田批樂記題似易而難且作者
多在後二句欠安頓着實輙以成己成物善始善終立
破可厭此作取樂觀其深一語括之不覺意見自别且
通篇詞氣舂容殊不見有斧鑿痕是不可以
不錄也
考試官教諭林批觀子之文可以見子之
所養殆有得於樂之和者矣
考試官教授陳批樂義無出此者可作可作
原樂之為用也大著樂之所觀者深蓋為己為
punctuated:
惜乎！意如逐君，遺臭萬年；昭公孫齊，其鑒不遠。季斯既不能蓋前人之愆，哀公亦不知鑒覆車之轍，見囚之禍、適越之辱，豈非自貽伊戚哉？然則後之為君臣者宜柰何？亦曰：「我其立政立事，無有作福作威。」
《禮記》
「獨樂其志，不厭其道；備舉其道，不私其欲。是故情見而義立，樂終而德尊。」
陳煥
同考試官訓導田批：「樂記題似易而難，且作者多在後二句欠安頓着實，輙以成己成物、善始善終立破，可厭。此作取樂觀其深一語括之，不覺意見自别，且通篇詞氣舂容，殊不見有斧鑿痕，是不可以不錄也。」
考試官教諭林批：「觀子之文，可以見子之所養，殆有得於樂之和者矣。」
考試官教授陳批：「樂義無出此者，可作可作。」
原樂之為用也大，著樂之所觀者深。蓋為己為
translation_en:
…What a pity! Yiru drove out his ruler and left a name infamous for ten thousand years; Duke Zhao fled to Qi—a warning not far removed. Ji Si failed to make amends for his predecessor’s wrongdoing, while Duke Ai likewise failed to heed the warning of an overturned carriage. Were the calamity of imprisonment and the humiliation of going to Yue not troubles he brought upon himself? What, then, should later rulers and ministers do? Simply say: “Let us establish government and conduct affairs, without arrogating the power to bestow blessings or wield authority.”
Record of Rites
“He takes sole delight in his purpose and does not weary of his Way; he fully puts that Way into practice and does not pursue his desires selfishly. Thus his feelings become manifest and righteousness is established; when the music ends, his virtue is honored.”
Chen Huan
Comment by Associate Examiner Tian, Assistant Instructor: “Topics from the Record of Music seem easy but are difficult. Moreover, writers generally fail to give the final two clauses a firm and substantial treatment. They habitually frame their opening exposition in terms of ‘perfecting oneself and perfecting others’ or ‘beginning well and ending well’—a tiresome practice. This essay takes the single phrase ‘through music one observes what is profound’ to encompass the subject, and its interpretation emerges as distinctive without apparent effort. Throughout, moreover, its language and cadence are ample and unhurried, showing no trace of the axe or chisel. It could not be left unrecorded.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Reading your essay, one can perceive what you have cultivated within yourself. You seem indeed to have attained something of the harmony of music.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: “No exposition of the meaning of music surpasses this. Admirably composed, admirably composed!”
To trace the function of music is to show its greatness; to elucidate what can be observed through music is to show its profundity. For, whether for oneself or for…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
人非樂無以成其用之大也而德與義存焉者
又豈不於樂而可見哉古者樂舞之理蓋如此
且樂之道有所謂極幽不隱者矣舞之容有所
謂奮疾不拔者矣而脩己及人之道於是乎存
焉是故君子以之而為己則必歌咏以陶其情
性之正舞蹈以消其邪慢之非而悅懌之心優
游乎進脩之地者要所以養其和平之德也何
有於厭斁邪君子以之而為人〔則〕必因其情性之
失正教之歌咏以融液之因其邪慢之未消教
===
之舞蹈以動盪之而覺悟之方周悉乎誘掖之
間者要所以溥其至公之愛也肯終於獨樂邪
夫樂之為用如此則其本之所存從可知矣故
自樂之初言之先鼓警戒三步見方雖未及乎
文采節奏之飾而欣喜歡愛之情已見情之見
者一志和行成之發越也向使百體之義有未
正則情隨事遷樂以情爭而何以見其義之立
乎以樂之終言之君子好善小人聽過要不出
乎和平公愛之間而風移俗易之化以成化之
punctuated: 人，非樂無以成其用之大也。而德與義存焉者，又豈不於樂而可見哉？古者樂舞之理，蓋如此。且樂之道，有所謂極幽不隱者矣；舞之容，有所謂奮疾不拔者矣。而脩己及人之道，於是乎存焉。是故君子以之而為己，則必歌咏以陶其情性之正，舞蹈以消其邪慢之非，而悅懌之心優游乎進脩之地者，要所以養其和平之德也。何有於厭斁邪？君子以之而為人，〔則〕必因其情性之失正，教之歌咏以融液之；因其邪慢之未消，教之舞蹈以動盪之。而覺悟之方周悉乎誘掖之間者，要所以溥其至公之愛也。肯終於獨樂邪？夫樂之為用如此，則其本之所存從可知矣。故自樂之初言之，先鼓警戒，三步見方，雖未及乎文采節奏之飾，而欣喜歡愛之情已見。情之見者，一志和行成之發越也。向使百體之義有未正，則情隨事遷，樂以情爭，而何以見其義之立乎？以樂之終言之，君子好善，小人聽過，要不出乎和平公愛之間，而風移俗易之化以成。化之
translation_en:
…others: without music, its great efficacy cannot be fully realized. And how could the virtue and righteousness embodied in it fail to be discernible in music? Such, indeed, was the principle of music and dance in antiquity. Moreover, the Way of music is such that, as the saying goes, “even the most hidden is not concealed”; the movements of dance are such that “vigorous speed does not wrench one out of place.” Herein lies the Way of cultivating oneself and extending that cultivation to others.

Thus, when the gentleman uses music for his own cultivation, he must sing to nurture the correctness of his feelings and nature, and dance to dispel the faults of depravity and arrogance. His delighted heart moves at ease in the realm of advancing self-cultivation: the essential purpose is to nurture his harmonious and balanced virtue. How could there be any weariness? When the gentleman uses music for others, 〔then〕, because their feelings and nature have lost their proper direction, he teaches them singing to soften and transform them; because their depravity and arrogance have not yet been dispelled, he teaches them dancing to stir and shake them free. His methods of awakening them are comprehensive and thorough in guiding and supporting them: the essential purpose is to extend his utterly impartial love to all. Would he be content, in the end, to enjoy music alone?

Since music functions in this way, we can accordingly understand wherein its foundation lies. To speak of the beginning of a musical performance: the opening drum alerts and admonishes, and three steps display the prescribed pattern. Even before the embellishments of patterned display and rhythm appear, feelings of joy, delight, affection, and love are already manifest. These manifest feelings are entirely the expression of harmonious intent and perfected conduct. If the right ordering of all the body's parts had not been established, feelings would shift with circumstances, and music would contend with those feelings. How, then, could the establishment of righteousness be seen?

To speak of the conclusion of a musical performance: gentlemen come to love goodness, and common people heed the correction of their faults. In essence, this remains within the sphere of harmony, balance, impartiality, and love, and thus the transforming influence that alters customs and changes popular practices is accomplished. The transformation's …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
成者一反情和志之充周也向使一身之德有
未脩則以欲忘道教與民違而何以見其德之
尊乎是則成已成物之功每溢乎聲容之表而
善始善終之妙恒存乎德義之間信乎樂觀其
深矣吁是其可以僞為之哉抑求之樂舞之為
道先王所以動天地感鬼神推之政治無施不
可故足以成化善俗如古之雍熈太和所謂感
人心而天下和平要皆一德之流行無間也後
世不知出此適足以為導慾增悲之具觀之害
===
德之音祭祀弗用八佾之舞忍於僭竊者可鍳
已又何義立德尊之足云也邪
盡其道端其義而教生焉
張瀾
同考試官訓導田 批 祭統一題塲中作者
惑於下文類多泛說殊不知此篇專為祭言下
文之意蓋謂必如此絜矩方能盡道端義固非即
指絜矩為道義也恠得此篇深合經傳且法度嚴
整宜録以為學經者式
punctuated:
成者，一反情和志之充周也。向使一身之德有未脩，則以欲忘道，教與民違，而何以見其德之尊乎？是則成已成物之功，每溢乎聲容之表，而善始善終之妙，恒存乎德義之間。信乎，樂觀其深矣！吁！是其可以僞為之哉？抑求之樂舞之為道，先王所以動天地、感鬼神，推之政治，無施不可，故足以成化善俗。如古之雍熈太和，所謂感人心而天下和平，要皆一德之流行無間也。後世不知出此，適足以為導慾增悲之具。觀之害德之音，祭祀弗用；八佾之舞，忍於僭竊者，可鍳已。又何義立德尊之足云也邪？

盡其道，端其義，而教生焉。
張瀾

同考試官訓導田批：《祭統》一題，塲中作者惑於下文，類多泛說。殊不知此篇專為祭言，下文之意，蓋謂必如此絜矩，方能盡道端義，固非即指絜矩為道義也。恠得此篇深合經傳，且法度嚴整，宜録以為學經者式。
translation_en:
…the accomplishment of this transformation is wholly the full realization of returning to one’s true feelings and harmonizing one’s intentions. Had the virtue of one’s own person remained uncultivated, desire would have caused one to forget the Way, and instruction would have run counter to the people. How, then, could the exaltation of virtue have been manifest? Thus, the work of perfecting oneself and other beings always extends beyond sounds and gestures, while the subtle achievement of beginning well and ending well always resides in virtue and righteousness. Truly, through music one observes their depth! Ah! Could this possibly be counterfeited? Moreover, if we seek the Way embodied in music and dance, it was by this that the former kings moved Heaven and Earth and stirred the ghosts and spirits. Extended to government, it could be applied everywhere. It was therefore sufficient to accomplish moral transformation and improve customs. The flourishing concord and supreme harmony of antiquity—what is meant by moving people’s hearts so that all under Heaven is peaceful and harmonious—were, in essence, the uninterrupted operation of a single virtue. Later generations did not know to proceed from this and merely made music an instrument for encouraging desire and increasing sorrow. Sounds that harm virtue were excluded from sacrifices; yet some could bring themselves to usurp the dance in eight ranks. These examples offer a warning. How, then, could there be any further talk of establishing righteousness and exalting virtue?

“Fully realize its Way and set right its righteousness, and instruction arises from it.”
Zhang Lan

Comment by Associate Examiner Tian, Assistant Instructor: On this topic from “The Meaning of Sacrifices,” candidates in the examination hall were misled by the text that follows and mostly offered vague discussions. They failed to understand that this chapter speaks specifically of sacrifice. The meaning of the ensuing text is that only by thus applying the measuring square of reciprocity can one fully realize the Way and set right righteousness; it certainly does not identify the measuring square itself with the Way and righteousness. This essay [?] accords closely with the classics and their commentaries, and its composition is rigorous and orderly. It should be recorded as a model for students of the classics.

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭林批以祭講盡道端義最是
考試官教授陳批合經傳旨
祭有以順其當然斯教之所由興也蓋祭者教
之本也然有不以順於禮而致其備焉教亦何
自而興哉祭統君子之意謂夫祭之所以成教
者豈徒本於備物之謂哉亦曰求諸道義而致
其備焉耳誠以祭必有道所以達是禮之當然
循而行之者也君子則竭誠共物務盡其道而
無所遺三牲八簋之具水草陸產之陳凡所以
===
致其備者一以是爲之定制焉曾何執已見而
有所乖亂邪祭必有義所以協是禮之當然行
而宜之者也君子則因物稱情務端其義而有
所立宜少者不可多應隆者不可殺凡所以備
於物者一以是爲之裁制焉曾何徇已私而有
所加損邪夫君子盡道端義如此則其祭以嚴
上自足以感人心一念之忠祭以追養自足以
觸人心一念之孝由是已以度物教之以尊其
君長則凡臣工之效職於下莫不知尊所當尊
punctuated:
考試官教諭林批：以祭講盡道端義，最是。
考試官教授陳批：合經傳旨。
祭有以順其當然，斯教之所由興也。蓋祭者，教之本也。然有不以順於禮而致其備焉，教亦何自而興哉？《祭統》君子之意，謂夫祭之所以成教者，豈徒本於備物之謂哉？亦曰求諸道義而致其備焉耳。誠以祭必有道，所以達是禮之當然，循而行之者也。君子則竭誠共物，務盡其道而無所遺。三牲八簋之具，水草陸產之陳，凡所以致其備者，一以是爲之定制焉。曾何執已見而有所乖亂邪？祭必有義，所以協是禮之當然，行而宜之者也。君子則因物稱情，務端其義而有所立。宜少者不可多，應隆者不可殺，凡所以備於物者，一以是爲之裁制焉。曾何徇已私而有所加損邪？夫君子盡道端義如此，則其祭以嚴上，自足以感人心一念之忠；祭以追養，自足以觸人心一念之孝。由是已以度物，教之以尊其君長，則凡臣工之效職於下，莫不知尊所當尊
translation_en:
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “Explaining ‘fully realizing the Way and setting right what is fitting’ in terms of sacrifice is entirely correct.”
Examiner Chen, Director of Studies, comments: “Accords with the purport of the classics and their commentaries.”
When sacrifice accords with what is proper to it, moral instruction arises from this. For sacrifice is the foundation of moral instruction. Yet if its full provision is not achieved through conformity to ritual, how could instruction arise? The intent of the gentleman spoken of in “The Principles of Sacrifice” (Jitong) is this: does sacrifice accomplish moral instruction merely through providing all the offerings? It is simply that one seeks completeness through the Way and what is fitting.
For sacrifice necessarily has a Way: this gives expression to what is proper in these rites and is what one follows in carrying them out. The gentleman therefore exhausts his sincerity in supplying the offerings, striving to fulfill that Way without omission. The provision of the three sacrificial animals and eight gui vessels, the presentation of aquatic plants and the products of the land—all arrangements for making the offerings complete take this alone as their established standard. How could he cling to his own views and introduce disorder? Sacrifice necessarily has what is fitting: this accords with what is proper in these rites and ensures that their performance is appropriate. The gentleman therefore works through the offerings to give due expression to his feelings, striving to set right what is fitting and establish it firmly. What should be sparing must not be made abundant; what calls for lavish treatment must not be diminished. All provision of offerings takes this alone as its measure. How could he indulge his private inclinations and make additions or reductions?
When the gentleman thus fully realizes the Way and sets right what is fitting, his sacrifices, by honoring those above, are sufficient in themselves to awaken an impulse of loyalty in people’s hearts; his sacrifices, by continuing to nourish the departed, are sufficient in themselves to stir an impulse of filial devotion. Thus, taking himself as the measure of others [?], he teaches them to honor their rulers and superiors. Then all officials performing their duties below know to honor those who ought to be honored…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
事君能致其身焉所謂明君在上而諸臣服從
是已天下之教不本於祭之嚴上而生乎由是
推已及人教之以孝於其親則凡子孫之克念
於家莫不知親所當親事父母能竭其力焉所
謂崇事宗廟社稷而子孫順孝是已天下之教
不本於祭之追養而生乎夫教生於祭祭主乎
順而所以順於禮者即所以順於道義也立教
君子可不知所務哉抑又驗之天下之教固必
以祭為本而行之實存乎人故下文必舉而歸
===
乏絜矩之君子誠得其人則一德格天百神受
職至禮不讓而天下自治三代之隆尚矣竊惑
乎是禮不明於後世乃至有神君太乙瀆亂不
經太禘太嘗尊卑無序而圓丘方澤亦或分合
而無常是蓋不知禮為何物尚何望教之成也
噫
第貳塲
論
脩身則道立
punctuated:
事君能致其身焉。所謂「明君在上，而諸臣服從」，是已。天下之教，不本於祭之嚴上而生乎？由是推已及人，教之以孝於其親，則凡子孫之克念於家，莫不知親所當親，事父母能竭其力焉。所謂「崇事宗廟社稷，而子孫順孝」，是已。天下之教，不本於祭之追養而生乎？夫教生於祭，祭主乎順，而所以順於禮者，即所以順於道義也。立教君子，可不知所務哉？抑又驗之，天下之教固必以祭為本，而行之實存乎人，故下文必舉而歸乏絜矩之君子。誠得其人，則一德格天，百神受職，至禮不讓，而天下自治。三代之隆，尚矣。竊惑乎是禮不明於後世，乃至有神君太乙，瀆亂不經；太禘太嘗，尊卑無序；而圓丘方澤，亦或分合而無常。是蓋不知禮為何物，尚何望教之成也？噫！

第貳塲

論

脩身則道立
translation_en:
…and can devote their very persons to serving their ruler. This is what is meant by “When an enlightened ruler is above, all his ministers obey.” Does not the moral instruction of all under Heaven arise from the reverence for superiors embodied in sacrifice? By extending consideration of oneself to others and teaching them filial devotion to their parents, all descendants who remain mindful of their duties at home come to know whom they ought to cherish, and can exert their utmost strength in serving their parents. This is what is meant by “When the ancestral temple and the altars of Soil and Grain are served with reverence, descendants are obedient and filial.” Does not the moral instruction of all under Heaven arise from the continued nurture of the departed embodied in sacrifice? Moral instruction arises from sacrifice, and sacrifice rests principally upon accordance: that by which one accords with ritual propriety is precisely that by which one accords with the Way and righteousness. Can the gentleman who establishes moral instruction fail to know where to direct his efforts?

Consider this further: although the moral instruction of all under Heaven must be rooted in sacrifice, its actual practice depends upon the person. Thus the text below necessarily brings the matter back to the gentleman who applies the measuring square of reciprocity [?]. If the right person is indeed found, his undivided virtue reaches Heaven, the hundred spirits receive their offices, and in the highest ritual there is no yielding of precedence; all under Heaven then comes to order of itself. How exalted was the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties! Yet I am troubled that these rites were not understood in later ages. There were even the cults of Shenjun and Taiyi, profane, disorderly, and contrary to canonical norms; in the great di and chang sacrifices, the distinctions between higher and lower ranks were disordered; and the sacrifices at the Round Mound and Square Pool were sometimes separated and sometimes combined, with no fixed practice. This surely shows ignorance of what ritual propriety is. How could one still hope for moral instruction to succeed? Alas!

Second Session

Discourse

When One Cultivates Oneself, the Way Is Established

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
陳器
同考試官教諭何批連日閱卷論場文字殊無
可人意者晚得此篇議論馴雅亹亹千餘言若不出於
風簷寸晷之下者可敬也
同考試官教諭戴批論題本自平正但作者不
能體認類皆凌虛駕空率意滿紙殊為可厭晚得此卷
本旨不失而文思清新可以式後學矣
同考試官教諭吳批論場文字作者類千餘
言而馴雅者甚少惟此卷不離九經達道而命辭立意
===
自然出群是可錄也
考試官教諭林批初得前場固已知為佳
士及讀此論尤可以占胸中所養秋闈首選舍子其
誰歟
考試官教授陳批論題雖平易而作者實
難措手惟此卷不為章旨所繞而讀之灑然佳作也
治天下國家有機也有本也君子端其本
斯可以運其機而神其化矣夫天下國家
之大兆民之眾君子欲以一人之身號令
punctuated:
陳器

同考試官教諭何批：連日閱卷，論場文字殊無可人意者。晚得此篇，議論馴雅，亹亹千餘言，若不出於風簷寸晷之下者，可敬也。

同考試官教諭戴批：論題本自平正，但作者不能體認，類皆凌虛駕空，率意滿紙，殊為可厭。晚得此卷，本旨不失，而文思清新，可以式後學矣。

同考試官教諭吳批：論場文字，作者類千餘言，而馴雅者甚少。惟此卷不離九經達道，而命辭立意自然出群，是可錄也。

考試官教諭林批：初得前場，固已知為佳士；及讀此論，尤可以占胸中所養。秋闈首選，舍子其誰歟？

考試官教授陳批：論題雖平易，而作者實難措手。惟此卷不為章旨所繞，而讀之灑然，佳作也。

治天下國家，有機也，有本也。君子端其本，斯可以運其機而神其化矣。夫天下國家之大，兆民之眾，君子欲以一人之身號令
translation_en:
Chen Qi

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: For days I have been reading examination scripts, and scarcely any of the discourses has pleased me. Late in the day I came upon this essay. Its argument is measured and elegant, flowing steadily for more than a thousand words, as though it had not been composed beneath wind-swept eaves within the brief time allotted. It deserves respect.

Comment by Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor: The discourse topic is itself straightforward and balanced, but the writers have failed to grasp it. Almost all soar into empty abstraction, filling their pages with whatever comes to mind; this is thoroughly tiresome. Late in the day I came upon this script. It preserves the topic’s essential meaning, while its literary conception is lucid and fresh. It can serve as a model for later students.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: Writers of discourses generally produce more than a thousand words, but very few achieve a measured elegance. This script alone stays close to the nine guiding principles of government and the universally binding Way, while its phrasing and conception naturally stand above the rest. It merits selection.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: When I first received his script from the preceding session, I already recognized him as a fine scholar. Reading this discourse gives still further insight into what he has cultivated within himself. For first place in the autumn Provincial Examination, whom could we choose but you?

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: Although the discourse topic is plain and accessible, writers actually find it difficult to make a start. This script alone avoids becoming entangled in the meaning of the chapter, and reading it leaves one refreshed. It is an excellent composition.

In governing the realm, the state, and the family, there is a pivotal mechanism and there is a foundation. When the gentleman sets his foundation right, he can set that mechanism in motion and make his transforming influence wondrously effective. Given the vastness of the realm, the state, and the family, and the multitude of the people, the gentleman wishes, through his own person alone, to issue orders…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
指揮於其間而使之風動景從未可以強
而致也有機焉有本焉君子修其身以端
其本神其機立其表則一鼓舞振作間殆
猶風行草上無不偃仆而化行矣人徒見
其神也然不知本端於此機在於我其觀
法感化之功固已妙於不言之表而亦何
待於容力也邪孔子告哀公問政而曰脩
身道立其亦示之以本與機也請論其㫖
凡天下之事循其本執其機則所務者寡
===
而可以御煩所守者近而可以及遠若逐
末遺本事事而爲之制物物而爲之防則
吾心愈勞事物愈衆日不暇給亦徒見其
勞擾而已何以明之今夫一人之身至靜
也以一人而化一人至少也諄諄而告諭
之切切而戒飭之明遣而導之拜受而退
巳違矣况天下國家之大民物之衆欲恃
吾聰明謹吾條章嚴吾政刑驅引之使偕
歸大道不巳遠乎故夫天之生物也必敦
punctuated:
指揮於其間，而使之風動景從，未可以強而致也。有機焉，有本焉。君子修其身以端其本，神其機，立其表，則一鼓舞振作間，殆猶風行草上，無不偃仆，而化行矣。人徒見其神也，然不知本端於此，機在於我，其觀法感化之功，固已妙於不言之表，而亦何待於容力也邪？孔子告哀公問政而曰：「脩身道立。」其亦示之以本與機也。請論其㫖。
凡天下之事，循其本，執其機，則所務者寡，而可以御煩；所守者近，而可以及遠。若逐末遺本，事事而爲之制，物物而爲之防，則吾心愈勞，事物愈衆，日不暇給，亦徒見其勞擾而已。何以明之？今夫一人之身，至靜也；以一人而化一人，至少也。諄諄而告諭之，切切而戒飭之，明遣而導之，拜受而退，巳違矣。况天下國家之大，民物之衆，欲恃吾聰明，謹吾條章，嚴吾政刑，驅引之使偕歸大道，不巳遠乎？故夫天之生物也，必敦
translation_en:
…to direct and command within it, making the people respond as to the wind and follow like shadows, cannot be achieved by force. There is a pivotal mechanism, and there is a foundation. The gentleman cultivates himself to set his foundation right, works his pivotal mechanism with wondrous efficacy, and establishes himself as an example. Then, with a single act of encouragement and inspiration, it is almost as though wind were passing over grass: none fails to bend, and his transforming influence spreads. People see only its wondrous efficacy; they do not understand that the foundation is set right here, and that the pivotal mechanism lies within oneself. The work of transformation through observing and emulating his example already operates wondrously beyond words. What need, then, is there to apply force [?]? When Duke Ai asked about government, Confucius told him: “Cultivate yourself, and the Way will be established.” This, too, showed him the foundation and the pivotal mechanism. Let me discuss its meaning.
In all affairs under Heaven, if one follows the foundation and grasps the pivotal mechanism, one can manage complexity while attending to few things, and reach far while holding to what is near. If, instead, one pursues the branches and neglects the root, devising a regulation for every affair and a precaution for every thing, one's mind grows ever more weary and one's affairs ever more numerous. There are not enough hours in the day, and all one achieves is exhausting turmoil. How can this be demonstrated? Consider a single person: in himself, he is utterly still; for one person to transform one other is an undertaking of the smallest scope. Yet even if one earnestly instructs him, urgently admonishes him, and clearly directs and guides him [?], he bows, accepts the instruction, and withdraws, only to disobey it already. How much more is this so with the vastness of all under Heaven, the states, and the ruling houses, and the multitude of people and things! If I wish to rely on my intelligence, make my regulations exact, and make my administration and punishments strict, driving and leading people so that all return together to the Great Way, am I not already far from the goal? Thus, when Heaven brings living things into being, it must make abundant…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
厚其化而後形者形色者色若物物而雕
刻之則不能矣戶之啓閉也必圓轉其樞
而後左則左右則右若時時而上下之則
不能矣君子之於天下國家不端其本執
其機而亦何能神其化也邪且吾以一人
之身立乎萬民之上有所言論震若雷霆
有所作為明並日月過言過動下之人得
於觀法視效之餘固已深入於心而不可
解矣乃為之條章立之法制驅之而從於
===
善所令反於所好其誰聽從之邪故君子
知機在於我本在於身而身不可以不脩
也身之所主者心而內不可以不一也內既
一而衣服容儀不可以不飭也敬以自守
動由於規矩之中禮以自防務立於無過
之地凡有一言必擬之而後言惟恐過言
而招尤凡舉一事必議之而後動惟恐過
動而招悔姦聲亂色不敢留於聰明淫樂
慝禮不敢接於心術惰慢邪僻之氣不敢
punctuated: 厚其化，而後形者形，色者色。若物物而雕刻之，則不能矣。戶之啓閉也，必圓轉其樞，而後左則左，右則右。若時時而上下之，則不能矣。君子之於天下國家，不端其本、執其機，而亦何能神其化也邪？且吾以一人之身，立乎萬民之上，有所言論，震若雷霆；有所作為，明並日月。過言過動，下之人得於觀法視效之餘，固已深入於心而不可解矣。乃為之條章，立之法制，驅之而從於善，所令反於所好，其誰聽從之邪？故君子知機在於我，本在於身，而身不可以不脩也。身之所主者心，而內不可以不一也。內既一，而衣服容儀不可以不飭也。敬以自守，動由於規矩之中；禮以自防，務立於無過之地。凡有一言，必擬之而後言，惟恐過言而招尤；凡舉一事，必議之而後動，惟恐過動而招悔。姦聲亂色，不敢留於聰明；淫樂慝禮，不敢接於心術；惰慢邪僻之氣，不敢
translation_en:
…give fullness to its transforming activity; only then do things take their forms and assume their colors. If Heaven were to carve and fashion each thing individually, it could not accomplish this. For a door to open and close, its pivot must turn freely; only then will it move left when directed left and right when directed right. If one were constantly to raise and lower it, this could not be accomplished. In governing all under Heaven, the state, and the family, how can the gentleman make his transforming influence wondrously effective unless he sets the root right and grasps the pivotal mechanism? Moreover, I stand as a single person above the myriad people. Whatever I say resounds like thunder; whatever I do shines alongside the sun and moon. As those below observe and emulate me, my errant words and actions have already entered deeply into their hearts and cannot be dislodged. If I then draw up regulations for them, establish laws and institutions, and drive them to follow goodness, my commands will contradict my own preferences. Who will heed and obey them?

Thus the gentleman knows that the pivotal mechanism lies in himself and that the root lies in his own person: he cannot fail to cultivate himself. What governs the person is the heart, so his inner life must be unified. Once it is unified, his clothing, appearance, and bearing must also be put in order. He maintains himself through reverence, keeping his movements within the bounds of proper standards; he guards himself through ritual propriety, striving to place himself beyond fault. Whenever he has a word to say, he weighs it before speaking, fearing only that a mistaken utterance may invite blame. Whenever he undertakes a matter, he deliberates before acting, fearing only that a mistaken action may bring regret. He dares not let corrupt sounds and disorderly sights linger in his hearing and vision; he dares not let licentious music and depraved rites touch the workings of his heart; and he dares not allow the impulses of indolence, arrogance, perversity, and depravity…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
施於四體深宮得肆之地所以謹飭而防
閑者無異於大廷清廟之上ㄧ念萌動之
天所以省察而克治者無異於十手十目
之間好學以為知力行以為仁知恥以為
勇語父子則極其仁語君臣則極其義語
夫婦長幼朋友無不各止其極而五倫備
矣由是身修行立道成德尊以之而親師
友則賢否明以之而處家人則九族睦以
之而待小大之臣各得其情以之而治庶
===
民百工各安其分以之而御諸侯遠人各
歸其德而懷其仁出乎身而加乎民動不
離於規矩發乎邇而見乎遠舉不踰於法
度人誰不有父子舍吾何以為親人誰不
有君臣舍吾何以為義人誰不有夫婦長
幼朋友舍吾何以求其序別信焉譬之表
立於此本身而家自家而朝廷而國而天
下咸於我乎取正所謂動而世為天下道
行而世為天下法言而世為天下則者是
punctuated: 施於四體。深宮得肆之地，所以謹飭而防閑者，無異於大廷清廟之上；ㄧ念萌動之天，所以省察而克治者，無異於十手十目之間。好學以為知，力行以為仁，知恥以為勇。語父子，則極其仁；語君臣，則極其義；語夫婦、長幼、朋友，無不各止其極，而五倫備矣。由是身修行立，道成德尊。以之而親師友，則賢否明；以之而處家人，則九族睦；以之而待小大之臣，各得其情；以之而治庶民百工，各安其分；以之而御諸侯遠人，各歸其德而懷其仁。出乎身而加乎民，動不離於規矩；發乎邇而見乎遠，舉不踰於法度。人誰不有父子？舍吾何以為親？人誰不有君臣？舍吾何以為義？人誰不有夫婦、長幼、朋友？舍吾何以求其序、別、信焉？譬之表立於此，本身而家，自家而朝廷而國而天下，咸於我乎取正。所謂「動而世為天下道，行而世為天下法，言而世為天下則」者，是
translation_en:
…be expressed in the four limbs. In the depths of the palace, where one could indulge oneself, the care taken to remain circumspect and guard against wrongdoing is no different from that exercised in the great court or the august ancestral temple. At the instant when a single thought begins to stir, the scrutiny and discipline applied to oneself are no different from those exercised amid ten pointing hands and ten watching eyes. Through a love of learning one develops wisdom; through strenuous practice, benevolence; and through a sense of shame, courage. In the relationship between father and son, one brings benevolence to its utmost; in that between ruler and minister, righteousness. In the relationships between husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends, each attains its highest standard, and thus the five human relationships are fully realized.

From this, the person is cultivated and conduct established; the Way is perfected and virtue held in honor. Applying this to one's association with teachers and friends, one distinguishes the worthy from the unworthy. Applying it to dealings with family members, one brings harmony to the nine degrees of kinship. Applying it to the treatment of ministers, great and small, one responds appropriately to each one's circumstances. Applying it to governing the common people and the various artisans, one enables each to rest content in their allotted role. Applying it to ruling the regional lords and people from afar, one causes each to turn toward one's virtue and cherish one's benevolence. What proceeds from one's person and reaches the people never departs, in any movement, from the compass and square of proper conduct. What begins nearby and manifests itself afar never exceeds, in any undertaking, the prescribed standards.

Who among people does not stand in the relationship of father and son? Without my example, how could they practice familial affection? Who does not stand in the relationship of ruler and minister? Without my example, how could they practice righteousness? Who does not stand in the relationships of husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends? Without my example, how could they seek the proper order, distinctions, and trustworthiness in these relationships? It is like a measuring post erected here: beginning with one's own person and extending to the family, and from the family to the court, the state, and all under Heaven, all take their standard of rectitude from me. What is meant by the saying, “In his movements he becomes for generations a guide for all under Heaven; in his conduct he becomes for generations a model for all under Heaven; in his words he becomes for generations a standard for all under Heaven,” is this…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也視效之餘不言而喻感化之妙不疾而
速吾但垂衣裳於九五之尊動容貌於穆
清之上一鼓舞一轉移之間天下固已從
風而靡矣尚何假於區區刑賞法制之具
諄諄言語告誡之末乎雖以魯國微弱勉
強而力行之端其本執其機神其化固可
以柔遠人而懷諸侯孔子之論不徒託之
空言惜乎哀公知問而不知用也抑孔子
告哀公以九經而天下國家之本在身是
===
脩身一言實為九者之本而其身之所以
脩者有要焉亦曰誠而已能主於誠則知
身之當脩而求其所以脩雖曰齊明盛服
非禮不動而日用事物之微動靜食息之
末何者為禮何者非禮必辨析而講明之
則所向不差而可以無過舉矣親親也尊
賢也敬大臣也體群臣也子庶民也來百
工也柔遠人也懷諸侯也尚何舉而不當
哉是脩身為九經之本而明善又為脩身
punctuated: 也。視效之餘，不言而喻；感化之妙，不疾而速。吾但垂衣裳於九五之尊，動容貌於穆清之上，一鼓舞、一轉移之間，天下固已從風而靡矣。尚何假於區區刑賞法制之具、諄諄言語告誡之末乎？雖以魯國微弱，勉強而力行之，端其本，執其機，神其化，固可以柔遠人而懷諸侯。孔子之論，不徒託之空言。惜乎哀公知問而不知用也！抑孔子告哀公以九經，而天下國家之本在身，是脩身一言實為九者之本。而其身之所以脩者有要焉，亦曰誠而已。能主於誠，則知身之當脩，而求其所以脩。雖曰齊明盛服，非禮不動，而日用事物之微、動靜食息之末，何者為禮，何者非禮，必辨析而講明之，則所向不差，而可以無過舉矣。親親也，尊賢也，敬大臣也，體群臣也，子庶民也，來百工也，柔遠人也，懷諸侯也，尚何舉而不當哉？是脩身為九經之本，而明善又為脩身
translation_en:
…such is the case. As people observe and emulate him, they understand without his speaking; through the subtle power of moral transformation, results come swiftly without haste. I need only let my robes hang down in the exalted position of the sovereign and maintain a dignified bearing in the serene purity of the court: with each act of inspiration and redirection, all under Heaven will already have bent like grass before the wind. What further need is there for the petty instruments of punishments, rewards, laws, and regulations, or the lesser expedients of repeated verbal admonitions? Even with Lu's weakness and small size, if its ruler exerted himself to put this into practice, set the foundation right, grasped the crucial means, and made his transforming influence wondrously effective, he could indeed conciliate people from afar and win the allegiance of the feudal lords. Confucius's teaching was no mere empty talk. Alas, Duke Ai knew to ask, but did not know to put it into practice!

Now, Confucius instructed Duke Ai in the nine guiding principles, yet the foundation of governing all under Heaven, the state, and the family lies in one's own person. Thus the single injunction to cultivate oneself is truly the foundation of all nine. There is, moreover, an essential means of cultivating oneself: sincerity, and nothing more. If one takes sincerity as one's governing principle, one will recognize that one must cultivate oneself and seek the means to do so. Although it is said, “Be purified and clear-minded, wear proper ceremonial dress, and make no movement contrary to ritual propriety,” one must still distinguish and explain clearly what accords with ritual propriety and what does not, even in the minutiae of everyday affairs and the smallest details of movement, rest, eating, and repose. Then one's course will not go astray, and one's actions can be free from error. Showing affection to one's kin, honoring the worthy, respecting the great ministers, showing consideration for the body of officials, treating the common people as one's children, attracting the various artisans, conciliating people from afar, and winning the allegiance of the feudal lords—what action, then, could fail to be appropriate? Thus self-cultivation is the foundation of the nine guiding principles, while understanding goodness is in turn the foundation of self-cultivation…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之本其要則主於一誠故曰凡爲天下國
家有九經所以行之者一也
表
擬宋起太師文彥博平章軍國重事班宰
相上謝表元祐元年
陸鈳
同考試官教諭唐批起用宿德元老是元祐
初盛事讀是表令人躍然
同考試官教諭蔡批人主重宗社之計而倚
===
毗老臣老臣念祖宗之恩而忠愛君上是作具見
此意錄之不專以其辭也
同考試官教諭郝批詞意並佳
考試官教諭林批得四六體而意勝之
可敬可敬
考試官教授陳批典麗宜錄
元祐元年四月某日臣彥博伏蒙
聖慈起臣以太師平章軍國重事班宰相上者
臣誠惶誠恐稽首頓首
punctuated:
之本，其要則主於一誠。故曰：「凡爲天下國家有九經，所以行之者一也。」

表

擬宋起太師文彥博平章軍國重事班宰相上謝表。元祐元年。
陸鈳

同考試官教諭唐批：「起用宿德元老，是元祐初盛事。讀是表，令人躍然。」

同考試官教諭蔡批：「人主重宗社之計而倚毗老臣，老臣念祖宗之恩而忠愛君上。是作具見此意，錄之不專以其辭也。」

同考試官教諭郝批：「詞意並佳。」

考試官教諭林批：「得四六體，而意勝之。可敬，可敬！」

考試官教授陳批：「典麗，宜錄。」

元祐元年四月某日，臣彥博伏蒙聖慈起臣以太師平章軍國重事，班宰相上者。臣誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。
translation_en:
…the foundation; the essential point is to make sincerity alone the guiding principle. Thus it is said: “There are nine guiding principles for governing the world, states, and families; that by which they are put into practice is one.”

Memorial

A thanksgiving memorial composed in the voice of Wen Yanbo of the Song, upon his recall as Grand Preceptor to deliberate on important military and state affairs, with precedence above the chief councilors. First year of the Yuanyou reign [1086].
By Lu Ke 陸鈳.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “The recall of a venerable elder of long-established virtue was a splendid event at the beginning of the Yuanyou reign. Reading this memorial makes one leap with delight.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: “The ruler attaches great weight to plans for preserving the ancestral temples and altars of state, and relies upon an elderly minister. The elderly minister remembers the grace of the imperial ancestors and serves his sovereign with loyalty and affection. This composition fully conveys these sentiments. It has been selected for inclusion not solely for its wording.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Hao, Instructor: “Both wording and meaning are excellent.”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “It captures the form of four-and-six-character parallel prose, yet its meaning surpasses its formal accomplishment. Admirable, admirable!”

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: “Classically elegant and ornate; worthy of inclusion.”

On a certain day of the fourth month of the first year of Yuanyou, your servant Yanbo has humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious command recalling me as Grand Preceptor to deliberate on important military and state affairs, with precedence above the chief councilors. Your servant, in deepest awe and fear, bows his head to the ground and kowtows…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
上言伏以朔輝紫極台階垂象于三師𠈁
羽
玉墀風采具瞻乎百辟顧舊銜之尚在而新
寵之洊加居公孤輔弼之先任彌綸參賛之
大幸非承乏懼益增慚盖必有不世之賢
斯可稱非常之任故商相有待於巖築而
三公不備於周官伏念臣彦博性本迂愚才
非經濟甫登仕版旋領州麾随事以就功
名矢心而圖報稱一資一級漸叨两府之
===
===
榮屢仆屢興不替
三朝之眷覩四時之有序敢戀
恩私慕二疏之見幾乞全骸骨濯纓伊洛喜
心志與俱清結社耆英訝鬚眉之盡白惟
宴閒之為幸付黜陟於不聞詎意衰殘復
蒙
甄拔兹盖伏遇
○○○
春秋鼎盛
punctuated:
上言：伏以朔輝紫極，台階垂象于三師；𠈁羽玉墀，風采具瞻乎百辟。顧舊銜之尚在，而新寵之洊加。居公孤輔弼之先，任彌綸參賛之大。幸非承乏，懼益增慚。盖必有不世之賢，斯可稱非常之任。故商相有待於巖築，而三公不備於周官。
伏念臣彦博，性本迂愚，才非經濟。甫登仕版，旋領州麾。随事以就功名，矢心而圖報稱。一資一級，漸叨两府之榮；屢仆屢興，不替三朝之眷。覩四時之有序，敢戀恩私？慕二疏之見幾，乞全骸骨。濯纓伊洛，喜心志與俱清；結社耆英，訝鬚眉之盡白。惟宴閒之為幸，付黜陟於不聞。詎意衰殘，復蒙甄拔。
兹盖伏遇○○○，春秋鼎盛。
translation_en:
… submits these words: I humbly consider that radiance shines upon the Purple Pole [?], and the Three Steps constellation displays the celestial counterparts of the Three Preceptors; upon the jade palace steps, 𠈁羽 [?], bearing and distinction are beheld by all the officials. My former title still remains, yet fresh favor has repeatedly been bestowed. I stand foremost among the Three Dukes and Three Solitary Dignitaries who assist the throne, bearing the great responsibility of coordinating affairs and aiding governance. Fortunate though I am not merely to fill a vacancy, my apprehension only deepens my shame. Only a worthy man such as appears but rarely can prove equal to an extraordinary appointment. Thus the Shang minister had to be sought among the builders at the cliffs, while the offices of the Three Dukes in the Offices of Zhou were not always all filled.
I humbly reflect that I, your servant Yanbo, am by nature impractical and foolish, and possess no talent for ordering the realm. Soon after entering official service, I received command of a prefecture. In each affair I sought to accomplish something worthy, pledging my heart to repay your favor fittingly. Rank by rank and grade by grade, I gradually received the undeserved honor of serving in the two chief councils. Repeatedly cast down and raised up again, I never lost the favor of three successive reigns. Seeing that the four seasons follow their proper sequence, how could I cling to personal favor? Admiring the two Shu for recognizing when to withdraw, I begged leave to retire with my person intact. Washing my cap strings in the Yi and Luo rivers, I rejoiced that my heart and aspirations grew clear along with their waters; joining a society of venerable worthies, I marveled that our beards and eyebrows were all white. I counted peaceful retirement alone my good fortune, taking no heed of dismissals and promotions. Who could have imagined that, decrepit as I am, I would again be singled out for appointment?
This is because I have humbly had the good fortune to encounter ○○○ [the sovereign’s designation is missing or unclear], in the prime of life …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
睿知夙成紹述
列聖之洪謨有因有革密邇
太皇之至訓克長克君剙新法而海宇騰歡去
儉人而仕途清軌首納元寮之薦深惟輔
德之言謂老臣寔繫天命而屬人心雖靖
恭可服四夷而尊中國濟事則日知不足
成功則歲計有餘曽無敝冕之嫌遂辱安
車之
召且
憫龍鍾之已甚更
加禮遇之過隆軍國平章細事不煩念慮
殿庭趨拜崇階特邁班行兩月始預
經筵六日一朝
斧扆禮不責全於筋骨人惟求舊於遺忘是
固
天地之洪恩而實
帝王之盛節臣敢不黽策頹齡對揚
休命譬息肩之已乆而重任曷辭慨髀肉之
punctuated:
睿知夙成，紹述列聖之洪謨，有因有革；密邇太皇之至訓，克長克君。剙新法而海宇騰歡，去儉人而仕途清軌。首納元寮之薦，深惟輔德之言，謂老臣寔繫天命而屬人心。雖靖恭可服四夷而尊中國，濟事則日知不足，成功則歲計有餘。曽無敝冕之嫌，遂辱安車之召。且憫龍鍾之已甚，更加禮遇之過隆。軍國平章，細事不煩念慮；殿庭趨拜，崇階特邁班行。兩月始預經筵，六日一朝斧扆。禮不責全於筋骨，人惟求舊於遺忘。是固天地之洪恩，而實帝王之盛節。
臣敢不黽策頹齡，對揚休命！譬息肩之已乆，而重任曷辭；慨髀肉之
translation_en:
…Your sagely wisdom matured early. You carry forward the grand designs of the successive sage emperors, retaining some practices and reforming others; closely following the supreme instructions of the Grand Emperor, you prove yourself both leader and sovereign. You institute new laws, and the whole realm rejoices; you remove the parsimonious men [?], and official careers follow a pure course. First you accepted the recommendation of your chief ministers, giving profound consideration to their words concerning assistance to your virtue. You declared that this old servant truly helps secure Heaven’s Mandate and unite the people’s hearts. Although reverent service can bring the peoples of the four quarters into submission and uphold the Central Kingdom, in carrying out affairs I daily recognize my shortcomings; in assessing accomplishments, however, the year’s reckoning shows a surplus. You did not disdain an old ceremonial cap, and thus graciously summoned me in a carriage in which I could ride seated.
Moreover, pitying my extreme decrepitude, you bestowed still more generous ceremonial honors. In deliberations on military and state affairs, you spare me the burden of attending to minor matters; when I approach and bow in the palace court, my exalted rank places me especially above the assembled officials. Only after two months do I participate in the Classics Colloquium, and once every six days I attend court before the imperial throne. In matters of ceremony, you do not demand full performance from my aging limbs; in choosing a man, you value long service despite forgetfulness. This is indeed a vast kindness like that of Heaven and Earth, and truly an emperor’s magnificent virtue.
How dare your servant fail to spur on his declining years and gratefully uphold your gracious command! Though I have long rested my shoulders, how could I decline a heavy responsibility? Lamenting that the flesh of my thighs …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
復生而據鞍思奮將見逼桑榆之晩皆為
効犬馬之年眇以求明快覩
太平之治前而復却尚追彙進之踪庶一言
以興邦有懷未泯假衆工而集事舊墨猶
存雖勵已之志未衰懼報
君之日已短伏願
緝熙聖學唯先正心
總攬乾綱永懷論相冀真才之必得期
大業以日隆
===
天休至而克堪周召釋二人之懼
君道成而勇退阿衡作一德之書
宗社靈長引歷年於勿替
明良終始歌
帝德以無疆臣彦博無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
punctuated: 復生而據鞍思奮，將見逼桑榆之晩，皆為効犬馬之年。眇以求明，快覩太平之治；前而復却，尚追彙進之踪。庶一言以興邦，有懷未泯；假衆工而集事，舊墨猶存。雖勵已之志未衰，懼報君之日已短。伏願緝熙聖學，唯先正心；總攬乾綱，永懷論相。冀真才之必得，期大業以日隆。天休至而克堪，周召釋二人之懼；君道成而勇退，阿衡作一德之書。宗社靈長，引歷年於勿替；明良終始，歌帝德以無疆。臣彦博無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以
translation_en:
…having grown back, I think of mounting the saddle and rousing myself to action. Thus even these years approaching the twilight of life shall all be years of devoted service, like that of a dog or horse. Though dim of sight, I seek clear vision, rejoicing to behold an age of great peace; though advancing and then drawing back, I still follow the footsteps of worthy men advancing together. Hoping that a single word may help the state flourish, I have not relinquished my aspirations; relying on the assembled officials to accomplish affairs, I still retain the old guiding lines. Though my determination to exert myself has not waned, I fear that my days for repaying my sovereign are already few.

I humbly pray that, in making Your sacred learning ever more luminous, You give first place to rectifying the mind; and that, in holding supreme authority over government, You always attend to the selection of chief councillors. I hope that men of true ability will assuredly be found and that Your great undertaking will flourish day by day. When Heaven’s blessings arrive and can be sustained, the fears of the two men, the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao, will be dispelled; when the sovereign’s Way is perfected and his minister resolutely retires, Aheng will compose the writing on Single Virtue. May the dynastic ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain endure in sacred potency, extending their years without decline; may the enlightened sovereign and his worthy ministers remain united from beginning to end, singing of imperial virtue without limit.

Your servant Yanbo, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, cannot contain his intense emotion and utmost awe and trepidation. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude and thereby…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聞
第叁塲
策
第一問
鄭蒙吉
同考試官教諭唐批初塲文勢滂沛論又有
波瀾至五策洶洶湧出而
聖製一策各遡源委非有本者不能如是噫子其衆水之滄海歟
同考試官教諭蔡批我
===
朝
聖製輝煌照耀今古真與二帝三王之德業同符合轍此策能鋪陳其盛
而揚厲于数言之間其亦漸染
聖化之深者與
同考試官教諭郝批此策能鋪叙我
孝宗皇帝制作之盛而末又以正心結之蓋有志於經世非沉酣口耳
者能到
考試官教諭林批鋪張
聖訓超越前代有識之士也
punctuated:
聞。

第叁塲
策
第一問
鄭蒙吉

同考試官教諭唐批：初塲文勢滂沛，論又有波瀾，至五策，洶洶湧出，而聖製一策，各遡源委，非有本者不能如是。噫！子其衆水之滄海歟？

同考試官教諭蔡批：我朝聖製，輝煌照耀今古，真與二帝三王之德業同符合轍。此策能鋪陳其盛，而揚厲于数言之間，其亦漸染聖化之深者與？

同考試官教諭郝批：此策能鋪叙我孝宗皇帝制作之盛，而末又以正心結之，蓋有志於經世，非沉酣口耳者能到。

考試官教諭林批：鋪張聖訓，超越前代，有識之士也。
translation_en:
…for Your Majesty’s information.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Zheng Mengji

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: The writing in the first session flowed abundantly, and the discourse, too, had surging waves. By the five policy essays, his words poured forth in a mighty torrent; in the essay on imperial compositions, he traced each matter from its source through its subsequent course. Only someone with a firm foundation could achieve this. Ah! Are you perhaps the vast ocean into which all waters flow?

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: The imperial compositions of our dynasty shine brilliantly across past and present. They truly accord with the virtue and achievements of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, as matching tallies fit together and wheels follow the same track. This policy essay fully sets forth their splendor and extols it in a few words. Surely its author, too, has been deeply imbued with the sage sovereign’s transforming influence!

Comment by Associate Examiner Hao, Instructor: This policy essay fully describes the flourishing achievements in institutions and compositions under our Emperor Xiaozong, and concludes with rectifying the mind. Its author clearly aspires to bring order to the world. Such an accomplishment is beyond those engrossed in merely repeating what they hear.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: He expansively sets forth the sage sovereign’s teachings, which surpass those of earlier dynasties. He is a man of discernment.

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授陳批我
孝宗制作之盛前代罕比此篇能條對詳盡非素服膺者不能
聖人繼治而守文不惟有全盛之治功而尤有
大備之制作治功之全盛者見之於當時
而天下有以蒙其仁制作之大備者垂之
於後世而後世有以被其澤於乎傳稱功
業之隆悠遠以致高厚高厚又悠久者於
此足徵矣請因明問而敬陳之昔者
高皇帝之興也殪滅群兇肅清中夏
駿德神功與天地同其大典章文物與日月
同其明制作之盛有
祖訓
大誥
諸司職掌諸書自古創業之君所未遑也
太宗文皇帝克纘武功益隆文治又有
聖學心法
孝順事實之作
宣宗章皇帝統承大業脩明百度又有五倫書
punctuated:
考試官敎授陳批：我孝宗制作之盛，前代罕比。此篇能條對詳盡，非素服膺者不能。
聖人繼治而守文，不惟有全盛之治功，而尤有大備之制作。治功之全盛者，見之於當時，而天下有以蒙其仁；制作之大備者，垂之於後世，而後世有以被其澤。於乎！傳稱功業之隆，悠遠以致高厚，高厚又悠久者，於此足徵矣。請因明問而敬陳之。昔者高皇帝之興也，殪滅群兇，肅清中夏，駿德神功與天地同其大，典章文物與日月同其明。制作之盛，有《祖訓》《大誥》《諸司職掌》諸書，自古創業之君所未遑也。太宗文皇帝克纘武功，益隆文治，又有《聖學心法》《孝順事實》之作。宣宗章皇帝統承大業，脩明百度，又有《五倫書》
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Chen, an Instructor: The splendor of our Emperor Xiaozong’s institutional and literary achievements has seldom been matched in earlier dynasties. This essay answers the questions point by point, fully and thoroughly—something possible only for one who has long taken these matters to heart.
When a sage succeeds to the governance of the realm and preserves its established institutions, he achieves not only consummate success in government but also an especially comprehensive body of institutions and writings. His consummate achievements in government manifest themselves in his own time, enabling all under Heaven to enjoy his benevolence; his comprehensive institutions and writings are handed down to later generations, enabling posterity to receive his beneficence. Ah! The commentary speaks of the grandeur of meritorious achievement extending far and long, attaining height and depth, and, through height and depth, enduring still longer. Here this is amply borne out. Allow me respectfully to set forth my response to your illuminating question.
In former times, when Emperor Gao arose, he annihilated the host of villains and restored peace throughout the central realm. His great virtue and wondrous achievements equaled Heaven and Earth in grandeur; his institutions and cultural accomplishments equaled the sun and moon in brilliance. Among his magnificent institutional and literary productions were such books as the Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun), the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao), and the Duties of the Various Offices (Zhusi zhizhang)—works that founding rulers since antiquity had never found the opportunity to undertake. Emperor Taizong Wen successfully continued these martial achievements and further enhanced civil governance; he also produced the Essential Method of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa) and Records of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi). Emperor Xuanzong Zhang inherited the great imperial enterprise and put the full range of institutions into good order; there was also the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu)…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之作凡此皆自古守成之君所難能也猗
歟休哉迨于
英宗嘗有條格之作未及成書而中已之豈亦
若有待者邪我
孝宗敬皇帝以天縱之資撫盈成之運緝煕
聖學達于古今躬親萬機明燭幽隱一十八
年之間深仁厚澤洽民肌膚大化旁流無
遠弗届守成之業於是乎至而無以復加
矣所謂全盛之治功者不在是哉然自
===
國初以來百司庶務之繁几閣文書之富日
就散漫遂
命儒臣纂集成編名曰會典遠有所取自洪
武戊申之歲近有所稽迄弘治壬戌之秋
主之以
諸司職掌類之以
頒降群書附之以歷年事例大綱槩舉而官
職制度寓焉衆目畢張而名數儀文繫焉
始於宗人府終于兩京諸衞其凡一百有
punctuated:
之作。凡此皆自古守成之君所難能也。猗歟休哉！迨于英宗，嘗有條格之作，未及成書而中已之，豈亦若有待者邪？我孝宗敬皇帝以天縱之資，撫盈成之運，緝煕聖學，達于古今，躬親萬機，明燭幽隱。一十八年之間，深仁厚澤洽民肌膚，大化旁流，無遠弗届。守成之業於是乎至，而無以復加矣。所謂全盛之治功者，不在是哉？
然自國初以來，百司庶務之繁，几閣文書之富，日就散漫，遂命儒臣纂集成編，名曰《會典》。遠有所取，自洪武戊申之歲；近有所稽，迄弘治壬戌之秋。主之以《諸司職掌》，類之以頒降群書，附之以歷年事例。大綱槩舉，而官職制度寓焉；衆目畢張，而名數儀文繫焉。始於宗人府，終于兩京諸衞，其凡一百有
translation_en:
…was also composed. All these were achievements difficult even for the rulers of antiquity who preserved an inherited realm. Ah, how splendid! In Yingzong’s reign, work was undertaken on a compilation of regulations, but it was halted before the book could be completed. Was this perhaps also awaiting its proper time? Our Emperor Xiaozong Jing, endowed by Heaven, presided over an age of established prosperity. He continually cultivated and illuminated his sagely learning, comprehending antiquity and the present; he personally attended to the myriad affairs of government, his discernment illuminating even what was hidden and obscure. Over eighteen years, his profound benevolence and abundant bounty penetrated the people’s very flesh and skin. His great transforming influence spread everywhere, reaching even the remotest places. The work of preserving the inherited realm thus attained a height beyond which nothing could be added. Was this not what is called the achievement of government in its fullest flourishing?
Yet since the dynasty’s founding, the manifold business of the many offices and the abundant documents on desks and in repositories had become increasingly scattered and disordered. He therefore commanded scholarly officials to gather and compile them into a work entitled Collected Statutes (Huidian). Its sources extended back to the wushen year of Hongwu (1368), and its examination of more recent material reached the autumn of the renxu year of Hongzhi (1502). It took the Duties of the Various Offices (Zhusi zhizhang) as its foundation, arranged material from the various imperially promulgated books by category, and appended precedents from successive years. Its main outlines encompass official posts and institutions; its detailed headings fully set forth the prescribed designations and numbers, ceremonial observances, and formal usages. It begins with the Court of the Imperial Clan and ends with the guards of the two capitals, numbering in all one hundred and…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
七均事實以分其卷多或析之少或合之
其凡百有八十如
大明律服制有圖則仍附禮部如詹事府職
掌未載則系以春坊六部之建置沿革總
書於吏部五府之建置沿革總書于中府
朝廷之
詔勅臣下之
奏議有增革沿罷者則直書之其事繫於年
或年繫於事則指事分款而連書之自有
===
載籍以来未有是典之明且備也開局之
年為弘治丁巳至正德辛未
今上皇帝孝隆繼述乃
命儒臣校正而刋布焉天下臣工争先快覩
信乎獲之者如拱璧蔵之者為世寶也明
問又欲聞夫今日臣工誦而習之體而行
之之要生也不敏敢出位而妄言邪竊嘗
窺之矣總建六部分設諸司則六卿不可
不知率屬之義政以類分事各責成則庶
punctuated:
七。均事實以分其卷，多或析之，少或合之，其凡百有八十。如《大明律》服制有圖，則仍附禮部；如詹事府職掌未載，則系以春坊。六部之建置沿革，總書於吏部；五府之建置沿革，總書于中府。朝廷之詔勅、臣下之奏議，有增革沿罷者，則直書之。其事繫於年，或年繫於事，則指事分款而連書之。自有載籍以来，未有是典之明且備也。開局之年為弘治丁巳，至正德辛未，今上皇帝孝隆繼述，乃命儒臣校正而刋布焉。天下臣工争先快覩，信乎獲之者如拱璧，蔵之者為世寶也。
明問又欲聞夫今日臣工誦而習之、體而行之之要。生也不敏，敢出位而妄言邪？竊嘗窺之矣。總建六部，分設諸司，則六卿不可不知率屬之義；政以類分，事各責成，則庶
translation_en:
…seven in all. The material was apportioned among the volumes: where abundant, it might be divided; where scant, it might be combined. There were 180 volumes in all. For example, the diagrams of mourning attire in the Great Ming Code were retained under the Ministry of Rites; where the duties of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent were not recorded, they were appended under the Secretariats of the Heir Apparent. The establishment and institutional changes of the Six Ministries were recorded together under the Ministry of Personnel; those of the Five Chief Military Commissions were recorded together under the Central Chief Military Commission. Imperial edicts and commands, and memorials and deliberations submitted by officials, were recorded directly wherever they concerned additions, reforms, continuations, or abolitions. Whether events were arranged by year or years attached to events, the material was divided into articles according to the matter concerned and recorded in sequence. Since written records first existed, there has never been a compendium so clear and comprehensive as this one. The compilation office opened in the ding si year of Hongzhi (1497). In the xin wei year of Zhengde (1511), His Majesty the reigning emperor, deeply filial in carrying forward his predecessors’ work, ordered Confucian officials to revise it and have it printed and distributed. Officials throughout the realm eagerly vied to see it first. Truly, those who obtained it esteemed it like a jade disc held in both hands, and those who kept it regarded it as a treasure for generations.
Your discerning question further asks to hear the essentials by which officials today should recite and study it, embody its principles, and put them into practice. Dull though I am, a mere student, dare I speak rashly beyond my station? Yet I have ventured to examine the matter. Since the Six Ministries are established to exercise general oversight, with their subordinate offices separately constituted, the six ministers must understand their duty to lead their subordinates. Since administrative affairs are divided by category and responsibility is assigned for the completion of each task, then the various…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
官不可不知董正之義自粟米之征以至
竹木之税皆有其數當體之以戒侵漁自
太學之教以至庠序之育皆有其方當體
之以崇道化體禮制以一民志則十一其
綱體律意以防民奸則四百六十其條論
功以勦殺北虜為首遼東女直次之内地
反賊又次之将臣之所當體也行止語黙
必須循理務循公義以協衆情毋求細事
羅織人過憲臣之所當體也典所是吾不
===
得而違也典所因吾不得而革也典所無
吾不得而有也則吾之所執者無非
先帝之舊章矣雖然
帝王之治本之於心焉耳是典主於記事而不
及心然非心存理得又何以盡事物之變
哉故
先帝御製序文又舉純乎天理以為之訓是即
先正其心之意草茅所負之暄也願以獻
于
punctuated:
官不可不知董正之義。自粟米之征以至竹木之税，皆有其數，當體之以戒侵漁；自太學之教以至庠序之育，皆有其方，當體之以崇道化。體禮制以一民志，則十一其綱；體律意以防民奸，則四百六十其條。論功以勦殺北虜為首，遼東女直次之，内地反賊又次之，将臣之所當體也。行止語黙，必須循理，務循公義以協衆情，毋求細事，羅織人過，憲臣之所當體也。典所是，吾不得而違也；典所因，吾不得而革也；典所無，吾不得而有也。則吾之所執者，無非先帝之舊章矣。

雖然，帝王之治，本之於心焉耳。是典主於記事而不及心，然非心存理得，又何以盡事物之變哉？故先帝御製序文，又舉純乎天理以為之訓，是即先正其心之意。草茅所負之暄也，願以獻于
translation_en:
…officials must understand their duty to supervise and rectify. From levies on grain to taxes on bamboo and timber, all have prescribed amounts; these provisions should be put into practice to guard against oppressive exactions. From instruction at the Imperial University to education in local schools, all have prescribed methods; these should be put into practice to promote moral transformation through the Way. To embody the ritual institutions and thereby unify the people’s aspirations, there are eleven main divisions; to embody the intent of the laws and thereby prevent wrongdoing among the people, there are 460 articles. In assessing military merit, destroying and killing the northern barbarians ranks first, the Jurchens of Liaodong next, and rebels within the realm after them: these are the provisions that military commanders ought to put into practice. In conduct and repose, speech and silence, one must follow principle, strive to uphold public justice so as to accord with the sentiments of all, and refrain from seeking out trivial matters to fabricate charges against others: these are the provisions that censorial officials ought to put into practice. What the compendium approves, I may not contravene; what it retains from earlier practice, I may not abolish; what it does not provide for, I may not introduce. Thus, everything I uphold will be among the established statutes of the late emperor.

Nevertheless, the government of emperors and kings is rooted in the heart alone. This compendium chiefly records affairs and does not address the heart. Yet unless the heart is preserved and principle apprehended, how can one fully respond to the changing circumstances of things and affairs? Hence, in his personally composed preface, the late emperor also set forth purity in accordance with Heaven’s principle as an admonition. This conveys precisely the intention of first rectifying one’s heart. These words are like the warmth of the sun cherished by a humble rustic, which I wish to offer to…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
明天子謹對
第二問
陳噐
同考試官教諭何批此策作者多欠斷案是
篇文整意到如老將用兵竒正迭出而終有節制士
林巨擘也
同考試官教諭戴批有考覈有斷制如燭照
數計略無所遺傑作也宜置優選
同考試官教諭吳批五策皆佳刑賞一策尤
詳明豐贍而必以公心為主其為知本之論與髙薦
何忝
考試官教諭林批斟酌刑賞合於古而宜
於今場中不多見
考試官教授陳批不惑問目卓有斷制可
知他日之猷為矣
行賞罰者當恊至公之道議賞罰者當求
至一之歸夫賞罰者人主之大柄治天下
之大法也有公心以為之本則處賞罰之
punctuated:
明天子。謹對。

第二問
陳噐

同考試官教諭何批：「此策作者多欠斷案，是篇文整意到，如老將用兵，竒正迭出，而終有節制，士林巨擘也。」

同考試官教諭戴批：「有考覈，有斷制，如燭照數計，略無所遺，傑作也，宜置優選。」

同考試官教諭吳批：「五策皆佳，刑賞一策尤詳明豐贍，而必以公心為主，其為知本之論與！髙薦何忝？」

考試官教諭林批：「斟酌刑賞，合於古而宜於今，場中不多見。」

考試官教授陳批：「不惑問目，卓有斷制，可知他日之猷為矣。」

行賞罰者當恊至公之道，議賞罰者當求至一之歸。夫賞罰者，人主之大柄，治天下之大法也。有公心以為之本，則處賞罰之
translation_en:
…the enlightened Son of Heaven. I respectfully submit my reply.

Second Question
Chen Qi 陳噐

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: “Most writers answering this policy question fail to reach a definite judgment. This essay is orderly in composition and fully develops its meaning. Like a veteran general deploying troops, it alternates unconventional and conventional tactics while maintaining discipline throughout. Its author is a towering figure among scholars.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor: “There is careful examination and decisive judgment. Like illuminating things with a candle and counting them up, it leaves virtually nothing out. A masterpiece: it deserves a place among the outstanding selections.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “All five policy essays are excellent. The one on punishments and rewards is especially clear, detailed, and ample, and consistently makes impartiality its guiding principle. Surely this is an argument that grasps the foundation! How could a high recommendation be undeserved?”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Its judicious assessment of punishments and rewards accords with antiquity and suits the present. Such work is rarely seen in the examination hall.”

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: “Not led astray by the question’s particulars, he displays outstanding decisiveness of judgment. From this one can discern what his future plans and accomplishments will be.”

Those who administer rewards and punishments should accord with the Way of perfect impartiality; those who discuss rewards and punishments should seek a single, unified conclusion. Rewards and punishments are the ruler’s great instruments of authority and the great means of governing all under Heaven. With an impartial mind as their foundation, then, in handling matters of rewards and punishments …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
事而無不當論賞罰之說而無不定矣然
則法固為治之所當有而本尤為治之不
可缺也歟請略陳之惟辟作福五服五彰
爵賞所以待有功也不及則吝吝固不可
然太過而僭則名器輕輕則人心賤如昔
之所謂車載斗量者得之非榮矣復何所
勸乎惟辟作威五刑五用刑罰所以待有
罪也不及則縱縱固不可然太過而濫則
刑政紊紊則人心駭如昔之所謂重足側
===
目者無所趨避矣亦何所懲乎故夫求郎
之請為公主若可以曲從也而懼其殃民
則漢明帝不之許秦邸官僚念舊人若可
以超遷也而害於至公則唐太宗不之許
至宋藝祖於曹彬與之以緡錢靳之以使
相以太原之未平耳之三君者謂之公可
也謂之吝不可也視刓印弗與者大有逕
庭肉刑之用舊矣而文帝始除之蓋感緹
縈之請也笞箠之令足矣而景帝復定之
punctuated: 事而無不當，論賞罰之說而無不定矣。然則法固為治之所當有，而本尤為治之不可缺也歟？請略陳之。「惟辟作福」，「五服五彰」，爵賞所以待有功也。不及則吝，吝固不可；然太過而僭，則名器輕，輕則人心賤。如昔之所謂「車載斗量」者，得之非榮矣，復何所勸乎？「惟辟作威」，「五刑五用」，刑罰所以待有罪也。不及則縱，縱固不可；然太過而濫，則刑政紊，紊則人心駭。如昔之所謂「重足側目」者，無所趨避矣，亦何所懲乎？故夫求郎之請，為公主若可以曲從也，而懼其殃民，則漢明帝不之許。秦邸官僚，念舊人若可以超遷也，而害於至公，則唐太宗不之許。至宋藝祖於曹彬，與之以緡錢，靳之以使相，以太原之未平耳。之三君者，謂之公可也，謂之吝不可也，視刓印弗與者，大有逕庭。肉刑之用舊矣，而文帝始除之，蓋感緹縈之請也。笞箠之令足矣，而景帝復定之。
translation_en:
… affairs are handled appropriately in every case, and discussions of rewards and punishments reach settled conclusions. Thus, while laws are certainly necessary for government, is its foundation not still more indispensable? Allow me to explain briefly.

“Only the sovereign confers blessings”; “the five kinds of ceremonial dress distinguish the five ranks.” Ranks and rewards are the means of treating those who have rendered meritorious service. To give too little is to be parsimonious, and parsimony is certainly unacceptable. Yet to go too far and confer honors improperly cheapens titles and insignia; once cheapened, people hold them in contempt. As with what was once described as “carried by the cartload and measured by the bushel,” obtaining them brings no honor. What encouragement can they then provide? “Only the sovereign exercises punitive authority”; “the five punishments have their five applications.” Punishments are the means of treating those who have committed offenses. To punish too little is to be indulgent, and indulgence is certainly unacceptable. Yet excessive and indiscriminate punishment disorders penal administration; once it is disordered, people become terrified. As with those once described as “standing with feet together and looking askance,” they have nowhere to turn or escape. What corrective effect can punishment then have?

Thus, a princess’s request for someone to be appointed a Gentleman might seemingly have warranted special accommodation; but Emperor Ming of Han, fearing that this would bring harm to the people, refused it. Officials of the Prince of Qin’s household might seemingly have merited promotion beyond the usual grades out of regard for their former service; but Emperor Taizong of Tang refused this because it would compromise perfect impartiality. As for Song Yizu, he gave Cao Bin strings of cash but withheld appointment as a Commissioner with the title of Grand Councilor, simply because Taiyuan had not yet been pacified. These three rulers [?] may be called impartial, but they cannot be called parsimonious. They differed greatly from the man who wore down the edges of a seal through handling it yet would not bestow it.

Mutilating punishments had long been in use when Emperor Wen first abolished them, moved by Tiying’s petition. The regulations for flogging were sufficient [?], yet Emperor Jing revised them again…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
蓋懼殘民之生也至於太宗之禁鞭背則
因鍼灸之書知五臟之附不得而不禁之
耳之數事者謂之公可也謂之縱不可也
與涕泣死刑者大相逺邈酌古之道定今
之宜賞不必予之太驟也奪之太速也賞
一人而當其功則人皆以為慶孰不敏於
為善刑不必加之太重也赦之太數也罰
一人而當其罪則人皆以為威孰不勇於
去惡且刑賞之說古人論之詳矣蔡聲子
===
曰善為國者賞不僭而刑不濫固矣而文
王之世祿所以重世功周官之重典所以
懲亂國其為不僭不濫均焉周人有言曰
為政者不賞私勞不罰私怨固矣而孔門
報怨以直者非矯情報德以德者非朋比
其與無私之意同焉有功不賞有罪不誅
雖唐虞不能以化天下宣帝有是言也示
人以治道之常耳不賞而民勸不怒而民
威中庸有是言也所以著誠敬之效不待
punctuated: 蓋懼殘民之生也。至於太宗之禁鞭背，則因鍼灸之書，知五臟之附，不得而不禁之耳。之數事者，謂之公可也，謂之縱不可也，與涕泣死刑者大相逺邈。酌古之道，定今之宜，賞不必予之太驟也、奪之太速也。賞一人而當其功，則人皆以為慶，孰不敏於為善？刑不必加之太重也、赦之太數也。罰一人而當其罪，則人皆以為威，孰不勇於去惡？且刑賞之說，古人論之詳矣。蔡聲子曰：「善為國者，賞不僭而刑不濫。」固矣。而文王之世祿，所以重世功；周官之重典，所以懲亂國。其為不僭不濫，均焉。周人有言曰：「為政者不賞私勞，不罰私怨。」固矣。而孔門報怨以直者，非矯情；報德以德者，非朋比。其與無私之意，同焉。「有功不賞，有罪不誅，雖唐虞不能以化天下。」宣帝有是言也，示人以治道之常耳。「不賞而民勸，不怒而民威。」中庸有是言也，所以著誠敬之效，不待
translation_en:
…because he feared destroying the lives of the people. As for Taizong’s prohibition on flogging the back, he learned from a book on acupuncture and moxibustion that the five internal organs were attached there, and thus had no choice but to prohibit it. These several acts may be called impartial, but cannot be called indulgent. They stand far apart from shedding tears over those condemned to death.

Weigh the ways of antiquity to determine what is appropriate today. Rewards should neither be conferred too hastily nor withdrawn too quickly. When one person is rewarded in proportion to his merit, everyone regards it as cause for rejoicing: who would not be eager to do good? Punishments should neither be imposed too severely nor remitted too frequently. When one person is punished in proportion to his crime, everyone regards it with awe: who would not strive resolutely to abandon evil?

Moreover, the ancients discussed punishments and rewards in detail. Cai Shengzi said: “Those skilled at governing a state do not bestow rewards beyond what is deserved or impose punishments indiscriminately.” This is certainly true. Yet King Wen’s hereditary emoluments served to honor service rendered over generations, and the severe statutes in the Offices of Zhou served to chastise disorderly states. Both equally exemplify rewards that do not exceed desert and punishments that are not indiscriminate. The people of Zhou had a saying: “Those who govern do not reward services rendered to them personally or punish private grudges.” This is certainly true. Yet in the school of Confucius, repaying resentment with uprightness is no forced suppression of feeling, and repaying kindness with kindness is no partisan favoritism. These accord equally with the principle of impartiality.

“If merit goes unrewarded and crime unpunished, even the rulers of Tang and Yu could not transform all under Heaven.” Emperor Xuan said this merely to show people the constant principles of government. “Without rewards, the people are encouraged; without anger, the people stand in awe.” The Doctrine of the Mean says this to reveal the efficacy of sincerity and reverence, without waiting for…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有言而人自化不待有為而人自服一則
以明其用一則以循其本體用相資何背
馳乎有功則賞有罪則刑誰敢不竭心盡
力以脩職業此太宗通論馭臣之道耳宋
臣蘇軾復有所謂無功之爵無罪之罰者
則言六德六行之賢偽言偽行之士先王
不待其功之顯而後爵之不待其罪之顯
而後罰之一則語其顯一則闡其微顯微
一道何抵捂乎由是觀之人君惟患其賞
===
之不公不患於人之不勸惟患其罰之不
公不患於人之不懲至于所以求其公者
又必黽勉於學問之間戒慎於理欲之際
在己之喜怒不妄在人之邪正莫逃然後
大道之公在我執此以應天下之變以盡
萬物之情將無所施而不當而况於刑賞
間邪鄙見如是不識執事以為何如
第三問
葉應驄
punctuated:
有言而人自化，不待有為而人自服。一則以明其用，一則以循其本，體用相資，何背馳乎？有功則賞，有罪則刑，誰敢不竭心盡力以脩職業？此太宗通論馭臣之道耳。宋臣蘇軾復有所謂無功之爵、無罪之罰者，則言六德六行之賢、偽言偽行之士，先王不待其功之顯而後爵之，不待其罪之顯而後罰之。一則語其顯，一則闡其微，顯微一道，何抵捂乎？由是觀之，人君惟患其賞之不公，不患於人之不勸；惟患其罰之不公，不患於人之不懲。至于所以求其公者，又必黽勉於學問之間，戒慎於理欲之際，在己之喜怒不妄，在人之邪正莫逃，然後大道之公在我。執此以應天下之變，以盡萬物之情，將無所施而不當，而况於刑賞間邪？鄙見如是，不識執事以為何如？

第三問
葉應驄
translation_en:
… words to be spoken before people transform themselves, nor action to be taken before people submit of their own accord. One statement elucidates the practical operation; the other traces the underlying foundation. Foundation and operation support each other: how could they run counter to one another? “Reward those who have merit and punish those who are guilty: who would dare fail to devote his whole mind and strength to fulfilling his official duties?” This is simply Emperor Taizong’s general account of the way to govern ministers. The Song minister Su Shi also spoke of “ennoblement without merit and punishment without guilt.” He was referring to worthy men possessing the six virtues and six forms of conduct, and to men whose words and conduct were false. The former kings did not wait for the merits of the former to become manifest before ennobling them, nor for the offenses of the latter to become manifest before punishing them. One statement addresses what is manifest; the other elucidates what is hidden. The manifest and the hidden belong to a single Way: how could there be any contradiction?

Viewed in this light, a ruler should worry only that his rewards are unjust, not that people will fail to be encouraged; only that his punishments are unjust, not that people will fail to be deterred. As for how to attain this impartiality, he must apply himself diligently to learning and remain watchful at the boundary between principle and desire. His own joy and anger must not be arbitrary, and the wickedness or uprightness of others must not escape his discernment. Only then will the impartiality of the Great Way reside in him. Holding to this in responding to changes throughout the realm and fully comprehending the true circumstances of all things, he will act appropriately wherever he applies it—how much more so in matters of punishment and reward! Such is my humble view; I do not know what you, honored examiners, will think of it.

Third Policy Question
Ye Yingcong

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭李批教化風俗作者類能言
之然不過就題搬補故實成文獨此乃能吐出胸中許多
奇氣議論有餘所謂士人美節子殆素養者矣
考試官教諭林批詞氣精彩波瀾浩瀚
自是不凡錄之以示式也
考試官教授陳批子平居抱負充足有
意於教化風俗於此可覘
善言天下之治者無貴乎遠有所慕亦無
貴乎近有所遺夫古今天下之心一也民
===
以是善亦以是偷治以是隆亦以是替是
必有教化風俗為之機焉以轉移于其間
者矣然則所以張主而維持之者亦何容
心於遠者之足慕而近者之可遺也哉羅
氏曰教化者朝廷之先務廉恥者士人之
美節風俗者天下之大事至哉言矣愚請
得而大其說焉以為今日明問復人之言
曰觀化在朝觀俗在野又曰慕古者為不
便於今好今者必無意於古愚則曰天下
punctuated:
同考試官教諭李批：教化風俗，作者類能言之，然不過就題搬補故實成文。獨此乃能吐出胸中許多奇氣，議論有餘。所謂士人美節，子殆素養者矣。
考試官教諭林批：詞氣精彩，波瀾浩瀚，自是不凡，錄之以示式也。
考試官教授陳批：子平居抱負充足，有意於教化風俗，於此可覘。
善言天下之治者，無貴乎遠有所慕，亦無貴乎近有所遺。夫古今天下之心一也，民以是善，亦以是偷；治以是隆，亦以是替。是必有教化風俗為之機焉，以轉移于其間者矣。然則所以張主而維持之者，亦何容心於遠者之足慕，而近者之可遺也哉？羅氏曰：「教化者，朝廷之先務；廉恥者，士人之美節；風俗者，天下之大事。」至哉言矣！愚請得而大其說焉，以為今日明問復。人之言曰：「觀化在朝，觀俗在野。」又曰：「慕古者為不便於今，好今者必無意於古。」愚則曰：天下
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Most writers can discuss moral instruction and social customs, but they merely assemble historical precedents to fit the topic and make an essay. This writer alone gives expression to the remarkable spirit within his breast, with arguments to spare. As for the so-called admirable integrity of scholars, you have surely long cultivated it.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The language and spirit are brilliant, its surging movement vast. This is certainly exceptional; it is recorded here to serve as a model.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: Your habitual aspirations are substantial, and you are concerned with moral instruction and social customs. This essay affords a glimpse of these qualities.

Those who speak well of governing All-under-Heaven do not prize admiring what is distant, nor do they prize neglecting what is close at hand. The hearts of people throughout the realm are the same in antiquity and today. Through this the people become good, and through this they become lax; through this government flourishes, and through this it declines. Moral instruction and social customs must be the pivot that brings about these transformations. How, then, could those responsible for upholding and sustaining them entertain the thought that the distant deserves admiration while the near may be neglected? Master Luo said: “Moral instruction is the court’s foremost duty; integrity and a sense of shame are the admirable virtues of scholars; social customs are a great concern of All-under-Heaven.” How consummate these words are! Permit me, in my humble capacity, to expand upon his account as a reply to your discerning question today. People say: “To observe moral transformation, look to the court; to observe customs, look among the people.” They also say: “Those who admire antiquity act in ways unsuited to the present; those who favor the present must have no regard for antiquity.” I, however, humbly say: All-under-Heaven …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之心一也舉放勳之憂勤泯於知識之地
則可以合朝野之歡以漢武之多慾假諸
仁義之途祗見其有古今之異耳蓋嘗徵
之於古求其可宜於今者而粗有得焉教
化本於朝廷而責任於守令執事之論公
矣然今之為守令者果能脫去因循苟免
之陋習嚴急集事之苛聲可續班范二史
所傳循良者乎信有之愚不可得而盡知
也風俗移于好尚而振作于士人執事之
===
憂切矣然今之為士人者果能涵養平居
廉靜之節君子長者之心可無愧於古之
嘉言善行者乎信有之愚亦不可得而盡
知也不可得而盡知則凡所以扶植教化
于上陶成風俗于下其責將安歸邪抑求
之遠而易忽近而易玩者邪夫亦曰驗之
古今人心而已矣古者力行教化若文翁
之守蜀郡若黃霸之守潁川一時光後相
望具載班史者六人至于今猶能使人動
punctuated:
之心一也。舉放勳之憂勤，泯於知識之地，則可以合朝野之歡；以漢武之多慾，假諸仁義之途，祗見其有古今之異耳。蓋嘗徵之於古，求其可宜於今者，而粗有得焉。
教化本於朝廷，而責任於守令，執事之論公矣。然今之為守令者，果能脫去因循苟免之陋習、嚴急集事之苛聲，可續班范二史所傳循良者乎？信有之，愚不可得而盡知也。風俗移于好尚，而振作于士人，執事之憂切矣。然今之為士人者，果能涵養平居廉靜之節、君子長者之心，可無愧於古之嘉言善行者乎？信有之，愚亦不可得而盡知也。不可得而盡知，則凡所以扶植教化于上、陶成風俗于下，其責將安歸邪？抑求之遠而易忽、近而易玩者邪？夫亦曰驗之古今人心而已矣。
古者力行教化，若文翁之守蜀郡，若黃霸之守潁川，一時光後相望，具載班史者六人，至于今猶能使人動
translation_en:
