…the hearts of all under Heaven are one. If Fangxun’s [Yao’s] anxious diligence is brought to bear until it passes beyond people’s conscious awareness, the court and countryside can be united in joy. But if Emperor Wu of Han’s many desires are cloaked in benevolence and righteousness, one sees only a divergence between antiquity and the present. I have examined antiquity, seeking what might suit the present, and have gained some rough understanding.
Moral instruction originates at court, while responsibility for it rests with prefects and magistrates: your judgment is impartial. Yet can those who serve as prefects and magistrates today truly cast off the bad habits of following routine and merely avoiding blame, and the harsh reputation earned by pressing urgently to get things done? Can they carry on the tradition of the benevolent officials recorded in the two histories of Ban Gu and Fan Ye? Surely such men exist, but I cannot know them all. Customs shift according to prevailing preferences, and scholars give them renewed vigor: your concern is deeply felt. Yet can today’s scholars truly cultivate integrity and tranquility in their daily lives, and the dispositions of gentlemen and venerable elders, so that they need feel no shame before the admirable words and good deeds of antiquity? Surely such men exist, but again I cannot know them all. If they cannot all be known, where is responsibility to lie for sustaining moral instruction above and shaping customs below? Or should we seek it in what is distant and easily overlooked, or near at hand and easily treated lightly? One can only say: test it against human hearts, past and present.
In antiquity, men vigorously practiced moral instruction: Wen Weng when he governed Shu Commandery, and Huang Ba when he governed Yingchuan, for example. There were six such men, appearing in succession and illuminating later ages [?], all fully recorded in Ban Gu’s history. Even today they can still move people, whenever they act…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
必稽之以為美談興行禮讓若衞颯任延
若秦彭劉矩當時同為范史所傳者十有
二人要皆勞來躬行使民異地而同化故
說者謂三代而下惟兩漢風化近厚今也
守令之選簡自天曹而授之以政凡所以
承宣教化豈不以古之人望之也然而每
病於奉行之未至者無乃文程束約之過
嚴使豪傑不得得其志乎否則陋習苛聲
之咎將何以自釋也古者善行著稱如劉
===
文饒之宏度龐德公之高致范希文之不
私其家司馬君實之恬退自娛而京兆小
民猶能却歸亡父之金是皆高風靖節百
世而下凛乎猶可想見者嘉言可述如羅
仲素論舜之孝蘇瓊息普明兄弟之爭古
語所謂善終乎夫婦朋友之道禮曰不非
其大夫以全上下之交而卓茂又有律設
大法禮順人情以為通變之說是皆微言
正論藹然有益於世教可舉而行之者故
punctuated: 必稽之以為美談。興行禮讓，若衞颯、任延，若秦彭、劉矩，當時同為范史所傳者十有二人，要皆勞來躬行，使民異地而同化。故說者謂三代而下，惟兩漢風化近厚。今也，守令之選，簡自天曹而授之以政，凡所以承宣教化，豈不以古之人望之也？然而每病於奉行之未至者，無乃文程束約之過嚴，使豪傑不得得其志乎？否則，陋習苛聲之咎，將何以自釋也？古者善行著稱，如劉文饒之宏度、龐德公之高致、范希文之不私其家、司馬君實之恬退自娛，而京兆小民猶能却歸亡父之金，是皆高風靖節，百世而下，凛乎猶可想見者。嘉言可述，如羅仲素論舜之孝、蘇瓊息普明兄弟之爭、古語所謂善終乎夫婦朋友之道，《禮》曰「不非其大夫」，以全上下之交，而卓茂又有「律設大法，禮順人情」，以為通變之說，是皆微言正論，藹然有益於世教，可舉而行之者。故
translation_en:
…invariably consult their examples and recount them as praiseworthy tales. As for promoting ritual propriety and deference, there were Wei Sa and Ren Yan, Qin Peng and Liu Ju: twelve men in all whose lives were recorded in Fan Ye’s History of the Later Han. In essence, they all comforted and encouraged the people and practiced these virtues themselves, bringing people in different places under the same moral influence. Thus commentators say that, since the Three Dynasties, only under the two Han dynasties did moral influence and customs approach such generosity and sincerity. Today, prefects and county magistrates are selected by the Ministry of Personnel and entrusted with government. In all their work of transmitting and promulgating moral instruction, are they not expected to measure up to the men of antiquity? Yet their implementation is repeatedly found wanting. Might this be because administrative regulations impose excessively strict constraints, preventing outstanding men from realizing their aspirations? Otherwise, how can they absolve themselves of blame for entrenched bad practices and a reputation for harshness?

Among the ancients renowned for good conduct were Liu Wenrao, with his magnanimity; Pang Degong, with his lofty aspirations; Fan Xiwen, who did not favor his own household; and Sima Junshi, who found contentment in peaceful retirement. Even an ordinary person of Jingzhao could refuse and return gold belonging to a deceased father [?]. These are all examples of lofty character and steadfast integrity whose awe-inspiring presence can still be imagined a hundred generations later. Among worthy sayings deserving to be recounted are Luo Zhongsu’s discussion of Shun’s filial piety, Su Qiong’s words that ended the dispute between Puming and his brother, and the ancient saying about fulfilling to the end the proper way between husband and wife and between friends. The Book of Rites says, “Do not criticize one’s great officer,” thereby preserving the relationship between superiors and inferiors. Zhuo Mao also said, “Statutes establish broad rules; ritual accords with human feelings,” as an explanation of adapting to changing circumstances. These are all subtle sayings and sound judgments, abundantly beneficial to the moral instruction of the age and fit to be put into practice. Therefore…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
說者謂古今風俗惟有道君子可以維持
之今也士人之節出自天性而養之以善
凡所以激勵風化孰不以古之人期之也
然而每患於積習之相移者無乃群排聚
笑之弗容使頓失其心乎否則飭躬勵行
之戒亦可以自治也若之何而可逃其責
哉矧夫天下之大以一人而領萬化不見
其不足以兆民而懷一人不見其有餘方
今天下之教化天下之風俗亦匪必人人
===
而面命之事事而拘持之也責之守令使
各以古人之心為心則循良傳不可以不
讀也他日紹前脩而輝史筆者將非今之
賢守令而誰歸飭之士人使各以古人之
言行為法則座右銘不可一日無也他日
追往哲而風後世者將非今之賢士大夫
而誰歸若是而曰教化之不可行風俗之
不可厚吾不之信也雖然成天下之化者
守令士人也所以運天下之化者吾
punctuated:
說者謂古今風俗，惟有道君子可以維持之。今也士人之節，出自天性，而養之以善，凡所以激勵風化，孰不以古之人期之也？然而每患於積習之相移者，無乃群排聚笑之弗容，使頓失其心乎？否則飭躬勵行之戒，亦可以自治也，若之何而可逃其責哉？矧夫天下之大，以一人而領萬化，不見其不足；以兆民而懷一人，不見其有餘。方今天下之教化、天下之風俗，亦匪必人人而面命之，事事而拘持之也。

責之守令，使各以古人之心為心，則《循良傳》不可以不讀也。他日紹前脩而輝史筆者，將非今之賢守令而誰歸？飭之士人，使各以古人之言行為法，則座右銘不可一日無也。他日追往哲而風後世者，將非今之賢士大夫而誰歸？若是而曰教化之不可行、風俗之不可厚，吾不之信也。雖然，成天下之化者，守令士人也；所以運天下之化者，吾
translation_en:
…commentators say that, in ancient times and today, only gentlemen who possess the Way can uphold proper customs. Now, the integrity of scholars springs from their innate nature and is nurtured through goodness. In all efforts to encourage moral influence and transform customs, who does not expect them to measure up to the ancients? Yet there is constant concern that ingrained habits will lead them astray. Might this be because collective rejection and ridicule leave them no room, causing them suddenly to lose their moral resolve? Otherwise, the admonition to discipline themselves and strive for upright conduct should itself enable them to govern themselves. How, then, can they evade their responsibility? Moreover, vast though the realm is, one person presides over its myriad transformations without proving unequal to the task; its countless people cherish that one person without their numbers proving excessive. As for the moral instruction and customs of the realm today, there is certainly no need to instruct every person face to face or to constrain and control every affair.

Charge the prefects and magistrates with this responsibility, making each take the minds of the ancients as his own: then they must read the Biographies of Exemplary Officials. In days to come, who but today's worthy prefects and magistrates will carry on the achievements of their virtuous predecessors and lend lustre to the historical record? Admonish scholars to take the words and deeds of the ancients as their models: then they must never pass a day without an admonitory inscription beside their seats. In days to come, who but today's worthy scholar-officials will emulate past sages and exert a moral influence upon later generations? If, under these conditions, anyone says that moral instruction cannot be put into practice and customs cannot be made more sound, I do not believe it. Nevertheless, those who bring the moral transformation of the realm to fruition are its prefects, magistrates, and scholars; those who set that transformation in motion are our…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
君與吾相也運之以仁民亦從而仁之運之
以非仁則亦唯恐其從矣其成與否何足
計哉噫此所以禮義之風廉恥之俗每必
於人心去惡從善之機而轉移之誠使士
人賢矣守令賢矣天下之人心得以大其
善而小其惡矣夫然後反而求之教化本
原之地為之勸懲黜陟之典行焉此則機
之謂也亦所以守天下之化者也愚不敏
他又何足以知之
===
第四問
陳煥
同考試官訓導田批秋闈策士以節義正欲觀
其所養何如此卷於前人行事之槩條答無遺可以占平居
之志向矣他日效用其所建立必有可觀者
考試官教諭林批節義雖非士君子全節
然亦兩間正氣扶植世教所不可少者此卷條對詳明
且能知所宗尚可佳也
考試官教授陳批此卷隨問而對充然不
punctuated:
君與吾相也。運之以仁，民亦從而仁之；運之以非仁，則亦唯恐其從矣。其成與否，何足計哉！噫！此所以禮義之風、廉恥之俗，每必於人心去惡從善之機而轉移之。誠使士人賢矣，守令賢矣，天下之人心得以大其善而小其惡矣。夫然後反而求之教化本原之地，為之勸懲黜陟之典行焉，此則機之謂也，亦所以守天下之化者也。愚不敏，他又何足以知之？

第四問
陳煥

同考試官訓導田批：秋闈策士以節義，正欲觀其所養何如。此卷於前人行事之槩，條答無遺，可以占平居之志向矣。他日效用，其所建立必有可觀者。

考試官教諭林批：節義雖非士君子全節，然亦兩間正氣，扶植世教所不可少者。此卷條對詳明，且能知所宗尚，可佳也。

考試官教授陳批：此卷隨問而對，充然不
translation_en:
…ruler and our chief councillor. If they guide transformation through benevolence, the people will follow them in being benevolent; if they guide it through what is not benevolent, one can only fear that the people will follow them. What point is there then in reckoning whether transformation succeeds? Alas! This is why the cultivation of ritual propriety and righteousness, integrity and a sense of shame, invariably turns upon the moment when people’s hearts reject evil and follow goodness. If the scholars and the prefects and magistrates truly become worthy, the hearts of all under Heaven can enlarge their goodness and diminish their evil. Only then should we turn back to seek the source of moral instruction and put into effect the established measures of encouragement and punishment, dismissal and promotion. This is what is meant by the pivotal opportunity; it is also the means of preserving moral transformation throughout the realm. I am of dull understanding: what else could I presume to know of this?

Fourth Question
Chen Huan

Comment by Associate Examiner Tian, Assistant Instructor: The autumn Provincial Examination tests candidates through policy questions on integrity and righteousness precisely to discern what they have cultivated within themselves. This paper answers point by point, omitting nothing from its outline of the deeds of earlier men. From it one can judge the aspirations the candidate cherishes in everyday life. When he enters service in the future, his accomplishments will surely merit attention.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Although integrity and righteousness do not encompass the whole moral character of a gentleman, they are nevertheless manifestations of the upright vital force between Heaven and Earth, indispensable to sustaining moral instruction in the world. This paper’s answers are detailed and clear; the candidate also understands what he should revere and esteem. It is commendable.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: This paper responds to each question with ample substance and does not …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
寤參之前二場皆稱本房之冠固無以易子矣
對崇節義者君子之美名稽名實者後儒
之公論蓋有節義之名不若循其實若併
與其實而亡之不若猶崇其名之為愈也
此後儒之責實者有取於西京史氏之憫
時者獎進乎東漢而不及唐宋吾士君子
立身行己之間又安得不擇取於是哉請
因明問而陳之三代而上聖學大明公論
素著士君子生於其時幼而學壯而仕行
===
其所無事而已降自秦漢人心放失聖學
湮微輿論不主於廟堂而縉紳草茅或執
其柄於是乎始有節義之名者矣且以兩
漢言之高祖除秦之暴約法三章史氏稱
其尚寬大是也若光武當士夫頑鈍之後
而大興振作之功召嚴光褒卓茂論文講
道崇尚儒學而東都一代之士風已倡起
於斯時矣於是陳蕃竇武之徒繼世而起
高名大節與日月而爭光危言峻行雖死
punctuated:
寤。參之前二場，皆稱本房之冠，固無以易子矣。
對：崇節義者，君子之美名；稽名實者，後儒之公論。蓋有節義之名，不若循其實；若併與其實而亡之，不若猶崇其名之為愈也。此後儒之責實者有取於西京，史氏之憫時者獎進乎東漢而不及唐宋。吾士君子立身行己之間，又安得不擇取於是哉？請因明問而陳之。三代而上，聖學大明，公論素著，士君子生於其時，幼而學，壯而仕，行其所無事而已。降自秦漢，人心放失，聖學湮微，輿論不主於廟堂，而縉紳草茅或執其柄，於是乎始有節義之名者矣。且以兩漢言之，高祖除秦之暴，約法三章，史氏稱其尚寬大，是也。若光武當士夫頑鈍之後，而大興振作之功，召嚴光，褒卓茂，論文講道，崇尚儒學，而東都一代之士風已倡起於斯時矣。於是陳蕃、竇武之徒繼世而起，高名大節，與日月而爭光；危言峻行，雖死
translation_en:
… [The opening character is doubtful: 寤, “awaken.”] [?] Comparing this with his work in the preceding two sessions, all rank foremost in this examining group. Certainly, no one could replace you.
Answer: To esteem integrity and righteousness is to honor the good reputation of exemplary men; to examine reputation against reality is the impartial judgment of later Confucian scholars. Possessing a reputation for integrity and righteousness is inferior to putting them into practice. Yet if their substance too would otherwise be lost, continuing to honor their name is preferable. Thus later Confucian scholars who demanded substance found merit in the Western Han, while historians who lamented their times praised the Eastern Han without extending such praise to the Tang and Song. In establishing ourselves and conducting our lives, how could we scholars fail to choose discriminatingly among these examples? Allow me to set this out in response to your illuminating question.
During the Three Dynasties and earlier, the learning of the sages shone brightly, and impartial judgments were long established. Exemplary men born in those times studied in youth and entered office in maturity, simply acting without contrivance. From the Qin and Han onward, people’s hearts became unrestrained and lost their proper direction, while the learning of the sages became obscured and diminished. Public judgment was no longer governed by the court; sometimes officials and scholars outside office took control of it. Only then did a reputation for integrity and righteousness emerge as a distinct designation.
Consider the two Han dynasties. Gaozu swept away Qin’s tyranny and reduced the laws to three articles. Historians rightly describe him as esteeming leniency and generosity. Guangwu, coming after a period when scholars and officials had grown obdurate and apathetic, undertook a great effort to rouse and invigorate them. He summoned Yan Guang, commended Zhuo Mao, discussed writings and expounded the Way, and honored Confucian learning. The ethos of scholars throughout the Eastern Han dynasty was already being fostered at this time. Thus men such as Chen Fan and Dou Wu arose in succeeding generations. Their lofty reputations and great integrity rivaled the sun and moon in brilliance; upright in speech and exacting in conduct, even though they died …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
亡而不悔桓靈以後國家失柄姦雄拱手
環視神器莫敢先動猶延數十年而後亡
史氏謂東漢之尚節義者不以此歟以西
漢人物而言坐事下獄不肯受卒徒之唾
背有若田延年者矣因誣被逮不肯受兩
吏之挾持有若蕭望之者矣以大將軍之
尊重而長揖不拜有汲長孺焉以匈奴之
暴驁而漢節不屈有蘇子卿焉高帝欲興
禮樂召魯兩生守乎儒禮而不至武帝大
===
崇文教迎魯申公告以力行之一言西京
高尚之士如此初不聞有節義之名蓋能
循其實耳故東萊呂氏謂東漢之節義不
如西漢豈不以東都之張其名而西京之
得其實乎若史氏謂東漢尚節義而西漢
不之尚者豈不以西漢之嫚罵折辱東漢
之能振作乎自是而後有唐焉其節義之
臣若巡遠力守睢陽捍安史之亂而江淮
賴之以保障陽城欲壞相麻劾裴延齡之
punctuated: 亡而不悔。桓、靈以後，國家失柄，姦雄拱手環視神器，莫敢先動，猶延數十年而後亡。史氏謂東漢之尚節義者，不以此歟？以西漢人物而言，坐事下獄，不肯受卒徒之唾背，有若田延年者矣；因誣被逮，不肯受兩吏之挾持，有若蕭望之者矣。以大將軍之尊重，而長揖不拜，有汲長孺焉；以匈奴之暴驁，而漢節不屈，有蘇子卿焉。高帝欲興禮樂，召魯兩生，守乎儒禮而不至；武帝大崇文教，迎魯申公，告以力行之一言。西京高尚之士如此，初不聞有節義之名，蓋能循其實耳。故東萊呂氏謂東漢之節義不如西漢，豈不以東都之張其名，而西京之得其實乎？若史氏謂東漢尚節義，而西漢不之尚者，豈不以西漢之嫚罵折辱，東漢之能振作乎？自是而後，有唐焉。其節義之臣，若巡、遠力守睢陽，捍安史之亂，而江淮賴之以保障；陽城欲壞相麻，劾裴延齡之
translation_en:
…death without regret. After the reigns of Huan and Ling, the dynasty lost its grip on power. Treacherous strongmen stood with folded hands, eyeing the sacred vessel of sovereignty, yet none dared move first; the dynasty thus endured several more decades before falling. Was this not why historians said that the Eastern Han esteemed integrity and righteousness?

Among Western Han figures, there was Tian Yannian, who, imprisoned for an offense, refused to suffer guards and convicts spitting on his back; and Xiao Wangzhi, who, arrested on a false accusation, refused to be held between two officers. There was Ji Changru, who merely bowed deeply with clasped hands rather than prostrating himself before even the exalted General-in-Chief; and Su Ziqing, who, despite the Xiongnu’s brutality and arrogance, remained unbending in his fidelity to the Han and its envoy’s staff. Emperor Gao wished to promote rites and music and summoned two scholars from Lu, but they held fast to Confucian ritual principles and would not come. Emperor Wu greatly promoted cultural instruction and welcomed Master Shen of Lu, who offered him the single counsel to put principles into practice.

Such were the lofty-minded men of the Western Capital. At the time, one heard nothing of their reputation for integrity and righteousness: they simply lived up to its substance. Thus Master Lü of Donglai said that the integrity and righteousness of the Eastern Han fell short of those of the Western Han. Was this not because the Eastern Capital vaunted the reputation, whereas the Western Capital attained the substance? As for historians saying that the Eastern Han esteemed integrity and righteousness while the Western Han did not, was this not because the Western Han subjected scholars to abuse and humiliation, whereas the Eastern Han succeeded in rousing their spirit?

Thereafter came the Tang. Among its ministers of integrity and righteousness were Xun and Yuan, who stoutly defended Suiyang against the An–Shi rebellion, providing protection upon which the Jiang–Huai region depended; and Yang Cheng, who wished to destroy the hemp-paper edict appointing a chief councillor and impeach Pei Yanling for his…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
奸朝廷賴之而振肅劉蕡對制策極言時
政雖權奸無所避忌何蕃在太學倡以大
義而六館不敢從亂其氣節有可尚也自
唐而後有宋焉其節義之臣若富弼奉使
虜庭議論慷慨而折服其君臣錢若水年
當強仕急流勇退而輕視乎富貴唐介謫
於英州困亦極矣而終無一書以至京師
劉器之交於温公情亦厚矣而卒無一言
抵於政府其節槩有可嘉也夫唐宋之節
===
義無愧於西京而西京之節義不讓於東
漢史氏獨以是名歸之東京者蓋以漢唐
宋三代士之蹈節而仗義者代不乏人元
氣賴之以不絕國家賴之以久存天地賴
之以有立者也至於上人之振作者獨光
武明章之為烈耳噫國家而不尚節義則
其後也苟且廢墮而無以振作乎人心士
大夫而不尚節義則其流也委靡頑鈍而
無以興起乎事業是節義雖非三代以上
punctuated:
奸，朝廷賴之而振肅。劉蕡對制策，極言時政，雖權奸無所避忌。何蕃在太學，倡以大義，而六館不敢從亂。其氣節有可尚也。自唐而後有宋焉，其節義之臣，若富弼奉使虜庭，議論慷慨，而折服其君臣；錢若水年當強仕，急流勇退，而輕視乎富貴；唐介謫於英州，困亦極矣，而終無一書以至京師；劉器之交於温公，情亦厚矣，而卒無一言抵於政府。其節槩有可嘉也。
夫唐宋之節義，無愧於西京，而西京之節義，不讓於東漢。史氏獨以是名歸之東京者，蓋以漢唐宋三代，士之蹈節而仗義者，代不乏人，元氣賴之以不絕，國家賴之以久存，天地賴之以有立者也。至於上人之振作者，獨光武、明、章之為烈耳。噫！國家而不尚節義，則其後也苟且廢墮，而無以振作乎人心；士大夫而不尚節義，則其流也委靡頑鈍，而無以興起乎事業。是節義雖非三代以上
translation_en:
…treachery, and through him the court regained its vigor and discipline. Liu Fen, answering an imperially prescribed policy question, spoke with utmost frankness about contemporary government, showing no fear or restraint even before powerful, treacherous officials. When He Fan was at the Imperial University, he championed the great principles of righteousness, and the students of the six colleges dared not join the rebellion. Their moral courage and integrity deserve esteem. After the Tang came the Song. Among its ministers of integrity and righteousness were men such as Fu Bi, who went as an envoy to the barbarian court, argued with impassioned conviction, and won over its ruler and ministers; Qian Ruoshui, who, at forty—the age for vigorous official service—courageously withdrew from the rushing current of office, holding wealth and rank in little regard; Tang Jie, who, though banished to Yingzhou and reduced to extreme hardship, never sent a single letter to the capital; and Liu Qizhi, who, though bound by deep affection to the Duke of Wen, never addressed a single word to the chief councilors’ offices. Their steadfast integrity deserves praise.
The integrity and righteousness of the Tang and Song were no disgrace when measured against the Western Han, and those of the Western Han were in no way inferior to those of the Eastern Han. As for historians’ attributing this distinction exclusively to the Eastern Han: throughout the Han, Tang, and Song, no age lacked men who upheld integrity and stood for righteousness. Through them the primal vitality remained unbroken, the state long endured, and Heaven and Earth retained their foundations. Yet when it came to those above actively fostering such qualities, only Emperors Guangwu, Ming, and Zhang achieved outstanding results. Alas! If a state does not esteem integrity and righteousness, the eventual result is expediency, neglect, and decay, leaving it unable to rouse people’s hearts. If scholar-officials do not esteem integrity and righteousness, the resulting tendency is toward listlessness, insensibility, and dullness, leaving them unable to advance their undertakings. Thus, although integrity and righteousness were not celebrated designations in the Three Dynasties and earlier …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之美名而實士君子立身行己之大端也
若徒託東都黨錮之名而專為全身固位
之計以小人之無忌憚而曰由大中以出
則是相率為孔光張禹而後已世道將焉
攸賴哉昔人有言求士於三代之上惟恐
其好名三代之下惟恐其不好名愚於節
義亦云不識執事以為何如
第五問
俞振強
===
同考試官訓導張批論兵食而末歸之守令
尤為確論天下事有一不由於良吏乎他日效用稱良
吏者必若而人矣
考試官教諭林批時務策只看處置處
置有方儘是策手
考試官教授陳批鋪叙詳明斷制允當其
策場中之傑出者乎
法有垂於久者守之不可以不固事有變
於今者處之不可以不宜蓋體國經久百
punctuated:
之美名，而實士君子立身行己之大端也。若徒託東都黨錮之名，而專為全身固位之計，以小人之無忌憚，而曰由大中以出，則是相率為孔光、張禹而後已，世道將焉攸賴哉？昔人有言：「求士於三代之上，惟恐其好名；三代之下，惟恐其不好名。」愚於節義亦云，不識執事以為何如？

第五問
俞振強

同考試官訓導張批：論兵食，而末歸之守令，尤為確論。天下事有一不由於良吏乎？他日效用稱良吏者，必若而人矣。

考試官教諭林批：時務策只看處置，處置有方，儘是策手。

考試官教授陳批：鋪叙詳明，斷制允當，其策場中之傑出者乎！

法有垂於久者，守之不可以不固；事有變於今者，處之不可以不宜。蓋體國經久，百
translation_en:
…a laudatory designation from the Three Dynasties or earlier, yet integrity and righteousness are indeed fundamental to how a gentleman establishes himself and conducts his life. If one merely invokes the partisan proscriptions of the Eastern Han as a pretext, while devoting oneself exclusively to preserving one’s person and securing one’s position, acting with a petty man’s utter lack of restraint yet claiming to proceed from the great Mean, then people will lead one another into becoming Kong Guang and Zhang Yu, and stop only there. On what, then, could the moral order of the world rely? Someone of old said: “When seeking men of worth in the Three Dynasties and earlier, one fears only that they might love reputation; after the Three Dynasties, one fears only that they might not love reputation.” In my humble view, the same applies to integrity and righteousness. I wonder what you, sir, think of this.

Fifth Question
Yu Zhenqiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: He discusses military affairs and provisions, ultimately placing responsibility with prefects and magistrates: a particularly sound argument. Is there a single matter under Heaven that does not depend on good officials? When he enters service in the future, a man such as this will surely earn the name of a good official.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: In a policy essay on current affairs, one need only examine the proposed measures. His measures are well conceived: he is a thoroughly accomplished writer of policy essays.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Professor: His exposition is detailed and clear, and his judgments and proposed measures are sound and appropriate. Surely he is among the outstanding writers in this policy examination!

There are laws handed down for lasting observance: one must uphold them firmly. There are circumstances that have changed in the present: one must handle them appropriately. For establishing the framework of the state and ensuring its enduring order, through a hundred…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
世不刋者
祖宗創置之法事變之來因時損益者後人捄
弊之權也自古以來率由斯道於乎此我
國家兵食之計當守
祖宗之舊而制今日之宜也歟請為執事陳之
天下之務亦多矣所以重於兵食者以今
日盜賊之故非兵則無以衞民非食則無
以養兵也古者寓兵於農入之則比閭族
黨出之則軍師伍兩而無不足之兵藏富
===
於民斂之則什一之征散之則三年之積
故無不足之食厥後創業如漢高誅秦蹙
項提兵數十萬以一蕭何饋餉而有餘意
者得人專運之故歟守成如漢文遣將四
出以大禦匈奴累蠲田租而軍儲不匱意
者恭儉休息之效歟我
國家之兵制掌於司馬督於憲臣有五府都
司以總其綱有衞所官旗以分其目其制
可謂密矣况簡閱有法清理有規乎邇者
punctuated:
世不刋者，祖宗創置之法；事變之來，因時損益者，後人捄弊之權也。自古以來，率由斯道。於乎！此我國家兵食之計，當守祖宗之舊而制今日之宜也歟？請為執事陳之。
天下之務亦多矣，所以重於兵食者，以今日盜賊之故，非兵則無以衞民，非食則無以養兵也。古者寓兵於農，入之則比閭族黨，出之則軍師伍兩，而無不足之兵；藏富於民，斂之則什一之征，散之則三年之積，故無不足之食。厥後，創業如漢高，誅秦蹙項，提兵數十萬，以一蕭何饋餉而有餘，意者得人專運之故歟？守成如漢文，遣將四出，以大禦匈奴，累蠲田租而軍儲不匱，意者恭儉休息之效歟？我國家之兵制，掌於司馬，督於憲臣，有五府都司以總其綱，有衞所官旗以分其目，其制可謂密矣。况簡閱有法，清理有規乎？邇者……
translation_en:
…unchanged through the generations are the institutions established by our imperial ancestors; adjustments made as circumstances change are the discretionary measures by which later generations remedy abuses. Since antiquity, this has generally been the way. Ah! In planning for our dynasty’s troops and provisions, should we not preserve the old institutions of our imperial ancestors while devising measures suited to present needs? Allow me to set this out for you, honored examiners.
The affairs of the realm are many. Troops and provisions receive particular emphasis because of the banditry of the present day: without troops there is no means of protecting the people, and without provisions there is no means of sustaining the troops. In antiquity, soldiers were incorporated into the farming population. At home they were organized into residential groups—the bi, lü, zu, and dang; on campaign, into military formations—the jun, shi, wu, and liang. Thus there was no shortage of troops. Wealth was stored among the people: revenue was collected through a tithe, and distributions were supplied from reserves sufficient for three years. Thus there was no shortage of provisions. Later, among founders of dynasties, Gaozu of Han destroyed Qin and pressed Xiang Yu hard, leading several hundred thousand troops; yet with Xiao He alone providing supplies, there was more than enough. Was this perhaps because he had secured the right man to take sole charge of transport? Among those who preserved an inherited dynasty, Emperor Wen of Han dispatched generals in all directions to repel the Xiongnu on a large scale. He repeatedly remitted the land tax, yet military stores were never exhausted. Was this perhaps the result of his respectful restraint and frugality, and of allowing the people respite and recovery? Our dynasty’s military system is administered by the Minister of War and overseen by censorial officials. The Five Chief Military Commissions and the Regional Military Commissions coordinate its overall structure, while officers and bannermen of the guards and battalions divide responsibility for its particulars. Its organization may well be called thorough. Moreover, there are established procedures for selection and inspection, and regulations for checking and rectifying the military rolls. Recently…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有事于蜀于江于
畿內而所在兵力為之不足至廑
宵旰之憂而募土兵調邊將者其故有三焉埋
沒紊於坐冊逃亡隱於偽籍一也寄名於
籍而役占於私家二也承平日乆人不知
兵為將者皆膏粱之蔭子為兵者皆尺五
之市人三也安得我兵之不寡哉
國家之國計掌於户部有京兆藩司以總其
政有郡守縣令以分其職其制可謂善矣
況征輸有法儲峙有規乎邇因饋餉于蜀
于江于
畿內而兵食為之告匱至煩
九重之聽以發
內帑截綱運者其故亦有二焉旱潦相仍歲
無全賦一也豪黠侵漁而不畏禁網二也
五方之財止有此數高庾大廩鮮有蓋藏
冗食奢華一切糜費三也安得我財之不
匱為今之計於軍政也必以
punctuated:
有事于蜀、于江、于畿內，而所在兵力為之不足，至廑宵旰之憂，而募土兵、調邊將者，其故有三焉：埋沒紊於坐冊，逃亡隱於偽籍，一也；寄名於籍，而役占於私家，二也；承平日乆，人不知兵，為將者皆膏粱之蔭子，為兵者皆尺五之市人，三也。安得我兵之不寡哉！
國家之國計掌於户部，有京兆、藩司以總其政，有郡守、縣令以分其職，其制可謂善矣。況征輸有法，儲峙有規乎！邇因饋餉于蜀、于江、于畿內，而兵食為之告匱，至煩九重之聽，以發內帑、截綱運者，其故亦有二焉：旱潦相仍，歲無全賦，一也；豪黠侵漁，而不畏禁網，二也；五方之財，止有此數，高庾大廩，鮮有蓋藏，冗食奢華，一切糜費，三也。安得我財之不匱？為今之計，於軍政也，必以
translation_en:
…military disturbances arose in Shu, in Jiang [?], and within the capital region, and the troops available in each place proved insufficient. This caused His Majesty anxiety from before dawn until late at night, necessitating the recruitment of local troops and the transfer of frontier commanders. There are three reasons for this. First, men are lost from view amid confused standing registers [?], while desertions are concealed in falsified rolls. Second, men are enrolled in name but appropriated for service in private households. Third, peace has lasted so long that people no longer understand warfare: commanders are all sons of wealthy families advanced through hereditary privilege, while soldiers are all undersized men of the marketplace. How could our troops fail to be too few?
The state's finances are administered by the Ministry of Revenue. The metropolitan prefecture and the Provincial Administration Commissions oversee fiscal administration, while prefects and district magistrates divide its duties among themselves. This system may well be called sound. Moreover, there are established methods for collecting and transporting revenue and regulations for maintaining reserves. Recently, however, provisioning troops in Shu, in Jiang [?], and within the capital region has exhausted military food supplies. The matter has even had to be brought to His Majesty's attention, requiring the release of funds from the palace treasury and the diversion of grain convoys. There are likewise two reasons for this [the text proceeds to list three]. First, droughts and floods follow one another, so that no year yields the full tax revenue. Second, powerful and cunning men embezzle and exploit without fear of the law. Third, the wealth of all regions is finite; lofty granaries and vast storehouses hold few reserves, while those who consume without contributing, together with luxury and extravagance, squander resources in every way. How could our finances fail to be depleted? In devising a remedy for the present, military administration must be put in order by means of…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
祖宗之法而整頓之搜其埋沒禁其偽籍嚴其
訓練剔其隱占而又有不從者重罰以懲
之其既從也生息以蕃之如此則諸路之
兵亦足以禦諸路之寇矣於
國計也必以
祖宗之法而調度之備其旱潦稽其侵漁汰其
冗食禁其奢靡有羨餘也則倉庾以儲之
有措置也則歲月以積之如此則天下之
食亦足以供天下之兵矣然此特就事論
===
事耳若要其極與其急於兵食孰若急於
弭盜與其急於弭盜孰若急於安民安民
之道無他焉在乎慎選守令重其權乆其
任使民尊之信之而已今之守令固未必
皆賢也而民恒有輕忽之心何者利不能
為民興也害不能為民除也以近事言之
賊至而不能禦賊去而不能追也其無益
於民者如此而欲民相信而服從也不亦
難乎必也得其賢也言聽而計用信賞而
punctuated:
祖宗之法而整頓之，搜其埋沒，禁其偽籍，嚴其訓練，剔其隱占，而又有不從者，重罰以懲之；其既從也，生息以蕃之。如此，則諸路之兵亦足以禦諸路之寇矣。於國計也，必以祖宗之法而調度之，備其旱潦，稽其侵漁，汰其冗食，禁其奢靡。有羨餘也，則倉庾以儲之；有措置也，則歲月以積之。如此，則天下之食亦足以供天下之兵矣。
然此特就事論事耳。若要其極，與其急於兵食，孰若急於弭盜？與其急於弭盜，孰若急於安民？安民之道無他焉，在乎慎選守令，重其權，乆其任，使民尊之信之而已。今之守令固未必皆賢也，而民恒有輕忽之心。何者？利不能為民興也，害不能為民除也。以近事言之，賊至而不能禦，賊去而不能追也。其無益於民者如此，而欲民相信而服從也，不亦難乎？必也得其賢也，言聽而計用，信賞而
translation_en:
…reorganize military affairs according to the laws of the imperial ancestors: seek out those concealed from the rolls, prohibit fraudulent registration, enforce rigorous training, and eliminate the covert appropriation of soldiers for private service. Those who still refuse to comply should receive severe punishment as a deterrent; once they comply, foster their livelihood and increase their numbers. In this way, the troops of the various regions will suffice to repel the bandits of those regions. As for state finances, these too must be managed according to the laws of the imperial ancestors: prepare against droughts and floods, investigate embezzlement and exploitation, eliminate unnecessary mouths maintained at public expense, and prohibit extravagance. When there is a surplus, store it in granaries; where provisions have been arranged, accumulate them over months and years. In this way, the grain of the realm will suffice to provision its troops.
Yet this is merely to discuss each matter on its own terms. If we seek the ultimate solution, rather than make troops and provisions our urgent concern, would it not be better to give priority to suppressing banditry? Rather than give priority to suppressing banditry, would it not be better to give priority to securing the people's peace? The way to secure their peace is simply to select prefects and magistrates carefully, strengthen their authority, and lengthen their tenure, so that the people respect and trust them. The prefects and magistrates of today are certainly not all necessarily worthy, and the people habitually regard them with contempt. Why? They cannot promote what benefits the people or remove what harms them. To speak of recent events, when bandits arrive they cannot resist them, and when bandits depart they cannot pursue them. When they are so useless to the people, is it not difficult to expect the people to trust and obey them? We must obtain worthy men, heed their words and employ their plans, make rewards dependable and…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
必罰藩司觀其風俗之大而不較其簿領
之煩瑣監司察其賢否之大而不較其一
刑一政之得失使其志得以上達而其澤
得以卞敷如是而民不相敬信不相悅服
乃復去而為盜萬萬無是理也明問所謂
大處分者亦唯不過責之有司之職如前
之云耳舍是固不能以有為也自古有治
人無治法此雖老生之常談而至理實不
外是惟執事進而教之幸甚
punctuated: 必罰。藩司觀其風俗之大，而不較其簿領之煩瑣；監司察其賢否之大，而不較其一刑一政之得失，使其志得以上達，而其澤得以卞敷。如是而民不相敬信，不相悅服，乃復去而為盜，萬萬無是理也。明問所謂大處分者，亦唯不過責之有司之職，如前之云耳。舍是，固不能以有為也。自古有治人，無治法。此雖老生之常談，而至理實不外是。惟執事進而教之，幸甚。
translation_en: …and punishments invariably imposed. The Provincial Administration Commission should consider the broad state of local customs rather than quibble over the minutiae of registers and documents; the surveillance officials should assess the broad question of these officials’ worthiness rather than quibble over the merits or faults of a single punishment or administrative act. This would allow their intentions to be conveyed upward and their beneficence to spread downward [?]. Under such circumstances, it is utterly inconceivable that the people would fail to respect and trust them, fail to submit willingly, and instead turn to banditry again. The major measures mentioned in your illuminating question amount simply to holding the responsible officials accountable for their duties, as stated above. Apart from this, nothing effective can be accomplished. Since antiquity, there have been men who bring about good government, but no laws that do so of themselves. Though this is an old scholar’s commonplace, the ultimate principle truly extends no further. I would be most fortunate if you would offer me further instruction.

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
三歲取士額浙江九十人度
地定才著為令甲遵行既久
奉率彌周是為正德八年之
秋巡按浙江監察御史袁宗
儒循近
制限列郡之士一千八百人以世
===
明等典試事鎖院校閱中式
者二十而一擇其文之醇與
士之邑里名氏內外百執事
職名為鄉試錄錄成謂世明
當序其後竊惟浙古揚州地
也其見於圖經記序辭賦倡
和諸集者曰帶江海抱湖山
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

三歲取士，額浙江九十人，度地定才，著為令甲。遵行既久，奉率彌周。是為正德八年之秋，巡按浙江監察御史袁宗儒循近制，限列郡之士一千八百人，以世明等典試事。鎖院校閱，中式者二十而一。擇其文之醇，與士之邑里名氏、內外百執事職名，為鄉試錄。錄成，謂世明當序其後。竊惟浙，古揚州地也。其見於圖經、記序、辭賦、倡和諸集者，曰：「帶江海，抱湖山。」
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

Scholars are selected every three years, with Zhejiang allotted a quota of ninety. The number of talented men to be selected is determined according to the territory, and this is established in the statutes. These provisions have long been observed, and compliance has become ever more thorough. In the autumn of the eighth year of Zhengde [1513], Yuan Zongru, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Zhejiang, followed recent regulations and limited the candidates from the various prefectures to eighteen hundred, appointing Shiming and others to oversee the examination. Sequestered within the examination compound, we assessed their work; one in twenty passed. We selected the most accomplished of their compositions and compiled the Record of the Provincial Examination, together with the successful candidates’ home localities and names and the titles and names of all officials serving inside and outside the compound. When the record was complete, I, Shiming, was told that I should write its postface.

I humbly reflect that Zhejiang was part of ancient Yangzhou. In illustrated geographical accounts, records and prefaces, literary compositions and rhapsodies, and collections of poems exchanged in response to one another, it is described as “girdled by rivers and sea, embracing lakes and mountains”…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
曰江東一都會東南一大都
會而會稽天目赤城鴈蕩之
為山錢塘震澤浙江鏡湖姚
江之為水峻嶒秀麗巉嵽蜿
蜒流注停蓄環抱委蛇清淑
所鍾陶和孕粹物受其偏尚
有嘉木異卉以資民用魚龍
===
隱見變怪滄溟萬頃間時出
雲雨以蘇枯槁而況人受其
正者乎故求其美俗曰士知
所學曰家習儒業同受學漢
祖者懷仁輔義詞約而達是
雖投札口授萬世立言者所
不能踰遭遇唐宗者十八登
punctuated: 曰江東一都會、東南一大都會。而會稽、天目、赤城、鴈蕩之為山，錢塘、震澤、浙江、鏡湖、姚江之為水，峻嶒秀麗，巉嵽蜿蜒，流注停蓄，環抱委蛇，清淑所鍾，陶和孕粹。物受其偏，尚有嘉木異卉以資民用；魚龍隱見，變怪滄溟萬頃間，時出雲雨以蘇枯槁，而況人受其正者乎？故求其美俗，曰士知所學，曰家習儒業。同受學漢祖者，懷仁輔義，詞約而達，是雖投札口授，萬世立言者所不能踰。遭遇唐宗者，十八登
translation_en:
…it is called “a metropolis east of the Yangzi” and “a great metropolis of the southeast.” Its mountains—Kuaiji, Tianmu, Chicheng, and Yandang—and its waters—Qiantang, Zhenze, the Zhejiang, Jinghu, and the Yaojiang—are lofty, rugged, and beautiful, steep and winding; they flow and gather, encircle and meander. Here pure and beneficent influences converge, fostering harmony and nurturing excellence. Even creatures that receive only a partial share of these influences include fine trees and unusual plants that serve the people’s needs. Fish and dragons appear and disappear, undergoing wondrous transformations amid the vast expanses of the blue sea, sometimes bringing forth clouds and rain to revive what has withered and dried. How much more, then, must this hold for human beings, who receive these influences in their fullness?
Thus, when we seek accounts of its admirable customs, we find it said that “scholars know what they should study” and that “households cultivate Confucian learning.” Those who “together received instruction from the founder of the Han” [?] cherished benevolence and upheld righteousness, their words concise yet expressive. Even when they committed their words to writing or delivered them orally, those who established enduring teachings in all subsequent ages could not surpass them. One who found favor with a Tang emperor, at eighteen attained …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
進士瀉胸中之蘊論諫數百
皆本仁義文起八代之衰則
其考試時所取士也王忠文
紹興中廷對下筆數千言百
忠憤所激可與天人三策相
表裏高宗親擢為第一朱文
公嘗稱之曰磊磊落落君子
===
人也有梅溪集朗誦之氣象
自别呂成公召試館職文特
典美嘗讀陸九淵之文喜之
及試禮部得一卷曰此江西
小陸之文也揭示果九淵人
服其精陳文節公著書明道
簡冊充棟片言落筆傳誦震
punctuated: 進士，瀉胸中之蘊，論諫數百，皆本仁義，文起八代之衰，則其考試時所取士也。王忠文，紹興中廷對，下筆數千言，百忠憤所激，可與天人三策相表裏。高宗親擢為第一。朱文公嘗稱之曰：「磊磊落落君子人也。」有《梅溪集》，朗誦之，氣象自别。呂成公召試館職，文特典美。嘗讀陸九淵之文，喜之。及試禮部，得一卷，曰：「此江西小陸之文也。」揭示，果九淵，人服其精。陳文節公著書明道，簡冊充棟，片言落筆，傳誦震
translation_en:
…attained the jinshi degree and poured forth what lay within his breast in hundreds of discourses and remonstrances, all grounded in benevolence and righteousness. His writing revived literature after eight dynasties of decline; he was among the men selected through the examinations of that time.

Wang, posthumously titled Zhongwen, answered questions at court during the Shaoxing era, writing several thousand words, all [?] inspired by loyal indignation. His response could stand alongside the Three Policy Responses on Heaven and Humanity, each illuminating the other. Emperor Gaozong personally placed him first. Master Zhu, posthumously titled Wengong, once praised him, saying: “He is an upright and open-hearted gentleman.” His collected writings are entitled the Meixi Collection; read aloud, they reveal a distinctive spirit.

Lü, posthumously titled Chenggong, was summoned to take an examination for an academy post; his writing was particularly refined and elegant. He once read an essay by Lu Jiuyuan and delighted in it. Later, while examining at the Ministry of Rites, he came upon a paper and said: “This is the writing of young Lu from Jiangxi.” When the identity was disclosed, it was indeed Jiuyuan, and people admired Lü’s discernment.

Chen, posthumously titled Wenjie, wrote books to elucidate the Way, his volumes filling the rafters. Even a few words from his brush were passed about and recited, resounding…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
響場屋相師文體丕變其作
為論學論者謂之决科之文
吕公以為其長不獨在文字
間金仁山所著大學疏義尚
書表註論孟考證中庸標註
諸書許白雲聞而從之求聖
賢之心而著為四書叢說二
===
人之書雖非專為科舉而作
要亦科舉之士之所不能遺
也我
朝國初宋景濂劉伯温王忠文
諸大儒作為文字微詞奥義
渾厚典則是正國人之所矜
式今所取士冀得諸若人而
punctuated:
響，場屋相師，文體丕變。其作為《論學論》者，謂之决科之文。吕公以為其長不獨在文字間。金仁山所著《大學疏義》《尚書表註》《論孟考證》《中庸標註》諸書，許白雲聞而從之，求聖賢之心，而著為《四書叢說》。二人之書，雖非專為科舉而作，要亦科舉之士之所不能遺也。
我朝國初，宋景濂、劉伯温、王忠文諸大儒，作為文字，微詞奥義，渾厚典則，是正國人之所矜式。今所取士，冀得諸若人而
translation_en:
…resounded; candidates in the examination halls took one another as models, and literary style underwent a great transformation. His composition entitled “Discourse on Learning” was called a work that could secure examination success. Master Lü held that his strengths lay not merely in literary composition. Jin Renshan wrote such books as Explications of the Great Learning, Tabulated Annotations to the Book of Documents, Textual Studies of the Analects and Mencius, and Key Annotations to the Doctrine of the Mean. Hearing of him, Xu Baiyun became his follower, sought to understand the minds of the sages and worthies, and composed Collected Explanations of the Four Books. Although these two men’s books were not written specifically for the civil-service examinations, they were nevertheless works that examination candidates could not neglect.
At the beginning of our dynasty, the great Confucian scholars Song Jinglian, Liu Bowen, Wang Zhongwen, and others composed writings whose subtle language and profound meaning, substantial richness and classical propriety, provided models for the people of the realm [?]. In selecting men through the examinations today, we hope to obtain men like these and …

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
用之其仰止思齊效規摸矩
力追古作於千百載之上渾
厚正大典則純明與理俱勝
者固深嘉樂進求其進也則
融通變化師其意不泥其迹
豈但獵涉記誦祖襲陳言而
務為同次則理勝乎文雖無
===
前輩渾厚正大典則純明氣
象要亦近似無相齟齬繼是
而勉焉以充以馴致其極拭
目改觀莫可涯涘故在不遺
下此則非所敢知焉今日取
士他日用之其光明俊偉立
遠大事業以步鄉先哲後塵
punctuated: 用之。其仰止思齊，效規摸矩，力追古作於千百載之上，渾厚正大，典則純明，與理俱勝者，固深嘉樂進。求其進也，則融通變化，師其意，不泥其迹，豈但獵涉記誦，祖襲陳言而務為同？次則理勝乎文，雖無前輩渾厚正大、典則純明氣象，要亦近似，無相齟齬。繼是而勉焉，以充以馴，致其極，拭目改觀，莫可涯涘，故在不遺。下此則非所敢知焉。今日取士，他日用之，其光明俊偉，立遠大事業，以步鄉先哲後塵，
translation_en: …and employ them. Those who look up to these predecessors and aspire to equal them, follow their standards and models, and strive to emulate ancient writings of hundreds or thousands of years ago—whose compositions are substantial and broad, upright and grand, exemplary and pure and lucid, excelling in both literary expression and principle—we certainly commend deeply and gladly advance. In seeking their further progress, we expect them to integrate what they have learned and transform it, taking the predecessors’ intent as their teacher without clinging to their outward traces. How could this mean merely reading widely, memorizing, and repeating inherited phrases in pursuit of sameness? Next come those whose grasp of principle surpasses their literary expression. Although they lack the substantial breadth, upright grandeur, exemplary form, purity, and lucidity of their predecessors, they nevertheless approach them and are not at odds with them. If they continue their efforts, developing their capacities and gradually attaining the highest level, we may look upon them with fresh eyes: their potential knows no bounds. Hence they too must not be overlooked. Those below this level are not such as I would presume to recognize. We select men today to employ them in days to come. May they be enlightened, outstanding, and great in talent, establishing far-reaching and substantial achievements and following in the footsteps of the earlier worthies of their native region…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text:
又由是而求其上焉是固以
人事君者至願若但假文詞
以為進身之階而他日所行
與今所學經傳所傳授聖賢
所議觀鄉邦先哲無一相當
者遂使論者謂以文欺人襲
取之敝至謂文不可以得士
===
嗚呼是豈文之罪哉故以文
取士固主司者之所當盡心
而勉焉以塞責者也至於主
司之所願望而不能悉用其
力者則爾多士之責也其勉
之哉
山東兗州府東平州汶上縣
punctuated:
又由是而求其上焉，是固以人事君者至願。若但假文詞以為進身之階，而他日所行，與今所學、經傳所傳授、聖賢所議觀、鄉邦先哲，無一相當者，遂使論者謂以文欺人，襲取之敝，至謂文不可以得士。嗚呼！是豈文之罪哉？故以文取士，固主司者之所當盡心而勉焉以塞責者也。至於主司之所願望而不能悉用其力者，則爾多士之責也。其勉之哉！
山東兗州府東平州汶上縣
translation_en:
…and, proceeding from this, seek to rise still higher: this is indeed the deepest wish of those who serve their ruler by providing him with worthy men. But if you merely use literary composition as a stepping-stone to advancement, and your conduct in later days accords in no respect with what you now study, what the classics and their commentaries transmit, what the sages and worthies discussed and observed [?], or the earlier worthies of your native region, you will lead critics to say that literary composition is used to deceive others. The abuses of gaining advancement through imitation may lead them even to claim that literary composition cannot serve to identify worthy men. Alas! Can this be the fault of literary composition? Thus, selecting men through literary composition is certainly a duty to which those presiding over the examination must devote their whole minds and energies, so as to discharge their responsibility. But bringing about what the presiding examiners hope for, yet cannot fully accomplish through their own efforts, is the responsibility of you, the assembled candidates. Apply yourselves diligently!
Wenshang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong…

title: 正德八年浙江鄉試錄
text: 儒學教諭林世明謹序
punctuated: 儒學教諭林世明謹序。
translation_en: …Lin Shiming, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wenshang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, respectfully composed this preface.
